title: The site
text: How this site is built, previewed, published and extended. It is one Quarto website over this repository’s docs/ and opengwasdb’s docs, rendered on the host where the data lives, and published from the gh-pages branch at https://blog.opengwas.io/opengwasdb-stores/.

title: The site
text:
The commands



Command
What it does




pixi run site
Stage both repositories’ docs, render the site, and check every served path.


pixi run site-preview
The same staging, then Quarto’s live-reloading preview on http://localhost:4200.


pixi run site-publish --dry-run
Render a clean checkout of origin/dev and commit it to gh-pages without pushing.


pixi run site-publish
The same, then push gh-pages. The owner runs this.


pixi run docs
Refresh a report: render its .qmd and copy the HTML to the name the site serves.



Nothing is rendered in CI: every page repeats the site’s navigation, so committed output would make parallel pull requests conflict.

title: The site
text:
Where a render puts things







Path
What




/data/opengwasdb/work/site/<checkout>/_site
The rendered site ($OPENGWASDB_SITE_OUT overrides it).


/data/opengwasdb/work/site/<checkout>/_stage
The mirror of docs/ the render reads ($OPENGWASDB_SITE_ROOT moves the work root).


/data/opengwasdb/work/site/opengwasdb.git
The bare clone the engine’s docs are staged from ($OPENGWASDB_SITE_ENGINE_CLONE overrides it).


docs/opengwasdb/
The engine’s docs staged at the pinned revision. Git-ignored, regenerated on every render.


docs/glossary.md
CONTEXT.md, staged as the glossary page. Git-ignored, regenerated.



Nothing the site build writes goes under /home or /tmp.
The render reads a mirror of docs/, not docs/ itself. That is deliberate: the mirror is where the link rewrite and the Mermaid spelling happen, so no source file is ever edited, and docs/ stays readable on GitHub.

title: The site
text:
Publishing
site-publish renders a clean detached worktree of the ref, so nothing depends on an uncommitted change in your checkout, and commits the output to a gh-pages worktree with a message naming the source commit. It creates gh-pages as an orphan branch when it is absent, so the published branch shares no history with a source branch.
It refuses a ref that is not on the remote, and it refuses a gh-pages worktree with uncommitted changes, because a publish replaces what that worktree holds.





flowchart TD
  A["pixi run site-publish --ref origin/dev"] --> B{"ref on the remote?"}
  B -- no --> X["refuse"]
  B -- yes --> C["fetch origin, resolve the source commit"]
  C --> D["clean detached worktree of that commit"]
  D --> E["stage the engine's docs at the pixi.lock pin"]
  E --> F["mirror docs/, rewrite outbound links, spell mermaid fences"]
  F --> G["quarto render into /data/opengwasdb/work/site/"]
  G --> H["replace the gh-pages worktree contents"]
  H --> I{"--dry-run?"}
  I -- yes --> J["commit to gh-pages locally, push nothing"]
  I -- no --> K["commit to gh-pages and push"]






The default ref is origin/dev until the cutover, after which it becomes origin/main.

title: The site
text:
Adding a page

Add a Markdown file under docs/ — docs/my-page.md — with a single # heading as its title. It is served at /my-page.html.
If it belongs to a section, add it to docs/_quarto.yml: the navbar for a section index, or a sidebar’s contents. A glob such as adr/*.md already covers a new ADR, so most pages need no configuration.
Use ```mermaid for a diagram and it renders as one, as it does on GitHub; dot files under docs/diagrams/ are served as the files they are.
Link to a sibling with its relative path (../spec/release-config.md). Link to anything outside docs/ with the relative path you would use on GitHub — the build rewrites it to that file on GitHub at the commit being rendered. A link the build rewrites is reported if the commit does not have the target.
Never move or rename a page that is already published. A reader’s link would break. If a page must move, keep the old path as an aliases entry in the new page’s YAML front matter; Quarto then writes a redirect page there, which the served-path check counts as an alias rather than a missing path.
Historical reports are not rendered: their source .qmd lives in docs/reports/, and pixi run docs renders it and copies the self-contained HTML to the root name the site serves. Do not add .qmd files to docs/ outside reports/ unless the page really must execute code at render time.

title: The site
text:
Checking a change
pixi run site ends with the served-path check: every path origin/main serves under docs/ today must be present or aliased in the output, and a missing path fails the build. Run it before opening a pull request that touches docs/.
You can run the check on its own against an existing render:
pixi run -e dev python3 -m project_site.urlcheck \
  --git-rev origin/main \
  --output /data/opengwasdb/work/site/<checkout>/_site

title: Resolver reference-overlap diagnostics
text:
resolve-analyses --variant-reference PATH accepts a plain-text or gzip-compressed Hybrid axis of canonical ALIDs (one per line, or a table with alid, variant_id, or id header). The parent loads it once and fork-shares the set. A SHA-256 fingerprint of its bytes invalidates resumed records when the axis changes. Missing/empty axes fail setup rather than silently skipping overlap.
Each successful per-Analysis record’s diagnostics includes ancestry_reference_rows_matched / ancestry_rows_read and variant_reference_rows_matched / rows_read. The former counts rows on the full ancestry Reference Resource up to ancestry accumulation’s stopping point, even when an extraction panel narrows the fit, before AF/SE/palindromic filters; ancestry_sites still counts distinct usable sites for the ancestry fit. The latter counts rows on the supplied Hybrid axis over the physical scan, regardless of AF/SE eligibility. Repeated rows are counted repeatedly. The stream is never reread for either measurement. Without --variant-reference, variant_reference_rows_matched is null. Failed scans retain partial diagnostics; downstream release policy must not treat those as complete overlap estimates. An ancestry-site bound can stop a non-quantitative physical scan early; quantitative phenotype-SD scans normally continue to EOF.
Overlap is a canonical-ALID measurement, not a guarantee of Dense routing. For GRCh38 sources, the Hybrid builder matches reference source keys without regard to allele-letter case (while preserving the source effect-allele order, Z sign, and EAF orientation); an on-axis source row must fill its Dense row, not become an off-reference Overflow association. The resolver-versus-built-store parity test covers this separately from ancestry/SD eligibility. A routing defect must not be classified as a low-overlap source exclusion. Cross-assembly comparisons still require explicit source-key/liftover evidence; canonical overlap alone does not establish that an hg19 source matches a GRCh38 axis.
With a provider-declared INFO policy (stores #175) or a numeric MAF threshold (stores #176), a positive threshold removes only below-threshold usable rows before ancestry, SD and routing evidence, so ancestry_reference_rows_matched counts only admitted rows while the legacy variant_reference_rows_matched and rows_read stay pre-admission canonical-row counts. Naming a variant reference also makes the Analysis whole-stream (stores #176, section 0): the physical scan continues to EOF, so rows_read and variant_reference_rows_matched are no longer a prefix even for a case-control Analysis the ancestry bound would once have stopped early. A publication projection over a filtered source must use that record’s build_eligible_rows_off_variant_reference / build_eligible_rows diagnostics rather than these legacy counts; see info-score-resolver.md.


Every record’s diagnostics carries ancestry_scope and ancestry_measurement_id (issue #282, ADR 0062). For every one-Analysis-per-file format the scope is analysis and the id is null: the ancestry_* counts above describe the Analysis’s own scan. For a BESD probe the scope is source_file: its ancestry fit and orientation were measured once over its file set’s whole .esi and are shared by every probe of that file set, so ancestry_sites, ancestry_rows_read, ancestry_stop_reason and ancestry_reference_rows_matched describe the .esi, while rows_read, variant_reference_rows_matched and the build-eligible counts stay the probe’s own. Records sharing one measurement carry the same ancestry_measurement_id, and index.json’s source_measurements lists each measurement made in that invocation once, with its Analyses. See besd-resolver.md.

title: Preregistration: Bounded-Prefix and Compiled-Parser Acceleration for Resolver Evidence Scans
text:
Document status: Locked before result inspection (issue #209). Results are recorded separately in bounded-evidence-scan-report.md, generated from the committed JSON artifacts once the study has run. Issue: opengwasdb#209 Depends on: opengwasdb#207 / ADR 0044 (resolve_analysis), opengwasdb#208 (resolve-analyses), and the full-reference policy study in opengwasdb-stores#152.



The Phase B resolver (opengwasdb.build.resolve.resolve_analysis, ADR 0044) reads each compressed GWAS-SSF source once and accumulates both the ancestry fit’s frequencies and the phenotype-SD evidence in that pass. It still decompresses the whole source and normalises every row in Python.
The full-reference policy study (opengwasdb-stores#152) rejected the fixed 10,000-site extraction panel: genome-wide assignment concordance was 95.10%, below the locked 98% threshold. That decision does not establish that every row of a sorted GWAS file must be read. This study asks whether a deterministic prefix of the source – fixed raw rows, or a fixed number of usable ancestry-reference matches – preserves the full-scan resolution, and separately whether a faster compiled parser exists that preserves GWAS-SSF semantics.
Two effects are measured separately: early termination and parser throughput.

The manifest is the frozen 106-Analysis stratified sample from opengwasdb-stores#152 (50 quantitative decile rows, 50 case-control decile rows, 6 explicit edge cases). It is copied here verbatim so the evaluation frame is committed with the study; its data_file paths are the acquisition mirror and are read-only.
Gates are fixed at the ADR-0028 / config-full.yaml values: tau=0.50, delta=0.20, n_min=5000, residual_max=0.06, orientation_flip_r=-0.5, maf_floor=0.01, evidence_sample=20_000. Method tiers are the release’s: quantitative → stored_effect_scale=sd, original_sd_method=estimated_from_source_maf; case-control → stored_effect_scale=log_or, original_sd_method=binary_trait. No gate, tier or reference is retuned at any point in this study.



Every rule is applied with the same resolver, gates and references. The full scan (scan_limit=None, stop_reason=eof) is the comparator.
Fixed raw-row prefixes (ScanLimit.max_rows): 25,000; 50,000; 100,000; 250,000; 500,000; 1,000,000 source rows.
Evidence-driven prefixes (ScanLimit.max_ancestry_sites): stop once the ancestry fit has accumulated 5,000; 10,000; 20,000; or 50,000 distinct reference sites with a usable frequency. The counted quantity is the evidence the NNLS fit consumes, not raw matches, so a repeated ALID cannot inflate it.
Every rule is reported, including ones that fail. No threshold is added, removed or moved after results are seen.



Per Analysis and rule the harness records: stop_reason; source rows consumed; usable ancestry sites; distinct chromosomes and maximum chromosome reached; compressed source bytes (file size) and uncompressed bytes consumed (instrumented faithful counter); wall/user/system seconds; peak RSS; the whole AncestryAssignment (assigned ancestry, dominant super-population, proportions, margin, overlap, residual, gate reason, EAF orientation outcome and r, compositions); the whole phenotype-SD resolution (status, reason, SD, dispersion, evidence considered, estimate inputs, evidence_sampled); and the difference from the full-scan record.
The exact input manifest, commands, tool versions and cache condition are recorded with the artifact.



A stopping rule is acceptable only if all criteria hold across every stratum (source layout, study design, size decile, AF availability, chromosome ordering, known failure mode):
Ancestry (at least as strict as opengwasdb-stores#152):

Assignment/gate concordance ≥ 98% — the fraction of Analyses whose assigned_ancestry and gate_reason both match the full scan.
Orientation sensitivity 100% — every Analysis whose full scan fails the eaf_orientation gate is also reported as eaf_orientation by the rule.
Zero false-positive EUR assignments — no Analysis that the full scan leaves Unassigned (or gates out) is assigned EUR by the rule.
Zero execution errors — no rule introduces an error the full scan does not have.

Phenotype SD (quantitative Analyses with a full-scan estimate):

Status agreement 100% — estimated/skipped/unavailable and the reason agree exactly.
Estimate difference ≤ 2% relative difference in implied SD.
Dispersion difference ≤ 2% relative difference in dispersion.

Quantitative Analyses lacking usable source AF are reported as controlled exclusions and are kept in the reported denominator rather than dropped from it (criterion 5 still applies to them; criteria 6–7 apply where a full-scan estimate exists).



Among the rules that satisfy every criterion, adopt the smallest: fewest max_rows first, then fewest max_ancestry_sites, then the rule that consumes fewest rows on the evaluation set. Ties are broken by the rule with the lower mean wall time.

If a rule passes: propose it as an explicit, non-default resolver option (ScanLimit), carrying a stopping-rule version, thresholds, parser implementation/version, rows and usable matches consumed, and whether EOF or an early-stop condition ended the scan in the resume fingerprint. Full scanning stays the default.
If no rule passes: retain the full scan; report the negative result and adopt only a semantics-preserving compiled-parser improvement if the parser benchmark supports one.




Measured on the same warm-cache condition, with decompression and parsing separated:

stream_projected_metrics — current Python gzip + bytes projection.
External gzip -dc (argv-safe, filenames never shell-interpolated) feeding the same projection.
External pigz -dc feeding the same projection.
pandas C-engine chunked read with usecols, explicit types and NA handling (pandas is already a project dependency).
PyArrow open_csv streaming, only if an isolated import is available; never added as a production dependency for the experiment.
R data.table::fread(cmd=...) as a reference upper bound where R is available; never a production dependency.

Decompression-only throughput is measured separately for Python gzip, gzip -dc and pigz -dc. A prototype that stops before EOF must reap its decompressor and handle the expected broken pipe.
A candidate parser is admissible only if its projected rows are field-for-field identical to stream_projected_metrics over parity fixtures covering: ordinary and hm_* GWAS-SSF projections; reordered and extra columns; ragged/short and quoted rows; missing, invalid and non-finite numerics; chromosome and allele normalization; effect-allele flipping and EAF orientation; palindromic/invalid identities; and duplicate/file-order determinism.




Reconsidering the rejected 10k extraction panel without new evidence.
Adding R or PyArrow as OpenGWASDB runtime dependencies.
Trading false-positive EUR assignments or orientation sensitivity for speed.
Introducing a second physical source scan for phenotype-SD evidence.
Changing Phase B candidate acceptance or invoking Phase A Store construction.
Mutating or re-downloading the source mirror.

  --manifest docs/benchmark-output/opengwasdb_resolver_evidence_scan_manifest.tsv \
  --ancestry-reference /data/opengwasdb/reference/ancestry-mixture/ref_freqs.hg38.tsv.gz \
  --ancestry-groups /data/opengwasdb/reference/ancestry-mixture/ancestry_groups.tsv \

# Parser/decompressor prototype benchmark

  --ancestry-reference /data/opengwasdb/reference/ancestry-mixture/ref_freqs.hg38.tsv.gz \

# Render the results report from the two artifacts (never hand-edited numbers)

  --manifest docs/benchmark-output/opengwasdb_resolver_evidence_scan_manifest.tsv \
  --ancestry-reference /data/opengwasdb/reference/ancestry-mixture/ref_freqs.hg38.tsv.gz \
  --ancestry-groups /data/opengwasdb/reference/ancestry-mixture/ancestry_groups.tsv \
  --report-only docs/benchmark-output/opengwasdb_resolver_evidence_scan_v2.json \
  --merge docs/benchmark-output/opengwasdb_resolver_evidence_scan_parsers.json \
  --report docs/spec/bounded-evidence-scan-report-v2.md
Note: The historical v1 evaluation artifacts remain preserved at docs/benchmark-output/opengwasdb_resolver_evidence_scan.json and docs/spec/bounded-evidence-scan-report.md.

title: Preregistration: Bounded-Prefix and Compiled-Parser Acceleration for Resolver Evidence Scans
text:
Every rule is applied with the same resolver, gates and references. The full scan (scan_limit=None, stop_reason=eof) is the comparator.
Fixed raw-row prefixes (ScanLimit.max_rows): 25,000; 50,000; 100,000; 250,000; 500,000; 1,000,000 source rows.
Evidence-driven prefixes (ScanLimit.max_ancestry_sites): stop once the ancestry fit has accumulated 5,000; 10,000; 20,000; or 50,000 distinct reference sites with a usable frequency. The counted quantity is the evidence the NNLS fit consumes, not raw matches, so a repeated ALID cannot inflate it.
Every rule is reported, including ones that fail. No threshold is added, removed or moved after results are seen.

title: Preregistration: Bounded-Prefix and Compiled-Parser Acceleration for Resolver Evidence Scans
text:
Per Analysis and rule the harness records: stop_reason; source rows consumed; usable ancestry sites; distinct chromosomes and maximum chromosome reached; compressed source bytes (file size) and uncompressed bytes consumed (instrumented faithful counter); wall/user/system seconds; peak RSS; the whole AncestryAssignment (assigned ancestry, dominant super-population, proportions, margin, overlap, residual, gate reason, EAF orientation outcome and r, compositions); the whole phenotype-SD resolution (status, reason, SD, dispersion, evidence considered, estimate inputs, evidence_sampled); and the difference from the full-scan record.
The exact input manifest, commands, tool versions and cache condition are recorded with the artifact.

title: Preregistration: Bounded-Prefix and Compiled-Parser Acceleration for Resolver Evidence Scans
text:
A stopping rule is acceptable only if all criteria hold across every stratum (source layout, study design, size decile, AF availability, chromosome ordering, known failure mode):
Ancestry (at least as strict as opengwasdb-stores#152):

Assignment/gate concordance ≥ 98% — the fraction of Analyses whose assigned_ancestry and gate_reason both match the full scan.
Orientation sensitivity 100% — every Analysis whose full scan fails the eaf_orientation gate is also reported as eaf_orientation by the rule.
Zero false-positive EUR assignments — no Analysis that the full scan leaves Unassigned (or gates out) is assigned EUR by the rule.
Zero execution errors — no rule introduces an error the full scan does not have.

Phenotype SD (quantitative Analyses with a full-scan estimate):

Status agreement 100% — estimated/skipped/unavailable and the reason agree exactly.
Estimate difference ≤ 2% relative difference in implied SD.
Dispersion difference ≤ 2% relative difference in dispersion.

Quantitative Analyses lacking usable source AF are reported as controlled exclusions and are kept in the reported denominator rather than dropped from it (criterion 5 still applies to them; criteria 6–7 apply where a full-scan estimate exists).

title: Preregistration: Bounded-Prefix and Compiled-Parser Acceleration for Resolver Evidence Scans
text:
Among the rules that satisfy every criterion, adopt the smallest: fewest max_rows first, then fewest max_ancestry_sites, then the rule that consumes fewest rows on the evaluation set. Ties are broken by the rule with the lower mean wall time.

If a rule passes: propose it as an explicit, non-default resolver option (ScanLimit), carrying a stopping-rule version, thresholds, parser implementation/version, rows and usable matches consumed, and whether EOF or an early-stop condition ended the scan in the resume fingerprint. Full scanning stays the default.
If no rule passes: retain the full scan; report the negative result and adopt only a semantics-preserving compiled-parser improvement if the parser benchmark supports one.

title: Preregistration: Bounded-Prefix and Compiled-Parser Acceleration for Resolver Evidence Scans
text:
Measured on the same warm-cache condition, with decompression and parsing separated:

stream_projected_metrics — current Python gzip + bytes projection.
External gzip -dc (argv-safe, filenames never shell-interpolated) feeding the same projection.
External pigz -dc feeding the same projection.
pandas C-engine chunked read with usecols, explicit types and NA handling (pandas is already a project dependency).
PyArrow open_csv streaming, only if an isolated import is available; never added as a production dependency for the experiment.
R data.table::fread(cmd=...) as a reference upper bound where R is available; never a production dependency.

Decompression-only throughput is measured separately for Python gzip, gzip -dc and pigz -dc. A prototype that stops before EOF must reap its decompressor and handle the expected broken pipe.
A candidate parser is admissible only if its projected rows are field-for-field identical to stream_projected_metrics over parity fixtures covering: ordinary and hm_* GWAS-SSF projections; reordered and extra columns; ragged/short and quoted rows; missing, invalid and non-finite numerics; chromosome and allele normalization; effect-allele flipping and EAF orientation; palindromic/invalid identities; and duplicate/file-order determinism.

title: OpenGWAS Roadmap
text:
Status: draft
Last updated: 2026-07-06


OpenGWAS should move from being a very large online archive of GWAS summary statistics into a modular, reproducible, high-performance summary-statistics compute substrate.
The current model is economically and operationally fragile: around 20 TB of GWAS VCF files plus multiple derived query formats, all maintained centrally, with cloud costs growing faster than plausible revenue. OpenGWASDB changes the shape of the problem. It lets us publish compact, immutable Store Releases that can be queried locally, on HPC, or behind a thin API without rebuilding many specialised copies of the same data.
The strategic aim is to create a pipeline from published GWAS to performant storage to whole-phenome enabled analyses.



OpenGWASDB gives OpenGWAS a different architecture:

Store data once in compact, self-contained releases rather than keeping many query-specific representations.
Use Dense stores for full GWAS batches that share a large variant axis.
Use Ragged stores for sparse molecular QTL, cis-plus-signals, and other uneven datasets.
Complete stores against declared reference panels at build time so common query paths do not require online LD proxy computation.
Keep stores modular by data batch, ancestry, assay, or release cycle.
Query stores through the same layout-independent API whether they are local files, mounted HPC storage, or routed through a remote service.
Treat published Store Releases as immutable; editing means building a new release from a changed manifest, not mutating a live object.

This makes OpenGWAS less like a single cloud-hosted database and more like a family of versioned analytical assets.
Performance:

A full UK Biobank dense observed-only benchmark built 2,514 GWAS VCFs into a 58.05 GB store from 425.4 GB of source VCFs, a 7.33x reduction.
The same benchmark retained fast stateless query patterns over a genome-wide store, including PheWAS, regional, top-hit, random lookup, and full-analysis extraction.
A ragged eQTLGen cis benchmark shows the separate sparse path for molecular-style datasets where dense storage is the wrong default.

Main finding: GWAS summary statistics can be stored in a compact way with highly performant querying.




Store releases are the unit of trust. A Store Release must be self-identifying, immutable, validated, and interpretable without a running catalogue service.
Local-first, service-compatible. The same store should support laptop, HPC, and cloud/API usage. The service layer should route and authorise queries, not become the only place the data can be used. The interface to the store should be user friendly and easy to install.
Build once, query many. Expensive normalisation, liftover, reference completion, and indexing should happen during build or release generation, not inside interactive user queries.
Dense and Ragged are peers. Full-coverage GWASs and sparse molecular datasets need different storage layouts. The roadmap should not force sparse biology into dense arrays just for uniformity.
Reference completion is a release enhancement. Imputed associations must remain distinguishable from observed associations, and quality metrics must be recorded. Completion produces a new release.
The catalogue is outside the store. Store discovery, remote routing, default release selection, billing, and access control belong in a catalogue/service layer above the file format.
Reference-panel assignment should be data-derived where possible. Source ancestry labels are useful but incomplete. Allele-frequency similarity between each analysis and a pool of LD reference panels should help decide which reference panel and therefore which store an analysis belongs to.




Reference completion depends on having the right LD reference panel. The existing UKB EUR LD eigenvector scripts should become the first implementation of a reusable reference-panel build pipeline, then be repeated for each major ancestry.
A possible EBI assignment workflow:

Build a pool of ancestry-specific LD reference panels, each with eigenvectors, LD blocks, variant lists, allele frequencies, checksums, and provenance.
For each incoming analysis, compute an allele-frequency fingerprint over a shared, well-behaved set of variants.
Compare the analysis fingerprint against each reference panel using metrics such as allele-frequency correlation, weighted RMSE, principal-component projection, and missingness.
Assign the analysis to the best matching reference panel when the distance is clearly below a threshold.
Cluster analyses with the same reference-panel assignment into the same store when their coverage, source format, access class, and release cadence also align.
Mark mixed, uncertain, or low-information analyses explicitly rather than forcing them into a confident ancestry bucket.
Record the selected panel, competing panel scores, variants used, thresholds, and assignment confidence in the build manifest and catalogue.

This gives the store factory a practical partitioning rule: stores can be organised around reference panels, not only around source collections. It also makes reference completion, query semantics, and downstream causal inference more transparent.
Caveats:

Allele-frequency similarity is a proxy for LD compatibility, not proof of it.
Multi-ancestry meta-analyses may need a mixed/unassigned class, multiple completed releases, or a policy of observed-only storage.
EAF availability and scope vary by source; the assignment algorithm must tolerate missing, variant-scoped, and association-scoped frequencies.
Palindromic alleles, strand issues, low INFO variants, and allele-orientation errors should be excluded or down-weighted during assignment.
Panel choice should remain auditable and overrideable when curator knowledge is stronger than the automatic score.






Goal: make OpenGWASDB reliable enough to replace the expensive internal query formats for the main OpenGWAS data classes.
Deliverables:

Freeze a v0.1/v0.2 Store Release contract for Dense Observed-Only full-GWAS stores.
Complete the Ragged Observed-Only path for cis-plus-signals and molecular QTL stores.
Maintain one public sparse array query contract across Dense and Ragged layouts.
Harden build pipelines from GWAS VCF, GWAS-SSF-like tabular sources, BESD-like sparse inputs, and batch manifests.
Expand validation so corrupted manifests, indexes, arrays, association status, and variant axes fail before query time.
Maintain benchmark reports for storage footprint, build time, and query latency by store type.
Define acceptance targets for production replacement, such as storage ratio, build throughput, query latency, and validation runtime.

Key decision:

OpenGWASDB should become the canonical analytical representation for summary statistics; legacy VCF and source formats should become provenance and rebuild inputs, not the primary query substrate.




Goal: remove query-time imputation and make stores comparable on declared reference panels.
Deliverables:

Define an LD reference panel registry with panel identity, assembly, ancestry, variant set, LD blocks, checksums, allele convention, and provenance.
Generalise the current UKB EUR LD eigenvector scripts into a repeatable panel-build workflow for each major ancestry.
Store allele-frequency fingerprints for LD reference panels and, when available, for analyses.
Prototype automated reference-panel assignment for EBI analyses using allele-frequency similarity.
Implement Dense Reference-Completed releases for full GWAS batches.
Implement Ragged Reference-Completed regions for cis and significant trans regions without expanding suggestive singleton signals.
Store imputed z and se, association status, imputation masks, and block-by-analysis quality summaries.
Support observed-only query mode over completed stores.
Benchmark completion cost and query-time savings across ancestry-specific panels.

Key decision:

Reference completion should be treated as a reproducible release-generation step, not as an online service feature. The API can expose completed results, but should not be responsible for computing them interactively.
Store partitioning should be allowed to follow reference-panel assignment: if two analyses match different LD panels, they should usually not be forced into the same completed store.




Goal: make it feasible to build and maintain many stores, including dozens of small sparse stores and several very large multi-ancestry stores.
Deliverables:

Create a store-build factory that consumes source manifests and emits validated Store Releases plus build reports.
Support batch-level build manifests for ancestry, assay, consortium, source format, access class, and release cadence.
Add analysis-to-panel assignment reports so curators can inspect why an analysis entered a particular ancestry-specific store.
Add resumable and parallel build execution for large dense stores.
Add incremental build planning for unpublished working sets, while preserving immutable published releases.
Represent add/remove/edit operations as manifest diffs that produce new releases.
Track release lineage: source release, observed-only store, completed store, derived products, and superseded releases.
Build a registry of expected stores, likely including full GWAS stores, ancestry-specific stores, molecular sparse stores, and derived-analysis stores.
Produce operational dashboards for storage footprint, build time, validation failures, and query benchmark regressions.

Key decision:

“Editing stores” should mean editing build manifests and producing new releases. Mutable published stores would undercut reproducibility and make downstream analyses hard to audit.




Goal: provide remote access to many stores while keeping the stores usable without the service.
Deliverables:

Design a RESTful API for exact variant, range, PheWAS, top-hit, sparse lookup, analysis extraction, and metadata queries.
Add a catalogue that maps store IDs, releases, ancestries, assays, traits, and access policies to physical store locations.
Route one request across multiple Store Releases and return a unified sparse array result plus metadata joins.
Support stateless workers that can mount stores from local disk, object storage, or HPC filesystems.
Add authentication, authorisation, quotas, and audit logging outside the Store Release format.
Add client libraries that can use either local paths or remote API endpoints with similar query semantics.
Keep expensive derived computations out of synchronous API paths unless they operate on precomputed store products.

Key decision:

The API should be a router and access layer over Store Releases, not a replacement for the Store Release abstraction.




Goal: leverage the assembled, performant store system to create analyses that are difficult or impossible with the current archive.
Deliverables:

Build MR of everything versus everything from precomputed instruments and store-native sparse queries.
Store sample-overlap matrices, using the pleiodb approach as prior art, so downstream causal and genetic-correlation analyses can account for overlap.
Store fine-mapping credible sets and very sparse Bayes factors as first-class derived products linked back to source Store Releases.
Extend the format strategy for WGS-scale summary statistics where variant counts and allele complexity exceed current GWAS assumptions.
Produce cross-store trait, variant, instrument, locus, and ancestry indexes for discovery and batch analysis.
Feed completed and harmonised stores into GPMap analyses as a stable summary-statistics layer.

Key decision:

OpenGWASDB becomes most valuable when it is not only a fast lookup engine, but the substrate for repeatedly generated derived datasets: instruments, overlap matrices, credible sets, fine-mapping summaries, and all-by-all causal scans.





This approach gives us two things:

A cost effective way to continue hosting OpenGWAS sustainably
An analytical substrate for causal inference.

The exact value proposition needs to be refined.



Highest priority:

Productionise dense full-GWAS builds and validation.
Finish ragged observed-only build/query/validation for molecular datasets.
Turn the UKB EUR LD eigenvector scripts into a reusable reference-panel build pipeline.
Prototype EBI analysis-to-reference-panel assignment using allele-frequency similarity.
Define production acceptance metrics and run them on representative stores.
Make build manifests explicit enough to reproduce store releases.
Decide the first official store partitioning strategy: by reference panel, ancestry, data source, assay, release, or a combination.

Next priority:

Implement reference completion against one GPMap/LD panel path.
Design the external catalogue schema.
Specify REST endpoints and response shapes around the existing sparse array query contract.
Define derived-product store types for sample overlap, credible sets, Bayes factors, and MR results.

Later priority:

Multi-panel and multi-ancestry completion at scale.
WGS-scale format extensions.
All-by-all MR production pipeline.
Cost-aware deployment across object storage, HPC filesystems, and API workers.





What is the first production store family that proves the replacement: UK Biobank full GWAS, all current OpenGWAS full GWAS, or a mixed dense-plus-ragged pilot?
What are the storage and latency thresholds required before OpenGWASDB can retire a current query format?
Should official public stores be partitioned primarily by source collection, ancestry, access policy, assay type, or release cadence?
Should official completed stores be partitioned primarily by assigned LD reference panel?
Which reference panels should define the first completed releases, and how will ancestry labels be governed?
What thresholds should decide confident, uncertain, mixed, or unassigned allele-frequency matches?
How should multi-ancestry meta-analyses be represented: observed-only, assigned to the closest panel, or completed separately against multiple panels?
What derived product should be the flagship demonstration of the new platform: all-by-all MR, fine-mapped credible sets, sample-overlap-aware scans, or GPMap integration?
How much of the service layer should be OpenGWAS-specific, and how much should remain generic over Store Releases?

Define derived-product store types for sample overlap, credible sets, Bayes factors, and MR results.

Later priority:

Multi-panel and multi-ancestry completion at scale.
WGS-scale format extensions.
All-by-all MR production pipeline.
Cost-aware deployment across object storage, HPC filesystems, and API workers.

title: OpenGWAS Roadmap
text:
What is the first production store family that proves the replacement: UK Biobank full GWAS, all current OpenGWAS full GWAS, or a mixed dense-plus-ragged pilot?
What are the storage and latency thresholds required before OpenGWASDB can retire a current query format?
Should official public stores be partitioned primarily by source collection, ancestry, access policy, assay type, or release cadence?
Should official completed stores be partitioned primarily by assigned LD reference panel?
Which reference panels should define the first completed releases, and how will ancestry labels be governed?
What thresholds should decide confident, uncertain, mixed, or unassigned allele-frequency matches?
How should multi-ancestry meta-analyses be represented: observed-only, assigned to the closest panel, or completed separately against multiple panels?
What derived product should be the flagship demonstration of the new platform: all-by-all MR, fine-mapped credible sets, sample-overlap-aware scans, or GPMap integration?
How much of the service layer should be OpenGWAS-specific, and how much should remain generic over Store Releases?

title: Resolving GWAS-VCF Analysis metadata
Resolving GWAS-VCF Analysis metadata
text:
Every manifest row must provide source_genome_build. source_assembly is a compatibility alias; if both are populated, their normalized builds must agree. --source-build is an explicit fallback only for rows that omit both. The ancestry reference build is always supplied with --reference-build.
Same-build inputs proceed without transformation. A GRCh37/hg19 GWAS-VCF used with a GRCh38/hg38 reference requires --chain-file. Each lifted SNP must have one mapping; a reverse-strand mapping complements both source alleles before canonical orientation, so AF and signed effects still name the transformed effect allele. Ambiguous mappings and indels (whose target alleles a single position lift cannot establish) fail rather than choosing or inventing Variant Identity. Other build directions and cross-build Source Formats without an implemented liftover projection produce a controlled failure before source records are read. Builds are not inferred from filenames, coordinates, or VCF headers.
Source build, reference build, chain path, chain SHA-256, chain size and chain mtime are stored in each resolution record and its resume fingerprint. Source identity continues to use the manifest-recorded checksum together with the observed file size and mtime; the resolver does not hash every source body.

title: Resolving GWAS-VCF Analysis metadata
Resolving GWAS-VCF Analysis metadata
text: GWAS-VCF resolution does not support a declared INFO/imputation-score filter. The manifest parser refuses that configuration rather than silently ignoring it. The path does not choose method tiers, alter ancestry gates or formulas, decide Store membership, or execute a Store build. Those remain caller-owned policy as described by ADR 0044.

title: Converting a Store Release to format 0.2.0
text:
Format 0.2.0 is Zarr v3 with the sharding codec: the unit a query reads (the inner chunk) is decoupled from the unit stored as a file (the shard), so the Dense Analysis-axis inner chunk can narrow without multiplying the file count. ADR 0057 records what 0.2.0 is and why conversion—not a rebuild—is the migration route; spec §10a describes the physical layout.


pixi run -e dev python scripts/convert_store_to_0_2_0.py \
    /data/opengwasdb/stores/OGS-00009/store.opengwasdb \
    --into /data/opengwasdb/work/epic240/245/OGS-00009-v3-c64 \
    --dense-analysis-chunk 64 \
    --dense-shard 100000x1024 \
    --workers 32







flag
meaning




STORE
the 0.1.0 release to convert (Dense, Ragged or Hybrid); never written


--into DEST
where the new 0.2.0 release is published; must not exist


--dense-analysis-chunk N
Dense planes’ Analysis-axis inner chunk (default 64). The variant-axis inner chunk stays 1,000


--dense-shard ROWSxCOLS
Dense planes’ shard, a whole multiple of the inner chunk (default 100000x1024)


--workers N
processes writing destination shards (default 1). Each worker owns whole shards





Every layout whose arrays the role table can name:







layout
data.zarr trees converted




Dense Observed-Only
data.zarr


Dense Reference-Completed
data.zarr (the imputed mask, on_panel, eaf_reference and the SE/EAF side tables included); the completion-quality data lives in index.sqlite and is copied unchanged


Ragged Observed-Only
data.zarr/ragged (the CSR sequences, offsets and the z overflow table) and top_hits


Ragged Reference-Completed
the same, plus imputed and eaf_reference


Hybrid
the outer release and its nested Dense Component (data.zarr and dense/data.zarr), so a half-converted Hybrid cannot be published



rho/* is converted where present. An array or group the role table does not name fails the conversion; nothing is copied with a guessed layout.



The Dense inner chunk and shard are parameters because #246 benchmarks them. The Ragged 1-D shards are fixed here, by the seam’s role table (opengwasdb.store.arrays), because they are not shape-dependent:









array role
inner chunk
shard
why




Ragged association sequences (z, se, variant_index, eaf, imputed)
200,000
50,000,000 elements, clipped to a whole number of inner chunks
OGS-00011’s overflow sequences are 3,085,080,783 entries: 62 files per array at ~50–200 MB each, not 3,086 at the old one-million cap and not one multi-GB file


Ragged per-variant side arrays (eaf_baseline, eaf_reference)
the serving sequence’s chunk
10,000,000 elements
read whole or per position, so the shard only bounds the file and the writer’s block


Ragged exception/overflow tables (z_overflow_*, eaf_exception_*, se_exception_*)
the role policy’s 200,000, clipped
10,000,000 elements
OGS-00011’s Ragged eaf_exception_index is 180,396,687 entries: 19 files of 80 MB, rather than one 1.4 GB file


Ragged CSR offsets
10,000
one shard holding the array
a handful of Analyses; read whole



The Ragged sequence shard is bounded by cells, not by one Analysis’s run, so a future variant-side index can be added beside the Analysis-sorted arrays (#252) without re-sharding them.




Shard-writing is parallel over destination shards; each worker holds one shard block (the default Dense shard is 100,000 × 1,024 int16 ≈ 205 MB; the widest Ragged sequence shard is 50,000,000 × 4 B ≈ 200 MB). More workers bound throughput, never correctness, because no two workers own one shard. /usr/bin/time -v around the run records peak RSS.



opengwasdb validate <dest> must report no errors, and
from opengwasdb.store.convert import verify_conversion
verify_conversion(source, dest)   # raises on any bit difference
re-runs the bit-exact check on its own; for a Hybrid it checks both Zarr trees. benchmarks/benchmark_store_comparison.py runs the seven query shapes on both stores and fails if any result differs.

The two large changes have different causes, and only one is the encoding.
A wide scan pays for the decode. Reading one band directly through DenseSePlane, 52,253,910 cells: 0.0050 µs/cell at float16, 0.0700 µs/cell at int8_residual — 14×, because reconstructing se needs eaf decoded and an exp per cell. That is the whole of the all-Analysis regional regression. The selected-Analysis query is 364.29× faster than global filtering and meets the stated under-10-ms target. Every chunk trial matched its global subset.
The rebuilt index occupies 905,110,866 bytes (863.2 MiB) at the selected 16,384-entry chunk size, against 722,241,274 bytes (688.8 MiB) for the same store’s index before this change. Adding eaf therefore cost 174.4 MiB, not the 40-80 MiB #131 estimated — a 2.2-4.4x overrun. That added array is 0.31% of the 55.4 GiB store against the “under 0.15%” #131 projected, so the trade is still strongly favourable and the conclusion does not change; but the estimate was wrong, and the measured figure is what should be quoted from here on.
Historical identical benchmark runs varied by 13% for bulk and 27% for top hits, so changes below roughly 1.5× are not distinguishable from noise at this repetition count. The recovered 1.301 ms result is only 11.2% above the 1.17 ms pre-EAF baseline. PheWAS and regional queries are unchanged by this ticket: neither uses the top-hit index, so no improvement is attributed here. Their absolute figures do differ from the ones recorded against the EAF regression (PheWAS 20.5 ms, regional 938 ms) because this store also carries the #135 baseline-chunking repair, which is what moved them.
Bulk is the one figure this record cannot account for: 33,426 ms against the regression, 19,298 ms here — 1.73x, above the 1.5x floor at which this benchmark can distinguish a change from noise. It is not attributable to the top-hit index, which a bulk query never reads. The #135 repair is the likely cause, but that is a hypothesis and is not measured here; it should not be claimed as a result of this work.
The corrected millisecond-aware parser records the original build duration as 41,714.021 seconds (11.59 hours). The MR smoke test is unchanged at beta 0.115089, SE 0.005386, p=2.60e-101 with 66 instruments.
The complete post-hoc migration (stored-Z scan, decoded-EAF collection, and three tier writes) took approximately 21 minutes on this host, 3.0% of the original 11.59-hour VCF build.
#132’s added inline pass is much cheaper than that upper bound, and is now measured rather than bounded. On a ukb-b Dense-from-VCF pilot build (10 analyses, 9,847,701 variants, 422.007 s wall), the pass logs its own start and end:
16:10:11,898 Collecting top-hit EAF in variant-row order for 1517509 candidate cells
16:10:15,686 Writing top-hit index from 1517509 harvested candidate cells
3.788 s for 1,517,509 candidate cells — 0.898% of build wall time. It does not repeat the stored-Z scan, because the build already holds the candidate coordinates. This is consistent with the genome-scale result: finngen-r13 r13-pilot-20 (21,230,615 variants) built in 4,414.7 s against 4,539.9 s for the same release before the pass existed, i.e. 2.8% faster, within run-to-run variation.
Those log lines are only visible if the caller configures logging; the store registry’s generators did not, which is fixed in opengwasdb-stores.

The second pair exists because the first pair put four peak-memory results within 30% of the 300 MB cap (212–217 MB), and the ticket requires such a result to be confirmed by a second back-to-back pair. Both pairs pass every limit.
The four conversion logs are the converter’s own phase timings plus /usr/bin/time -v’s wall clock and peak RSS. v3-c1000 was converted before the top_hit_shard_chunks provenance field existed (its write path is unchanged, so its bytes are what today’s converter writes); its top-hit shard is still recorded in provenance.zarr_v3_conversion.layouts.



A conversion (w248’s OGS-00010) was running in the same window, so the top-hit comparison is an interleaved A/B rather than a quiet absolute harness run: v3-c64 and v3-c64-topshard1 alternate within one process, sample by sample (an earlier cross-process design was too noisy to settle the difference), 100 pairs in each of 5 fresh-process rounds, and the per-array result digests are compared between the sides in every round. The committed JSON records 500 samples per side, medians 12.064 ms (sharded, v3-c64) against 11.083 ms (unsharded), ratio 1.0885, 0.1635 ms per read, identity holding. Those absolute medians are contended-machine numbers; the ratio is what answers whether the top-hit index should be sharded. python benchmarks/zarr3_lever_tables.py decision regenerates the tables from this file and reproduces the numbers above.

(cd /tmp/epic240/244/base-src && pixi run -e dev python benchmarks/benchmark_store_comparison.py \
   --store v2-c1000=$OGS9 --reps 5 --output $D/opengwasdb_store_comparison_ogs00009_zarr2.json)
pixi run -e dev python benchmarks/benchmark_store_comparison.py \
   --store v2-c1000=$OGS9 \
   --store v3-c1000=/data/opengwasdb/work/epic240/246/OGS-00009-v3-c1000 \
   --store v3-c128=/data/opengwasdb/work/epic240/246/OGS-00009-v3-c128 \
   --store v3-c64=/data/opengwasdb/work/epic240/245/OGS-00009-v3-c64 \
   --reps 5 --output $D/opengwasdb_store_comparison_ogs00009_shapes.json
pixi run -e dev python benchmarks/zarr3_lever_tables.py shapes \
   --base $D/opengwasdb_store_comparison_ogs00009_zarr2.json \
   --head $D/opengwasdb_store_comparison_ogs00009_shapes.json \
   > $D/opengwasdb_store_comparison_ogs00009_shapes_set_l.md

# the top-hit A/B
pixi run -e dev python benchmarks/top_hit_shard_ab.py \
   --config sharded=/data/opengwasdb/work/epic240/245/OGS-00009-v3-c64 \
   --config unsharded=/data/opengwasdb/work/epic240/246/OGS-00009-v3-c64-topshard1 \
   --rounds 5 --reps 100 --output $D/opengwasdb_top_hit_shard_ab.json

# the report
cd $D && pixi run -e report quarto render opengwasdb_ogs00009_shapes.qmd

title: Withhold an rsid its sources dispute, and read compound ids as their rs identifier
text:
A Hybrid build’s rsid harvest refuses a routing key whose sources name it with two different rsids (issue #255 round 4). OGS-00011, the GWAS Catalog EUR Hybrid release, has 99,577 such keys over 3,169 Analyses, so its rebuild cannot finish (opengwasdb-stores #225). This ADR records what a build may do instead, and the reader rule that removes the disagreements that were never real (issue #306).


A Hybrid routing key upper-cases alleles (_routed_site_key), because case is not an orientation change: a source writing c/t reports the same variant as one writing C/T. The single-pass rsid harvest keys every source site the same way, so two spellings of one site meet on one key. When their sources name it differently, there is no evidence in the sources for either name. Until issue #255 round 4 the harvest kept the last one silently; since then it refuses, which is right for a fixture and fatal for OGS-00011.
The opengwasdb-stores #225 scan of every OGS-00011 source found the disagreements are all one shape: 133 Analyses write every allele in lower case, and 105 Analyses (87 upper-case, 18 lower-case) name a shared key differently. By kind:







kind
keys




plain rsX against plain rsY (dbSNP merges, indel naming)
58,690


compound rsX:pos:a:b against a different rsY
31,455


a ; list against a plain name
8,824


compound against plain with the same rs number
304



Only the last kind is one name written two ways (rs199633771:13122834:C:T in GCST004988, rs199633771 in GCST010723, at 1:905). The rest are two different names for one stored variant, and only the rsid label depends on the choice: association values do not.



A source cell names its first rs item, ending at its first :. The GWAS-SSF reader, directly or through a Column Map, reads a ;-separated list as its first item that begins rs, and an rs identifier as ending at its first : (opengwasdb.variants.rsid.normalise_rsid). The rule runs in the reader, before any name is compared, so the harvest, the Dense and Hybrid builds and the full-row parser all see one name. It turns the 304 same-number keys into agreement, and a variant that only a compound id names is stored under its plain rs identifier, which is what a user looks it up by.
build-hybrid --on-rsid-conflict {refuse,drop}, default refuse. refuse is the issue #255 behaviour, unchanged. drop gives no rsid to every stored variant a disputed routing key reaches over the build’s final combined routing, including one that a second key — the same site in the other allele order — reaches with a name of its own: the variant’s sources disagree on its name either way. It is written with rsid . and left out of the rsid search index, as a variant no source names is, and is found by ALID and by position, with every association, and by no name.
The counts are always reported. The build’s JSON summary carries rsid_conflicts — policy, n_keys (disputed routing keys), n_variants (the stored variants they reach, left unnamed under drop) and the first 20 keys in genomic order with their names in (rank, site) order — whatever the policy and whatever the counts, so a release’s step record shows them even when they are 0, including a harvest whose sources name nothing. A build that compared no names (a --reference-panel build, or a reference that names its variants) reports both as null, not 0. A checkpoint records the policy and the counts, so a run resumed after the fold reports the first run’s, and a resume under the other policy is refused like any changed parameter. A resume past the fold whose recorded counts are missing is refused as lost evidence, unless the checkpoint predates the option (its parameters record no on_rsid_conflict), when the counts are null.
The build’s own check finds the disputed variants again. Under drop the pre-publication oracle (expected_rsids_by_routed_key) works out from the raw harvest which keys are disputed rather than taking the build’s list, and expects no name on any variant they reach, so a build that left one named fails instead of publishing it.
Out of scope: two allele orders that each agree internally. A variant whose keys are each named consistently, but differently from each other, is not reached by a disputed key and keeps the first name, as in a Dense or two-pass build (issue #192). In the two-Analysis build below that is 61,406 variants, 59,963 of them indels written C/CT in one source and CT/C in the other under different rs numbers; they are not counted in n_variants.




Keep the first name in (rank, site) order. The rule the harvest uses everywhere else, and the cheapest. Rejected by the opengwasdb-stores owner on 2026-10-22: where sources disagree there is no reason to prefer the Analysis listed first, and a possibly-wrong name looks exactly like a right one. Absence is distinguishable; a wrong name is not.
Rewrite the source files. They are EBI’s harmonised files, checksummed as downloaded; rewriting 133 or 87 of them changes the bundle’s checksums and leaves a derived file labelled as EBI’s, and the 99% of disagreements that are different names would remain.
Exclude Analyses. No small set removes the conflicts: dropping the 18 lower-case Analyses that win lets another lower-case one win. Clean removal is all 133 lower-case Analyses, a membership change.
Normalisation alone. Removes 304 of 99,577 keys.
Withhold only the disputed key’s names. The first implementation: the disputed key contributed no name, but a second key reaching the variant still named it by the first-name rule. Built on the two Analyses of the 1:905 case alone (below), 83 of the 89,580 disputed variants kept a name that way — 39 one of the disputed names, 44 a third — because GCST004988 reports some indels in both allele orders under different names. Rejected by the opengwasdb-stores owner on 2026-10-22: where the sources disagree on a variant’s name, the variant stores none.




A drop build of GCST004988 and GCST010723 alone against the gnomAD v4 EUR reference (EUR-variants.txt.gz, 13,415,936 ALIDs; 23,040,587 harvested sites) reports n_keys 89,580 and n_variants 89,580, and writes every one of those variants with rsid .; none has both allele orders disputed. The first 200 are found by ALID and by neither disputed name, and the Store validates. An independent scan of the two files, sharing no code with the build, finds the same 89,580 disputed keys and variants after normalisation, and 129,843 keys before it: 40,263 of the pair’s disagreements are compound against plain with the same rs number (GCST004988 writes 526,194 compound ids; neither file writes a ; list). The refuse build of the same pair now stops at 1:8170 (rs184698020 against rs28517440) rather than at 1:905. The pairwise counts exceed the release-wide scan’s because in the full manifest an earlier-ranked Analysis names most of these keys first.




OGS-00011 can be rebuilt with on-rsid-conflict: drop in its Build Recipe; the stores side records the counts from the step’s stdout.
A variant stored unnamed because of a dispute looks, in the Store, like one no source named. The Store records no per-variant reason; the release’s build record carries the count and the sample.
refuse stays the default, so every existing recipe builds exactly as it did, and a recipe must choose drop to lose a name.
A Dense build never meets this: its routing key is the source’s own spelling, so two sites never share one, and the option is Hybrid-only.
Reading every identifier cell through the rule costs the GWAS-SSF variant projection, which every harvest runs over every source row, about 4.8%. On GCST004988 (11,629,203 rows) stream_variants() took 37.5 s and 38.6 s, against 35.8 s and 36.8 s on the parent commit 32f47b3. Those are two runs each on a shared compute node, interleaved, with run-to-run variation of about a second; a later run of the change took 36.3 s. Measure it from each tree with:
pixi run -e dev python - /data/opengwasdb/raw/ebi-gwas-catalog/GCST004001-GCST005000/GCST004988/harmonised/29059683-GCST004988-EFO_0000305.h.tsv.gz <<'EOF'
import sys, time
from opengwasdb.readers.gwas_ssf import GwasSsfReader
start = time.perf_counter()
rows = sum(1 for _ in GwasSsfReader(sys.argv[1]).stream_variants())
print(rows, f"{time.perf_counter() - start:.1f} s")
EOF
The cost buys a name a user can look the variant up by, in place of a compound id no lookup finds. The committed benchmark_reader_projection.py artifact was measured at b688892, before this change, and was not re-run for it.
The normalisation changes the stored rsid of any GWAS-SSF source that writes compound or listed ids, in Dense and Hybrid builds alike. The GWAS-VCF reader’s ID, the native FinnGen reader and the Ragged SSF builder keep their own rules.

title: Association Coverage is a build input, not a layout constant
text:
Narrows ADR 0009’s two-valued vocabulary and completes what that ADR separated out. Issue #298, a prerequisite for the Analysis Catalog in opengwasdb-stores (stores #313, #341).


ADR 0009 made Association Coverage a first-class axis of a Store Release, independent of Primary Storage Layout and of Completion State. The manifest got the field, docs/spec/store-format.md §2 got the contract, and then the builders quietly turned it back into a property of the layout:

layouts/dense/build.py, layouts/dense/build_vcf.py, layouts/hybrid/build.py (both manifests) and layouts/hybrid/complete.py wrote full unconditionally;
layouts/ragged/build_ssf.py and layouts/ragged/build_besd.py wrote cis_and_signals unconditionally.

No build took the value as an input, so no manifest could disagree with its layout’s constant. Two published Stores show what that cost:

OGS-00006 (Chen 2023, plasma metabolites) is filtered to significant trans signals and suggestive leads (sig-trans-1mb_suggestive-leads). A metabolite has no cis region, yet the release says cis_and_signals.
eQTLGen’s cis-eQTL Stores hold cis associations only, with no trans signals at all, and also say cis_and_signals.

Both are wrong answers that look like right answers, in a field a reader is expected to trust: the first over-states what the release holds, the second is wrong in both directions depending on how it is read. Nothing failed, because nothing could.
There is a second problem with full itself: it does not say what it is full of. A Dense store’s full means “every association the source reports”, which is a meaningful guarantee; the name made it easy to read as “the complete matrix”, which it is not.












value
what the release retains




gwas
every association the source reports, genome-wide


cis
a cis window around each Analysis’s target, and nothing else


cis_and_signals
a cis window plus significant signals elsewhere


signals_only
significant signals and their flanks, with no cis window



full is read as gwas and never written again. AssociationCoverage implements this in _missing_, the one place a manifest string becomes a value, so every reader — StoreManifest.load, info, validation — gets the mapping without repeating it. A published release needs no rewrite: it opens, validates and reports gwas. The alias is transitional (§5a): it exists only while a supported pin still writes full.
A writer that edits manifest.json as JSON — the converter, the restamp, the Provenance Amendment, the variant-index build — never constructs a StoreManifest, so _missing_ never runs for it. Each of them normalises the value through normalise_coverage instead, which is why “never written again” holds on those paths too rather than only on the enum’s.



build-ragged-ssf and build-ragged-besd take --association-coverage with no default: the same command builds a cis-eQTL release, a significant-signals metabolite release and a full sum-statistics release of the same layout, and a default would be the layout constant this ADR removes. The library functions take it as a required keyword for the same reason — a caller that does not know the coverage of what it is building does not know what it is publishing.
build-dense, build-dense-vcf, build-hybrid and build-hybrid-from-catalogue take the option, default to gwas, and refuse any other value.
The refusal is a representation constraint, not a re-conflation of ADR 0009’s axes. A Dense or Hybrid release holds one cell per (variant, Analysis). An association a narrower coverage excluded is therefore not absent from the matrix: it is a cell, and a cell left missing means “the source did not report this” — which is exactly what Reference Completion fills in from the reference panel, and what a query reports as an imputed or unobserved association. Two different facts with one representation is the failure class this project exists to avoid, so a Dense or Hybrid build cannot faithfully hold cis, cis_and_signals or signals_only and says so instead of writing a manifest that claims otherwise. A Ragged sequence is the list of associations kept, so absence states itself, and all four are representable there.
COVERAGES_BY_LAYOUT in model/enums.py is the single statement of which layout carries which values, and both the builders and validate read it — a build cannot write a release validation would reject, and validation cannot invent a rule no build is held to.



Reference Completion writes imputed cells into its source’s arrays. It does not retain more or fewer of the source’s associations, so the coverage is carried across rather than re-decided, exactly as format_version, store_id, reference_assembly and the encoding are (ADR 0038 §4). complete-dense still requires a gwas source, because Dense completion is defined over a matrix in which every missing cell is an imputation target.



info showed it and still does. #294 makes opengwasdb-stores’ register read association_coverage from the stdout JSON of its build or complete step, and record null for a key nothing prints, so every builder and completion command now prints it. The CLI reads it back from the release it just wrote rather than echoing an argument: the recorded value is then the one on disk, including for a resumed or a completed build where the argument does not exist.



format_version is 0.2.0, below 1.0.0, and spec §21.0 decides this case: before 1.0.0, a change confined to a manifest vocabulary or to required metadata is applied by editing the existing Stores’ metadata in place, as one coherent step across this package, opengwasdb-stores and the published Stores; it does not move the format version, it is recorded in CHANGELOG.md, and an older package may refuse the new values.
That last consequence is real here, so it is stated plainly rather than argued away. A package built before this change meets association_coverage: gwas and refuses the release, because the vocabulary is closed and an unknown value is refused by name instead of guessed at (spec §21.2). The owner’s decision of 23 Oct 2026 accepts that: one coherent vocabulary across the three repositories and the published Stores is worth more than an old package reading a release written after it, and the alternative — a series bump plus a rebuild or converter for every Store — buys only the opposite direction of compatibility, for a project that has not released 1.0 and will change the format again.
From 1.0.0 the rule returns to ADR 0038 §1 / ADR 0041 §2: a vocabulary change is incompatible and moves the series, because a released format is a contract with readers outside this project. ADRs 0038 and 0041 carry a banner naming this decision, and spec §21.1/§21.2 point at §21.0 for it.
What the rename does not need is a conversion. Every 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 release stays readable, because full is read as gwas (§1); the in-place metadata edit that brings a published Store’s own manifest onto the new vocabulary is a stores-side sweep, run once, and every edited Store is re-validated. Completion is untouched: it preserves its source’s coverage either way, so no release becomes un-completable (which the alternative — moving CURRENT_FORMAT_VERSION — would have caused, since completion refuses a source it cannot write: ADR 0038 §4).



AssociationCoverage._missing_ maps full to gwas for a limited time, and for two reasons: Stores built at the pin in use keep writing full until opengwasdb-stores re-pins past this change, and the in-place metadata sweep has not run yet. Both are transitional.
It is removed — with the full case in _missing_, and nothing else — once no published Store says full and no supported pin writes it. So that this is not forgotten, CHANGELOG.md records it as transitional, and removing it is a no-changelog-exempt-able change of one method plus a test.





Keep full as a written value and add gwas as an alias for it. Rejected: two spellings of one fact is the ambiguity the rename removes, and the next reader has to know which builds write which. full is read, never written.
Give the Ragged builders a cis_and_signals default so existing callers keep working. Rejected: that is precisely the defect. The default is the layout constant, and the two published Stores above are what it produces.
Let a Dense build write any coverage and rely on validation. Rejected: the release would be written, published and only then refused, and a distributor that never runs validate would ship it.
Drop association_coverage from Dense and Hybrid manifests instead of constraining it. Rejected: the field is required by spec §2 and read by consumers that do not know a release’s layout; gwas states the guarantee explicitly and keeps one schema.
Move format_version to 0.3.0. Rejected under spec §21.0: it is not what a below-1.0 vocabulary change does, and it would force a converter on every published Store — completion preserves its source’s version and refuses one it cannot write (ADR 0038 §4), so nothing could be completed until it was converted, to record a rename of one manifest string.
Keep full forever, and let both spellings mean gwas. Rejected: the read alias is transitional (§5a) because two spellings of one fact is the ambiguity the rename removes; a distinct value in a closed vocabulary is read by everyone forever.





A manifest’s association_coverage now describes the Store, and two Ragged releases of one Source Collection can honestly differ.
opengwasdb-stores must pass the coverage for every Ragged build. A Ragged build.yaml that does not state it fails at the CLI rather than building a release whose manifest is a guess.
Every pre-#298 release reports gwas where it reported full, in info, in validation and in the Analysis Catalog. Nothing about its data changed.
validate gains one rule per layout: a Dense or Hybrid release declaring a coverage its layout cannot carry is invalid, and so is a value outside the four.
The Analysis Catalog can group and filter Stores by retained coverage, which is what stores #341 needs.

There is a second problem with full itself: it does not say what it is full of. A Dense store’s full means “every association the source reports”, which is a meaningful guarantee; the name made it easy to read as “the complete matrix”, which it is not.

title: Association Coverage is a build input, not a layout constant
text:
value
what the release retains




gwas
every association the source reports, genome-wide


cis
a cis window around each Analysis’s target, and nothing else


cis_and_signals
a cis window plus significant signals elsewhere


signals_only
significant signals and their flanks, with no cis window



full is read as gwas and never written again. AssociationCoverage implements this in _missing_, the one place a manifest string becomes a value, so every reader — StoreManifest.load, info, validation — gets the mapping without repeating it. A published release needs no rewrite: it opens, validates and reports gwas. The alias is transitional (§5a): it exists only while a supported pin still writes full.
A writer that edits manifest.json as JSON — the converter, the restamp, the Provenance Amendment, the variant-index build — never constructs a StoreManifest, so _missing_ never runs for it. Each of them normalises the value through normalise_coverage instead, which is why “never written again” holds on those paths too rather than only on the enum’s.



build-ragged-ssf and build-ragged-besd take --association-coverage with no default: the same command builds a cis-eQTL release, a significant-signals metabolite release and a full sum-statistics release of the same layout, and a default would be the layout constant this ADR removes. The library functions take it as a required keyword for the same reason — a caller that does not know the coverage of what it is building does not know what it is publishing.
build-dense, build-dense-vcf, build-hybrid and build-hybrid-from-catalogue take the option, default to gwas, and refuse any other value.
The refusal is a representation constraint, not a re-conflation of ADR 0009’s axes. A Dense or Hybrid release holds one cell per (variant, Analysis). An association a narrower coverage excluded is therefore not absent from the matrix: it is a cell, and a cell left missing means “the source did not report this” — which is exactly what Reference Completion fills in from the reference panel, and what a query reports as an imputed or unobserved association. Two different facts with one representation is the failure class this project exists to avoid, so a Dense or Hybrid build cannot faithfully hold cis, cis_and_signals or signals_only and says so instead of writing a manifest that claims otherwise. A Ragged sequence is the list of associations kept, so absence states itself, and all four are representable there.
COVERAGES_BY_LAYOUT in model/enums.py is the single statement of which layout carries which values, and both the builders and validate read it — a build cannot write a release validation would reject, and validation cannot invent a rule no build is held to.



Reference Completion writes imputed cells into its source’s arrays. It does not retain more or fewer of the source’s associations, so the coverage is carried across rather than re-decided, exactly as format_version, store_id, reference_assembly and the encoding are (ADR 0038 §4). complete-dense still requires a gwas source, because Dense completion is defined over a matrix in which every missing cell is an imputation target.



info showed it and still does. #294 makes opengwasdb-stores’ register read association_coverage from the stdout JSON of its build or complete step, and record null for a key nothing prints, so every builder and completion command now prints it. The CLI reads it back from the release it just wrote rather than echoing an argument: the recorded value is then the one on disk, including for a resumed or a completed build where the argument does not exist.



format_version is 0.2.0, below 1.0.0, and spec §21.0 decides this case: before 1.0.0, a change confined to a manifest vocabulary or to required metadata is applied by editing the existing Stores’ metadata in place, as one coherent step across this package, opengwasdb-stores and the published Stores; it does not move the format version, it is recorded in CHANGELOG.md, and an older package may refuse the new values.
That last consequence is real here, so it is stated plainly rather than argued away. A package built before this change meets association_coverage: gwas and refuses the release, because the vocabulary is closed and an unknown value is refused by name instead of guessed at (spec §21.2). The owner’s decision of 23 Oct 2026 accepts that: one coherent vocabulary across the three repositories and the published Stores is worth more than an old package reading a release written after it, and the alternative — a series bump plus a rebuild or converter for every Store — buys only the opposite direction of compatibility, for a project that has not released 1.0 and will change the format again.
From 1.0.0 the rule returns to ADR 0038 §1 / ADR 0041 §2: a vocabulary change is incompatible and moves the series, because a released format is a contract with readers outside this project. ADRs 0038 and 0041 carry a banner naming this decision, and spec §21.1/§21.2 point at §21.0 for it.
What the rename does not need is a conversion. Every 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 release stays readable, because full is read as gwas (§1); the in-place metadata edit that brings a published Store’s own manifest onto the new vocabulary is a stores-side sweep, run once, and every edited Store is re-validated. Completion is untouched: it preserves its source’s coverage either way, so no release becomes un-completable (which the alternative — moving CURRENT_FORMAT_VERSION — would have caused, since completion refuses a source it cannot write: ADR 0038 §4).



AssociationCoverage._missing_ maps full to gwas for a limited time, and for two reasons: Stores built at the pin in use keep writing full until opengwasdb-stores re-pins past this change, and the in-place metadata sweep has not run yet. Both are transitional.
It is removed — with the full case in _missing_, and nothing else — once no published Store says full and no supported pin writes it. So that this is not forgotten, CHANGELOG.md records it as transitional, and removing it is a no-changelog-exempt-able change of one method plus a test.

title: Association Coverage is a build input, not a layout constant
text:
Keep full as a written value and add gwas as an alias for it. Rejected: two spellings of one fact is the ambiguity the rename removes, and the next reader has to know which builds write which. full is read, never written.
Give the Ragged builders a cis_and_signals default so existing callers keep working. Rejected: that is precisely the defect. The default is the layout constant, and the two published Stores above are what it produces.
Let a Dense build write any coverage and rely on validation. Rejected: the release would be written, published and only then refused, and a distributor that never runs validate would ship it.
Drop association_coverage from Dense and Hybrid manifests instead of constraining it. Rejected: the field is required by spec §2 and read by consumers that do not know a release’s layout; gwas states the guarantee explicitly and keeps one schema.
Move format_version to 0.3.0. Rejected under spec §21.0: it is not what a below-1.0 vocabulary change does, and it would force a converter on every published Store — completion preserves its source’s version and refuses one it cannot write (ADR 0038 §4), so nothing could be completed until it was converted, to record a rename of one manifest string.
Keep full forever, and let both spellings mean gwas. Rejected: the read alias is transitional (§5a) because two spellings of one fact is the ambiguity the rename removes; a distinct value in a closed vocabulary is read by everyone forever.
crumbs: Association Coverage is a build input, not a layout constant

title: Association Coverage is a build input, not a layout constant
text:
A manifest’s association_coverage now describes the Store, and two Ragged releases of one Source Collection can honestly differ.
opengwasdb-stores must pass the coverage for every Ragged build. A Ragged build.yaml that does not state it fails at the CLI rather than building a release whose manifest is a guess.
Every pre-#298 release reports gwas where it reported full, in info, in validation and in the Analysis Catalog. Nothing about its data changed.
validate gains one rule per layout: a Dense or Hybrid release declaring a coverage its layout cannot carry is invalid, and so is a value outside the four.
The Analysis Catalog can group and filter Stores by retained coverage, which is what stores #341 needs.
