title: Source connectors and freeze
text:
What acquisition produced for a Source Collection: one row per Analysis it acquired a file for, or tried to and could not. It records availability, never intent. A row with a non-ready status records why acquisition has no usable file for that Analysis – an explained absence (see Freeze).



Column
Required
Description




source_analysis_id
Yes, every row
The Analysis the file was acquired for: its claim. Unique.


status
Yes, every row
The readiness vocabulary of source_inventory.py: ok and already_present are ready; missing_remote_harmonised_yaml, header_rejected, metadata_rejected, data_absent_upstream, data_failed, yaml_failed, dry_run and error record why there is no usable file. A Source Collection whose acquisition only records identities re-verifies them instead, and reports missing_file, missing_index, size_mismatch, checksum_mismatch, index_mismatch, bad_index or integrity_failed (SOURCE_VERIFICATION_STATUSES, #289). An unknown status is refused.


location
Column yes; value on every ready row
The exact local path acquisition wrote. Becomes the inventory’s data_file.


bytes
Column yes; value on every ready row
The file’s size in bytes, with no leading zero. Becomes data_bytes. On a refused row it is the size the run holds the Analysis to (see the FinnGen writer below).


sha256
Column yes; value on every ready row
The file’s lower-case sha256. On a refused row it is the digest the run holds the Analysis to, so the refusal does not erase its own pin.


source_url
No
Where the file was fetched from. Becomes data_url.


sidecar_location, sidecar_url, sidecar_bytes
No
A per-Analysis metadata file acquisition fetched with it (GWAS-SSF -meta.yaml). Become yaml_file, yaml_url, yaml_bytes.


error
No
The acquisition error, when there was one.


original_location, original_sha256, reformat_tool
No; all three or none
Lineage of a file acquisition changed: the original’s path and sha256 and the tool, with its version, that changed it. Only on a ready row. Acquisition changes a file in two cases: a structural change no reader or Column Map can cope with, such as splitting one file into one per Analysis, and filtering it to a release’s region policy (#300, below).


original_bytes
No; only with lineage
The original’s size. It stands in for original_sha256 only for an original filtered before acquisition checksummed it, and since deleted: Chen 2023’s files, filtered by the retired R generator, whose filter_summary.tsv recorded each original’s size and no checksum.


region_policy
No; only with lineage
The region policy a region-filtered file was filtered to: one JSON object with sorted keys and no spaces, naming region_policy_id and association_coverage (signals_only or cis_and_signals), trans_flank_bp and suggestive_lead_min_distance_bp (whole bases), significant_p and suggestive_p (in (0, 1]), the QC panel’s resource_id and sha256 (every policy keeps one, ADR 0036), and for a cis policy cis_flank_bp and the target span used (chromosome, start, end). A policy missing any of them, or a cis flank or target on a signals-only one, is refused.


source_probe_id, members
No; both or neither, only on a ready row
A BESD file set several Analyses share (#291): location is the file set’s prefix, source_probe_id the .epi probe this Analysis reads, and members one JSON object with sorted keys and no spaces naming exactly .besd, .epi and .esi, each with its bytes and lower-case sha256. The bytes and sha256 columns are the .besd member’s and are refused if they are not. Identity and verification are defined once, in the release metadata schema.



A duplicate source_analysis_id is refused, and so is a file – a location or sidecar_location – claimed by two rows.
A file set is the one shared claim. Rows with members may share one location, because a BESD file holds an Analysis per probe. They are accepted only when every claimant records identical members and each source_probe_id is claimed once in the file set; a member whose size or sha256 differs between claimants, or a probe claimed twice, is refused by name. A plain file is still one Analysis’s, and a file set’s prefix may not also be a plain row’s location.


A release whose config declares a region_policy (release config) is acquired filtered, for scale (ADR 0036, clarified by #300):
python3 -m manifest_generation.region_filtered_acquisition \
  --config <release config> --originals <originals' Acquisition Manifest> \
  --out-dir <filtered files> --out <Acquisition Manifest> [--workers N] [--keep-originals]
It reads the Acquisition Manifest of the downloaded originals, checks each original’s sha256 against it, filters the original with the shared region filter (manifest_generation.region_filter) into <out-dir>/<id>.filtered.tsv.gz, records the filtered file’s location, size and sha256 with its lineage (original_location, original_sha256, reformat_tool, region_policy), and syncs the manifest. Only then does it delete the original: a failure to record leaves the original in place. An Analysis the originals’ manifest records as unavailable stays an explained absence. A re-run resumes only a run that is this one: before anything is skipped, filtered or deleted, the plan and the summary beside the manifest (below) must both be present with the sha256s its run record binds, and every Analysis the output manifest records must still be a ready original of this run, filtered from that original (location and sha256), to this run’s region policy, QC panel and target, into a filtered file that still has its recorded size and sha256. Any difference refuses the run, naming each Analysis, and deletes nothing; otherwise an original an interrupted run left behind is deleted. --keep-originals only reads the originals and never deletes one: for originals a built release still cites, such as Sun 2018’s (OGS-00007), so the lineage names them where they are kept. A cis policy refuses the run if an Analysis has no target span in the Source Metadata Table.
The filter is the retired R gwas-ssf-ragged generator’s, reproduced row for row: every row within cis_flank_bp of the target (cis only); every row within trans_flank_bp of a row outside the cis window with p_value <= significant_p, the flanks merged; of the other rows with significant_p < p_value <= suggestive_p, the strongest first, each kept only when every lead already kept on its chromosome is more than suggestive_lead_min_distance_bp away (equal p-values in file order); and every row at a QC-panel position, whatever its p-value, so Analysis Resolution can still measure ancestry and phenotype SD. A row with no position or p-value is dropped. Kept rows are the source’s own lines, with its header: the filter selects and never reformats.
Before a filtered file’s row is recorded, its plan and counts go beside the manifest, as the R filter recorded them, and the run record is rewritten to bind them:

<manifest-stem>.sparse-regions.tsv, one row per region kept, in R’s columns (analysis_id, region_id = <id>__<cis|sig_trans|suggestive|qc_panel>__<nnn>, region_kind, chromosome, start, end, source_genome_build, target_id, target_label, lead_variant_id, pvalue_threshold, n_variants_retained, region_policy_id): the cis window and each merged significant-trans range with the rows kept in it, each suggestive lead as a one-base region named by its variant_id (else rsid), and the QC-panel rows kept on each chromosome, first to last;
<manifest-stem>.filter-summary.tsv, one row per filtered file: analysis_id, status, error, source_url, downloaded_bytes, input_rows, retained_rows, retained_fraction, cis_rows, significant_trans_regions, significant_trans_rows, suggestive_leads, qc_panel_rows, output_file, output_bytes, checksum_algorithm, checksum – R’s columns without its per-run attempt and timing ones.

<manifest-stem>.meta.yaml records the run: the originals’ manifest and its sha256, the filter tool, the policy, and under evidence each of the two files’ path and sha256. Freeze checksums it into the inventory’s provenance, and a candidate carries both files’ selected rows into its bundle (schema).
A release reads only files filtered to its own policy (#282 review). Preflight refuses, before resolution, a frozen acquisition that is not the release config’s, and rendering refuses it again however the stages are run (region_filtered_acquisition.region_lineage_problems). Every ready row of the frozen Acquisition Manifest must record, as its region_policy, the config’s policy, its QC panel’s resource_id with the sha256 the panel has now, and for a cis policy the target span the frozen Source Metadata Table gives the Analysis. The pass lineage the freeze bound must name both the plan and the summary, each still with the sha256 its run record binds, and the summary must cover every ready Analysis. A changed flank, threshold, QC panel or target therefore refuses the files filtered under the old one, naming each Analysis and what differs: their rows are the old policy’s, so they are re-acquired and re-frozen. A policy declared over files nobody filtered is refused the same way, and a config with no region_policy refuses region-filtered files and their evidence.



OGS-00006 (Chen 2023) was built from files the R gwas-ssf-ragged generator filtered, deleting each original. src/manifest_generation/providers/gwas_catalog/legacy_ragged_acquisition.py writes the Acquisition Manifest of its filtered files as they are, with lineage from its sidecars/filter_summary.tsv: original_location (the URL R downloaded), original_bytes and no original_sha256 (R recorded none), R’s policy, and the tool. A file whose sha256 is the one R recorded is the R generator’s output. One whose sha256 differs is accepted only when the reviewed list of re-materialisations (resources/generators/gwas-catalog-ragged/ogs-00006-rematerialised-2026-09-15.tsv) names its (recorded, on-disk) sha256 pair – the 198 files materialise-gwas-ssf-ragged.R re-created from sparse_regions.tsv on 15 Sep 2026, each holding R’s rows plus the multi-allelic siblings of some of its leads – and its tool then says so. Any other difference is refused, naming the Analysis, and nothing is written. Its run record checksums the list and, as evidence, the bundle’s own sparse_regions.tsv and filter_summary.tsv, which a regenerated candidate carries unchanged.



An acquisition writer may record the passes a manifest was written from in <manifest-stem>.meta.yaml beside it (acquisition_manifest.pass_lineage_path). Freeze checksums that file into the inventory’s provenance when it exists.
The GWAS Catalog’s writer, src/manifest_generation/providers/gwas_catalog/write_acquisition_manifest.py, overlays the EBI downloader’s per-pass status manifests – earliest first; a later pass wins for every analysis_id it covers and may not regress a ready Analysis – and records each pass’s path, sha256, size, row count, readiness counts and overrides there. The pass columns, their parsing, the overlay and the regression check are this writer’s alone (#347): no shared module knows the download manifests’ shape. It drops the download manifests’ study columns (intent, the table’s job) and per-run seconds.
Example (abridged):
source_analysis_id  status                          location                                          bytes     sha256     source_url                                    sidecar_location                          sidecar_bytes
GCST000028          ok                              /data/…/17463246-GCST000028-EFO_0001360.h.tsv.gz  35279386  fd598567…  https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/…/…EFO_0001360.h.tsv.gz  /data/…/…EFO_0001360.h.tsv.gz-meta.yaml  811
GCST000803          missing_remote_harmonised_yaml



src/manifest_generation/providers/finngen/acquire.py has two interfaces. The canonical one is the writer a release config’s connectors name:
python3 -m manifest_generation.providers.finngen.acquire \
  --manifest <provider endpoint manifest> --source-dir <dir> --out <acquisition manifest>
It fetches every listed endpoint’s file into --source-dir (resumable: .part files and HTTP Range; a complete file is checksummed and kept, never refetched) and writes the manifest above, plus <manifest-stem>.meta.yaml pass lineage. An endpoint upstream no longer serves is data_absent_upstream; a failed transfer is data_failed; the manifest is written either way and the run exits non-zero, so an unattended retry reuses every completed file.
The second is a compatibility mode the R era used, because its generator emitted a working bundle before acquisition ran; it stays because the recorded receipts of OGS-00003 and OGS-00017 cite it (#288):
python3 -m manifest_generation.providers.finngen.acquire --release-dir=<dir>
It reads <dir>/analyses.tsv, fetches each row’s source_url into its source_file with the same downloader, writes the rows back with checksum and size_bytes filled, writes <dir>/sidecars/downloads.tsv with the download evidence, merges checks.files into <dir>/validation.yaml, and records the same acquisition as the shared Acquisition Manifest at <dir>/acquisition-manifest.tsv. The two interfaces are exclusive: combining --release-dir with --manifest, --source-dir or --out is refused.
A recorded digest is identity evidence. In the canonical mode, the manifest at --out is the pin, read from every row that carries a digest whether that row is ready or refused. An existing file whose bytes no longer match is refused by name – status data_failed, location empty, the error naming the Analysis and both digests – and never re-hashed into a fresh row. A fresh download is held to the same pin and refused before promotion if it does not match. A refused row keeps the pin in bytes and sha256, so the next retry is held to it rather than accepting the bytes the previous run refused; only a ready row’s bytes and sha256 describe a file on disk. In compatibility mode a row’s own checksum is the pin, as the R emitter leaves it blank on a fresh emit: a mismatch refuses the bytes before promotion, leaving the staged .part file and the recorded checksum untouched.



The dbGaP MVP acquisition (src/manifest_generation/providers/dbgap/mvp/acquire_dbgap_phs002453.py, manifest) writes one manifest for the whole Source Collection, not one per candidate store key (#290). A mapped Analysis whose converted file is absent is an explained absence with status data_absent_upstream and the path it would have had. --recorded-manifests lets it reuse the sha256 the acquisition recorded while converting, re-checking each file’s size, so a metadata-only reproduction does not re-read the corpus; without it the writer hashes the files itself.
Every ready row carries the reformatting lineage ADR 0036 requires (#290 review). The original is a member of a published tar, so original_location is <tar path>#<member>; original_sha256 and original_bytes are the extracted member’s own, cross-checked against the deposit’s table of contents (the tar itself is deleted after extraction, so only its recorded md5 survives, and it identifies the container rather than these bytes); and reformat_tool names the code that actually rewrote the file, never the code writing the manifest (#290 review). convert records its own module_sha256 and the executing commit in a receipt under GIA/convert-receipts/, which a later manifest run reads; for files acquired before that, --conversion-history reads a conversion run’s own record (parent-run-summary.json’s code_sha and refresh-receipt.tsv’s per-Analysis action), so a file it converted carries that commit and a file it only re-canonicalised carries sha256:unrecorded with the evidence searched, because no conversion-time record names that code. A rewritten file whose extracted original is gone is refused by name rather than given an invented identity.



ukb-b’s files were copied into the mirror, not downloaded by an acquisition run, so there is no transfer to report. What the restored inventory recorded once is the mirror’s identity, and src/manifest_generation/providers/ukb_b/write_acquisition_manifest.py turns that record – never a fresh read of 425 GB – into the canonical manifest (#289):
python3 -m manifest_generation.providers.ukb_b.write_acquisition_manifest \
  --declared-selection resources/inventories/ukb-b-restored-2026-10-11.declared-selection.tsv \
  --source-dir /data/opengwasdb/raw/gwas-vcf/ukb-b \
  --checksums <the recorded checksum receipt> \
  --integrity <the recorded integrity receipt> \
  --verification <the recorded deep-verification report> \
  --out <acquisition manifest>
One row per declared Analysis, with its VCF (location, bytes, sha256) and its provider JSON as the sidecar (sidecar_location, sidecar_bytes). The readiness status is derived from the recorded evidence and the cheap checks a writer can make without reading a byte, in this order, so the most fundamental failure is the one reported: the file is still there (missing_file), its size is still the recorded one (size_mismatch), the deep verification still holds the recorded sha256 (checksum_mismatch), its .tbi is still there (missing_index), the index is still the recorded one (index_mismatch), and the compressed stream and index still open (integrity_failed, bad_index). A non-ready row keeps the recorded location, size and sha256 – the identity the run holds the Analysis to – and its error says which check failed and what it saw.
The deep verification report is required, and it is evidence or it is refused. It must be a JSON object carrying ok and deep (both booleans), rows (the number of files it verified) and the four per-Analysis lists missing, size_mismatch, checksum_mismatch and index_mismatch; a report that verified nothing is not evidence, so {}, a shallow report (deep: false – it compares sizes and mtimes, never a checksum), rows: 0, a report whose rows is not this Selection’s size, one that names an Analysis the Selection does not contain, one whose ok is true while it lists failures, and one whose ok is false while it names none are each refused by name. Every failure it lists becomes that row’s non-ready status, missing included, so a file the verification found absent is a missing_file row with the reason rather than a ready one.
The writer refuses a declared Analysis the recorded evidence does not cover, a recorded file outside --source-dir or not named <id>.vcf.gz, and a missing provider JSON sidecar: silently marking one ready, or inventing an identity for it, would be guessing about a frozen input. It records each receipt’s path, sha256 and row count beside the manifest (<out-stem>.meta.yaml), plus how many Analyses the verification refused, which freeze checksums into the inventory’s provenance as the pass lineage.



eQTLGen’s cis-eQTL summary statistics (the 2019 whole-blood meta-analysis, 31,684 samples) are one genome-wide BESD file set, /data/opengwasdb/raw/eqtlgen/eqtlgen-sparse: an Analysis per probe, an Ensembl gene. Its connectors are two modules in src/manifest_generation/providers/eqtlgen/, and nothing source-specific is in the pipeline.
The metadata adapter (source_metadata_adapter) writes the Source Metadata Table from a BESD file set, one row per probe:
python3 -m manifest_generation.providers.eqtlgen.source_metadata_adapter \
  --prefix <file set> --tissue whole_blood --sample-size-table <per-pair table> \
  --first-author Võsa --publication-pmid 34475573 --gene-symbols <gene-symbols.tsv> \
  --out <source metadata table>
source_analysis_id is the bare probe id, the id build-ragged-besd gives the Analysis when the Build Recipe passes it no tissue, so no Store-identity column is declared. It is never <probe>::<tissue>, as OGS-00001 and OGS-00002 named theirs: an analysis_id never contains : (issue #319), and bundle.check() refuses one that does. source_probe_id is the probe, source_trait_label the gene’s published symbol (below), study_design is quantitative, tissue is the operator’s statement (never a default) and sample_size is the probe’s maximum published N, as below. The tissue is recorded in its own column, never in the id, and a blank or padded --tissue is refused before anything is written. The probe is the target: target_ensembl_gene_id is the probe, target_chromosome its chromosome, and target_start and target_end both its base pair, a one-base span (the file gives a position, not the gene’s extent). It declares no ancestry label (Assigned Ancestry is measured), no build (the release config’s defaults.source_genome_build, GRCh37) and no trait ontology term. A chromosome outside the vocabulary, a repeated probe or a short row fails the whole adapter, by line and probe.
Publication and labels. first_author and publication_pmid (Võsa et al., Nature Genetics 2021, PMID 34475573, DOI 10.1038/s41588-021-00913-z) are adapter arguments written on every row and recorded, with the label counts, in <table>.provenance.yaml. The Analysis Label (source_trait_label) is eQTLGen’s published GeneSymbol, which the .epi does not carry. gene_symbols (python3 -m manifest_generation.providers.eqtlgen.gene_symbols --url <published cis-eQTL file> --epi <file set>.epi --out gene-symbols.tsv) streams the published file once and writes the small gene/gene_symbol connector input, with its URL, the compressed file’s sha256 and byte count and the download date in gene-symbols.tsv.meta.yaml. A gene given two symbols is refused by name; a probe with none keeps its Ensembl id as the label and is counted. The map feeds the label only: analysis_id and source_probe_id stay the bare Ensembl ids. The source_url (https://eqtlgen.org/cis-eqtls.html) is an acquire --source-url argument, written on every Acquisition Manifest row and recorded in the pass lineage; a resume with another URL is refused like any other changed lineage. The full release’s map has 19,250 of 19,250 probes with a symbol, from the 2019-12-11 file (3,880,187,026 bytes).
Sample size is the probe’s maximum pair N as published (#282): the largest NrSamples the per-pair table (the sample-size table below, the same file build-ragged-besd --sample-size-table stores as the n plane) holds for the probe. The adapter reads only the .epi and that table, never the BESD’s beta and SE, so an Analysis’s sample_size equals the maximum of its own stored n and is an observed count, not a recovered one (spec section 8). It no longer takes a study total or caps anything: the published maximum is at most the study’s 31,684. A probe the table has no pair for, and an n that is not a whole number from 1, are refused by name; table rows of probes the file set does not hold are ignored. The table’s path, sha256 and row count are recorded in <table>.provenance.yaml.
An earlier version recovered N from the BESD, N = 1 / (2p(1-p) se^2) - z^2, over pairs with |z| >= 1, capped at the study total. Against the published maxima of the full release that was equal for 5,554 of 19,250 probes, above by at most 13 for 13,645 and below by up to 1,402 for 51, so it is retired.

The Analysis’s SD is declared, not estimated (the release config below), and the sample size kind is variant_level.

The sample-size table (sample_size_table) turns eQTLGen’s published cis-eQTL file into build-ragged-besd --sample-size-table’s input (opengwasdb#302, ADR 0067), aligned to a BESD file set:
python3 -m manifest_generation.providers.eqtlgen.sample_size_table \
  --published <cis-eQTL file .txt.gz> --source-url <its URL> \
  --prefix <file set> --out <file set>.sample-size.tsv.gz
It writes probe_id, snp_id, n for every (probe, SNP) pair the BESD holds that the published file also holds, with n the published NrSamples, probes in .epi order and pairs in BESD order within a probe; a BESD pair the published file lacks gets no row (the build stores it missing, never estimated). The published file’s (Gene, SNP) pairs are matched by the .epi probe id and the .esi SNP id. A pair published twice among those the file set holds, an .esi SNP id one probe reaches twice, and an NrSamples that is not a whole number from 1 are refused by name and nothing is written; the tool never overwrites. Beside the table, <table>.provenance.yaml records the source URL, sha256 and byte count, the BESD members’ sha256s, the table’s sha256, and the counts: BESD pairs, published rows, matched, unmatched (BESD pairs with no published row) and published-only. For full-19250 that is 127,339,354 BESD pairs, 127,341,798 published rows, all matched, 2,444 published-only. It is not bounded streaming: it holds every published pair the file set could hold in memory to sort and join them, 7.75 GB peak RSS and about 11 minutes on one core for full-19250 (budget 10 GB). A damaged .besd offset table or length is refused before the published file is read. The --eaf-reference is the declared Reference Resource ukb-ancestry-mixture-hg38-uk-eaf: the “United Kingdom” column of ukb-ancestry-mixture-hg38, never an hgdp1kgp-hg38 panel (#348).
The acquisition writer (acquire) subsets the genome-wide file set to a release’s Selection, because build-ragged-besd demands that its file set hold exactly the probes it builds, and writes the Acquisition Manifest:
python3 -m manifest_generation.providers.eqtlgen.acquire \
  --config <release config> --source-prefix <genome-wide file set> \
  --out-dir <subset dir> --name <subset name> --out <acquisition manifest>
The Selection is the release config’s, resolved over the Source Metadata Table it names, so acquisition and freeze cannot disagree. The subset is written with subset_besd.write_besd_subset – a standalone .besd/.epi/.esi set, in Selection order – under --out-dir; the source directory is only read. Every selected Analysis gets a row claiming the one file set (see Acquisition Manifest): location the subset’s prefix, source_probe_id its probe, members each member’s size and sha256, and bytes/sha256 the .besd member’s. Its lineage is the original’s prefix, the original .besd’s sha256, and the tool: the subset writer’s module and the sha256 of its source. Beside the manifest, <manifest-stem>.meta.yaml (the pass lineage) records the Selection, the probes in order, every original member’s size and sha256, the subset’s members and the tool, and the probe, SNP and association counts of the original and of the subset. The writer keeps only the SNPs a kept probe references, so a subset of every probe has the original’s probes and associations and can have fewer SNPs (the full eQTLGen set drops 20 unreferenced SNPs); the counts record that.
A re-run resumes only the run it is: with the manifest present, the subset’s members must still be the bytes it records, and are kept, and the original (its prefix and every member’s sha256), the tool and the Selection must be the ones the manifest and its pass lineage record. A different Selection, a changed member, or a changed original or tool is refused by name, and nothing is rewritten: retained output is never relabelled with a new original.
The release config (resources/generators/eqtlgen-cis-pilot/release-pilot-10.yaml) is OGS-00001’s Selection, by bare probe id: layout: ragged, command: build-ragged-besd, the option source-build: hg19 (passed to the command verbatim) and no tissue option, which would name each Analysis <probe>::<tissue>, defaults.source_genome_build: GRCh37, and one method tier, quantitative: stored_effect_scale: sd, original_sd_method: declared_standardised (the effects are z-standardised, so the SD is 1 by construction; the resolver reports scale_already_declared and original_sd stays blank, #300), sample_size_kind: variant_level. The release names no reader: build-ragged-besd reads BESD, so the resolver’s reader is opengwasdb.besd (candidate_workflow.COMMAND_READER_CAPABILITY). The source is hg19 and the reference GRCh38, so the resolver needs a liftover chain, which the release config names as a Reference Resource (#292).
Verification is of the member files, not the prefix: see the release metadata schema for the one definition of a BESD file set’s identity and how preflight and the record check hold it.

title: Source connectors and freeze
text:
A release config declares exactly one form in its selection block:
selection:
  all: true                        # every row of the Source Metadata Table
selection:
  analyses: [GCST000028, GCST90006908]   # an explicit list
selection:
  where:                           # a rule: AND over canonical columns
    store_key: hybrid__European    #   a value is equality
    study_design: [quantitative, case-control]   # a list is membership
Any form may also carry expect_rows: N, the Selection’s intended size. It is a bound, not a filter: freeze refuses a Selection that takes a different number of rows, by name, and preflight re-checks the frozen inventory against it. It is recorded in the provenance with the rule, so a changed bound is a reviewed re-freeze under a new snapshot id (#290).
Rule values are strings or integers, compared with the cell’s text; a blank cell matches nothing. A rule column must be canonical and carried by the table. Refused: a list naming an Analysis the table does not intend or naming one twice, a Selection that selects nothing, two forms at once, and an empty Selection. There is no negation, range or OR: anything a rule cannot say is said with a list.
The legacy grammar. Today’s generator configs carry a selection block in an older grammar (store_key, ancestry_group, study_design, n_analyses, mode, pubmed_id, binary_count, probe_ids, fail_if_target_unresolved). It is recognised and refused by name, never read as a rule: #287 migrates every release config to the forms above.

title: Source connectors and freeze
text:
python3 -m manifest_generation.freeze \
  --source-metadata-table T --acquisition-manifest M \
  --selection CONFIG --snapshot-id ID --source-collection-id C --out-dir DIR
reads only the two connector files and the Selection. It lists no directory and opens no source file, so an unrecorded file on disk changes nothing. It fails (ReconciliationError) on:

a selected Analysis with no Acquisition Manifest row – no file and no recorded reason there is none;
an Acquisition Manifest row no Analysis in the table claims;

and a duplicate Analysis or file is refused when either connector loads.
A selected Analysis whose row has a non-ready status is an explained absence: it stays in the inventory as a non-ready row with its error, as every Source Inventory has kept unavailable inputs, and never becomes a release member. A row claimed by an Analysis the Selection leaves out is counted, not frozen.
It writes four files into DIR and never overwrites any of them – a re-freeze is a new snapshot id:







File
Content




ID.tsv
The Source Inventory: one row per selected Analysis, sorted by analysis_id, in the inventory columns. publication_pmid, trait, study_design and sample_size come from the table, the rest from the manifest.


ID.source-metadata.tsv
The frozen Source Metadata Table: the selected rows, verbatim, in the original’s columns.


ID.acquisition-manifest.tsv
The frozen Acquisition Manifest: the selected Analyses’ rows, verbatim, in the original’s columns.


ID.meta.yaml
The provenance, written last.



Later generation reads the frozen connectors, never the originals: freeze.load_frozen_connectors(ID.meta.yaml) checks each against its recorded sha256 and loads it, and the frozen files alone reproduce the inventory.


The sidecar keeps the counts preflight re-checks, computed by source_inventory.inventory_counts for both freezes, and records:







Key
Description




snapshot_id, source_collection_id, frozen_at
Identity.


frozen_by
manifest_generation.freeze.


selection
The Selection declaration, as written in the release config.


rows, readiness_counts, ready_rows, ready_bytes, study_design_counts, ready_study_design_counts, duplicate_content_groups
The inventory’s counts. Duplicate-content groups – ready Analyses whose files share one sha256 – are reported for review, never collapsed.


inventory_tsv_sha256
Binds the sidecar to ID.tsv.


source_metadata_table.frozen
path (relative to the sidecar), sha256, bytes, rows of the frozen table.


source_metadata_table.original
path, sha256, bytes, rows of the table freeze read. A path inside the checkout is recorded relative to it, so a committed snapshot names the same file in every checkout (freeze.recorded_path, #300); any other is absolute.


acquisition_manifest.frozen
The same, for the frozen manifest.


acquisition_manifest.original
path, sha256, bytes, rows, readiness_counts of the manifest freeze read, and pass_lineage: the path and sha256 of its pass lineage, or null when it has none.


acquisition_manifest.unselected_entries
Rows claimed by Analyses the Selection leaves out.


lineage
One entry per selected reformatted file: analysis_id and its lineage.



A release config drives this freeze (pixi run inventory-freeze --config <release config>, or the candidate entry point’s freeze stage, #287): it freezes the config’s Selection into source_collection.inventory.directory and, when the snapshot already exists, writes nothing and refuses one frozen for another Source Collection or Selection. The candidate-table freeze this replaced is gone (#287); the inventories it wrote stay as history. The ukb-b reconciliation is recorded in resources/generators/ukb-b/README.md (#289).
Preflight (pixi run preflight --config <release config>) requires a ready row’s location, bytes and sha256. The Acquisition Manifest makes source_url and the sidecar columns optional, so a ready row without a source URL is a preflight warning (its analyses.tsv source_url is blank), and a ready row with no recorded sidecar is counted, not failed. A recorded sidecar must still exist, but preflight never opens it: the build is checked from the Source Metadata Table’s source_genome_build, which must be the release config’s default, and an Analysis declaring no build is counted (#347; a source’s adapter turns what its sidecar says into the canonical column). Harmonisation is not a preflight requirement: the GWAS Catalog downloader gates it at acquisition and records a failure as metadata_rejected.



pixi run preflight --config A --config B ... preflights each release config, then checks that the Selections of their one Source Collection partition it: they name the same collection, no Analysis is selected twice, and each Selection’s declared expect_rows matches its frozen inventory. The retired dbGaP MVP partition proved exactly this for its five ancestry buckets (#290); the check now follows the Selections rather than a written-out partition.
Completeness is proved against the collection, not against the Selections (#290 review): the command reads the Source Collection’s checksummed intent – the whole-collection Source Metadata Table and Acquisition Manifest the frozen snapshot’s provenance records – and fails, naming each one, on an Analysis no Selection covers and on a selected Analysis the collection does not intend. An expect_rows bound cannot see a row that has been added to the collection, and a set of Selections that is merely disjoint is not a partition; a preflight that cannot read those originals fails rather than reporting a partial result as complete.

title: Source connectors and freeze
text: Pilot configs selected a deterministic prefix with n_analyses. The Selection grammar has no such form: a migrated pilot writes the prefix out as an analyses list (release config, #287).

title: Preregistration: QC Panel Concordance Study & Reference-AF Fallback Policy
text:
Document status: Locked / Preregistered (Final report and decision recorded in docs/qc-panel-concordance-report.md).
Issue: opengwasdb-stores#152
Parent: opengwasdb-stores#150
Next Step: opengwasdb-stores#153 (Phase B candidate generation)
Seam dependencies: opengwasdb#207 (opengwasdb.build.resolve.resolve_analysis), opengwasdb-stores#151 (Frozen Source Inventory gwas-catalog-ssf-eur-hybrid-2026-09-10).



Generating the full EBI GWAS Catalog European Hybrid Release Candidate requires resolving two Reference Resource questions before executing the production candidate run:

Ancestry extraction panel decision: Whether the fixed 10,000-variant qc-panel-hg38 (resources/reference-resources/qc-panel-hg38/qc_panel.tsv) provides scientifically interchangeable ancestry assignment and effect-scale evidence compared to scanning against the full 5.8-million-variant ancestry reference (/data/opengwasdb/reference/ancestry-mixture/ref_freqs.hg38.tsv.gz).
Reference-AF fallback policy decision: What explicit outcome is produced when a quantitative Analysis lacks usable source allele frequencies, given that the previously declared /data/opengwasdb/reference/ukb-hg38 panel is absent on this host.

Neither decision may be made implicitly at runtime or adjusted post-hoc. This document locks the sample frame, comparison metrics, acceptance criteria, decision rules, and fallback policy prior to running the real-data concordance study.




Every input resource is recorded with its canonical path, size, and cryptographic checksum:

The concordance sample is derived deterministically from the 4,570 ready rows of the frozen Source Inventory (resources/inventories/gwas-catalog-ssf-eur-hybrid-2026-09-10.tsv).


The sample consists of 106 Analyses partitioned into:

Quantitative trait size deciles (50 Analyses):

3,513 ready quantitative rows partitioned into 10 deciles by recorded data_bytes (from 221 KB to 4.04 GB).
5 Analyses selected deterministically per decile (at 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% relative rank within each decile).

Case-control trait size deciles (50 Analyses):

1,057 ready case-control rows partitioned into 10 deciles by recorded data_bytes (from 248 KB to 2.94 GB).
5 Analyses selected deterministically per decile (including small accession GCST90271757 in decile 1).

Explicit edge cases & anomaly fixtures (6 Analyses):

GCST90446781: Known inverted-EAF source (\(r \approx -0.98\) against reference consensus; verifies orientation gate sensitivity).
GCST000553: Old GWAS-SSF format with hm_ prefix headers and unpopulated allele frequency rows.
GCST90565871 & GCST90565872: First byte-identical duplicate accession pair (329,444,995 bytes).
GCST90624704 & GCST90624705: Second byte-identical duplicate accession pair (388,828,307 bytes).


The sample manifest is frozen at resources/inventories/gwas-catalog-ssf-eur-hybrid-qc-sample-2026-09-10.tsv with provenance sidecar .meta.yaml.





Both evaluations use the one-pass bounded Analysis resolver opengwasdb.build.resolve.resolve_analysis (ADR 0044) with default gates \(\tau=0.50\), \(\delta=0.20\), \(n_{\min}=5000\), \(\text{residual}_{\max}=0.06\), \(\text{flip}_r=-0.50\):

Method A (Full Reference Scan): extraction_panel=None (scans all 5,808,902 reference variants).
Method B (QC Panel Extraction): extraction_panel=qc_panel_alids (extracts only the 10,000 panel sites).



For every Analysis \(i\), the study extracts and compares:









Metric

Delta / Concordance Criterion




assigned_ancestry

\(A_P \in \{\text{EUR}, \text{AFR}, \dots, \text{None}\}\)
Categorical identity: \(A_F == A_P\)

\(p_F \in [0, 1]\)
\(p_P \in [0, 1]\)

Any divergence between Method A and Method B is classified into an explicit category:

assigned_ancestry_flip (Critical): One method assigns an ancestry (e.g. EUR) while the other assigns a different ancestry or leaves the Analysis Unassigned.
dominant_superpop_flip (Critical): The fitted dominant ancestry group differs between methods.
gate_reason_divergence (Major): Both methods reject/unassign, but cite different reasons (e.g. margin vs residual).
overlap_drop (Diagnostic): Panel overlap \(N_P < 5000\) on a source with limited genomic coverage where full reference had \(N_F \ge 5000\).
orientation_flip_missed (Critical): A mis-oriented or flipped frequency column is caught by Full Reference but missed by Panel.
residual_divergence (Minor): Proportion/margin concordant, but RMS residual shifts by \(> 0.02\).

Zero False Positives: Zero cases where Full Reference gates out / unassigns an Analysis but QC Panel admits it as EUR.
100% Orientation Sensitivity: Every known orientation anomaly (including GCST90446781 and synthetic flipped fixtures) is detected by QC Panel (\(G_P = \text{eaf\_orientation}\)).
\(\ge 98\%\) Full-GWAS Concordance: For genome-wide files with \(\ge 500,000\) source variants, assigned_ancestry concordance must be \(\ge 98\%\).
No Gate Tuning: Acceptance thresholds (\(\tau=0.50, \delta=0.20, n_{\min}=5000, \text{residual}_{\max}=0.06\)) remain strictly fixed; no relaxation of gates is permitted to force concordance.
Documented Disposition for Targeted Sources: If targeted/sparse sources (<50,000 variants, e.g. GCST90271757) fail the \(n_{\min}=5000\) overlap gate under the 10k panel, this must be documented as an expected characteristic of sparse panels rather than masked.

FAIL: Retain extraction_panel: null in config-full.yaml (full reference scan for all Analyses).









Option 1: Materialise /data/opengwasdb/reference/ukb-hg38:

Requires generating or acquiring ~140 GB of block-partitioned UK Biobank allele frequencies.
Status: Absent on current host; unverified provenance.

Option 2: Register a replacement Reference Resource:

Requires validating a replacement panel (e.g. 1kGP/HGDP) against the registry schema and verifying coverage across all 4,570 sources.
Status: No replacement is currently approved or verified for this Source Collection.

Option 3: Source-AF-Only Policy (Recommended):

In accordance with ADR 0019, quantitative Analyses with usable source AF use estimated_from_source_maf.
Quantitative Analyses lacking usable source AF receive an explicit skipped resolution with reason no_reference_resource_for_ancestry and are excluded from the Store Release Candidate.
Case-control Analyses receive an explicit skipped resolution with reason non_quantitative_effect_scale (binary_trait).





Option 3 (Source-AF-Only Policy) is selected for the Full GWAS Catalog EUR Hybrid Release.

config-full.yaml explicitly sets effect_scale_validation.reference_resources: [].
Preflight asserts that no missing reference path is treated as usable evidence.
Quantitative Analyses with missing/unusable source AF are classified as explicit exclusions (no_reference_resource_for_ancestry) rather than fabricated estimates against a missing panel.
Adding a fallback panel in a future release requires registering a validated Reference Resource and updating config, not changing code.

pixi run --environment dev python3 resources/generators/gwas-catalog-eur-hybrid/run_concordance_study.py \
  --manifest resources/inventories/gwas-catalog-ssf-eur-hybrid-qc-sample-2026-09-10.tsv \
  --config resources/generators/gwas-catalog-eur-hybrid/config-full.yaml \
  --cores 64 \
  --out-dir /data/opengwasdb/work/gwas-catalog-eur-hybrid/concordance

title: Preregistration: QC Panel Concordance Study & Reference-AF Fallback Policy
text:
Generating the full EBI GWAS Catalog European Hybrid Release Candidate requires resolving two Reference Resource questions before executing the production candidate run:

Ancestry extraction panel decision: Whether the fixed 10,000-variant qc-panel-hg38 (resources/reference-resources/qc-panel-hg38/qc_panel.tsv) provides scientifically interchangeable ancestry assignment and effect-scale evidence compared to scanning against the full 5.8-million-variant ancestry reference (/data/opengwasdb/reference/ancestry-mixture/ref_freqs.hg38.tsv.gz).
Reference-AF fallback policy decision: What explicit outcome is produced when a quantitative Analysis lacks usable source allele frequencies, given that the previously declared /data/opengwasdb/reference/ukb-hg38 panel is absent on this host.

Neither decision may be made implicitly at runtime or adjusted post-hoc. This document locks the sample frame, comparison metrics, acceptance criteria, decision rules, and fallback policy prior to running the real-data concordance study.

title: Unified software management proposal
text:
Status: proposed. This document turns the inventory in software-management-audit.md into one repository-wide execution contract.


Adopt Pixi at the repository root, with one committed pixi.toml and pixi.lock. The sole user-facing execution interface becomes:
pixi run <task>
Pixi is the deep environment module: its small interface hides Conda/Bioconda resolution, Python and R runtimes, native executables, environment activation, and task invocation. The repository’s scripts remain implementations behind that interface. Artifact/reference roots remain data configuration and never contain software environments.
Pixi is a particularly good fit here because one workspace can compose reusable features into smaller environments, attach tasks to those environments, and record all resolved environments in one lock file. Its documented examples explicitly cover small tool environments, docs environments, developer supersets, and CI selection of named environments. See the official multi-environment documentation.



Use Conda packages for Python, R, compiled libraries, Quarto, and bioinformatics executables. Use PyPI only for packages unavailable or intentionally sourced there. Configure conda-forge and bioconda once at workspace level.
Suggested features:








Feature
Contents
Used by




python
Python, NumPy, SciPy, PyYAML
Python utilities and tests


store-build
pinned install of opengwasdb
ancestry/build integration


r
R, data.table, yaml
generators and R tests


reporting
tidyverse, ggplot2, knitr, scales, jsonlite, curl, Quarto
reports/site


ld-panel
bcftools, plink2, Python/SciPy
panel acquisition and generation


dev
lint/test-only tools
contributor and CI checks



Suggested environments:

default: Python + R + store-build; normal generator/test work.
docs: R + reporting.
ld-panel: Python + ld-panel; no reporting stack.
dev: default + reporting + ld-panel + development tools.

This avoids installing the full stack for every job while retaining a single manifest and lock. Environments that must share versions should use a solve group, so the tested version is the production version.



The first task set should be deliberately small:
pixi run test
pixi run test-python
pixi run test-r
pixi run docs
pixi run ld-acquire -- <arguments>
pixi run ld-materialize -- <arguments>
pixi run validate-environment
test owns test ordering and cleanup. Callers should not locate a sibling virtualenv, activate Conda, or know which interpreter runs a script. Tests invoke sys.executable or the executable already selected by Pixi.
validate-environment should report tool versions and fail early when a required executable is unavailable. Long-running job provenance should record the git commit, pixi.lock hash, task name, arguments, and external artifact root.



Use explicit data variables with repository defaults documented in one place:
OPENGWASDB_ARTIFACT_ROOT=/data/opengwasdb/stores
OPENGWASDB_REFERENCE_ROOT=/data/opengwasdb/reference
OPENGWASDB_ARTIFACT_ROOT is the directory that contains one directory per Store Release id (<artifact-root>/OGS-00042/), per ADR 0022. It is now actually read by paths.artifact_root(), which resolves it after a workflow --config artifact_root= override and before the committed ogstores.yaml and the built-in default (issue #126).
Software lives in Pixi’s workspace/cache, not beneath either data root. Remove hard-coded sibling .venv discovery and the LD materializer’s <reference-root>/tools/bin/plink2 lookup. Resolve executables from the Pixi environment (PATH) and accept explicit overrides only for debugging.
The current temporary environment at /data/opengwasdb/reference/hgdp1kgp-hg38/tools must remain until the active panel job finishes, then can be deleted after the locked Pixi environment is installed and the job’s tool versions are recorded.




renv provides strong R isolation and lock/restore semantics, but it would still need a second manager for Python, Quarto, bcftools, and plink2. Its own documentation notes that source restoration can depend on system libraries. See renv project environments and package installation.
A plain environment.yml covers the languages and native tools but does not provide the repository task interface. Modern Conda supports exact lockfiles, including pixi.lock, so choosing Pixi does not abandon the Conda ecosystem; see the official Conda environment documentation.
Separate uv + renv + Conda environments would produce three dependency interfaces and three upgrade workflows. That reduces locality and makes it easy for CI, documentation, and production jobs to exercise different stacks.





Add pixi.toml, resolve and commit pixi.lock, and pin the minimum Pixi version in the workspace.
Add the named tasks and make all current test suites pass through them.
Declare opengwasdb as an explicit pinned dependency rather than borrowing ../opengwasdb/.venv; update tests and generator documentation.
Replace hard-coded tool/interpreter paths with PATH lookup and central root configuration. Add environment validation and provenance capture.
Add CI that installs from the lock without updating it, runs test, and separately exercises docs and the lightweight LD-panel synthetic tests.
Update all README command examples to pixi run ... and remove obsolete activation instructions.
Once the active LD build completes, verify its recorded bcftools/plink2 versions against the lock and remove its data-local Conda environment.





A fresh checkout needs only Pixi plus access to declared external data.
Every checked-in test and document build has a named task.
CI and local execution consume the committed lock without implicit solving.
No script reaches into a sibling checkout’s virtualenv or a reference-data directory for software.
Runtime provenance identifies the lock hash and exact native tool versions.
Updating software is one reviewed manifest/lock change, with all task suites passing before merge.

title: Dense SE codec re-encode — 2026-10-24 to 2026-10-26
text:
This report records the one-time, pre-release in-place re-encode authorised by opengwasdb#326. It does not weaken the rule that published Stores are immutable after the project’s first release.
The forward codec fix and lossless staged-swap implementation were merged in opengwasdb PR #330 (c769a712d31cd7fe64e656aca57a9eff25d34f3f). The release-aware command was merged in opengwasdb-stores PR #370 (a757ead98a710b2a84224989156a5c05dd0aad89) and ran the pinned implementation revision 5fc07666202d43500d5e48bbc48f1e4c9e34ef0f.


Each Store was processed separately with its release lock held, no active publication or partial-completion marker, temporary space on /data, and 16 Zarr codec-pipeline workers. Only data.zarr/se and data.zarr/se_exception_index were selected. For each array, the command staged a replacement on the same filesystem, compared every decoded chunk, and only then performed the rename swap. title: Reports
text:
Working artefacts for delineating GWAS Catalog full-summary-statistic analyses into candidate OpenGWASDB stores, and deciding what to build first. Their sources are in docs/reports/; the pages linked here are the committed, self-contained HTML the site copies as it is, so a report is refreshed with pixi run docs and never re-executed at render time.

Progress update, October 2026
Report. Where OpenGWASDB stands: build, reference-completion and query cost across Dense, Ragged and Hybrid stores; how a store holds an association in about 2 bytes; MR and regional-plot positive controls with and without imputed variants; how a Release Bundle drives the Snakemake build; and the twelve Store Releases built so far.


Getting started with stores
Guide. Start here if you’ve never opened a store: a hands-on command-line tour of the four pilot stores — what a store contains, the five opengwasdb query-* commands, how to turn their output into readable tables, and the gotchas that catch everyone first time.


Store curation report
Report. How 171,274 full-sumstats analyses split into dense, ragged, and hybrid candidate stores — grouped by publication and dominant ancestry, ragged stores labelled by molecular type, with reference-completed size estimates and the EUR-hybrid EFO-clustered prioritisation.


Canonical trait mapping
Analysis. The BioLORD + Jev pipeline that maps free-text trait labels to EFO terms: validation against GWAS Catalog curation (OGS-00011, ~99% estimated precision at the promotion threshold), the first ukb-b round (409 rows auto-accepted), and the defects only live runs exposed.


UKB-B trait mapping round 2
Analysis. The issue #185 rerun over 2,093 remaining labels: Showcase context, ICD-10 retrieval, top-100 shortlists, 141 new mappings, the fresh 845-label review queue, bucket movement, regression checks, and a published random spot check.


Prioritisation dashboard
Interactive tool. Drag each store card into High / Low / Discard columns; each column tallies its store count, analyses, and estimated storage. Filter, sort, and export the prioritisation to CSV. Your layout is saved in the browser.


Imputation-quality filters
Analysis. Choosing MAF and imputation-r² cutoffs before importing dense TOPMed-imputed summary statistics — r² by MAF bin, a retention grid of variants kept versus store size, and a worked tiered-threshold proposal.


EUR LD panel comparison
Analysis. Paired masking experiment across five UKB-B regions comparing held-out beta recovery with the UKB EUR and matched HGDP+1kGP EUR LD panels.


Beta-scale estimation
Analysis. A quick simulation of phenotype-SD estimation from random common-variant betas when source MAF is missing — comparing oracle, reference-profile, and uniform common-MAF assumptions for EUR-like and AFR-like GWAS.

The report sources and the recipes that refresh them are in ../docs/reports/ and pixi run docs; the data a report reads is under ../resources/.




 Back to top

title: Release Bundle schema
text:
A Store Release is defined by a small, self-contained Release Bundle: one directory per release under stores/, whose files record identity, membership, the Build Recipe, and (once built) validation evidence. The bundle is the output of Phase B and the fixed input of Phase A; see docs/spec/store-release-workflow.md for the workflow that consumes it and the ADRs it is governed by.
bundle.check() in src/ogstores/bundle.py is the executable definition of a valid Release Bundle. It accumulates every registry-side error it can find and never raises for invalid bundle content, so an author can run it and fix everything in one pass:
pixi run bundle-check        # discovers and checks every stores/<id>/ bundle
The contract holds only what both workflows share and what Store Release Build needs to consume a bundle. Manifest Generation’s own rules for a candidate’s analyses.tsv live beside it, in src/manifest_generation/generation_rules.py (#250): the columns a generator must resolve, and how it records the INFO and MAF filters it requests. The emitter runs them before a candidate lands, and pixi run bundle-check runs them with the contract over every committed bundle, so neither escapes CI.
A Release Bundle structure is:
stores/OGS-00042/
  release.yaml      identity, lineage, status, source snapshot, generation log, prose
  build.yaml        the recipe: an opengwasdb subcommand and its flags
  analyses.tsv      one row per Analysis; opengwasdb owns the shared schema
  summary.yaml      generated review view derived only from analyses.tsv
  validation.yaml   evidence, written back by the register step
  sidecars/         optional generated evidence (ancestry, SD, sparse regions)
  column_maps/      the Column Map a mapped Source Collection is read through
The store_id is the opaque OGS- identifier (ADR 0022). It is the directory name here and the directory name under the artifact root. In the built Store’s manifest it is the store_id, and the release_id of an Observed-Only release. A release that completes its own Store keeps store_id as the id once completed, and the completed Store carries release_id <id>-completed: a new release of the same Store (ADR 0037, opengwasdb ADR 0011). A two-id Reference-Completed child (ADR 0007) is the exception: its id is the release_id, and the store_id is its parent’s. There is no Store Family tier: the OGS- id is the only identifier (ADR 0028).
Large Release Artifacts live outside this repository, at a path that is a pure function of the identifier:
<artifact-root>/OGS-00042/
  source/                   acquired or filtered source files
  work/                     checkpoints, scratch, logs
  work/analyses.tsv         derived build manifest (exclude_from_build rows dropped)
  records/<step>.json       one per executed step
  store.opengwasdb          the Store Release
  store.opengwasdb.partial  transient staged destination
<artifact-root>/by-label/   generated symlinks
The artifact root is deployment configuration, not a bundle field: a bundle is immutable once accepted, so committing an absolute path into it would bind that bundle to one machine. paths.artifact_root() resolves it, highest precedence first, from a workflow --config artifact_root=, the OPENGWASDB_ARTIFACT_ROOT environment variable, the tracked ogstores.yaml, then the built-in default (/data/opengwasdb/stores). A Build Recipe must not declare an artifacts block (issue #126).


Following only this document, the three files below produce a bundle that passes bundle.check():
stores/OGS-99001/release.yaml
store_id: OGS-99001
label: example-release
access_posture: public
status: candidate
created_at: '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z'
source_snapshot_id: example-source-2026-01-01
description: 'A minimal Release Bundle authored from the schema documentation.'
generator:
  commands:
    - Rscript resources/generators/example/generate.R --mode=emit
stores/OGS-99001/build.yaml
store_id: OGS-99001
layout: dense
completion_state: observed_only
build:
  command: build-dense-vcf
  options:
    source-reader-capability: opengwasdb.example
    source-assembly: hg38
post:
  top_hits: true
  overview: true
stores/OGS-99001/analyses.tsv   (tab-separated; header plus at least one row)
analysis_id source_label    analysis_label  source_file checksum    checksum_algorithm  source_genome_build license trait_ontology_mapping_method   assigned_ancestry   ancestry_assignment_method  original_effect_scale   original_sd_method  stored_effect_scale sample_size_kind    sample_size_scope   sample_size
EXAMPLE-0001    Example trait   Example trait   /data/opengwasdb/example/source.tsv.gz  e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855    sha256  GRCh38  Example terms of use    unmapped    EUR source_trusted_no_af    sd  declared_standardised   sd  total   analysis_level  1000
That covers every column this document marks Yes. A candidate release needs no validation.yaml; a built or validated release does (see validation.yaml). A reference_completed release either completes its own Store under its id, and declares both a build and a complete block (ADR 0037), or is a two-id child that declares derived_from: OGS-00042 in release.yaml and a complete block instead of build (ADR 0007).



Phase B — what produces a bundle — is described here only in outline; the canonical command log for each release is recorded in release.yaml:generator.commands. A Manifest Generator conventionally has five stages:









Stage
Purpose
Typical inputs
Outputs




discover
Snapshot available upstream analyses and files.
Source inventory, GWAS Catalog studies table, source meta.yaml, provider APIs.
Raw candidate records and source-file locations.


select
Apply the Store Release’s inclusion rules.
Candidate records, generator config, priority lists, publication/analyte filters.
Selected Analysis set for a proposed Store Release.


derive
Add authoritative analytical metadata and generated evidence.
Selected rows, provider metadata resolvers, source files, OpenGWASDB readers, reference resources, Ensembl, checksums.
Resolved analyses.tsv columns and sidecar evidence.


emit
Write a reproducible release bundle.
Resolved rows, sidecars, build choices, generator provenance.
release.yaml, analyses.tsv, build.yaml, validation.yaml, sidecars.


accept
Check that the bundle is complete enough to build.
Release bundle, schema checks, lightweight source/readability checks.
Updated validation.yaml and release status.



Metadata resolution and summary-statistics reading are orthogonal concerns. A Source Collection chooses a provider-specific metadata resolver for study tables, APIs, or endpoint manifests, and separately declares an OpenGWASDB Source Reader Capability for source data. The resolved metadata shape is common even when the provider and source format differ.



Registry identity and provenance. Never read by opengwasdb. Required for an accepted Release Bundle; a candidate may leave lifecycle timestamps null.
The file trims to identity, lineage, Release Status, creation time, source snapshot identity, the generation command log, and the prose that explains the Store Release (issue #136, ADR 0029). Issue #137 removed the one-time migration provenance block (ADR 0030); the published artifact path is now a pure function of the identifier.



Field
Required
Description




store_id
Yes
Opaque OGS- 5-digit identifier (ADR 0022): the directory name under stores/, and must match it.


label
Yes
Source-natural display name; provenance, never an identifier (ADR 0022).


association_coverage
Yes
What associations the Store holds, in one vocabulary shared with opengwasdb: gwas (genome-wide), cis (a cis window around each Analysis’s target only), cis_and_signals (a cis window plus significant signals elsewhere) or signals_only (significant signals and their flanks, no cis window). It replaced full_gwas and cis_plus_signals (issue #341, ADR 0040). bundle.check() refuses any other value and a value that is not a string, and Bundle.association_coverage raises rather than answering a default, because the Analysis Catalog shows it and counts Analyses by it. It is also the value plan() passes to a Ragged build as --association-coverage (issue #341), so it is declared, never inferred from the Store Layout. A Dense or Hybrid release can carry only gwas, and bundle.check() refuses any other value there (opengwas/opengwasdb#298). A region-filtered release declares cis_and_signals or signals_only and must agree with its region_policy.association_coverage. Every committed bundle declares it.


access_posture
No
Declared availability category: public, controlled, or embargoed. The one store-level fact the retired Store Family tier genuinely declared (ADR 0028); every committed bundle declares it, but it is descriptive rather than structurally required.


status
Yes
Registry lifecycle state: candidate, accepted, built, validated, superseded, or withdrawn.


trial
No
Whether this is a Trial Store Release: a deliberately small Store Release used to exercise a Source Collection, Source Format or Store Layout (issue #321). Absent means false. Only a YAML boolean is accepted. The registry’s YAML loader follows YAML 1.1, so the unquoted spellings true, yes and on (and false, no, off) are booleans; a quoted trial: "yes" is a string and trial: 1 is a number, and bundle.check() refuses both. A reader that does not gate on check() refuses them too rather than reading them as false: the Analysis Catalog’s serving policy excludes every Trial Store Release, and a coerced value would serve one.


derived_from
No
Parent store_id when this release derives from another release, and the parent must be a registered Release Bundle. A two-id Reference-Completed release names its Observed-Only parent here (ADR 0007); a Reference-Completed release without it completes its own Store (ADR 0037).


superseded_by
No
The store_id of the Store Release that replaced this one, which must be an OGS- id naming a registered Release Bundle. Required on a superseded release and refused on any other Release Status, because it names what a reader of the old identifier is sent to (issue #321, #323). It is a fact about the release, not a serving decision (ADR 0008).


created_at
Yes
Timestamp when the candidate bundle was generated.


accepted_at
No
Timestamp when the bundle was accepted as the release input record.


source_snapshot_id
Yes
Dated or provider-native source snapshot used for this release, for example a GWAS Catalog studies-table release date.


source_snapshot
No
Source snapshot identity detail. For a BESD release: besd_prefix and source_genome_build – the prefix of the file set build-ragged-besd reads and the recipe’s source-build (issue #134 records the legacy releases’ prefix as an unverified path, a known integrity gap; a release generated by the pipeline records each member’s size and sha256 in its frozen Acquisition Manifest instead, #291). For a provider-manifest release: manifest_url, manifest_sha256, manifest_size_bytes, manifest_etag, manifest_last_modified.


generator
Yes
How the bundle was produced; a mapping.


generator.version
No
Generator package version, git commit, or script hash. A value beginning sha256: must carry a valid 64-hex digest.


generator.commands
Yes
The executed command log: a non-empty list of non-empty strings, the commands that produced the bundle, in the order they ran. A log, not a prediction (issue #136).


description
Yes
Short human-readable release description.


notes
No
Free-text release notes.



bundle.check() requires exactly the keys marked Yes above and rejects a generator that is not a mapping or whose commands is empty. It holds association_coverage to its four-value vocabulary (issue #341, ADR 0040), and the descriptive facts the Analysis Catalog’s serving policy reads (ADR 0008) to a checked shape: trial must be a YAML boolean, and absent means false (a quoted trial: "yes" or a numeric trial: 1 is refused, and Bundle.trial raises rather than answer false); and superseded_by is present on exactly the superseded releases, and names a registered Release Bundle, like derived_from (issue #321). Release Status transitions are a separate, optional check (validate_status_transition): the legal lifecycle graph is candidate -> accepted -> built -> validated -> {superseded, withdrawn} with withdrawn reachable from every state. See the workflow specification’s “Status lifecycle and transitions”.
For a BESD build (build-ragged-besd), source_snapshot.besd_prefix is required and must be a non-empty string; its referenced files are deliberately not inspected, because monolithic BESD source identity is an unverified host path prefix (issue #134, a known integrity gap).
 BESD file sets (#291): identity, resolution and verification. This is the one normative definition; the connector contract and the eQTLGen section link here. A BESD file set is .besd, .epi and .esi under one prefix, and holds an Analysis per probe. Its identity is each member’s own size and sha256, recorded in the Acquisition Manifest’s members (columns), with the .besd member’s size and sha256 standing for the set in the single-file bytes and sha256 columns; no composite checksum exists. The resolver manifest declares each Analysis with source_reader_capability opengwasdb.besd, source_file the file set’s prefix (no .besd, .epi or .esi) and a source_probe_id column naming its .epi probe. The column is required for a BESD row and refused for any other, and is blank everywhere else. checksum and size_bytes are the .besd member’s. Preflight holds every member the Acquisition Manifest records to its recorded size and names a missing or resized one. Because the prefix is not a file, a Resolution Record binds fingerprints.source_member_files (each member’s bytes and mtime_ns) and resolution_config.source_probe_id instead of a source file’s size and mtime, and Manifest Generation holds them against the files as they are when it verifies a record and when it preflights the frozen inventory. The resolver’s index.json also gains source_measurements: one entry per file set measured in that invocation (measurement_id, source_file, source_genome_build, the analyses that share it, and an error when the set could not be read), each measured once and shared by its probes’ records (diagnostics.ancestry_measurement_id). It is absent when every record resumed. The release’s source_snapshot.besd_prefix and source_genome_build are rendered from the resolver manifest’s prefix and the recipe’s source-build; the pipeline’s reader for build-ragged-besd is opengwasdb.besd, which the recipe cannot name because options pass to the command verbatim.



One row per Analysis, tab-separated. This is the membership record: the exact set of Analyses in the release. The shared interpretation-bearing core schema is owned by OpenGWASDB (ADR 0017); the registry may add registry-only columns needed to locate source files, record checksums, carry licence/publication provenance, or explain inclusion decisions. bundle.check() delegates the shared contract to the pinned opengwasdb.model.analyses module and adds registry-owned vocabularies on top.
Use empty strings for unknown optional values in TSV. Values are resolved after applying generator config defaults, even when that repeats store-level metadata.











Class
Owner
Where used
Examples




Shared core
OpenGWASDB
Release manifests and built stores. These columns carry interpretation-bearing Analysis metadata.
analysis_id, analysis_label, ontology fields, ancestry fields, effect-scale fields, sample-size fields, INFO policy fields (info_score_threshold, imputation_score_column, imputation_score_kind, imputation_score_provenance), the MAF floor (maf_threshold), Attribution Metadata (license, publication_doi, publication_pmid, consortium, first_author).


Registry-only
Store registry
Release manifests only. These columns locate source inputs, record provenance, or explain inclusion.
source_analysis_id, source_label, source_file, source_bundle_id, checksum, checksum_algorithm, size_bytes, analysis_group_id, inclusion_reason, exclude_from_build, trait_ontology_mapping_method.


Store-only
OpenGWASDB
Built stores only. These columns are produced during or after the build and therefore do not appear in accepted release manifests.
completed_against, reference-completion quality rollups, store artifact diagnostics.



Builders may ignore registry-only columns after using them to locate inputs. Store-only columns must not be required before the build has run. exclude_from_build is the exception that is enforced rather than merely ignored: the registry materialises a derived build manifest with every excluded row removed and points the builder at it, so opengwasdb never sees an excluded row at all (ADR 0025).
A bundle’s header carries these columns:
analysis_id  stored_effect_scale  sample_size_kind  sample_size_scope
sample_size  original_effect_scale  original_sd_method
ancestry_assignment_method  assigned_ancestry
The first eight are OpenGWASDB’s required set, which bundle.check() enforces through the pinned shared schema. assigned_ancestry is added by the registry and required by Manifest Generation’s rules, which also require ancestry_assignment_method, stored_effect_scale and original_sd_method (#250). bundle.check() enforces the shared required set, the retired-column list, and the ancestry vocabulary, case/control-count, and checksum rules below. The Required column in the reference table is the broader authoring convention for a complete bundle — columns marked Yes that check() does not itself demand (analysis_label, source_label, source_file, checksum, source_genome_build, license, trait_ontology_mapping_method) are what a reviewer and the pinned OpenGWASDB schema expect to see populated. Every required column must also be non-empty on every row, except that a release Store Release Build will not build and the two legacy trial releases OGS-00001 and OGS-00002 may leave required Analysis values blank (issue #134; see “Blank required values” below).
bundle.check() rejects any column named by the pinned upstream RETIRED_ANALYSIS_COLUMNS list: phenotype_id, phenotype_label, trait_id, gene_id, gene_name. The upstream schema is the single retired-column contract; the registry does not keep its own copy. It also rejects any analysis_id outside ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$, because the Analysis Catalog addresses an Analysis <store_id>:<analysis_id> and a client must be able to split that on : into its two parts (issue #319; see “Legacy analysis_id values” below). A Trait Ontology Mapping carries an ontology term and its trait label, never a gene identifier with an authority name standing in for the label: gene/target identity is annotation (analysis_label for a single-target Analysis; trait_chr/trait_bp and the target sidecar for the target itself). bundle.check() rejects a gene- or protein-shaped trait_ontology_id (Ensembl, HGNC, Entrez/NCBI Gene, UniProt) and the matching authority name in trait_ontology_label (issue #141). It checks each term of a list, so a gene identifier cannot hide behind an ontology term. The label is checked whole and never split, because a term’s own label may contain a comma (osteoarthritis, hip).
One split rule serves the contract and Manifest Generation alike (trait_ontology_id_terms): split on every comma and strip each part. A value is in canonical form only when its parts are all CURIEs and rejoining them with ", " gives the value back, so EFO:1,EFO:2, padding and empty terms are refused.
bundle.check() also rejects a trait_ontology_id term that is not a CURIE, such as a raw http:// URI (#286). OGS-00011 was accepted before this check with GWAS Catalog’s raw EFO and ORDO URIs in 2,972 rows. An accepted bundle is never rewritten, so those values are tolerated for that release by name (LEGACY_NON_CURIE_TRAIT_ONTOLOGY_RELEASES) and reported on check()’s second channel with their count. Every other bundle, buildable or not, is held to the CURIE form.






Field
Required
Description




analysis_id
Yes
Stable registry Analysis ID. Usually source-derived unless the source lacks stable IDs. It is one path segment matching ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$: the Analysis Catalog (ADR 0039) names an Analysis <store_id>:<analysis_id>, so the value must never contain :, and it is also the filename of the resolver’s per-Analysis record (issue #319).


source_analysis_id
No
Upstream analysis identifier, such as a GCST accession or OpenGWAS ID, when the Source Collection provides one.


source_label
Yes
Upstream trait or phenotype label preserved as source provenance. Registry-only; kept separate from analysis_label even when both hold the same source text.


analysis_label
Yes
Free-text, non-unique display label for the Analysis, carried into the built store. Typically the same source text as source_label; for a single-target gene-centric Analysis it is the resolved gene symbol, and for an aggregate assay it is the SomaScan SeqId, SomaLogic’s stable assay identifier (issue #141).


trait_ontology_label
No
Human-readable label of the ontology term itself that trait_ontology_id identifies, exactly as the defining ontology or controlled vocabulary names it — for example carnitine measurement (EFO:0010469) or multiple sclerosis (MONDO:0005301). It is never an identifier-authority or vocabulary label such as Ensembl, EFO, MONDO, or OBA: those name the vocabulary, not the Trait, and bundle.check() rejects an authority-name label (issue #141). Named trait_ontology_name before OpenGWASDB ADR 0034.


trait_ontology_id
No
Ontology or controlled-vocabulary identifier for the analysed Trait, when available. CURIE format, for example EFO:0001073, OBA:VT0001253 or Orphanet:101960; blank when unmapped. When the source maps the Trait to several terms, the CURIEs are joined by exactly ", " in the source’s order (MONDO:0005150, EFO:1001492), and trait_ontology_label keeps the source’s label verbatim: labels are not split per term, because a term’s own label may contain a comma (#286). Never a URI. Never a gene or protein identifier: bundle.check() rejects Ensembl, HGNC, Entrez/NCBI Gene, and UniProt identifiers, bare or authority-qualified (issue #141). Not required to be unique.


trait_ontology_mapping_method
Yes
Controlled value describing how trait_ontology_id/trait_ontology_label were resolved: source_provided, canonical_table_lookup, or unmapped. The #130 external_authority_lookup value is retired: gene/target identity is annotation, not a Trait Ontology Mapping (issue #141). Registry-only.


source_file
Yes
Source file or filtered source file consumed by the builder. Omitted in legacy monolithic BESD releases (OGS-00001 and OGS-00002), where source identity is currently recorded only as an unverified path prefix (a known integrity gap tracked in issue #134).


source_reader_capability
No
The OpenGWASDB reader that consumes source_file (for example opengwasdb.gwas-ssf). The builder reads it per row and falls back to the Build Recipe’s source-reader-capability when absent. No

A numeric value (including 0) is emitted only alongside the complete declaration triple below and only on resolver evidence: the record reports info_score_state disabled (explicit zero) or filtered (positive floor), info_rows_usable > 0, and a fingerprint that still binds the declaration. Literal NaN means unavailable – no approved declaration, a legacy record without the diagnostics, or unusable evidence. A source MAF/EAF or a lookalike INFO header is not evidence of imputation quality. This value alone does not imply any variants were filtered. Manifest Generation’s rules reject a numeric threshold without the complete triple. Omission remains valid for older bundles.

No

No

maf_threshold
No
Optional per-Analysis MAF floor in [0, 0.5]; 0 disables filtering and literal NaN means no MAF filter. A numeric value is emitted only on resolver evidence: the record reports a usable maf_state (disabled for an explicit zero, filtered for a positive floor) and the per-Analysis fingerprint still binds the same value. Every other Analysis – no configured default, a MAF-exempt genotyping technology, a legacy record without the diagnostics, or a changed fingerprint – emits literal NaN. The frequency is the reader’s af_alt (GWAS-SSF effect_allele_frequency); MAF = min(af, 1 - af). A row whose af is missing, non-finite or outside [0, 1] is retained, not dropped. Manifest Generation’s rules reject any non-NaN value outside [0, 0.5]. This value alone does not imply any variants were filtered. Omission remains valid for older bundles.

No

The row itself stays in the committed bundle, with its inclusion_reason, as the audit record of why the Analysis is absent. See ADR 0025.
