No
Optional family of columns for estimated reference ancestry proportions.



The four INFO columns are one policy: info_score_threshold is the requested floor and imputation_score_column/imputation_score_kind/ imputation_score_provenance are the exact source-column declaration it requires. Manifest Generation’s rules reject a numeric threshold without the complete triple and a triple without a numeric threshold, on every row; the pinned shared schema bundle.check() runs also checks the rows that will be built. A declared column is only meaningful to the GWAS-SSF reader, and the pinned OpenGWASDB validator reads the reader from the row, not from the Build Recipe’s source-reader-capability default. A row with a numeric threshold must therefore also carry source_reader_capability = opengwasdb.gwas-ssf. The Phase B candidate generator writes that column on every row.
For the Phase B GWAS Catalog EUR Hybrid candidate generator, a separate optional release_policy.imputation_score_declarations TSV supplies explicit, independently sourced per-Analysis score semantics to the resolver input. Its exact headers are analysis_id, imputation_score_column, imputation_score_kind, imputation_score_provenance; kinds are imputation_info or imputation_r2. The resolver input also carries the requested info_score_threshold, or literal NaN when unmapped. Finalisation copies the requested floor and the exact triple into the candidate analyses.tsv only for an Analysis whose resolver record carries the post-INFO state and at least one usable score (see the family README for the emission rule); every other Analysis emits literal NaN and empty triple cells. A declared Analysis with no usable score is retained: core no longer reports it as a controlled failure, the registry does not refuse it, and it is included with literal NaN INFO cells. Older bundles may omit all four columns entirely.
The MAF floor is a defaults.maf_threshold release decision applied per Analysis: an Analysis is exempt (and emits NaN) when its Source Metadata Table row’s genotyping_technology (;-joined, source order) is non-empty and every technology is in release_policy.maf_filter_exempt_genotyping_technologies; missing technology metadata is never an exemption. The column is a fact a source’s adapter writes (the GWAS Catalog’s from each -meta.yaml); the exemption is the release policy over it (#347). The resolver manifest carries the derived maf_threshold per Analysis and the resolver record’s maf_state plus its fingerprint binding decide the emitted candidate value, exactly as for INFO. Manifest Generation’s rules validate the column on every row, independently of the pinned OpenGWASDB Analysis schema.
A separate optional store_composition.require_maf_filtered generator-config rule decides whether a shared Store may admit an Analysis with no applied MAF floor. Absent or false, every otherwise admissible Analysis is included; true requires a positive defaults.maf_threshold and excludes an otherwise admissible Analysis whose emitted maf_threshold is NaN as not_maf_filtered (see the exclusions sidecar). The rule runs after every other membership decision and only at emit, so toggling it needs --stage emit and never a re-resolve. See ADR 0033.
A release whose Analyses each measure one molecular target – proteomics, such as Sun 2018’s SomaScan pQTLs – adds the target columns trait_chr, trait_bp, mhc, target_resolution_method and n_target_rows, rendered from the Source Metadata Table’s target annotation (#300; the retired R gwas-ssf-ragged generator also wrote n). A release with no such target (for example small-molecule metabolomics, issue #26) omits these columns entirely rather than filling them with placeholder or NA values — their absence is how a reviewer tells the two shapes apart. tissue and context likewise appear only in a release that declares them. These columns remain release-specific with no shared-core equivalent.
The target sidecar, sidecars/analysis_targets.tsv, lists each targeted Analysis’s target annotation (assay, gene symbol and Ensembl id, span, MHC flag, whether the assay is an aggregate, how the target was resolved); it is evidence, not duplicate Analysis columns. Bundles emitted by the R generator carry its wider form, with the raw SomaScan and Ensembl fields.



Accepted build rows must have usable sample-size metadata. Analyses with unknown sample size may appear in Source Inventories, candidate diagnostics, or review sidecars, but should not be included as buildable rows in an accepted analyses.tsv.
Case/control-style counts follow sample_size_kind, not the effect scale: an Analysis whose tier declares sample_size_kind = case_control carries n_cases and n_controls, and one whose tier declares any other kind leaves both blank. ukb-b is why the two are separate – its provider reports units: SD for binary traits too, so its case-control tier declares stored_effect_scale: sd beside sample_size_kind: case_control (#289). Most Sources pair them (log_or with case_control), which is why the scale looks like the deciding field. For time-to-event traits, n_cases is the event count and n_controls is the non-event or comparison count reported by the source. When the counts do not apply both must be blank rather than 0: zero is a real count, and writing it where the counts do not apply is exactly the absence-vs-zero confusion CONTRIBUTING.md rules out. bundle.check() rejects a non-empty count on a non-case-control Analysis (issue #133).
assigned_ancestry is one controlled vocabulary on every Analysis, regardless of ancestry_assignment_method: the ancestry-mixture reference’s super-population codes (AFR, AMR, EAS, EUR, MID, NAF, SAS) or empty for unassigned. It is never a free-text Source Ancestry Label (European, East Asian, and so on). The tracked translation from the candidates table’s free-text labels to these codes is resources/reference-resources/ukb-ancestry-mixture-hg38/source_label_map.tsv, read by both the Ancestry Assignment stage and the manifest generators so the two cannot drift apart. bundle.check() rejects any value outside the vocabulary, so the split cannot silently reappear.



bundle.check() normally fails a row that leaves a required column blank. Two deliberate exemptions exist, both narrow:

Releases Store Release Build will not build. A release whose status is not accepted, built or validated (#247) may leave values blank: a candidate is still being resolved, and what it must resolve before it lands is Manifest Generation’s policy, not the contract’s (#250). check() discloses the count as a tolerated gap cited not buildable.
Legacy monolithic BESD releases. OGS-00001 and OGS-00002 are exempt because their required Analytical Metadata is unpopulated in upstream BESD sources and cannot be resolved without external study metadata. The exemption is scoped to exactly those two named releases. Any new release — including any future ragged-BESD or completed release — must provide valid required values or fail bundle.check().

This is a known integrity gap, tracked by open issue #134, not an equivalent alternative to the per-Analysis checksums and source identity enforced for other formats.



bundle.check() fails a row whose analysis_id is not one path segment, and names the row. OGS-00001 and OGS-00002 are exempt: they carry eQTLGen’s <probe>::<tissue> ids (ENSG00000175445::whole_blood), which an accepted bundle may not be edited to remove (ADR 0004), so check() discloses the count as a tolerated gap cited #319 instead of reporting it as an error. The exemption is scoped to exactly those two named releases. Every other release — including any future eQTLGen or other ragged-BESD build, which names its Analyses by bare probe id and records the tissue in the tissue column — must satisfy the pattern. Retire the guard in favour of opengwasdb.model.analyses.validate_analyses() if OpenGWASDB ever validates the column (ADR 0017).




The Build Recipe describes how the accepted manifest becomes an OpenGWASDB store. It is the only input to plan(), and every value in it is either a registry fact or an opengwasdb flag. It does not record where artifacts land (issue #126).

Required
Description

Yes
Must equal the bundle’s store_id and its directory name.

Yes
dense, ragged, or hybrid.


completion_state
Yes
observed_only or reference_completed.


build
Yes for observed_only, and for reference_completed without derived_from
The observed-only build block. A single-id Reference-Completed release builds and publishes its Observed-Only Store with it first (ADR 0037).


complete
Yes for reference_completed
The completion block.


build.command / complete.command
Yes
An opengwasdb CLI subcommand; never a Python import path. Supported values are keyed by phase in plan.COMMANDS: build-dense-vcf, build-hybrid, build-ragged-ssf, build-ragged-besd; complete-dense, complete-hybrid, complete-ragged.

opengwasdb flag names passed through verbatim; see “The passthrough rule”.

Post-processing choices: top_hits, rho, overview, validate. rho defaults off and validate defaults on (plan.POST_DEFAULTS); a recipe states only what it chooses differently. top_hits and overview are always explicit because they vary per release.

No

A Build Recipe must not declare an artifacts block: bundle.check() rejects it, because the artifact root is deployment configuration (issue #126). It must also not declare the superseded family-first layout: the top-level store_family_id, family_release_id, and store_layout keys, or the nested builder, source, normalisation, effects, and shape blocks. Those are read by no code. Builder inputs that remain real flags go in options (for example source-reader-capability, source-assembly). Reference Resources, effect-scale validation, ancestry assignment, and QC-panel configuration are Manifest Generator configuration, not Build Recipe fields; see “Manifest Generator configuration” below.
store_id: OGS-00042
layout: dense
completion_state: observed_only
build:
  command: build-dense-vcf
  options:
    source-reader-capability: opengwasdb.finngen-r13
    source-assembly: hg38
    n-workers: 8
post:
  top_hits: true
  overview: true
A Reference-Completed release completes its own Store under its id (ADR 0037). It declares both blocks and has no derived_from: the build block builds and publishes the Observed-Only Store, exactly as the same file would as observed_only, and the complete block then completes that published Store and replaces it. The completion’s source is the id’s own Store path, so the recipe names no Store path at all. Dense, Hybrid and Ragged releases are all planned this way. A Ragged release’s complete options must name its ld-panel and ancestry, which the Observed-View Check is given too.
store_id: OGS-00043
layout: dense
completion_state: reference_completed
build:
  command: build-dense-vcf
  options:
    source-reader-capability: opengwasdb.finngen-r13
    source-assembly: hg38
complete:
  command: complete-dense
  options:
    ld-panel: /data/opengwasdb/reference/ld/hgdp1kgp-hg38
    ancestry: EUR
    n-workers: 16
post:
  top_hits: true
  overview: true
post applies to both phases. complete-dense builds the Top-Hit Index inline, so the completion phase plans no separate top_hits step.
Manifest Generation emits that file from the release config’s completion block (release config, #340):

a reference that is qualified and active gives one bundle under the Store’s id, with completion_state: reference_completed, the build block byte-identical to the one the same config emits as observed_only, and the complete block whose ld-panel and ancestry are its Reference Resource’s declaration;
a reference that is pending, on hold or blocked gives exactly the Observed-Only bundle a config with no completion block emits, so a bundle never declares a completion phase that the config has not qualified and activated. release.yaml’s notes say the recipe is blocked, and the candidate’s Validation Record records the reference, with blocked: true, under acceptance.completion_reference (see validation.yaml below).

Only an emitted candidate declares this; a Store published before its bundle declared completion gains the complete block through the one amendment an accepted bundle allows (#305), not through a re-emit.
A two-id Reference-Completed release, from before ADR 0037, is the same file with a complete block instead of build. It carries no parent path: the parent is release.yaml’s derived_from, and its artifact path is a pure function of that ID. Existing two-id bundles (OGS-00002, OGS-00022, OGS-00023) stay valid.
store_id: OGS-00043
layout: dense
completion_state: reference_completed

  options:
    ld-panel: /data/opengwasdb/reference/ld/hgdp1kgp-hg38

A Dense or Hybrid Build Recipe may declare optional named Indexed Variant Subsets (stores #209). Each declaration becomes one opengwasdb build-indexed-subset Step, planned after the Store and its inline top-hit/rho steps exist and before overview and validate, so overview reports the subset and validation audits it. The Step’s durable records/indexed-subset-<name>.json is written by the ordinary step executor; no new record schema is introduced.








Field
Required
Description




name
Yes
The subset identity. The consumer’s grammar [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}, and the registry additionally refuses .. because the name becomes part of the record filename. Unique within the release.


resource_id
Yes
resource_id of a maintained kind: variant_list Reference Resource (resources/reference-resources/<id>/resource.yaml).


variant_list
Yes
The concrete canonical-ALID list path the build passes as --variant-list. It must match the resource declaration’s location. Recorded so the immutable bundle is self-contained; plan() never opens it.


reference_assembly
Yes
The list’s assembly, passed as --reference-assembly. It must match the resource declaration’s genome_build.


checksum
No
The maintained list’s sha256 as 64 hex characters. When present it must equal the resource declaration’s checksums.alid_sha256.


options
No
build-indexed-subset flags passed through verbatim (plan.render_options), so the same declared policy reaches both phases’ subset steps. overwrite is refused, and so is any key that normalises (strip().lstrip('-')) to variant-list or reference-assembly: those are the declaration’s own verified inputs, and re-specifying one in options would let the executed CLI use a value the runtime did not hash or check. A value must render as CLI tokens – a string, number or bool, or a non-empty list of them; a mapping would arrive as its own repr and null or an empty list as nothing at all, so both are refused.



The key is optional; omit it to declare no subsets. An explicit indexed_subsets: null is malformed rather than treated as omitted, so a generator cannot silently drop a declaration.
indexed_subsets:
  - name: hm3
    resource_id: hapmap3-hg38
    variant_list: /data/opengwasdb/reference/hapmap3-hg38/hm3.grch38.alid.txt
    reference_assembly: GRCh38
    checksum: 4a7c82aa625a006ff437dcaa2769b00e056413d54c72e98f7378327c69513398
    options:
      overflow-only: skip
That last declaration is OGS-00011’s (stores #225). A requested ALID that only a Hybrid release’s shared axis carries cannot be indexed in its Dense Component, and --overflow-only skip leaves such an ALID out and records how many the subset skipped (opengwas/opengwasdb#324, and that repository’s ADR 0065). The planner does not interpret the flag: it renders the mapping into the two build-indexed-subset steps, build phase and completion phase alike, exactly as declared.
bundle.check() validates the declaration shape (names, required strings, checksum syntax, uniqueness, Dense/Hybrid only, no overwrite, and options values that render as CLI tokens) without any resource I/O. Whether the resource_id resolves, whether the list matches the maintained checksum, and whether the runtime provides build-indexed-subset are run-time facts the release entry point verifies before a build; the tracked opengwasdb pin provides the capability since stores#218, so the entry point needs no PATH overlay. See ADR 0034 and the workflow specification’s “Indexed Variant Subsets”.



A tabular Source Collection read through OpenGWASDB’s generic tabular reader has a Column Map: a TOML file declaring which provider column supplies each field and the collection’s conventions (opengwasdb ADR 0063). ADR 0036 has it travel in the Release Bundle, checksummed, so Analysis Resolution and Store Release Build read every file the same way (#292).
An Analysis reads through a Column Map when its source_reader_capability is opengwasdb.column-map. A row that leaves source_reader_capability blank, or has no such column, inherits the Build Recipe’s build/complete options.source-reader-capability. Both values are compared with surrounding whitespace stripped. A bundle with at least one such Analysis is mapped. A recipe default of opengwasdb.column-map does not map a bundle whose every row names its own reader. A mapped bundle’s Build Recipe binds exactly one map, since files that need different maps belong to different Source Collections:
column_map:
  name: dbgap-phs002453-mvp-gia
  sha256: 3f0c...e9a1   # 64 lower-case hex characters
  file: dbgap-phs002453-mvp-gia.toml








Field
Required
Description




name
Yes
The map’s own name, as its TOML declares it. Any non-empty string, as OpenGWASDB accepts.


sha256
Yes
The sha256 of the map file’s bytes, as 64 lower-case hex characters.


file
Yes, except for a built-in
The file the bundle carries the map in, under column_maps/. A file name, not a path: the Indexed Variant Subset grammar [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127} with no .., ending .toml.



name and sha256 are the fingerprint OpenGWASDB records in a mapped Resolution Record (resolution_config.column_map) and in a mapped Store’s manifest.json (provenance.column_map). The three can therefore be compared field for field. file is kept apart from name so that a map’s name never has to be a safe file name.
Built-in maps. OpenGWASDB ships two maps, gwas-ssf and finngen-r13. A binding with no file names one of them, and the bundle carries nothing for it, because the pinned OpenGWASDB package holds the bytes. Its sha256 records the built-in’s checksum as the Resolution Records report it. A binding with no file and any other name is refused. A carried copy of a built-in, bound with a file, is an ordinary carried map. A bundle whose rows use the dedicated readers opengwasdb.gwas-ssf or opengwasdb.finngen-r13 is not mapped and needs neither a binding nor a file. That covers every bundle registered before #292.
bundle.check() (_check_column_map) refuses, reporting every one it finds in one pass:

a mapped bundle whose Build Recipe binds no column_map;
a binding in a bundle that is not mapped: a map no Analysis reads through;
a bound file the bundle does not carry at column_maps/<file>, or one that is a symbolic link or not a regular file;
a carried map whose bytes do not hash to the bound sha256;
any other entry in column_maps/: a carried map that is not bound;
a column_maps that is a symbolic link or not a directory;
a malformed binding: not a mapping, null (omit the key to bind none), an unknown key, an empty name, a sha256 that is not 64 lower-case hex characters, a file outside the grammar, or no file with a name that is not a built-in;
column-map in build.options, complete.options or a variant_reference block’s options. The flag is composed from the checksummed binding, never passed through around it.

The contract checks a carried map shallowly. It must be UTF-8 TOML with a column_map_version and a name equal to the binding’s. Its full validation, covering fields, conventions and refusals, belongs to OpenGWASDB, which applies it at Analysis Resolution and at every build that reads through the map. The contract does not copy those rules.
A built-in binding’s sha256 must be that of the map file the pinned OpenGWASDB ships: bundle.check() takes the built-in names, and each file’s checksum, from opengwasdb.readers.column_map and refuses any other value, naming both.
The checksum contract. The binding’s name and sha256 are one value everywhere the map is used, and each use is checked against it:

Manifest Generation passes the resolver --column-map (a built-in’s name, or the release config’s column_map.path). Every mapped Resolution Record’s resolution_config.column_map must equal the binding, and the map’s checksum is part of the resolver’s settings digest and of the receipt’s resolution contract, so a changed map makes its Resolution Records stale: the resolver re-resolves them, and verify refuses records made under another map. The emitter writes the binding and copies a non-built-in map to column_maps/<file>.
Store Release Build passes --column-map to every build command that reads source files through it: build-dense-vcf, build-hybrid and the variant-reference pre-stage. A completion reads a Store and takes none; a command that takes no map (build-ragged-ssf) is refused for a bundle that binds one. A built-in goes by name. A carried map goes as a copy staged at <artifact root>/<store id>/work/column_maps/<file>, as the derived build manifest is, so the planned argv is the same from any checkout.
Before any build the release entry point, and the Snakefile’s onstart and column_map rule, re-hash column_maps/<file> against the binding and refuse a mismatch, naming the map. The staging rule re-hashes again as it copies. Snakemake treats an existing staged copy as up to date, so each step that lists it as an input checks the staged bytes against the binding immediately before it runs (resources.verify_staged_column_map), and a retried build whose staged copy changed is refused naming the map.
plan() is a pure function (ADR 0031): it reads only the binding’s recorded fields. That a built-in’s sha256 is the pinned package’s is check()’s to say.

assign-ancestry and estimate-phenotype-sd take no map yet (opengwasdb ADR 0063, opengwas/opengwasdb#285).



options keys are opengwasdb flag names. plan() renders key: value as --key value, booleans as bare flags (--key for true, --no-key for false), lists by repeating the flag, and never interprets a key. The registry does not know what --min-cor means and must not acquire a copy of opengwasdb’s parameter schema (ADR 0023).
An unrecognised or invalid flag fails in the CLI argument parser in milliseconds, before any expensive work. plan() composes only the arguments that are the registry’s own facts — store identity, the declared association_coverage for a Ragged build, the derived build manifest path, and artifact paths. Everything else comes from options.
A flag the registry composes is refused in options, because a recipe’s copy would be a second declaration: plan() refuses a build.options key that renders --association-coverage on a Ragged build, since release.yaml declares that value (ADR 0040) and a recipe change would be a new Store Release (ADR 0004).

Release-level acceptance and build validation summary. This table is the one definition of the format; the workflow specification explains how register produces it rather than restating the fields. A measurement the build did not report is written as null — absence is recorded, never guessed or defaulted (issue #135).
Two writers produce this file at different times: - A Manifest Generator writes a candidate bundle’s record (Phase B): its acceptance checks, sidecar reports and warnings. - register writes the record of a built release (issue #119).
register replaces the candidate’s record; it does not merge with it. Its status, checks, warnings and errors hold only that run’s findings: the opengwasdb validate --format json verdict as checks.store, with that run’s warnings and errors exactly as validate printed them. None of them carries anything from the record being replaced (#195).
The candidate’s Phase B acceptance evidence is kept in its own labelled acceptance block, apart from those findings, and nothing in it feeds them (#195). register fills the block in one of three ways: - From a candidate record (one whose validator.name is not opengwasdb validate): every block it holds, verbatim – its checks, warnings and reports, and whatever evidence its generator records, such as reference_overlap (OGS-00011), store_composition (#203) or a dbGaP candidate’s own acceptance – except the fields that describe the generator’s run rather than the bundle: status, validated_at, validator, build_environment, observed and errors. The block is dated by the candidate’s own validated_at and tied to the commit that record came from. A candidate block named recorded_at or commit is refused, since it would overwrite that dating. - From a register-written record: its acceptance block is passed on verbatim, because the accepted bundle it describes is immutable. - Not at all, from a record #135 migrated (OGS-00001..7). Those records mix Phase B evidence with an earlier build’s findings, so nothing is extracted from them; git keeps them.
register names no generator’s evidence, so a generator that records a new kind is carried without changing register (#250).
A built or validated release must carry a validation.yaml whose status is one of not_run, passed, passed_with_warnings, or failed; bundle.check() rejects any other value. A validated release needs passed or passed_with_warnings: a passing opengwasdb validate is what makes a release validated, and its warnings are kept in the record (#195; see the workflow specification’s “The Release Status a Validation Record gives”). A candidate, accepted, superseded, or withdrawn release needs none.

A check’s stage is a precedence slot in the release policy: the policy settles an Analysis in a fixed order and, at each slot, the first failed exclusion check there decides. The slot fixes which reason wins when several apply and what the audit row carries: resolved (a successful Resolution Record, before Assigned Ancestry is read; the row carries none), ancestry_read (Assigned Ancestry read but not yet assessed; the row keeps the value read), selection (Assigned Ancestry tested against the Selection; the row carries it as af_assigned when it is a super-population code) and target_ancestry (the Analysis has the Selection’s ancestry, and its case-control counts when it needs them). Within a slot, registry order decides. A new check can use an existing slot without a policy change; a new slot is a change to the release policy.
A measurement an exclusion cannot use is never a silent pass. An invalid result where its check would decide membership stops the run; on an Analysis an earlier rule already excluded, it is only recorded. An Analysis that nothing excluded but that an exclusion check recorded as unmeasured (or invalid) is refused, naming the Analysis and the check, rather than included untested.
The INFO and MAF floors (defaults.info_score_threshold, defaults.maf_threshold) are not Quality Checks, because OpenGWASDB applies them to rows during Analysis Resolution and neither one decides an Analysis’s membership; their effect is measured by build_eligible_rows.
Contract. The sidecar is an optional Release Bundle contract file (ADR 0036: the contract grows per-Analysis Quality Check results). A bundle without it is valid; every bundle emitted before #285 has none. When it is present, bundle.check() (_check_quality_checks) requires:

the columns analysis_id, exclude_from_build, exclusion_reason, then one <check>, <check>_measured pair per check, at least one, with no check named twice;
one row per analyses.tsv Analysis, excluded audit rows included, in the same order, and no other row;
every <check> value in the result vocabulary above;
exclude_from_build exactly true or empty, agreeing with analyses.tsv; exclusion_reason non-empty exactly when excluded, and, when sidecars/exclusions.tsv is present, equal to its reason for that Analysis.

Store Release Build never reads it: membership is already decided in analyses.tsv (tests/packaging/test_boundary.py holds this).

target_id
No
Gene, analyte, or other target defining the region.


target_label
No
Human-readable target label.


lead_variant_id
No
Lead variant for signal-defined regions.


pvalue_threshold
No
Threshold used to define signal-derived regions.


n_variants_retained
No
Number of variants retained in the filtered source file for this region.


region_policy_id
Yes
Named sparse-region policy declared in generator configuration.






Suggested path: sidecars/filter_summary.tsv. One row per region-filtered source file, carried from acquisition as the sparse-region sidecar is (#300). A release acquired from the retired R generator’s files carries that bundle’s own file, whose further columns (attempt, retry_count and per-run timings) the shared filter does not write, so the same files give the same bytes.








Field
Required
Description




analysis_id
Yes
Registry Analysis ID matching analyses.tsv.


status, error
Yes
ok and blank for a filtered file.


source_url
No
Where the original was fetched from.


downloaded_bytes
No
The original’s size.


input_rows
Yes
Source rows with a position and a p-value.


retained_rows, retained_fraction
Yes
Rows kept, and their fraction of input_rows to 6 decimal places.


cis_rows
Yes
Rows kept in the cis window (0 for a signals-only policy).


significant_trans_regions, significant_trans_rows
Yes
Merged significant-trans ranges and the rows kept in them.


suggestive_leads
Yes
Suggestive leads kept.


qc_panel_rows
Yes
Rows kept at QC-panel positions.


output_file, output_bytes, checksum_algorithm, checksum
Yes
The filtered file, as the Acquisition Manifest records it.






Suggested path: sidecars/derivations.tsv. Use only when compact analyses.tsv fields need additional evidence that does not belong in a specialised sidecar.



Field
Required
Description




analysis_id
Yes
Registry Analysis ID matching analyses.tsv.


field
Yes
Manifest field being explained.


value
No
Resolved value written to the manifest.


method
Yes
Controlled or script-local method name.


evidence
No
Compact evidence string or URI.


notes
No
Free-text notes for audit.







A Source Collection plugs into Manifest Generation through files, never through code the pipeline calls (ADR 0036). Two of them meet at freeze (python3 -m manifest_generation.freeze, #283):

the Source Metadata Table: one row per intended Analysis in canonical columns – source_analysis_id (the only required one), Source Trait Label and ontology terms, Source Ancestry Label and super-population, study design, declared effect scale, sample size and case counts, genome build, Publication Metadata, licence, a provider grouping (store_key) and optional target columns for single-target Analyses;
the Acquisition Manifest: per Analysis, the file acquisition produced – location, size, sha256, source URL, metadata sidecar, lineage for a reformatted file – or the readiness status recording why there is none.

A release config’s Selection (all, an analyses list, or a where rule) picks the Analyses one release takes. Freeze reconciles them, fails on a selected Analysis with no manifest row, a row no Analysis claims or a duplicate, keeps an explained absence as a non-ready inventory row, and writes the Source Inventory with the selected connector rows frozen beside it.
docs/spec/source-connectors.md specifies every column, the vocabularies, the GWAS Catalog adapter and writer, the Selection grammar and the frozen inventory’s provenance.



The blocks below are Phase B generator configuration, not Release Bundle fields. They are recorded here because they determine the sidecar and validation.yaml evidence a generator writes into a bundle. A generator’s config also carries its selection and output settings; the blocks that affect release metadata are documented here.


Phase B selects release membership from a frozen Source Inventory rather than from a glob over an acquisition mirror (issue #151). That directory’s README is the authority on the inventory’s columns, its readiness vocabulary and the freeze/preflight commands. A generator config names the snapshot it selects from and the acquisition output that snapshot was frozen from:








Field
Required
Description




source.source_collection_id
Yes
The Source Collection string recorded on the release, gwas-catalog-ssf for the GWAS Catalog GWAS-SSF collection.


source.store_key
Yes
The candidate-pool key this release’s Analyses were selected from. Every inventory row must belong to it.


source.ancestry_group
Yes
The source-declared ancestry group the pool is scoped to. Provenance, never a substitute for Assigned Ancestry.


source.candidates
Yes
The candidate table the pool came from. Generated and not tracked in git, so the freeze records its checksum to pin the selection scope.


source.inventory.snapshot_id
Yes
The snapshot’s identity. Must equal the inventory file’s stem and the provenance sidecar’s snapshot_id.


source.inventory.path
Yes
resources/inventories/<snapshot-id>.tsv.


source.inventory.provenance_path
Yes
resources/inventories/<snapshot-id>.meta.yaml, the sidecar whose inventory_tsv_sha256 binds the TSV to the bytes that were frozen.


source.inventory.freeze_inputs
Yes, for a GWAS Catalog config (a pre-#287 key)
The ordered {role, path} acquisition status manifests, earliest pass first. Only the GWAS Catalog’s src/manifest_generation/providers/gwas_catalog/write_acquisition_manifest.py reads it (#347): it overlays the passes into the Acquisition Manifest and its pass lineage, before freeze, and freeze then reads that manifest like any other source’s. It is therefore required wherever that writer is given --config, and the writer refuses a config that declares none rather than defaulting to one pass. No shared module reads this key, and a release config names its connector files under source_collection.connectors instead (docs/spec/release-config.md maps the pre-#287 keys). Order is the precedence rule: a later pass is authoritative for every analysis_id it covers, and it may not regress a ready Analysis to a non-ready one.



Which readiness_status values count as a usable source is not a config key: it is owned by src/manifest_generation/source_inventory.py (READY_STATUSES: ok and already_present), so the vocabulary has one spelling rather than one per generator config. An unknown status fails rather than defaulting to unavailable.



A release whose pool mixes study designs cannot carry one release-wide stored_effect_scale: a quantitative trait on the SD scale and a case-control trait on the log-OR scale need different tiers. defaults.by_study_design declares one tier per study_design value the inventory may carry:








Field
Required
Description




defaults.by_study_design.<study_design>.stored_effect_scale
Yes
Controlled analyses.tsv vocabulary: sd, log_or, or log_hazard.


defaults.by_study_design.<study_design>.original_effect_scale
Yes
The source’s own scale before OpenGWASDB rescaling.


defaults.by_study_design.<study_design>.original_sd_method
Yes
The phenotype-SD tier: an estimable method for a quantitative design, or binary_trait/unavailable where SD estimation does not apply.


defaults.by_study_design.<study_design>.sample_size_kind
Yes
total, case_control, effective, or variant_level.



A ready Analysis whose study_design has no declared tier fails preflight, naming the design and the number of Analyses affected: guessing a tier is the silent-failure class this repository exists to prevent. runtime.cores (the planned worker count, capped per release) and runtime.min_free_gb (the free space preflight requires under output.work_root) are checked the same way.



A metadata resolver is a small, independently callable module owned by one Source Collection (gwas-catalog-ssf, opengwas-gwas-vcf, …) that resolves the interpretation-bearing fields derive cannot safely infer from the raw summary-statistics file alone: stored_effect_scale, sample_size_kind, sample_size, n_cases, and n_controls. Resolvers read the provider’s own authoritative study/analysis metadata (a study table row, an API response, an endpoint manifest) — never the summary-statistics file itself, which may disagree with or omit this metadata (see issue #15’s ieu-a-7 example, where a GWAS-VCF ##SAMPLE header declares StudyType=Continuous for a study the source API correctly reports as case-control).
Conventionally, resolver modules live beside their provider, under src/manifest_generation/providers/<provider>/, one file per Source Collection, named for the resolved field set they share: resolve_<source_collection>_metadata(...).
Input is whatever raw metadata unit the provider exposes for one Analysis (free text, a parsed API record, …); shape is provider-specific and not part of this contract. Output is always a single resolved record with these fields:








Field
Required
Description




resolution_status
Yes
resolved or unresolved. Never a silent default — an Analysis whose metadata can’t be established gets an explicit unresolved record, not a defaulted value that looks plausible.


resolution_notes
No
Free-text reason when resolution_status = unresolved.


stored_effect_scale
No
Same controlled vocabulary as analyses.tsv: sd, log_or, or log_hazard. NA when resolution_status = unresolved.


sample_size_kind
No
Same controlled vocabulary as analyses.tsv: total, case_control, effective, or variant_level. NA when resolution_status = unresolved.


sample_size
No
Scalar study N. NA when resolution_status = unresolved.


n_cases
No
Case (or event) count. NA when not applicable (sample_size_kind != case_control) or unresolved.


n_controls
No
Control (or non-event) count. NA when not applicable or unresolved.



A caller (a derive stage, or a curation script such as ebi-studies.r) may adapt this generic record onto its own column names, but the resolver itself must not know which downstream shape it feeds — this is what lets derive stay agnostic to which provider it is talking to.
These implementations exist:

src/manifest_generation/providers/gwas_catalog/gwas_catalog_ssf.R (resolve_gwas_catalog_ssf_metadata()) resolves GWAS Catalog’s free-text “INITIAL SAMPLE SIZE” study field: a study whose parsed components include any cases/controls counts resolves as case_control with stored_effect_scale = log_or; otherwise it resolves as total with stored_effect_scale = sd; a field with no parseable numeric component resolves as unresolved.
src/manifest_generation/providers/ukb_b/provider_metadata.py (resolve_record(), issue #219), for the opengwas-gwas-vcf Source Collection, and the adapter that writes its Source Metadata Table (#289). It resolves a study’s ncase/ncontrol/sample_size from the OpenGWAS “gwasinfo” record – the provider JSON sidecar ukb-b ships beside each VCF, since the stored API token expired – rather than the source GWAS-VCF file’s ##SAMPLE header, which is not authoritative. A usable ncase/ncontrol pair resolves sample_size_kind as case_control; otherwise a usable sample_size resolves it as total; a record with neither resolves as unresolved. stored_effect_scale primarily follows the record’s units field (SD -> sd, log odds/logOR -> log_or, a hazard-ratio unit -> log_hazard), falling back to log_or/sd from ncase/ncontrol presence only when units is absent or unrecognised (issue #50: the ukb-b batch reports every trait on the SD scale, so inferring scale from case/control-count presence alone is wrong for that batch). The R resolver that held this contract (lib/metadata_resolvers/opengwas_api.R) retired with ukb-b’s R path (#289).
src/manifest_generation/providers/finngen/source_metadata_adapter.py (issue #288, docs/spec/source-connectors.md), FinnGen’s endpoint manifest, for the finngen-r13 Source Collection. It keeps the classification the collection’s retired R resolver applied: binary endpoint rows carry num_cases and num_controls and are case-control; FinnGen encodes its inverse-rank-normalised quantitative endpoints with category = Quantitative endpoints, the total N in num_cases, and num_controls = 0, and those rows are quantitative without misrepresenting that total as a case count. It refuses an endpoint it cannot describe honestly rather than leaving it unresolved; the release config’s method tiers turn study_design into stored_effect_scale/sample_size_kind.




Manifest Generation’s shared step (#286, ADR 0036 step 5). The Python pipeline maps every Analysis in src/manifest_generation/trait_ontology_mapping.py, after the resolver records are verified. It reads the source term from the Source Metadata Table’s source_trait_ontology_id/source_trait_ontology_label (GWAS Catalog’s MAPPED_TRAIT_URI/MAPPED_TRAIT) and the Source Trait Label. Precedence and methods are those below: - a source term is kept as source_provided; - otherwise an exact match of the trimmed, lower-cased Source Trait Label is canonical_table_lookup; - otherwise the Analysis is unmapped.
A source term is normalised to CURIEs term by term:







Source form
CURIE




http://www.ebi.ac.uk/efo/EFO_0004839
EFO:0004839


http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/MONDO_0005148 (any NS_local)
MONDO:0005148


http://www.orpha.net/ORDO/Orphanet_101960
Orphanet:101960


a CURIE
unchanged



Any other form is refused, naming the Analysis and the term: the run fails rather than emitting a URI or a guess. A comma-separated source list stays a list, its CURIEs joined by ", " in the source’s order, and the source label is kept verbatim (see trait_ontology_id above).
A source term is rejected using ogstores.bundle’s #141 guards when: - any term is gene- or protein-shaped, checked both before and after normalisation, so a PURL HGNC_1234 is caught as HGNC:1234; - or its label, taken whole, is an identifier-authority name.
A rejected term falls through to the table, and the rejection and its reason are recorded. A source term with no label is kept as source_provided, and the run counts how many there are.
The table is read from resources/reference-resources/canonical-trait-mapping-efo/, a directory named explicitly: no network is involved. Its resource.yaml location is resolved against that directory: the declared file must be in the resource’s own directory, and a declared location_kind must be tracked_file. A malformed curated row fails the load, and the refusal lists up to twenty problems and counts the rest: - a blank lookup value; - a non-CURIE term; - a gene-shaped term or an authority-name label; - a label listed twice.
The table’s identity, the method counts, the count of source terms without a label, and the rejected source terms are recorded in validation.yaml’s trait_ontology_mapping block.
The lookup lives in this registry rather than in OpenGWASDB ADR 0021. A source-provided term is kept even when the ontology has deprecated it, and is recorded as source_provided; a plausible-looking invented replacement would be worse than the genuine obsolete term.



Each item in a generator config’s reference_resources list describes one auxiliary build-time resource (see ADR 0011). The canonical form of a declaration is a resource.yaml under resources/reference-resources/<resource-id>/; a generator config may repeat the fields it needs inline. A reference-AF resource used for effect-scale validation should declare at least:








Field
Required
Description




resource_id
Yes
Stable ID for this Reference Resource, referenced from effect_scale_validation.reference_resources or ancestry_assignment.reference_resource_id.


kind
Yes
reference_af for single-ancestry allele-frequency lookup resources used by effect-scale validation; ancestry_mixture for multi-ancestry mixture-frequency resources used by AF-based ancestry assignment (issue #23); qc_panel for the fixed QC variant panel unconditionally retained regardless of significance (issue #28/#29); trait_ontology_mapping for a curated trait-label-to-ontology-term lookup; hybrid_dense_panel for a Hybrid release’s Dense Component reference panel; variant_list for a canonical ALID list consumed as an Indexed Variant Subset build input (hapmap3-hg38, epic #214); other kinds (for example LD panels) may reuse the same declaration shape.


ancestry
Yes for reference_af
Ancestry/population label the resource represents, matching the controlled assigned_ancestry vocabulary. For ancestry_mixture resources, which cover multiple super-populations at once, use ancestry: multi and list the covered super-populations in super_populations instead. Not applicable for trait_ontology_mapping.


super_populations
Yes for ancestry_mixture
List of super-population labels the mixture reference can assign to (for example AFR, AMR, EAS, EUR, MID, NAF, SAS).


genome_build
Yes, except trait_ontology_mapping
Genome build of the resource’s coordinates. Not applicable for trait_ontology_mapping, which has no genomic coordinates.


variant_id_convention
Yes, except trait_ontology_mapping
Variant identifier/allele convention used by the resource, for example chr:pos_ref_alt, or chr:pos:A1:A2 (A1 = min(allele1, allele2)) for the canonical ALID convention opengwasdb.ancestry uses.


allele_columns
No
Column-name mapping the resource uses for effect/other allele and frequency, for example {effect: EA, other: OA, freq: EAF}.


location
Yes
External path or URI for the resource, outside this repository — except kind: qc_panel and kind: trait_ontology_mapping, both small enough to track directly in this repository, so location is a repo-relative path instead.


location_kind
No
How to interpret location, for example external_directory, external_file, or tracked_file for a small resource tracked directly in this repository.


row_count
Yes for variant_list
Number of variant rows the resource contains. Verification fails on a mismatch, so a truncated or appended list cannot pass as the declared one.


checksums
Yes for variant_list
The exact bytes the resource was accepted at: alid_sha256 and alid_bytes for the maintained list, plus source_md5/source_sha256 for the upstream source snapshot. The consumer hashes the same bytes (opengwasdb build-indexed-subset records the list’s SHA-256 in the subset metadata), so this is the identity a reviewer compares against.


source
Yes for variant_list
Upstream provenance of the list: source name, file, download URL, snapshot path, size, columns and source row count.


derivation
Yes for variant_list
How the maintained list was derived from the source and the counts that reconcile it, including rsids_requested, resolved, absent_from_store_axis, allele_incompatible and duplicate_alids. The arithmetic must balance and resolved must equal row_count; verification refuses otherwise.


fine_group_map
Yes for ancestry_mixture
External path to the fine-ancestry-group -> super-population map (one row per fine group in the resource) used to aggregate a fitted mixture to super-population composition.



Reference-AF and ancestry-mixture resources are recorded here for provenance; the resource data itself lives under the configured artifact root or another external location, never inside this repository (ADR 0015). A kind: variant_list resource is the same shape for an Indexed Variant Subset build input: the hapmap3-hg38 declaration records the canonical-ALID list’s row_count and byte checksums, its LDSC source checksum and snapshot, and the rsID reconciliation, and tools/reference-resources/hapmap3-hg38/verify_hm3_resource.py is the executable check of all of them.



Every future Dense and Hybrid Store Release declares the maintained hm3 Indexed Variant Subset by default (stores #210, epic #214); a Ragged-only release does not. The pipeline resolves that declaration through src/manifest_generation/indexed_subsets.py, which reads the one maintained hapmap3-hg38 Reference Resource, so no writer copies the list path, assembly or checksum. The default is not a requirement:








Field
Required
Description




indexed_subsets
No
A Dense or Hybrid release that omits the key gets the default hm3 declaration. An explicit [] is a deliberate opt-out and must be paired with indexed_subsets_opt_out. A non-empty list overrides the default verbatim (validated by bundle.check()). A Ragged release may not declare one.


indexed_subsets_opt_out
Yes when indexed_subsets: []
The written reason a Dense or Hybrid release omits the default. The generator records it in release.yaml notes so the omission is reviewable; an empty list with no reason, a null value, or a malformed entry is a generator error rather than a silent omission.



The resolved declaration is written to build.yaml in the shape documented under build.yaml. Because a subset-declaring release needs an opengwasdb providing build-indexed-subset, the release entry point probes for it and refuses a missing capability before any write; the repository’s pinned current-format runtime provides it (stores#218). See src/ogstores/resources.py, src/ogstores/runtime.py and the release runtime.



A generator config’s optional top-level quality_checks block overrides a Quality Check’s shared default threshold for one release (#285):
quality_checks:
  build_eligible_rows: 1000   # exclude an Analysis with fewer build-eligible rows
Each key names a registered check that has a threshold; its value is parsed by that check (build_eligible_rows takes a whole number of rows of at least 1). An unknown name, a check with no threshold (one that tests a status), or a value the check refuses is a config error. A check’s kind is part of its declaration and cannot be overridden.
Thresholds are recorded twice. validation.yaml quality_checks.<check> carries the effective and default thresholds and whether this release overrode it. The resolution receipt’s contract always carries a quality_checks entry holding the effective thresholds, defaults included, and the release’s overrides, so changing an override or a shared default makes the receipt stale and verify/emit refuse it until resolution is re-run. A receipt written before #285 has no such entry and is stale for the same reason.



A generator config’s effect_scale_validation block configures the reference-AF effect-scale validation stage (issue #16) for one release:








Field
Required
Description




enabled
Yes
Whether this release opts into empirical effect-scale validation.


reference_resources
Yes when enabled
List of {ancestry, resource_id} pairs mapping an assigned ancestry to a declared Reference Resource resource_id. An ancestry without an entry here produces an explicit skipped sidecar row rather than silently omitting evidence.


maf_min / maf_max
Yes when enabled
Reference-MAF bounds a variant must fall within to be used for implied-SD estimation.


min_overlap_variants
Yes when enabled
Minimum number of safely aligned, in-bounds variants required before an Analysis is scored rather than skipped as low_overlap.


sd_tolerance
Yes when enabled
Maximum abs(median implied SD - 1) for a declared-standardised Analysis to pass.


warning_multiplier
Yes when enabled
Multiplier applied to sd_tolerance defining the boundary between a warning and a failed scale-inconsistency status.


dispersion_max
Yes when enabled
Maximum robust dispersion (median absolute deviation over median implied SD) before the result is downgraded to warning regardless of the central estimate.



A generator config may set defaults for these values and override them per release, per the source’s molecular or population-scale GWAS tolerances. When the block is absent or enabled: false, the release has not opted into empirical effect-scale validation, and validation.yaml checks.effect_scale/checks.sd_estimation should read not_run rather than imply a pass.



A generator config’s ancestry_assignment block configures the AF-based ancestry assignment stage (issue #23) for one release. Unlike effect_scale_validation (which maps one Reference Resource per assigned ancestry, since each reference-AF panel is single-ancestry), a single ancestry-mixture Reference Resource covers every super-population at once, so this block references exactly one Reference Resource rather than an ancestry-keyed list:








Field
Required
Description




enabled
Yes
Whether this release opts into AF-based ancestry assignment.


reference_resource_id
Yes when enabled
resource_id of the declared kind: ancestry_mixture Reference Resource to fit against.


maf_floor
No
Minimum reference-wide MAF for a variant to be used in the mixture fit; defaults to 0.01. Lower for tiny fixture panels where all variants are informative.


gates.tau
Yes when enabled
Minimum dominant super-population proportion required to admit an assignment.


gates.delta
Yes when enabled
Minimum margin of the dominant super-population’s proportion over the runner-up.


gates.n_min
Yes when enabled
Minimum number of allele-frequency sites overlapping the reference required before fitting. Ragged/sparse releases (signal-derived regions only, not a full-genome scan) typically need a much lower n_min than a dense, full-GWAS release.


gates.residual_max
Yes when enabled
Maximum NNLS mixture-fit residual before the assignment is gated out as unreliable.



Only Analyses with usable source allele frequencies attempt AF-based assignment; Analyses without usable source AF keep ancestry_assignment_method: source_trusted_no_af untouched, per issue #11’s settled trust-vs-validate policy. When an assignment is attempted but fails a gate, ancestry_assignment_method becomes unassigned (not left at its prior value), because the prior value would otherwise misleadingly imply validation was never attempted.



The shared pipeline keeps the QC panel in every region-filtered file: a release config’s region_policy.qc_panel_resource_id names it, and acquisition records the panel’s identity in each file’s lineage (#300, release config). The R generators’ filter.qc_panel block, described below for the bundles they emitted, retired with them.
A generator config’s filter.qc_panel block configured unconditional retention of the fixed QC variant panel (issue #28/#29/#30) for one release. Unlike the signal-driven sparse regions (cis/significant_trans/suggestive_trans), the QC panel is retained regardless of an Analysis’s p_value distribution, so ancestry assignment and reference-AF effect-scale validation have a stable variant backbone even for Analyses with few or no genome-wide-significant hits:








Field
Required
Description




enabled
Yes
Whether this release retains the QC panel in every Analysis’s filtered file.


resource_id
Yes when enabled
resource_id of the declared kind: qc_panel Reference Resource to retain (see “Reference Resource declaration”).



QC-panel retention is purely additive: a release that does not configure filter.qc_panel behaves exactly as before, and enabling it for one release never changes another’s filtered output. Retained QC-panel rows are recorded in the sparse-region sidecar with region_kind: qc_panel (one row per chromosome the panel actually matched in that Analysis’s source file, spanning the matched positions), distinct from the signal-driven region kinds, and sidecars/filter_summary.tsv gets a qc_panel_rows count per Analysis (0 for releases that do not configure a panel).
Effect-scale validation (issue #16) and ancestry assignment (issue #23/#25) deliberately do not distinguish QC-panel rows from signal-driven rows when choosing which retained variants to use for AF/SD computations — both continue to consume every retained row with usable allele-frequency data uniformly. Retaining the QC panel already directly grows that pool for low-power Analyses; preferring QC-panel rows exclusively would need to discard perfectly good signal-driven rows for well-powered Analyses, for no demonstrated ascertainment benefit. This can be revisited if evidence of an ascertainment problem emerges, but is not assumed by default.




A release bundle is acceptable when analyses.tsv is enough for OpenGWASDB to build the intended store, release.yaml and build.yaml are enough to explain what the store is and how to rebuild it, and sidecars are enough to audit any non-obvious derived metadata without blocking low-effort source ingestion. Run pixi run bundle-check to confirm it.

title: Release Bundle schema
text:
Following only this document, the three files below produce a bundle that passes bundle.check():
stores/OGS-99001/release.yaml
store_id: OGS-99001
label: example-release
access_posture: public
status: candidate
created_at: '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z'
source_snapshot_id: example-source-2026-01-01
description: 'A minimal Release Bundle authored from the schema documentation.'
generator:
  commands:
    - Rscript resources/generators/example/generate.R --mode=emit
stores/OGS-99001/build.yaml
store_id: OGS-99001
layout: dense
completion_state: observed_only
build:
  command: build-dense-vcf
  options:
    source-reader-capability: opengwasdb.example
    source-assembly: hg38
post:
  top_hits: true
  overview: true
stores/OGS-99001/analyses.tsv   (tab-separated; header plus at least one row)
analysis_id source_label    analysis_label  source_file checksum    checksum_algorithm  source_genome_build license trait_ontology_mapping_method   assigned_ancestry   ancestry_assignment_method  original_effect_scale   original_sd_method  stored_effect_scale sample_size_kind    sample_size_scope   sample_size
EXAMPLE-0001    Example trait   Example trait   /data/opengwasdb/example/source.tsv.gz  e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855    sha256  GRCh38  Example terms of use    unmapped    EUR source_trusted_no_af    sd  declared_standardised   sd  total   analysis_level  1000
That covers every column this document marks Yes. A candidate release needs no validation.yaml; a built or validated release does (see validation.yaml). A reference_completed release either completes its own Store under its id, and declares both a build and a complete block (ADR 0037), or is a two-id child that declares derived_from: OGS-00042 in release.yaml and a complete block instead of build (ADR 0007).

title: Release Bundle schema
text:
Phase B — what produces a bundle — is described here only in outline; the canonical command log for each release is recorded in release.yaml:generator.commands. A Manifest Generator conventionally has five stages:









Stage
Purpose
Typical inputs
Outputs




discover
Snapshot available upstream analyses and files.
Source inventory, GWAS Catalog studies table, source meta.yaml, provider APIs.
Raw candidate records and source-file locations.


select
Apply the Store Release’s inclusion rules.
Candidate records, generator config, priority lists, publication/analyte filters.
Selected Analysis set for a proposed Store Release.


derive
Add authoritative analytical metadata and generated evidence.
Selected rows, provider metadata resolvers, source files, OpenGWASDB readers, reference resources, Ensembl, checksums.
Resolved analyses.tsv columns and sidecar evidence.


emit
Write a reproducible release bundle.
Resolved rows, sidecars, build choices, generator provenance.
release.yaml, analyses.tsv, build.yaml, validation.yaml, sidecars.


accept
Check that the bundle is complete enough to build.
Release bundle, schema checks, lightweight source/readability checks.
Updated validation.yaml and release status.



Metadata resolution and summary-statistics reading are orthogonal concerns. A Source Collection chooses a provider-specific metadata resolver for study tables, APIs, or endpoint manifests, and separately declares an OpenGWASDB Source Reader Capability for source data. The resolved metadata shape is common even when the provider and source format differ.

title: Release Bundle schema
text:
Registry identity and provenance. Never read by opengwasdb. Required for an accepted Release Bundle; a candidate may leave lifecycle timestamps null.
The file trims to identity, lineage, Release Status, creation time, source snapshot identity, the generation command log, and the prose that explains the Store Release (issue #136, ADR 0029). Issue #137 removed the one-time migration provenance block (ADR 0030); the published artifact path is now a pure function of the identifier.



Field
Required
Description




store_id
Yes
Opaque OGS- 5-digit identifier (ADR 0022): the directory name under stores/, and must match it.


label
Yes
Source-natural display name; provenance, never an identifier (ADR 0022).


association_coverage
Yes
What associations the Store holds, in one vocabulary shared with opengwasdb: gwas (genome-wide), cis (a cis window around each Analysis’s target only), cis_and_signals (a cis window plus significant signals elsewhere) or signals_only (significant signals and their flanks, no cis window). It replaced full_gwas and cis_plus_signals (issue #341, ADR 0040). bundle.check() refuses any other value and a value that is not a string, and Bundle.association_coverage raises rather than answering a default, because the Analysis Catalog shows it and counts Analyses by it. It is also the value plan() passes to a Ragged build as --association-coverage (issue #341), so it is declared, never inferred from the Store Layout. A Dense or Hybrid release can carry only gwas, and bundle.check() refuses any other value there (opengwas/opengwasdb#298). A region-filtered release declares cis_and_signals or signals_only and must agree with its region_policy.association_coverage. Every committed bundle declares it.


access_posture
No
Declared availability category: public, controlled, or embargoed. The one store-level fact the retired Store Family tier genuinely declared (ADR 0028); every committed bundle declares it, but it is descriptive rather than structurally required.


status
Yes
Registry lifecycle state: candidate, accepted, built, validated, superseded, or withdrawn.


trial
No
Whether this is a Trial Store Release: a deliberately small Store Release used to exercise a Source Collection, Source Format or Store Layout (issue #321). Absent means false. Only a YAML boolean is accepted. The registry’s YAML loader follows YAML 1.1, so the unquoted spellings true, yes and on (and false, no, off) are booleans; a quoted trial: "yes" is a string and trial: 1 is a number, and bundle.check() refuses both. A reader that does not gate on check() refuses them too rather than reading them as false: the Analysis Catalog’s serving policy excludes every Trial Store Release, and a coerced value would serve one.


derived_from
No
Parent store_id when this release derives from another release, and the parent must be a registered Release Bundle. A two-id Reference-Completed release names its Observed-Only parent here (ADR 0007); a Reference-Completed release without it completes its own Store (ADR 0037).


superseded_by
No
The store_id of the Store Release that replaced this one, which must be an OGS- id naming a registered Release Bundle. Required on a superseded release and refused on any other Release Status, because it names what a reader of the old identifier is sent to (issue #321, #323). It is a fact about the release, not a serving decision (ADR 0008).


created_at
Yes
Timestamp when the candidate bundle was generated.


accepted_at
No
Timestamp when the bundle was accepted as the release input record.


source_snapshot_id
Yes
Dated or provider-native source snapshot used for this release, for example a GWAS Catalog studies-table release date.


source_snapshot
No
Source snapshot identity detail. For a BESD release: besd_prefix and source_genome_build – the prefix of the file set build-ragged-besd reads and the recipe’s source-build (issue #134 records the legacy releases’ prefix as an unverified path, a known integrity gap; a release generated by the pipeline records each member’s size and sha256 in its frozen Acquisition Manifest instead, #291). For a provider-manifest release: manifest_url, manifest_sha256, manifest_size_bytes, manifest_etag, manifest_last_modified.


generator
Yes
How the bundle was produced; a mapping.


generator.version
No
Generator package version, git commit, or script hash. A value beginning sha256: must carry a valid 64-hex digest.


generator.commands
Yes
The executed command log: a non-empty list of non-empty strings, the commands that produced the bundle, in the order they ran. A log, not a prediction (issue #136).


description
Yes
Short human-readable release description.


notes
No
Free-text release notes.



bundle.check() requires exactly the keys marked Yes above and rejects a generator that is not a mapping or whose commands is empty. It holds association_coverage to its four-value vocabulary (issue #341, ADR 0040), and the descriptive facts the Analysis Catalog’s serving policy reads (ADR 0008) to a checked shape: trial must be a YAML boolean, and absent means false (a quoted trial: "yes" or a numeric trial: 1 is refused, and Bundle.trial raises rather than answer false); and superseded_by is present on exactly the superseded releases, and names a registered Release Bundle, like derived_from (issue #321). Release Status transitions are a separate, optional check (validate_status_transition): the legal lifecycle graph is candidate -> accepted -> built -> validated -> {superseded, withdrawn} with withdrawn reachable from every state. See the workflow specification’s “Status lifecycle and transitions”.
For a BESD build (build-ragged-besd), source_snapshot.besd_prefix is required and must be a non-empty string; its referenced files are deliberately not inspected, because monolithic BESD source identity is an unverified host path prefix (issue #134, a known integrity gap).
 BESD file sets (#291): identity, resolution and verification. This is the one normative definition; the connector contract and the eQTLGen section link here. A BESD file set is .besd, .epi and .esi under one prefix, and holds an Analysis per probe. Its identity is each member’s own size and sha256, recorded in the Acquisition Manifest’s members (columns), with the .besd member’s size and sha256 standing for the set in the single-file bytes and sha256 columns; no composite checksum exists. The resolver manifest declares each Analysis with source_reader_capability opengwasdb.besd, source_file the file set’s prefix (no .besd, .epi or .esi) and a source_probe_id column naming its .epi probe. The column is required for a BESD row and refused for any other, and is blank everywhere else. checksum and size_bytes are the .besd member’s. Preflight holds every member the Acquisition Manifest records to its recorded size and names a missing or resized one. Because the prefix is not a file, a Resolution Record binds fingerprints.source_member_files (each member’s bytes and mtime_ns) and resolution_config.source_probe_id instead of a source file’s size and mtime, and Manifest Generation holds them against the files as they are when it verifies a record and when it preflights the frozen inventory. The resolver’s index.json also gains source_measurements: one entry per file set measured in that invocation (measurement_id, source_file, source_genome_build, the analyses that share it, and an error when the set could not be read), each measured once and shared by its probes’ records (diagnostics.ancestry_measurement_id). It is absent when every record resumed. The release’s source_snapshot.besd_prefix and source_genome_build are rendered from the resolver manifest’s prefix and the recipe’s source-build; the pipeline’s reader for build-ragged-besd is opengwasdb.besd, which the recipe cannot name because options pass to the command verbatim.

title: Release Bundle schema
text:
One row per Analysis, tab-separated. This is the membership record: the exact set of Analyses in the release. The shared interpretation-bearing core schema is owned by OpenGWASDB (ADR 0017); the registry may add registry-only columns needed to locate source files, record checksums, carry licence/publication provenance, or explain inclusion decisions. bundle.check() delegates the shared contract to the pinned opengwasdb.model.analyses module and adds registry-owned vocabularies on top.
Use empty strings for unknown optional values in TSV. Values are resolved after applying generator config defaults, even when that repeats store-level metadata.











Class
Owner
Where used
Examples




Shared core
OpenGWASDB
Release manifests and built stores. These columns carry interpretation-bearing Analysis metadata.
analysis_id, analysis_label, ontology fields, ancestry fields, effect-scale fields, sample-size fields, INFO policy fields (info_score_threshold, imputation_score_column, imputation_score_kind, imputation_score_provenance), the MAF floor (maf_threshold), Attribution Metadata (license, publication_doi, publication_pmid, consortium, first_author).


Registry-only
Store registry
Release manifests only. These columns locate source inputs, record provenance, or explain inclusion.
source_analysis_id, source_label, source_file, source_bundle_id, checksum, checksum_algorithm, size_bytes, analysis_group_id, inclusion_reason, exclude_from_build, trait_ontology_mapping_method.


Store-only
OpenGWASDB
Built stores only. These columns are produced during or after the build and therefore do not appear in accepted release manifests.
completed_against, reference-completion quality rollups, store artifact diagnostics.



Builders may ignore registry-only columns after using them to locate inputs. Store-only columns must not be required before the build has run. exclude_from_build is the exception that is enforced rather than merely ignored: the registry materialises a derived build manifest with every excluded row removed and points the builder at it, so opengwasdb never sees an excluded row at all (ADR 0025).
A bundle’s header carries these columns:
analysis_id  stored_effect_scale  sample_size_kind  sample_size_scope
sample_size  original_effect_scale  original_sd_method
ancestry_assignment_method  assigned_ancestry
The first eight are OpenGWASDB’s required set, which bundle.check() enforces through the pinned shared schema. assigned_ancestry is added by the registry and required by Manifest Generation’s rules, which also require ancestry_assignment_method, stored_effect_scale and original_sd_method (#250). bundle.check() enforces the shared required set, the retired-column list, and the ancestry vocabulary, case/control-count, and checksum rules below. The Required column in the reference table is the broader authoring convention for a complete bundle — columns marked Yes that check() does not itself demand (analysis_label, source_label, source_file, checksum, source_genome_build, license, trait_ontology_mapping_method) are what a reviewer and the pinned OpenGWASDB schema expect to see populated. Every required column must also be non-empty on every row, except that a release Store Release Build will not build and the two legacy trial releases OGS-00001 and OGS-00002 may leave required Analysis values blank (issue #134; see “Blank required values” below).
bundle.check() rejects any column named by the pinned upstream RETIRED_ANALYSIS_COLUMNS list: phenotype_id, phenotype_label, trait_id, gene_id, gene_name. The upstream schema is the single retired-column contract; the registry does not keep its own copy. It also rejects any analysis_id outside ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$, because the Analysis Catalog addresses an Analysis <store_id>:<analysis_id> and a client must be able to split that on : into its two parts (issue #319; see “Legacy analysis_id values” below). A Trait Ontology Mapping carries an ontology term and its trait label, never a gene identifier with an authority name standing in for the label: gene/target identity is annotation (analysis_label for a single-target Analysis; trait_chr/trait_bp and the target sidecar for the target itself). bundle.check() rejects a gene- or protein-shaped trait_ontology_id (Ensembl, HGNC, Entrez/NCBI Gene, UniProt) and the matching authority name in trait_ontology_label (issue #141). It checks each term of a list, so a gene identifier cannot hide behind an ontology term. The label is checked whole and never split, because a term’s own label may contain a comma (osteoarthritis, hip).
One split rule serves the contract and Manifest Generation alike (trait_ontology_id_terms): split on every comma and strip each part. A value is in canonical form only when its parts are all CURIEs and rejoining them with ", " gives the value back, so EFO:1,EFO:2, padding and empty terms are refused.
bundle.check() also rejects a trait_ontology_id term that is not a CURIE, such as a raw http:// URI (#286). OGS-00011 was accepted before this check with GWAS Catalog’s raw EFO and ORDO URIs in 2,972 rows. An accepted bundle is never rewritten, so those values are tolerated for that release by name (LEGACY_NON_CURIE_TRAIT_ONTOLOGY_RELEASES) and reported on check()’s second channel with their count. Every other bundle, buildable or not, is held to the CURIE form.






Field
Required
Description




analysis_id
Yes
Stable registry Analysis ID. Usually source-derived unless the source lacks stable IDs. It is one path segment matching ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$: the Analysis Catalog (ADR 0039) names an Analysis <store_id>:<analysis_id>, so the value must never contain :, and it is also the filename of the resolver’s per-Analysis record (issue #319).


source_analysis_id
No
Upstream analysis identifier, such as a GCST accession or OpenGWAS ID, when the Source Collection provides one.


source_label
Yes
Upstream trait or phenotype label preserved as source provenance. Registry-only; kept separate from analysis_label even when both hold the same source text.


analysis_label
Yes
Free-text, non-unique display label for the Analysis, carried into the built store. Typically the same source text as source_label; for a single-target gene-centric Analysis it is the resolved gene symbol, and for an aggregate assay it is the SomaScan SeqId, SomaLogic’s stable assay identifier (issue #141).


trait_ontology_label
No
Human-readable label of the ontology term itself that trait_ontology_id identifies, exactly as the defining ontology or controlled vocabulary names it — for example carnitine measurement (EFO:0010469) or multiple sclerosis (MONDO:0005301). It is never an identifier-authority or vocabulary label such as Ensembl, EFO, MONDO, or OBA: those name the vocabulary, not the Trait, and bundle.check() rejects an authority-name label (issue #141). Named trait_ontology_name before OpenGWASDB ADR 0034.


trait_ontology_id
No
Ontology or controlled-vocabulary identifier for the analysed Trait, when available. CURIE format, for example EFO:0001073, OBA:VT0001253 or Orphanet:101960; blank when unmapped. When the source maps the Trait to several terms, the CURIEs are joined by exactly ", " in the source’s order (MONDO:0005150, EFO:1001492), and trait_ontology_label keeps the source’s label verbatim: labels are not split per term, because a term’s own label may contain a comma (#286). Never a URI. Never a gene or protein identifier: bundle.check() rejects Ensembl, HGNC, Entrez/NCBI Gene, and UniProt identifiers, bare or authority-qualified (issue #141). Not required to be unique.


trait_ontology_mapping_method
Yes
Controlled value describing how trait_ontology_id/trait_ontology_label were resolved: source_provided, canonical_table_lookup, or unmapped. The #130 external_authority_lookup value is retired: gene/target identity is annotation, not a Trait Ontology Mapping (issue #141). Registry-only.


source_file
Yes
Source file or filtered source file consumed by the builder. Omitted in legacy monolithic BESD releases (OGS-00001 and OGS-00002), where source identity is currently recorded only as an unverified path prefix (a known integrity gap tracked in issue #134).


source_reader_capability
No
The OpenGWASDB reader that consumes source_file (for example opengwasdb.gwas-ssf). The builder reads it per row and falls back to the Build Recipe’s source-reader-capability when absent. Required on any row with a numeric info_score_threshold. opengwasdb.column-map reads the row through the bundle’s Column Map, which the Build Recipe must then bind, and which the resolver and every build command are passed as --column-map with its checksum checked at each use; see “Column Map binding” and its checksum contract.


source_bundle_id
No
Identifier for a multi-file Source Bundle when one file is insufficient.


checksum
Yes
Checksum for source_file or source bundle manifest. Omitted in legacy monolithic BESD releases (OGS-00001 and OGS-00002; known integrity gap tracked in issue #134). When both checksum and checksum_algorithm are present, bundle.check() validates the digest length for md5 (32), sha1 (40), or sha256 (64) hex; an unsupported algorithm is rejected.


checksum_algorithm
Yes
Algorithm used for checksum, for example sha256.


size_bytes
No
File size in bytes.


source_genome_build
Yes
Genome build of source coordinates for this Analysis.


license
Yes
Licence or usage terms after applying source defaults and row overrides. Attribution Metadata: carried into the built store, since a store that cannot be legally used or cited has failed self-containment even when its statistics are perfectly interpretable.


publication_doi
No
DOI for compact bibliographic provenance.


publication_pmid
No
PMID for compact bibliographic provenance.


consortium
No
Consortium or provider label when DOI/PMID is not enough for provenance.


first_author
No
First author for compact bibliographic/attribution provenance.


source_ancestry_label
No
Upstream ancestry/population label, preserved as provenance.


assigned_ancestry
Yes
Registry-normalised ancestry used for store inclusion and routing, from the ancestry mixture’s super-population vocabulary (AFR, AMR, EAS, EUR, MID, NAF, SAS). Empty means unassigned. A free-text Source Ancestry Label such as European is not valid here; source_ancestry_label preserves that provenance separately. bundle.check() rejects any other value.


ancestry_assignment_method
Yes
Controlled value: af_assigned, source_fallback, source_trusted_no_af, or unassigned.


original_effect_scale
Yes
Controlled value for upstream effect units, such as sd, cm, logOR, or another approved vocabulary item.


original_sd
No
Source-provided or estimated phenotype SD on the original scale. Empty for binary traits or unavailable values.


original_sd_method
Yes
Controlled value describing original_sd: declared_standardised, source_provided, estimated_from_source_maf, estimated_from_reference_maf, estimated_from_beta_distribution, binary_trait, or unavailable.


stored_effect_scale
Yes
Controlled value for the effect scale stored by OpenGWASDB for this Analysis: sd, log_or, or log_hazard.


sample_size_kind
Yes
total, case_control, effective, or variant_level. Accepted build rows must not use unknown.


sample_size_scope
Yes
analysis_level or variant_level. Use variant_level when N differs per SNP in the source file.


sample_size
Yes
Scalar study N for this Analysis. When source N differs per SNP, use the study’s maximum N.


n_cases
No
Case count for binary traits, or event count for time-to-event traits. Required when the Analysis’s method tier declares sample_size_kind = case_control; blank (not 0) when sample_size_kind is not case_control. The effect scale does not decide this: ukb-b’s binary traits are on the SD scale and still carry their counts (#289).


n_controls
No
Control count for binary traits, or non-event/comparison count for time-to-event traits when reported by the source. Same absence rule as n_cases.


analysis_group_id
No
Grouping key for analyses sharing a publication, analyte panel, phenotype batch, or source bundle.


inclusion_reason
No
