Short reason this Analysis was selected.


info_score_threshold
No
Optional per-Analysis requested imputation INFO/R² floor in [0,1]. A numeric value (including 0) is emitted only alongside the complete declaration triple below and only on resolver evidence: the record reports info_score_state disabled (explicit zero) or filtered (positive floor), info_rows_usable > 0, and a fingerprint that still binds the declaration. Literal NaN means unavailable – no approved declaration, a legacy record without the diagnostics, or unusable evidence. A source MAF/EAF or a lookalike INFO header is not evidence of imputation quality. This value alone does not imply any variants were filtered. Manifest Generation’s rules reject a numeric threshold without the complete triple. Omission remains valid for older bundles.


imputation_score_column
No
Exact, case-sensitive source column name the declaration cites as the imputation score. Emitted only with a numeric info_score_threshold and the other two triple columns; empty otherwise.


imputation_score_kind
No
imputation_info or imputation_r2. Manifest Generation’s rules reject any other non-empty value.


imputation_score_provenance
No
Independent provider semantic evidence (for example a provider data dictionary) for the declared column. A header guess, the column name itself, or MAF/EAF is not provenance.


maf_threshold
No
Optional per-Analysis MAF floor in [0, 0.5]; 0 disables filtering and literal NaN means no MAF filter. A numeric value is emitted only on resolver evidence: the record reports a usable maf_state (disabled for an explicit zero, filtered for a positive floor) and the per-Analysis fingerprint still binds the same value. Every other Analysis – no configured default, a MAF-exempt genotyping technology, a legacy record without the diagnostics, or a changed fingerprint – emits literal NaN. The frequency is the reader’s af_alt (GWAS-SSF effect_allele_frequency); MAF = min(af, 1 - af). A row whose af is missing, non-finite or outside [0, 1] is retained, not dropped. Manifest Generation’s rules reject any non-NaN value outside [0, 0.5]. This value alone does not imply any variants were filtered. Omission remains valid for older bundles.


exclude_from_build
No
true only for rows retained for audit but intentionally skipped by the build. The registry honours it at build time: it materialises a derived build manifest (<artifact-root>/<store-id>/work/analyses.tsv) with every true row removed and points the builder at that, so opengwasdb never sees an excluded row. The row itself stays in the committed bundle, with its inclusion_reason, as the audit record of why the Analysis is absent. See ADR 0025.


ancestry_prop_*
No
Optional family of columns for estimated reference ancestry proportions.



The four INFO columns are one policy: info_score_threshold is the requested floor and imputation_score_column/imputation_score_kind/ imputation_score_provenance are the exact source-column declaration it requires. Manifest Generation’s rules reject a numeric threshold without the complete triple and a triple without a numeric threshold, on every row; the pinned shared schema bundle.check() runs also checks the rows that will be built. A declared column is only meaningful to the GWAS-SSF reader, and the pinned OpenGWASDB validator reads the reader from the row, not from the Build Recipe’s source-reader-capability default. A row with a numeric threshold must therefore also carry source_reader_capability = opengwasdb.gwas-ssf. The Phase B candidate generator writes that column on every row.
For the Phase B GWAS Catalog EUR Hybrid candidate generator, a separate optional release_policy.imputation_score_declarations TSV supplies explicit, independently sourced per-Analysis score semantics to the resolver input. Its exact headers are analysis_id, imputation_score_column, imputation_score_kind, imputation_score_provenance; kinds are imputation_info or imputation_r2. The resolver input also carries the requested info_score_threshold, or literal NaN when unmapped. Finalisation copies the requested floor and the exact triple into the candidate analyses.tsv only for an Analysis whose resolver record carries the post-INFO state and at least one usable score (see the family README for the emission rule); every other Analysis emits literal NaN and empty triple cells. A declared Analysis with no usable score is retained: core no longer reports it as a controlled failure, the registry does not refuse it, and it is included with literal NaN INFO cells. Older bundles may omit all four columns entirely.
The MAF floor is a defaults.maf_threshold release decision applied per Analysis: an Analysis is exempt (and emits NaN) when its Source Metadata Table row’s genotyping_technology (;-joined, source order) is non-empty and every technology is in release_policy.maf_filter_exempt_genotyping_technologies; missing technology metadata is never an exemption. The column is a fact a source’s adapter writes (the GWAS Catalog’s from each -meta.yaml); the exemption is the release policy over it (#347). The resolver manifest carries the derived maf_threshold per Analysis and the resolver record’s maf_state plus its fingerprint binding decide the emitted candidate value, exactly as for INFO. Manifest Generation’s rules validate the column on every row, independently of the pinned OpenGWASDB Analysis schema.
A separate optional store_composition.require_maf_filtered generator-config rule decides whether a shared Store may admit an Analysis with no applied MAF floor. Absent or false, every otherwise admissible Analysis is included; true requires a positive defaults.maf_threshold and excludes an otherwise admissible Analysis whose emitted maf_threshold is NaN as not_maf_filtered (see the exclusions sidecar). The rule runs after every other membership decision and only at emit, so toggling it needs --stage emit and never a re-resolve. See ADR 0033.
A release whose Analyses each measure one molecular target – proteomics, such as Sun 2018’s SomaScan pQTLs – adds the target columns trait_chr, trait_bp, mhc, target_resolution_method and n_target_rows, rendered from the Source Metadata Table’s target annotation (#300; the retired R gwas-ssf-ragged generator also wrote n). A release with no such target (for example small-molecule metabolomics, issue #26) omits these columns entirely rather than filling them with placeholder or NA values — their absence is how a reviewer tells the two shapes apart. tissue and context likewise appear only in a release that declares them. These columns remain release-specific with no shared-core equivalent.
The target sidecar, sidecars/analysis_targets.tsv, lists each targeted Analysis’s target annotation (assay, gene symbol and Ensembl id, span, MHC flag, whether the assay is an aggregate, how the target was resolved); it is evidence, not duplicate Analysis columns. Bundles emitted by the R generator carry its wider form, with the raw SomaScan and Ensembl fields.



Accepted build rows must have usable sample-size metadata. Analyses with unknown sample size may appear in Source Inventories, candidate diagnostics, or review sidecars, but should not be included as buildable rows in an accepted analyses.tsv.
Case/control-style counts follow sample_size_kind, not the effect scale: an Analysis whose tier declares sample_size_kind = case_control carries n_cases and n_controls, and one whose tier declares any other kind leaves both blank. ukb-b is why the two are separate – its provider reports units: SD for binary traits too, so its case-control tier declares stored_effect_scale: sd beside sample_size_kind: case_control (#289). Most Sources pair them (log_or with case_control), which is why the scale looks like the deciding field. For time-to-event traits, n_cases is the event count and n_controls is the non-event or comparison count reported by the source. When the counts do not apply both must be blank rather than 0: zero is a real count, and writing it where the counts do not apply is exactly the absence-vs-zero confusion CONTRIBUTING.md rules out. bundle.check() rejects a non-empty count on a non-case-control Analysis (issue #133).
assigned_ancestry is one controlled vocabulary on every Analysis, regardless of ancestry_assignment_method: the ancestry-mixture reference’s super-population codes (AFR, AMR, EAS, EUR, MID, NAF, SAS) or empty for unassigned. It is never a free-text Source Ancestry Label (European, East Asian, and so on). The tracked translation from the candidates table’s free-text labels to these codes is resources/reference-resources/ukb-ancestry-mixture-hg38/source_label_map.tsv, read by both the Ancestry Assignment stage and the manifest generators so the two cannot drift apart. bundle.check() rejects any value outside the vocabulary, so the split cannot silently reappear.



bundle.check() normally fails a row that leaves a required column blank. Two deliberate exemptions exist, both narrow:

Releases Store Release Build will not build. A release whose status is not accepted, built or validated (#247) may leave values blank: a candidate is still being resolved, and what it must resolve before it lands is Manifest Generation’s policy, not the contract’s (#250). check() discloses the count as a tolerated gap cited not buildable.
Legacy monolithic BESD releases. OGS-00001 and OGS-00002 are exempt because their required Analytical Metadata is unpopulated in upstream BESD sources and cannot be resolved without external study metadata. The exemption is scoped to exactly those two named releases. Any new release — including any future ragged-BESD or completed release — must provide valid required values or fail bundle.check().

This is a known integrity gap, tracked by open issue #134, not an equivalent alternative to the per-Analysis checksums and source identity enforced for other formats.



bundle.check() fails a row whose analysis_id is not one path segment, and names the row. OGS-00001 and OGS-00002 are exempt: they carry eQTLGen’s <probe>::<tissue> ids (ENSG00000175445::whole_blood), which an accepted bundle may not be edited to remove (ADR 0004), so check() discloses the count as a tolerated gap cited #319 instead of reporting it as an error. The exemption is scoped to exactly those two named releases. Every other release — including any future eQTLGen or other ragged-BESD build, which names its Analyses by bare probe id and records the tissue in the tissue column — must satisfy the pattern. Retire the guard in favour of opengwasdb.model.analyses.validate_analyses() if OpenGWASDB ever validates the column (ADR 0017).

title: Release Bundle schema
text:
The Build Recipe describes how the accepted manifest becomes an OpenGWASDB store. It is the only input to plan(), and every value in it is either a registry fact or an opengwasdb flag. It does not record where artifacts land (issue #126).








Field
Required
Description




store_id
Yes
Must equal the bundle’s store_id and its directory name.


layout
Yes
dense, ragged, or hybrid.


completion_state
Yes
observed_only or reference_completed.


build
Yes for observed_only, and for reference_completed without derived_from
The observed-only build block. A single-id Reference-Completed release builds and publishes its Observed-Only Store with it first (ADR 0037).


complete
Yes for reference_completed
The completion block.


build.command / complete.command
Yes
An opengwasdb CLI subcommand; never a Python import path. Supported values are keyed by phase in plan.COMMANDS: build-dense-vcf, build-hybrid, build-ragged-ssf, build-ragged-besd; complete-dense, complete-hybrid, complete-ragged.


build.options / complete.options
No
opengwasdb flag names passed through verbatim; see “The passthrough rule”.


post
Yes
Post-processing choices: top_hits, rho, overview, validate. rho defaults off and validate defaults on (plan.POST_DEFAULTS); a recipe states only what it chooses differently. top_hits and overview are always explicit because they vary per release.


indexed_subsets
No
Optional named Indexed Variant Subset declarations (stores #209, epic #214). A list of {name, resource_id, variant_list, reference_assembly, checksum?, options?}. Dense and Hybrid only; a Ragged release rejects any declaration. Every declaration adds one build-indexed-subset Step before overview and validate. See “Indexed Variant Subset declarations”.


column_map
When an Analysis reads through opengwasdb.column-map
The Column Map binding {name, sha256, file} (#292), with no file for a built-in map. Required exactly when an analyses.tsv row names opengwasdb.column-map, or leaves its reader blank under a recipe source-reader-capability of opengwasdb.column-map. See “Column Map binding”.



A Build Recipe must not declare an artifacts block: bundle.check() rejects it, because the artifact root is deployment configuration (issue #126). It must also not declare the superseded family-first layout: the top-level store_family_id, family_release_id, and store_layout keys, or the nested builder, source, normalisation, effects, and shape blocks. Those are read by no code. Builder inputs that remain real flags go in options (for example source-reader-capability, source-assembly). Reference Resources, effect-scale validation, ancestry assignment, and QC-panel configuration are Manifest Generator configuration, not Build Recipe fields; see “Manifest Generator configuration” below.
store_id: OGS-00042
layout: dense
completion_state: observed_only
build:
  command: build-dense-vcf
  options:
    source-reader-capability: opengwasdb.finngen-r13
    source-assembly: hg38
    n-workers: 8
post:
  top_hits: true
  overview: true
A Reference-Completed release completes its own Store under its id (ADR 0037). It declares both blocks and has no derived_from: the build block builds and publishes the Observed-Only Store, exactly as the same file would as observed_only, and the complete block then completes that published Store and replaces it. The completion’s source is the id’s own Store path, so the recipe names no Store path at all. Dense, Hybrid and Ragged releases are all planned this way. A Ragged release’s complete options must name its ld-panel and ancestry, which the Observed-View Check is given too.
store_id: OGS-00043
layout: dense
completion_state: reference_completed
build:
  command: build-dense-vcf
  options:
    source-reader-capability: opengwasdb.finngen-r13
    source-assembly: hg38
complete:
  command: complete-dense
  options:
    ld-panel: /data/opengwasdb/reference/ld/hgdp1kgp-hg38
    ancestry: EUR
    n-workers: 16
post:
  top_hits: true
  overview: true
post applies to both phases. complete-dense builds the Top-Hit Index inline, so the completion phase plans no separate top_hits step.
Manifest Generation emits that file from the release config’s completion block (release config, #340):

a reference that is qualified and active gives one bundle under the Store’s id, with completion_state: reference_completed, the build block byte-identical to the one the same config emits as observed_only, and the complete block whose ld-panel and ancestry are its Reference Resource’s declaration;
a reference that is pending, on hold or blocked gives exactly the Observed-Only bundle a config with no completion block emits, so a bundle never declares a completion phase that the config has not qualified and activated. release.yaml’s notes say the recipe is blocked, and the candidate’s Validation Record records the reference, with blocked: true, under acceptance.completion_reference (see validation.yaml below).

Only an emitted candidate declares this; a Store published before its bundle declared completion gains the complete block through the one amendment an accepted bundle allows (#305), not through a re-emit.
A two-id Reference-Completed release, from before ADR 0037, is the same file with a complete block instead of build. It carries no parent path: the parent is release.yaml’s derived_from, and its artifact path is a pure function of that ID. Existing two-id bundles (OGS-00002, OGS-00022, OGS-00023) stay valid.
store_id: OGS-00043
layout: dense
completion_state: reference_completed
complete:
  command: complete-dense
  options:
    ld-panel: /data/opengwasdb/reference/ld/hgdp1kgp-hg38
    ancestry: EUR
    n-workers: 16
post:
  top_hits: true
  overview: true


A Dense or Hybrid Build Recipe may declare optional named Indexed Variant Subsets (stores #209). Each declaration becomes one opengwasdb build-indexed-subset Step, planned after the Store and its inline top-hit/rho steps exist and before overview and validate, so overview reports the subset and validation audits it. The Step’s durable records/indexed-subset-<name>.json is written by the ordinary step executor; no new record schema is introduced.








Field
Required
Description




name
Yes
The subset identity. The consumer’s grammar [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}, and the registry additionally refuses .. because the name becomes part of the record filename. Unique within the release.


resource_id
Yes
resource_id of a maintained kind: variant_list Reference Resource (resources/reference-resources/<id>/resource.yaml).


variant_list
Yes
The concrete canonical-ALID list path the build passes as --variant-list. It must match the resource declaration’s location. Recorded so the immutable bundle is self-contained; plan() never opens it.


reference_assembly
Yes
The list’s assembly, passed as --reference-assembly. It must match the resource declaration’s genome_build.


checksum
No
The maintained list’s sha256 as 64 hex characters. When present it must equal the resource declaration’s checksums.alid_sha256.


options
No
build-indexed-subset flags passed through verbatim (plan.render_options), so the same declared policy reaches both phases’ subset steps. overwrite is refused, and so is any key that normalises (strip().lstrip('-')) to variant-list or reference-assembly: those are the declaration’s own verified inputs, and re-specifying one in options would let the executed CLI use a value the runtime did not hash or check. A value must render as CLI tokens – a string, number or bool, or a non-empty list of them; a mapping would arrive as its own repr and null or an empty list as nothing at all, so both are refused.



The key is optional; omit it to declare no subsets. An explicit indexed_subsets: null is malformed rather than treated as omitted, so a generator cannot silently drop a declaration.
indexed_subsets:
  - name: hm3
    resource_id: hapmap3-hg38
    variant_list: /data/opengwasdb/reference/hapmap3-hg38/hm3.grch38.alid.txt
    reference_assembly: GRCh38
    checksum: 4a7c82aa625a006ff437dcaa2769b00e056413d54c72e98f7378327c69513398
    options:
      overflow-only: skip
That last declaration is OGS-00011’s (stores #225). A requested ALID that only a Hybrid release’s shared axis carries cannot be indexed in its Dense Component, and --overflow-only skip leaves such an ALID out and records how many the subset skipped (opengwas/opengwasdb#324, and that repository’s ADR 0065). The planner does not interpret the flag: it renders the mapping into the two build-indexed-subset steps, build phase and completion phase alike, exactly as declared.
bundle.check() validates the declaration shape (names, required strings, checksum syntax, uniqueness, Dense/Hybrid only, no overwrite, and options values that render as CLI tokens) without any resource I/O. Whether the resource_id resolves, whether the list matches the maintained checksum, and whether the runtime provides build-indexed-subset are run-time facts the release entry point verifies before a build; the tracked opengwasdb pin provides the capability since stores#218, so the entry point needs no PATH overlay. See ADR 0034 and the workflow specification’s “Indexed Variant Subsets”.



A tabular Source Collection read through OpenGWASDB’s generic tabular reader has a Column Map: a TOML file declaring which provider column supplies each field and the collection’s conventions (opengwasdb ADR 0063). ADR 0036 has it travel in the Release Bundle, checksummed, so Analysis Resolution and Store Release Build read every file the same way (#292).
An Analysis reads through a Column Map when its source_reader_capability is opengwasdb.column-map. A row that leaves source_reader_capability blank, or has no such column, inherits the Build Recipe’s build/complete options.source-reader-capability. Both values are compared with surrounding whitespace stripped. A bundle with at least one such Analysis is mapped. A recipe default of opengwasdb.column-map does not map a bundle whose every row names its own reader. A mapped bundle’s Build Recipe binds exactly one map, since files that need different maps belong to different Source Collections:
column_map:
  name: dbgap-phs002453-mvp-gia
  sha256: 3f0c...e9a1   # 64 lower-case hex characters
  file: dbgap-phs002453-mvp-gia.toml








Field
Required
Description




name
Yes
The map’s own name, as its TOML declares it. Any non-empty string, as OpenGWASDB accepts.


sha256
Yes
The sha256 of the map file’s bytes, as 64 lower-case hex characters.


file
Yes, except for a built-in
The file the bundle carries the map in, under column_maps/. A file name, not a path: the Indexed Variant Subset grammar [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127} with no .., ending .toml.



name and sha256 are the fingerprint OpenGWASDB records in a mapped Resolution Record (resolution_config.column_map) and in a mapped Store’s manifest.json (provenance.column_map). The three can therefore be compared field for field. file is kept apart from name so that a map’s name never has to be a safe file name.
Built-in maps. OpenGWASDB ships two maps, gwas-ssf and finngen-r13. A binding with no file names one of them, and the bundle carries nothing for it, because the pinned OpenGWASDB package holds the bytes. Its sha256 records the built-in’s checksum as the Resolution Records report it. A binding with no file and any other name is refused. A carried copy of a built-in, bound with a file, is an ordinary carried map. A bundle whose rows use the dedicated readers opengwasdb.gwas-ssf or opengwasdb.finngen-r13 is not mapped and needs neither a binding nor a file. That covers every bundle registered before #292.
bundle.check() (_check_column_map) refuses, reporting every one it finds in one pass:

a mapped bundle whose Build Recipe binds no column_map;
a binding in a bundle that is not mapped: a map no Analysis reads through;
a bound file the bundle does not carry at column_maps/<file>, or one that is a symbolic link or not a regular file;
a carried map whose bytes do not hash to the bound sha256;
any other entry in column_maps/: a carried map that is not bound;
a column_maps that is a symbolic link or not a directory;
a malformed binding: not a mapping, null (omit the key to bind none), an unknown key, an empty name, a sha256 that is not 64 lower-case hex characters, a file outside the grammar, or no file with a name that is not a built-in;
column-map in build.options, complete.options or a variant_reference block’s options. The flag is composed from the checksummed binding, never passed through around it.

The contract checks a carried map shallowly. It must be UTF-8 TOML with a column_map_version and a name equal to the binding’s. Its full validation, covering fields, conventions and refusals, belongs to OpenGWASDB, which applies it at Analysis Resolution and at every build that reads through the map. The contract does not copy those rules.
A built-in binding’s sha256 must be that of the map file the pinned OpenGWASDB ships: bundle.check() takes the built-in names, and each file’s checksum, from opengwasdb.readers.column_map and refuses any other value, naming both.
The checksum contract. The binding’s name and sha256 are one value everywhere the map is used, and each use is checked against it:

Manifest Generation passes the resolver --column-map (a built-in’s name, or the release config’s column_map.path). Every mapped Resolution Record’s resolution_config.column_map must equal the binding, and the map’s checksum is part of the resolver’s settings digest and of the receipt’s resolution contract, so a changed map makes its Resolution Records stale: the resolver re-resolves them, and verify refuses records made under another map. The emitter writes the binding and copies a non-built-in map to column_maps/<file>.
Store Release Build passes --column-map to every build command that reads source files through it: build-dense-vcf, build-hybrid and the variant-reference pre-stage. A completion reads a Store and takes none; a command that takes no map (build-ragged-ssf) is refused for a bundle that binds one. A built-in goes by name. A carried map goes as a copy staged at <artifact root>/<store id>/work/column_maps/<file>, as the derived build manifest is, so the planned argv is the same from any checkout.
Before any build the release entry point, and the Snakefile’s onstart and column_map rule, re-hash column_maps/<file> against the binding and refuse a mismatch, naming the map. The staging rule re-hashes again as it copies. Snakemake treats an existing staged copy as up to date, so each step that lists it as an input checks the staged bytes against the binding immediately before it runs (resources.verify_staged_column_map), and a retried build whose staged copy changed is refused naming the map.
plan() is a pure function (ADR 0031): it reads only the binding’s recorded fields. That a built-in’s sha256 is the pinned package’s is check()’s to say.

assign-ancestry and estimate-phenotype-sd take no map yet (opengwasdb ADR 0063, opengwas/opengwasdb#285).



options keys are opengwasdb flag names. plan() renders key: value as --key value, booleans as bare flags (--key for true, --no-key for false), lists by repeating the flag, and never interprets a key. The registry does not know what --min-cor means and must not acquire a copy of opengwasdb’s parameter schema (ADR 0023).
An unrecognised or invalid flag fails in the CLI argument parser in milliseconds, before any expensive work. plan() composes only the arguments that are the registry’s own facts — store identity, the declared association_coverage for a Ragged build, the derived build manifest path, and artifact paths. Everything else comes from options.
A flag the registry composes is refused in options, because a recipe’s copy would be a second declaration: plan() refuses a build.options key that renders --association-coverage on a Ragged build, since release.yaml declares that value (ADR 0040) and a recipe change would be a new Store Release (ADR 0004).



Post-steps are conditional on post and on the selected command’s Store-format support. plan() raises rather than planning a step the subcommand cannot support:








Step
Supported by
Notes




top_hits
build-dense-vcf, build-ragged-ssf; built inline by build-hybrid, build-ragged-besd, and every complete-*
Ragged and Hybrid releases often declare top_hits: false.


rho
Dense only (via complete-dense or build-dense-vcf)
Defaults off.


overview
Dense and Hybrid (regenerate-overview)
Ragged’s closed Store envelope excludes overview.html, so Ragged releases declare overview: false.


validate
Every release
Defaults on.

title: Release Bundle schema
text:
Release-level acceptance and build validation summary. This table is the one definition of the format; the workflow specification explains how register produces it rather than restating the fields. A measurement the build did not report is written as null — absence is recorded, never guessed or defaulted (issue #135).
Two writers produce this file at different times: - A Manifest Generator writes a candidate bundle’s record (Phase B): its acceptance checks, sidecar reports and warnings. - register writes the record of a built release (issue #119).
register replaces the candidate’s record; it does not merge with it. Its status, checks, warnings and errors hold only that run’s findings: the opengwasdb validate --format json verdict as checks.store, with that run’s warnings and errors exactly as validate printed them. None of them carries anything from the record being replaced (#195).
The candidate’s Phase B acceptance evidence is kept in its own labelled acceptance block, apart from those findings, and nothing in it feeds them (#195). register fills the block in one of three ways: - From a candidate record (one whose validator.name is not opengwasdb validate): every block it holds, verbatim – its checks, warnings and reports, and whatever evidence its generator records, such as reference_overlap (OGS-00011), store_composition (#203) or a dbGaP candidate’s own acceptance – except the fields that describe the generator’s run rather than the bundle: status, validated_at, validator, build_environment, observed and errors. The block is dated by the candidate’s own validated_at and tied to the commit that record came from. A candidate block named recorded_at or commit is refused, since it would overwrite that dating. - From a register-written record: its acceptance block is passed on verbatim, because the accepted bundle it describes is immutable. - Not at all, from a record #135 migrated (OGS-00001..7). Those records mix Phase B evidence with an earlier build’s findings, so nothing is extracted from them; git keeps them.
register names no generator’s evidence, so a generator that records a new kind is carried without changing register (#250).
A built or validated release must carry a validation.yaml whose status is one of not_run, passed, passed_with_warnings, or failed; bundle.check() rejects any other value. A validated release needs passed or passed_with_warnings: a passing opengwasdb validate is what makes a release validated, and its warnings are kept in the record (#195; see the workflow specification’s “The Release Status a Validation Record gives”). A candidate, accepted, superseded, or withdrawn release needs none.



Field
Required
Description




status
Yes
not_run, passed, failed, or passed_with_warnings. The release-level verdict.


validated_at
No
Timestamp of the latest validation run.


validator.name
No
The validator that produced the verdict. register writes opengwasdb validate; a deleted generator adapter is never named (issue #135).


validator.version
No
Validator version, git commit, or script hash. register writes opengwasdb@<commit>.


build_environment.opengwasdb_version
No
opengwasdb package version the record was produced against.


build_environment.opengwasdb_commit
No
opengwasdb revision the record was produced against.


build_environment.python_version
No
Python version of the registering environment.


build_environment.platform
No
Platform string of the registering environment.


observed.format_version
Yes
OpenGWASDB store format version the build reported, or null when it was not recorded. register never assumes one. Until #195 it defaulted to "1.0", which is why OGS-00001..3 record "1.0" for Stores whose manifests say 0.1.0.


observed.n_analyses
Yes
Analysis count the build reported, or null when it was not recorded.


observed.n_variants
Yes
Variant count the build reported, or null when it was not recorded.


observed.n_associations
Yes
The association count the producing step (build or complete) reported, or null when it was not recorded. It is the Store’s observed association count, never a value register derives: until #322 a Dense build that reported none recorded n_variants × n_analyses, which counts matrix cells and overstates a Store with empty cells.


observed.association_coverage
No
The Association Coverage the producing step reported, or null when it did not: evidence about the build, not the fact the Analysis Catalog serves, which is release.yaml:association_coverage (issue #341). The value is what opengwasdb reports, in the same four-value vocabulary as this repository (gwas, cis, cis_and_signals, signals_only); a legacy full in a Store built before opengwas/opengwasdb#298 reads as gwas. register records it as reported, checks no vocabulary of its own, and refuses a report that differs from the release’s declaration, naming both values (#341): the builder was given the declared value, so a Store at another coverage is not the Store the bundle describes. Read from the step’s stdout JSON, never from the Store’s manifest.json (ADR 0023, #322). A present value that is not a non-empty string is refused, not recorded as null. register writes the key on every publication from #322 on; records written before it do not carry it and are not migrated.


observed.reference_assembly
No
The reference assembly the producing step reported, or null when it did not, such as GRCh37 or GRCh38. Read from the step’s stdout JSON, never from the Store’s manifest.json (ADR 0023, #322). A present value that is not a non-empty string is refused, not recorded as null. register writes the key on every publication from #322 on; records written before it do not carry it and are not migrated.


observed.store_bytes
Yes
Store size in bytes the build reported, or null when it was not recorded.


observed.build_elapsed_s
Yes
Summed step elapsed seconds, or null when it was not recorded. For a release that completes its own Store it is the steps of both phases (ADR 0037).


observed.validate_status
Yes
The validate verdict the release-level status is derived from.


observed.completion_state
No
The completion state of the Store this publication published (#307, ADR 0037): observed_only for a build phase, which for a release that completes its own Store is the Observed-Only Store users can query while completion runs, and reference_completed for a completion phase or a two-id child. It follows the phase published, never build.yaml’s declaration, and is read from the plan and the bundle rather than from the Store (ADR 0023). Absent in records written before #307; the master list then reports the bundle’s declared state, which for an Observed-Only Store and for a two-id child is the state that record’s Store was published in.


observed.variant_reference
No
Variant-reference provenance (issue #148): provided when the artifact already existed (a skipped variant-reference pre-stage, or a build option naming an existing panel with no declared pre-stage, as OGS-00004/OGS-00005 do), extracted when the workflow ran extract-variant-reference, and absent when the release uses no variant reference.


observed.rsid_conflicts
No
What a Hybrid build’s rsid harvest compared across its sources (issue #225, opengwas/opengwasdb#306): policy, the on-rsid-conflict policy it built under (refuse or drop); n_keys, how many routing keys its sources named differently; and n_variants, how many stored variants that left with no rsid under drop. The counts are 0 when the harvest disputed nothing and null when it compared no names across sources (--reference-panel, or a reference that names its own rsids), so absence is never recorded as zero. A release that completes its own Store carries them from its build phase, whose builder reports them and whose complete-hybrid reports none (issue #225, ADR 0037). Absent when no build record carries the block, as one from a runtime without the policy does. The build’s sample of disputed keys is not a measurement and stays in its step record (records/build.json).


checks.store
Yes, register record
This run’s opengwasdb validate --format json verdict: failed when ok is false, passed_with_warnings when it reported a warning, passed otherwise, and not_run when the plan has no validate step. The only check a register-written record carries (#195).


checks.schema
Yes, Phase B record
Whether required files and fields conform to OpenGWASDB’s shared core schema and this registry’s release-bundle requirements. Written by a Manifest Generator; not carried into a registered record.


checks.files
Yes, Phase B record
Whether referenced source or filtered files exist and match checksums. Written by a Manifest Generator; not carried into a registered record.


checks.reader_smoke_test
No
Whether OpenGWASDB can read a small sample from each source file or bundle.


checks.ancestry
No
not_run when the release has not opted into ancestry_assignment (or opted in but every Analysis was skipped for lacking usable source AF). Otherwise reflects the AF-based ancestry sidecar evidence: passed when every attempted Analysis cleared its gates with no source/assigned mismatch, passed_with_warnings when at least one attempted Analysis failed a gate or disagreed with its source-declared ancestry, and never a bare passed implying validation ran when it did not.


checks.effect_scale
No
not_run when the release has not opted into effect_scale_validation, or when it has opted in but reflects only controlled-vocabulary validity. Once a release opts in, this must reflect the empirical reference-AF/source-AF SD-estimation sidecar outcome across attempted Analyses (passed, passed_with_warnings, or failed), not merely that declared vocabulary values are valid.


checks.sd_estimation
No
not_run when SD-estimation was not attempted. Otherwise passed only when the sidecar is internally consistent (every attempted, warned, or failed Analysis has a matching sidecar row with required fields populated) and no attempted Analysis has status failed; passed_with_warnings when at least one Analysis has status warning, or skipped for a reason that should be reviewed (for example no_reference_resource_for_ancestry); failed otherwise.


checks.sparse_regions
No
Whether ragged region sidecars match filtered files.


store_composition
No
The candidate’s Store composition rule evidence (Phase B record, #203; ADR 0033).


store_composition.require_maf_filtered
No
Whether the rule ran: true when the generator config set store_composition.require_maf_filtered, false otherwise.


store_composition.maf_floor
No
The configured defaults.maf_threshold as a string, or null when none was configured.


store_composition.unfiltered_included
No
Number of included Analyses with no applied MAF floor.


store_composition.unfiltered_included_off_reference_rows
No
Sum of those Analyses’ build-eligible rows off the variant reference, or null when no variant-reference is declared or any counted Analysis lacks the resolver count.


store_composition.unfiltered_routed
No
Number of Analyses excluded as not_maf_filtered.


store_composition.unfiltered_routed_off_reference_rows
No
The same off-reference sum for the routed Analyses, or null under the same absence rule.


trait_ontology_mapping
No
The Trait Ontology Mapping step’s evidence (Manifest Generation record, #286).


trait_ontology_mapping.canonical_trait_mapping_table
No
The Canonical Trait Mapping Table the run read: resource_id, version (from its resource.yaml), location, sha256 of the table file, and rows.


trait_ontology_mapping.method_counts
No
Analyses per trait_ontology_mapping_method: source_provided, canonical_table_lookup, unmapped.


trait_ontology_mapping.source_id_without_label
No
How many source_provided mappings carry a source term with no label. They are kept; the count is for review.


trait_ontology_mapping.rejected_source_terms
No
Each source term the #141 guards rejected: analysis_id, source_trait_ontology_id, source_trait_ontology_label and reason. Empty when none was rejected.


quality_checks
No
The candidate’s Quality Check summary (Manifest Generation record, #285; ADR 0036): one entry per check, keyed by its name. Per-Analysis results are in the Quality Check sidecar.


quality_checks.<check>.kind
No
exclusion or warning, as the check declares it.


quality_checks.<check>.stage
No
The precedence slot where a failed exclusion takes effect: resolved, ancestry_read, selection or target_ancestry (see the sidecar).


quality_checks.<check>.measures
No
What the check reads, in words; it names a reviewed listing where OpenGWASDB does not measure the value yet.


quality_checks.<check>.threshold
No
The threshold this release applied, or null for a check that tests a status.


quality_checks.<check>.default_threshold
No
The shared default, or null.


quality_checks.<check>.overridden
No
true when the generator config’s quality_checks block overrode the default.


quality_checks.<check>.results
No
How many Analyses had each result: passed, failed, not_applicable, unmeasured, invalid, warning.


quality_checks.<check>.excluded
No
For an exclusion: how many Analyses it excluded. An Analysis that failed it after an earlier rule excluded it is counted under results.failed only.


quality_checks.<check>.warned
No
For a warning: how many included Analyses failed it. Each warning check that warned also adds one line to warnings. For an exclusion that may warn (assigned_ancestry, #287): how many included Analyses had a warning result.


reports
No
URIs or paths to detailed reports. A Phase B record points at its sidecars; register writes no top-level reports (#195).


warnings
No
List of non-blocking warnings. In a register-written record, exactly the warnings list opengwasdb validate --format json printed for this run. Reference-AF effect-scale warnings should name the Analysis and reason, for example low reference-AF overlap, an allele mismatch, unstable implied SD, a missing reference resource for the assigned ancestry, or scale inconsistency versus the declared effect scale.


errors
No
List of blocking errors. In a register-written record, exactly the errors list opengwasdb validate --format json printed for this run.


replaced.archive
No
Written when this run replaced a published release (--config force=1, #195): the replaced/<UTC>/ directory beside the Store. It holds the replaced store.opengwasdb, its records/ and a copy of its validation.yaml, and nothing deletes it. Also written when a completion phase replaced its own Observed-Only Store (ADR 0037): that Store is deleted, and the archive holds copies of its records/register.json, of the passing records/completion-observed-view-check.json and of its validation.yaml (#309).


replaced.replaced_at
No
When this run replaced it.


acceptance
No
The accepted bundle’s Phase B acceptance evidence, kept apart from this run’s findings (#195). See above for when register writes it. Absent when there is none to keep.


acceptance.recorded_at
Yes, in the block
The candidate record’s own validated_at.


acceptance.commit
Yes, in the block
The commit the candidate record came from, or null when the file was untracked or modified since its last commit, so no commit describes it.


acceptance.<block>
No
Every other block of the candidate record, verbatim, except status, validated_at, validator, build_environment, observed and errors: its checks, warnings and reports, and any evidence its generator records. A block the candidate did not have is absent.



The record’s top-level status is the release-level verdict, and the generated master list publishes that value and no other. A per-check entry in checks describes one check and cannot override the record: a record reads status: failed precisely when a check failed, and publishing the passing check in its place is the “wrong answer that looks like a right answer” CONTRIBUTING names as the worst outcome.

title: Release Bundle schema
text: Every bundle carries a generated summary.yaml review view, written by the index rule and checked for drift in CI. It is derived solely from analyses.tsv and is not declared metadata or an input to building a Store Release: constants stay verbatim, varying identifiers become mixed (n), varying quantities become min-max, varying URLs become their common host/path prefix, and a missing column, an empty table, or any empty value renders as NA (zero is not absence). The same values are published in the master list. See bundle.summarise() and ADR 0014.

title: Release Bundle schema
text:
Generated evidence lives under sidecars/ inside the bundle. Sidecars are Phase B outputs; bundle.check() does not validate their fields, so a Manifest Generator is responsible for emitting them consistently. The one exception is the Quality Check sidecar, which is part of the Release Bundle contract: optional, but validated whenever it is present.

Suggested path: sidecars/sd_estimation.tsv. One row per Analysis whenever effect-scale validation was attempted, passed, warned, failed, or explicitly skipped. Skips are always explicit and reasoned; an Analysis with no source-provided or reference-derivable allele frequencies, no configured reference resource for its assigned ancestry, or a non-quantitative stored_effect_scale (log_or, log_hazard) still gets a row, with status = skipped and a skip_reason.








Field
Required
Description




analysis_id
Yes
Registry Analysis ID matching analyses.tsv.


source_analysis_id
No
Upstream analysis identifier, when the Source Collection provides one.


status
Yes
passed, warning, failed, or skipped.


skip_reason
No
Reason code when status = skipped, for example non_quantitative_effect_scale, no_retained_variants, no_reference_resource_for_ancestry, or low_overlap.


af_source
No
source, reference, or empty when no AF source was used. Source-provided AF is preferred whenever usable; reference AF is a fallback used only when source AF is missing, empty, or otherwise unusable.


ancestry_reference_id
No
Reference Resource resource_id used for reference MAF, when af_source = reference.


original_sd
No
Resolved phenotype SD written to analyses.tsv. Left as the source-declared value (unchanged) for original_sd_method = declared_standardised; populated from the estimate for estimated_from_source_maf / estimated_from_reference_maf when diagnostics pass.


original_sd_method
Yes
Same controlled value as analyses.tsv.


n_variants_considered
No
Number of retained source rows examined for this Analysis.


n_variants_overlapping
No
Number of considered variants with a same-position AF value available.


n_variants_excluded_ambiguous
No
Number of overlapping variants excluded because the allele pair was palindromic/strand-ambiguous.


n_variants_excluded_mismatch
No
Number of overlapping variants excluded because the alleles did not correspond to the reference in either orientation, or were not a usable single-nucleotide pair.


n_variants_excluded_missing_af
No
Number of source rows excluded because the source-provided allele-frequency value was missing or unusable (af_source = source only).


n_variants_excluded_maf
No
Number of safely aligned variants excluded for falling outside maf_min/maf_max.


n_variants_retained
Yes
Number of variants actually used to compute the implied-SD summary.


maf_min
No
Minimum MAF bound used for variant selection.


maf_max
No
Maximum MAF bound used for variant selection.


implied_sd_median
No
Robust (median) summary of per-variant implied phenotype SD, computed from standard error, sample size, and MAF.


sd_dispersion
No
Robust dispersion diagnostic (median absolute deviation over median) for implied-SD estimates across retained variants.


estimator_version
No
Estimator package version, git commit, or script hash.


sd_notes
No
Free-text notes for audit or review dashboards, including the reason for a warning/failed status.






Suggested path: sidecars/source_readiness.tsv. Written by the resumable candidate workflow (issue #153). One row per frozen Source Inventory row — all of them, not only release members — with the inventory’s columns plus two derived ones. It is the audit that keeps the inventory’s readiness evidence distinct from successfully selected membership: a reviewer can see that a non-ready input stayed a discovery fact, and why each ready input is or is not a release member.








Field
Required
Description




(inventory columns)
Yes
The frozen Source Inventory’s own columns (analysis_id, readiness_status, data_file, sha256, …); see resources/inventories/README.md.


duplicate_content_group
No
When two or more ready accessions share one source checksum, their accession ids joined by +; empty otherwise. Duplicates are reported, never collapsed.


candidate_membership
Yes
included, excluded (ready but a controlled exclusion), or not_ready (never selected).






Suggested path: sidecars/exclusions.tsv. Written by the candidate workflow (issue #153). One row per ready Analysis excluded from a candidate by the registry’s membership policy, so an absence has exactly one machine-checkable reason. The same reason is carried in the excluded analyses.tsv row’s inclusion_reason and exclude_from_build.



Field
Required
Description




analysis_id
Yes
Registry Analysis ID matching analyses.tsv.


source_analysis_id
No
Upstream analysis identifier.


study_design
No
The frozen inventory’s study_design.


category
Yes
ancestry, orientation, effect_scale, resolution, metadata, or store_composition.


reason
Yes
Controlled vocabulary: resolution_failed, ancestry_unassigned, ancestry_not_eur, orientation_failure, sd_no_reference_resource_for_ancestry, sd_no_qualifying_evidence, sd_no_usable_sample_size, sd_failed, missing_sample_size, missing_case_control_counts, no_build_eligible_rows, effect_placeholder_rows (a reviewed listing of Analyses whose source writes unestimated effects as a ±2.2e-308 placeholder with standard_error 0), or not_maf_filtered (an otherwise admissible Analysis with no applied MAF floor while store_composition.require_maf_filtered is on; ADR 0033).


detail
No
The concrete evidence (assigned ancestry, gate reason, resolver error, missing field).


resolver_status
No
The resolver record’s status (success, controlled_failure, or missing).


exclude_from_build
Yes
Always true; the exclusion is enforced at build time per ADR 0025.



Nine of these reasons are written by an exclusion Quality Check (see the Quality Check sidecar): no_build_eligible_rows, effect_placeholder_rows, orientation_failure, the Assigned Ancestry check’s ancestry_unassigned and ancestry_not_eur, and the four sd_* reasons. The other four are release policy, with no measurement to test: resolution_failed (no Resolution Record), missing_sample_size and missing_case_control_counts (candidate-table metadata), and the Store Composition Rule’s not_maf_filtered (ADR 0033).



Suggested path: sidecars/quality_checks.tsv. Written by the candidate workflow (issue #285; ADR 0036). One row per ready Analysis, included or excluded, in analyses.tsv order: a Quality Check’s measurement is recorded whether the Analysis passes or not, and whether or not that check decided its membership.
A Quality Check tests one measurement of an Analysis against a threshold, or, for a status, against the values it accepts. Its consequence is fixed when the check is declared (src/manifest_generation/quality_checks.py): an exclusion makes the Analysis an exclude_from_build audit row with the check’s reason (see the exclusions sidecar), and a warning keeps it and records the finding. Every registered check is evaluated for every Analysis.








Field
Required
Description




analysis_id
Yes
Registry Analysis ID matching analyses.tsv.


exclude_from_build
Yes
true when the Analysis is an audit row, empty when included; as in analyses.tsv.


exclusion_reason
No
The reason that decided the exclusion, whether a Quality Check’s or release policy’s; empty when included.


<check>
Yes
The check’s result, one of: passed; failed; not_applicable, the check does not apply to this Analysis (a phenotype SD on a log_or scale), decided before anything is measured, so it wins over unmeasured; unmeasured, there is no measurement to test (a record check without a successful Resolution Record); invalid, the measurement breaks its contract (an unknown eaf_orientation, a non-numeric SD), recorded on an Analysis an earlier rule already excluded; warning, an exclusion check’s measurement fails its test but a policy the release declared keeps the Analysis and records the finding (only assigned_ancestry, below).


<check>_measured
No
The measurement the result is based on, as the check renders it; empty when there is none.



The <check> column pairs follow the registry’s order. The built-in checks are:












Check
Kind
Stage
Measures
Default threshold
Fails when
Reasons




build_eligible_rows
exclusion
resolved
the record’s diagnostics.build_eligible_rows (rows with a finite effect and positive standard error, after any INFO and MAF floor); unmeasured when absent, invalid when not a non-negative integer
1 (minimum rows)
fewer rows than the threshold
no_build_eligible_rows


effect_placeholder_rows
exclusion
resolved
the reviewed release_policy.effect_placeholder_exclusions listing, because OpenGWASDB does not count placeholder rows yet (ADR 0036, clarified by #285); _measured is the listing’s reason, or not_listed
none
the Analysis is listed
effect_placeholder_rows


eaf_orientation
exclusion
ancestry_read
the record’s ancestry.eaf_orientation, gate_reason and eaf_orientation_r; passed and unverified pass, no outcome is unmeasured, a value outside the vocabulary invalid
none
eaf_orientation = failed or gate_reason = eaf_orientation
orientation_failure


assigned_ancestry
exclusion
selection
the record’s ancestry.assigned_ancestry against the Selection’s super-population (release_policy.selection_superpopulation, EUR for OGS-00011). A record showing no allele frequency (under a MAF request, diagnostics.maf_rows_missing equal to canonical_rows_observed, with ancestry_sites 0) is unmeasurable: with release_policy.trust_source_ancestry_without_af its Source Metadata Table source_superpopulation stands in, and matching the Selection is a warning result (Ancestry Assignment Method source_trusted_no_af, #287)
none
no assignment, or not a super-population code, or unmeasurable without the opt-in or a source super-population (ancestry_unassigned); a different super-population, measured or trusted (ancestry_not_eur)
ancestry_unassigned, ancestry_not_eur


phenotype_sd
exclusion
target_ancestry
the record’s phenotype_sd status, reason and estimate; not_applicable for log_or/log_hazard; a non-numeric estimate is invalid
none
not a positive finite estimate
sd_no_qualifying_evidence, sd_no_reference_resource_for_ancestry, sd_no_usable_sample_size, sd_failed



A check’s stage is a precedence slot in the release policy: the policy settles an Analysis in a fixed order and, at each slot, the first failed exclusion check there decides. The slot fixes which reason wins when several apply and what the audit row carries: resolved (a successful Resolution Record, before Assigned Ancestry is read; the row carries none), ancestry_read (Assigned Ancestry read but not yet assessed; the row keeps the value read), selection (Assigned Ancestry tested against the Selection; the row carries it as af_assigned when it is a super-population code) and target_ancestry (the Analysis has the Selection’s ancestry, and its case-control counts when it needs them). Within a slot, registry order decides. A new check can use an existing slot without a policy change; a new slot is a change to the release policy.
A measurement an exclusion cannot use is never a silent pass. An invalid result where its check would decide membership stops the run; on an Analysis an earlier rule already excluded, it is only recorded. An Analysis that nothing excluded but that an exclusion check recorded as unmeasured (or invalid) is refused, naming the Analysis and the check, rather than included untested.
The INFO and MAF floors (defaults.info_score_threshold, defaults.maf_threshold) are not Quality Checks, because OpenGWASDB applies them to rows during Analysis Resolution and neither one decides an Analysis’s membership; their effect is measured by build_eligible_rows.
Contract. The sidecar is an optional Release Bundle contract file (ADR 0036: the contract grows per-Analysis Quality Check results). A bundle without it is valid; every bundle emitted before #285 has none. When it is present, bundle.check() (_check_quality_checks) requires:

the columns analysis_id, exclude_from_build, exclusion_reason, then one <check>, <check>_measured pair per check, at least one, with no check named twice;
one row per analyses.tsv Analysis, excluded audit rows included, in the same order, and no other row;
every <check> value in the result vocabulary above;
exclude_from_build exactly true or empty, agreeing with analyses.tsv; exclusion_reason non-empty exactly when excluded, and, when sidecars/exclusions.tsv is present, equal to its reason for that Analysis.

Store Release Build never reads it: membership is already decided in analyses.tsv (tests/packaging/test_boundary.py holds this).



Suggested path: sidecars/sparse_regions.tsv. One row per retained region for ragged stores. A region-filtered release carries it from acquisition (#300): acquisition records each filtered file’s plan beside its Acquisition Manifest (manifest_generation.region_filtered_acquisition), checksummed through the frozen inventory’s provenance, and the candidate carries the Selection’s rows verbatim, in acquisition’s order, refusing a file changed since the freeze (candidate_workflow.acquisition_evidence). Regions are listed cis, then significant-trans ranges by chromosome (as text) and start, then suggestive leads and QC-panel chromosomes in file order; region_id is <analysis_id>__<cis|sig_trans|suggestive|qc_panel>__<nnn>, numbered per kind. A release acquired from the retired R generator’s files carries that bundle’s own file.

Required
Description

Yes

region_id
Yes
Stable region identifier within the Analysis.


region_kind
Yes
Controlled value such as cis, significant_trans, suggestive_trans, qc_panel, or manual. qc_panel rows (issue #28/#30) mark the fixed QC panel’s positions retained unconditionally, regardless of significance; unlike the signal-driven kinds, pvalue_threshold/lead_variant_id/target_id are not applicable and are left blank.


chromosome
Yes
Chromosome name in source coordinates.


start
Yes
1-based inclusive region start.


end
Yes
1-based inclusive region end.


source_genome_build
Yes
Genome build of the region coordinates.


target_id
No
Gene, analyte, or other target defining the region.


target_label
No
Human-readable target label.


lead_variant_id
No
Lead variant for signal-defined regions.


pvalue_threshold
No
Threshold used to define signal-derived regions.


n_variants_retained
No
Number of variants retained in the filtered source file for this region.


region_policy_id
Yes
Named sparse-region policy declared in generator configuration.
