title: Release Bundle schema
text:
A Source Collection plugs into Manifest Generation through files, never through code the pipeline calls (ADR 0036). Two of them meet at freeze (python3 -m manifest_generation.freeze, #283):

the Source Metadata Table: one row per intended Analysis in canonical columns – source_analysis_id (the only required one), Source Trait Label and ontology terms, Source Ancestry Label and super-population, study design, declared effect scale, sample size and case counts, genome build, Publication Metadata, licence, a provider grouping (store_key) and optional target columns for single-target Analyses;
the Acquisition Manifest: per Analysis, the file acquisition produced – location, size, sha256, source URL, metadata sidecar, lineage for a reformatted file – or the readiness status recording why there is none.

A release config’s Selection (all, an analyses list, or a where rule) picks the Analyses one release takes. Freeze reconciles them, fails on a selected Analysis with no manifest row, a row no Analysis claims or a duplicate, keeps an explained absence as a non-ready inventory row, and writes the Source Inventory with the selected connector rows frozen beside it.
docs/spec/source-connectors.md specifies every column, the vocabularies, the GWAS Catalog adapter and writer, the Selection grammar and the frozen inventory’s provenance.

title: Release Bundle schema
text:
The blocks below are Phase B generator configuration, not Release Bundle fields. They are recorded here because they determine the sidecar and validation.yaml evidence a generator writes into a bundle. A generator’s config also carries its selection and output settings; the blocks that affect release metadata are documented here.


Phase B selects release membership from a frozen Source Inventory rather than from a glob over an acquisition mirror (issue #151). That directory’s README is the authority on the inventory’s columns, its readiness vocabulary and the freeze/preflight commands. A generator config names the snapshot it selects from and the acquisition output that snapshot was frozen from:








Field
Required
Description




source.source_collection_id
Yes
The Source Collection string recorded on the release, gwas-catalog-ssf for the GWAS Catalog GWAS-SSF collection.


source.store_key
Yes
The candidate-pool key this release’s Analyses were selected from. Every inventory row must belong to it.


source.ancestry_group
Yes
The source-declared ancestry group the pool is scoped to. Provenance, never a substitute for Assigned Ancestry.


source.candidates
Yes
The candidate table the pool came from. Generated and not tracked in git, so the freeze records its checksum to pin the selection scope.


source.inventory.snapshot_id
Yes
The snapshot’s identity. Must equal the inventory file’s stem and the provenance sidecar’s snapshot_id.


source.inventory.path
Yes
resources/inventories/<snapshot-id>.tsv.


source.inventory.provenance_path
Yes
resources/inventories/<snapshot-id>.meta.yaml, the sidecar whose inventory_tsv_sha256 binds the TSV to the bytes that were frozen.


source.inventory.freeze_inputs
Yes, for a GWAS Catalog config (a pre-#287 key)
The ordered {role, path} acquisition status manifests, earliest pass first. Only the GWAS Catalog’s src/manifest_generation/providers/gwas_catalog/write_acquisition_manifest.py reads it (#347): it overlays the passes into the Acquisition Manifest and its pass lineage, before freeze, and freeze then reads that manifest like any other source’s. It is therefore required wherever that writer is given --config, and the writer refuses a config that declares none rather than defaulting to one pass. No shared module reads this key, and a release config names its connector files under source_collection.connectors instead (docs/spec/release-config.md maps the pre-#287 keys). Order is the precedence rule: a later pass is authoritative for every analysis_id it covers, and it may not regress a ready Analysis to a non-ready one.



Which readiness_status values count as a usable source is not a config key: it is owned by src/manifest_generation/source_inventory.py (READY_STATUSES: ok and already_present), so the vocabulary has one spelling rather than one per generator config. An unknown status fails rather than defaulting to unavailable.



A release whose pool mixes study designs cannot carry one release-wide stored_effect_scale: a quantitative trait on the SD scale and a case-control trait on the log-OR scale need different tiers. defaults.by_study_design declares one tier per study_design value the inventory may carry:








Field
Required
Description




defaults.by_study_design.<study_design>.stored_effect_scale
Yes
Controlled analyses.tsv vocabulary: sd, log_or, or log_hazard.


defaults.by_study_design.<study_design>.original_effect_scale
Yes
The source’s own scale before OpenGWASDB rescaling.


defaults.by_study_design.<study_design>.original_sd_method
Yes
The phenotype-SD tier: an estimable method for a quantitative design, or binary_trait/unavailable where SD estimation does not apply.


defaults.by_study_design.<study_design>.sample_size_kind
Yes
total, case_control, effective, or variant_level.



A ready Analysis whose study_design has no declared tier fails preflight, naming the design and the number of Analyses affected: guessing a tier is the silent-failure class this repository exists to prevent. runtime.cores (the planned worker count, capped per release) and runtime.min_free_gb (the free space preflight requires under output.work_root) are checked the same way.



A metadata resolver is a small, independently callable module owned by one Source Collection (gwas-catalog-ssf, opengwas-gwas-vcf, …) that resolves the interpretation-bearing fields derive cannot safely infer from the raw summary-statistics file alone: stored_effect_scale, sample_size_kind, sample_size, n_cases, and n_controls. Resolvers read the provider’s own authoritative study/analysis metadata (a study table row, an API response, an endpoint manifest) — never the summary-statistics file itself, which may disagree with or omit this metadata (see issue #15’s ieu-a-7 example, where a GWAS-VCF ##SAMPLE header declares StudyType=Continuous for a study the source API correctly reports as case-control).
Conventionally, resolver modules live beside their provider, under src/manifest_generation/providers/<provider>/, one file per Source Collection, named for the resolved field set they share: resolve_<source_collection>_metadata(...).
Input is whatever raw metadata unit the provider exposes for one Analysis (free text, a parsed API record, …); shape is provider-specific and not part of this contract. Output is always a single resolved record with these fields:








Field
Required
Description




resolution_status
Yes
resolved or unresolved. Never a silent default — an Analysis whose metadata can’t be established gets an explicit unresolved record, not a defaulted value that looks plausible.


resolution_notes
No
Free-text reason when resolution_status = unresolved.


stored_effect_scale
No
Same controlled vocabulary as analyses.tsv: sd, log_or, or log_hazard. NA when resolution_status = unresolved.


sample_size_kind
No
Same controlled vocabulary as analyses.tsv: total, case_control, effective, or variant_level. NA when resolution_status = unresolved.


sample_size
No
Scalar study N. NA when resolution_status = unresolved.


n_cases
No
Case (or event) count. NA when not applicable (sample_size_kind != case_control) or unresolved.


n_controls
No
Control (or non-event) count. NA when not applicable or unresolved.



A caller (a derive stage, or a curation script such as ebi-studies.r) may adapt this generic record onto its own column names, but the resolver itself must not know which downstream shape it feeds — this is what lets derive stay agnostic to which provider it is talking to.
These implementations exist:

src/manifest_generation/providers/gwas_catalog/gwas_catalog_ssf.R (resolve_gwas_catalog_ssf_metadata()) resolves GWAS Catalog’s free-text “INITIAL SAMPLE SIZE” study field: a study whose parsed components include any cases/controls counts resolves as case_control with stored_effect_scale = log_or; otherwise it resolves as total with stored_effect_scale = sd; a field with no parseable numeric component resolves as unresolved.
src/manifest_generation/providers/ukb_b/provider_metadata.py (resolve_record(), issue #219), for the opengwas-gwas-vcf Source Collection, and the adapter that writes its Source Metadata Table (#289). It resolves a study’s ncase/ncontrol/sample_size from the OpenGWAS “gwasinfo” record – the provider JSON sidecar ukb-b ships beside each VCF, since the stored API token expired – rather than the source GWAS-VCF file’s ##SAMPLE header, which is not authoritative. A usable ncase/ncontrol pair resolves sample_size_kind as case_control; otherwise a usable sample_size resolves it as total; a record with neither resolves as unresolved. stored_effect_scale primarily follows the record’s units field (SD -> sd, log odds/logOR -> log_or, a hazard-ratio unit -> log_hazard), falling back to log_or/sd from ncase/ncontrol presence only when units is absent or unrecognised (issue #50: the ukb-b batch reports every trait on the SD scale, so inferring scale from case/control-count presence alone is wrong for that batch). The R resolver that held this contract (lib/metadata_resolvers/opengwas_api.R) retired with ukb-b’s R path (#289).
src/manifest_generation/providers/finngen/source_metadata_adapter.py (issue #288, docs/spec/source-connectors.md), FinnGen’s endpoint manifest, for the finngen-r13 Source Collection. It keeps the classification the collection’s retired R resolver applied: binary endpoint rows carry num_cases and num_controls and are case-control; FinnGen encodes its inverse-rank-normalised quantitative endpoints with category = Quantitative endpoints, the total N in num_cases, and num_controls = 0, and those rows are quantitative without misrepresenting that total as a case count. It refuses an endpoint it cannot describe honestly rather than leaving it unresolved; the release config’s method tiers turn study_design into stored_effect_scale/sample_size_kind.




Manifest Generation’s shared step (#286, ADR 0036 step 5). The Python pipeline maps every Analysis in src/manifest_generation/trait_ontology_mapping.py, after the resolver records are verified. It reads the source term from the Source Metadata Table’s source_trait_ontology_id/source_trait_ontology_label (GWAS Catalog’s MAPPED_TRAIT_URI/MAPPED_TRAIT) and the Source Trait Label. Precedence and methods are those below: - a source term is kept as source_provided; - otherwise an exact match of the trimmed, lower-cased Source Trait Label is canonical_table_lookup; - otherwise the Analysis is unmapped.
A source term is normalised to CURIEs term by term:







Source form
CURIE




http://www.ebi.ac.uk/efo/EFO_0004839
EFO:0004839


http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/MONDO_0005148 (any NS_local)
MONDO:0005148


http://www.orpha.net/ORDO/Orphanet_101960
Orphanet:101960


a CURIE
unchanged



Any other form is refused, naming the Analysis and the term: the run fails rather than emitting a URI or a guess. A comma-separated source list stays a list, its CURIEs joined by ", " in the source’s order, and the source label is kept verbatim (see trait_ontology_id above).
A source term is rejected using ogstores.bundle’s #141 guards when: - any term is gene- or protein-shaped, checked both before and after normalisation, so a PURL HGNC_1234 is caught as HGNC:1234; - or its label, taken whole, is an identifier-authority name.
A rejected term falls through to the table, and the rejection and its reason are recorded. A source term with no label is kept as source_provided, and the run counts how many there are.
The table is read from resources/reference-resources/canonical-trait-mapping-efo/, a directory named explicitly: no network is involved. Its resource.yaml location is resolved against that directory: the declared file must be in the resource’s own directory, and a declared location_kind must be tracked_file. A malformed curated row fails the load, and the refusal lists up to twenty problems and counts the rest: - a blank lookup value; - a non-CURIE term; - a gene-shaped term or an authority-name label; - a label listed twice.
The table’s identity, the method counts, the count of source terms without a label, and the rejected source terms are recorded in validation.yaml’s trait_ontology_mapping block.
The lookup lives in this registry rather than in OpenGWASDB ADR 0021. A source-provided term is kept even when the ontology has deprecated it, and is recorded as source_provided; a plausible-looking invented replacement would be worse than the genuine obsolete term.



Each item in a generator config’s reference_resources list describes one auxiliary build-time resource (see ADR 0011). The canonical form of a declaration is a resource.yaml under resources/reference-resources/<resource-id>/; a generator config may repeat the fields it needs inline. A reference-AF resource used for effect-scale validation should declare at least:








Field
Required
Description




resource_id
Yes
Stable ID for this Reference Resource, referenced from effect_scale_validation.reference_resources or ancestry_assignment.reference_resource_id.


kind
Yes
reference_af for single-ancestry allele-frequency lookup resources used by effect-scale validation; ancestry_mixture for multi-ancestry mixture-frequency resources used by AF-based ancestry assignment (issue #23); qc_panel for the fixed QC variant panel unconditionally retained regardless of significance (issue #28/#29); trait_ontology_mapping for a curated trait-label-to-ontology-term lookup; hybrid_dense_panel for a Hybrid release’s Dense Component reference panel; variant_list for a canonical ALID list consumed as an Indexed Variant Subset build input (hapmap3-hg38, epic #214); other kinds (for example LD panels) may reuse the same declaration shape.


ancestry
Yes for reference_af
Ancestry/population label the resource represents, matching the controlled assigned_ancestry vocabulary. For ancestry_mixture resources, which cover multiple super-populations at once, use ancestry: multi and list the covered super-populations in super_populations instead. Not applicable for trait_ontology_mapping.


super_populations
Yes for ancestry_mixture
List of super-population labels the mixture reference can assign to (for example AFR, AMR, EAS, EUR, MID, NAF, SAS).


genome_build
Yes, except trait_ontology_mapping
Genome build of the resource’s coordinates. Not applicable for trait_ontology_mapping, which has no genomic coordinates.


variant_id_convention
Yes, except trait_ontology_mapping
Variant identifier/allele convention used by the resource, for example chr:pos_ref_alt, or chr:pos:A1:A2 (A1 = min(allele1, allele2)) for the canonical ALID convention opengwasdb.ancestry uses.


allele_columns
No
Column-name mapping the resource uses for effect/other allele and frequency, for example {effect: EA, other: OA, freq: EAF}.


location
Yes
External path or URI for the resource, outside this repository — except kind: qc_panel and kind: trait_ontology_mapping, both small enough to track directly in this repository, so location is a repo-relative path instead.


location_kind
No
How to interpret location, for example external_directory, external_file, or tracked_file for a small resource tracked directly in this repository.


row_count
Yes for variant_list
Number of variant rows the resource contains. Verification fails on a mismatch, so a truncated or appended list cannot pass as the declared one.


checksums
Yes for variant_list
The exact bytes the resource was accepted at: alid_sha256 and alid_bytes for the maintained list, plus source_md5/source_sha256 for the upstream source snapshot. The consumer hashes the same bytes (opengwasdb build-indexed-subset records the list’s SHA-256 in the subset metadata), so this is the identity a reviewer compares against.


source
Yes for variant_list
Upstream provenance of the list: source name, file, download URL, snapshot path, size, columns and source row count.


derivation
Yes for variant_list
How the maintained list was derived from the source and the counts that reconcile it, including rsids_requested, resolved, absent_from_store_axis, allele_incompatible and duplicate_alids. The arithmetic must balance and resolved must equal row_count; verification refuses otherwise.


fine_group_map
Yes for ancestry_mixture
External path to the fine-ancestry-group -> super-population map (one row per fine group in the resource) used to aggregate a fitted mixture to super-population composition.



Reference-AF and ancestry-mixture resources are recorded here for provenance; the resource data itself lives under the configured artifact root or another external location, never inside this repository (ADR 0015). A kind: variant_list resource is the same shape for an Indexed Variant Subset build input: the hapmap3-hg38 declaration records the canonical-ALID list’s row_count and byte checksums, its LDSC source checksum and snapshot, and the rsID reconciliation, and tools/reference-resources/hapmap3-hg38/verify_hm3_resource.py is the executable check of all of them.



Every future Dense and Hybrid Store Release declares the maintained hm3 Indexed Variant Subset by default (stores #210, epic #214); a Ragged-only release does not. The pipeline resolves that declaration through src/manifest_generation/indexed_subsets.py, which reads the one maintained hapmap3-hg38 Reference Resource, so no writer copies the list path, assembly or checksum. The default is not a requirement:








Field
Required
Description




indexed_subsets
No
A Dense or Hybrid release that omits the key gets the default hm3 declaration. An explicit [] is a deliberate opt-out and must be paired with indexed_subsets_opt_out. A non-empty list overrides the default verbatim (validated by bundle.check()). A Ragged release may not declare one.


indexed_subsets_opt_out
Yes when indexed_subsets: []
The written reason a Dense or Hybrid release omits the default. The generator records it in release.yaml notes so the omission is reviewable; an empty list with no reason, a null value, or a malformed entry is a generator error rather than a silent omission.



The resolved declaration is written to build.yaml in the shape documented under build.yaml. Because a subset-declaring release needs an opengwasdb providing build-indexed-subset, the release entry point probes for it and refuses a missing capability before any write; the repository’s pinned current-format runtime provides it (stores#218). See src/ogstores/resources.py, src/ogstores/runtime.py and the release runtime.



A generator config’s optional top-level quality_checks block overrides a Quality Check’s shared default threshold for one release (#285):
quality_checks:
  build_eligible_rows: 1000   # exclude an Analysis with fewer build-eligible rows
Each key names a registered check that has a threshold; its value is parsed by that check (build_eligible_rows takes a whole number of rows of at least 1). An unknown name, a check with no threshold (one that tests a status), or a value the check refuses is a config error. A check’s kind is part of its declaration and cannot be overridden.
Thresholds are recorded twice. validation.yaml quality_checks.<check> carries the effective and default thresholds and whether this release overrode it. The resolution receipt’s contract always carries a quality_checks entry holding the effective thresholds, defaults included, and the release’s overrides, so changing an override or a shared default makes the receipt stale and verify/emit refuse it until resolution is re-run. A receipt written before #285 has no such entry and is stale for the same reason.



A generator config’s effect_scale_validation block configures the reference-AF effect-scale validation stage (issue #16) for one release:








Field
Required
Description




enabled
Yes
Whether this release opts into empirical effect-scale validation.


reference_resources
Yes when enabled
List of {ancestry, resource_id} pairs mapping an assigned ancestry to a declared Reference Resource resource_id. An ancestry without an entry here produces an explicit skipped sidecar row rather than silently omitting evidence.


maf_min / maf_max
Yes when enabled
Reference-MAF bounds a variant must fall within to be used for implied-SD estimation.


min_overlap_variants
Yes when enabled
Minimum number of safely aligned, in-bounds variants required before an Analysis is scored rather than skipped as low_overlap.


sd_tolerance
Yes when enabled
Maximum abs(median implied SD - 1) for a declared-standardised Analysis to pass.


warning_multiplier
Yes when enabled
Multiplier applied to sd_tolerance defining the boundary between a warning and a failed scale-inconsistency status.


dispersion_max
Yes when enabled
Maximum robust dispersion (median absolute deviation over median implied SD) before the result is downgraded to warning regardless of the central estimate.



A generator config may set defaults for these values and override them per release, per the source’s molecular or population-scale GWAS tolerances. When the block is absent or enabled: false, the release has not opted into empirical effect-scale validation, and validation.yaml checks.effect_scale/checks.sd_estimation should read not_run rather than imply a pass.



A generator config’s ancestry_assignment block configures the AF-based ancestry assignment stage (issue #23) for one release. Unlike effect_scale_validation (which maps one Reference Resource per assigned ancestry, since each reference-AF panel is single-ancestry), a single ancestry-mixture Reference Resource covers every super-population at once, so this block references exactly one Reference Resource rather than an ancestry-keyed list:








Field
Required
Description




enabled
Yes
Whether this release opts into AF-based ancestry assignment.


reference_resource_id
Yes when enabled
resource_id of the declared kind: ancestry_mixture Reference Resource to fit against.


maf_floor
No
Minimum reference-wide MAF for a variant to be used in the mixture fit; defaults to 0.01. Lower for tiny fixture panels where all variants are informative.


gates.tau
Yes when enabled
Minimum dominant super-population proportion required to admit an assignment.


gates.delta
Yes when enabled
Minimum margin of the dominant super-population’s proportion over the runner-up.


gates.n_min
Yes when enabled
Minimum number of allele-frequency sites overlapping the reference required before fitting. Ragged/sparse releases (signal-derived regions only, not a full-genome scan) typically need a much lower n_min than a dense, full-GWAS release.


gates.residual_max
Yes when enabled
Maximum NNLS mixture-fit residual before the assignment is gated out as unreliable.



Only Analyses with usable source allele frequencies attempt AF-based assignment; Analyses without usable source AF keep ancestry_assignment_method: source_trusted_no_af untouched, per issue #11’s settled trust-vs-validate policy. When an assignment is attempted but fails a gate, ancestry_assignment_method becomes unassigned (not left at its prior value), because the prior value would otherwise misleadingly imply validation was never attempted.



The shared pipeline keeps the QC panel in every region-filtered file: a release config’s region_policy.qc_panel_resource_id names it, and acquisition records the panel’s identity in each file’s lineage (#300, release config). The R generators’ filter.qc_panel block, described below for the bundles they emitted, retired with them.
A generator config’s filter.qc_panel block configured unconditional retention of the fixed QC variant panel (issue #28/#29/#30) for one release. Unlike the signal-driven sparse regions (cis/significant_trans/suggestive_trans), the QC panel is retained regardless of an Analysis’s p_value distribution, so ancestry assignment and reference-AF effect-scale validation have a stable variant backbone even for Analyses with few or no genome-wide-significant hits:








Field
Required
Description




enabled
Yes
Whether this release retains the QC panel in every Analysis’s filtered file.


resource_id
Yes when enabled
resource_id of the declared kind: qc_panel Reference Resource to retain (see “Reference Resource declaration”).



QC-panel retention is purely additive: a release that does not configure filter.qc_panel behaves exactly as before, and enabling it for one release never changes another’s filtered output. Retained QC-panel rows are recorded in the sparse-region sidecar with region_kind: qc_panel (one row per chromosome the panel actually matched in that Analysis’s source file, spanning the matched positions), distinct from the signal-driven region kinds, and sidecars/filter_summary.tsv gets a qc_panel_rows count per Analysis (0 for releases that do not configure a panel).
Effect-scale validation (issue #16) and ancestry assignment (issue #23/#25) deliberately do not distinguish QC-panel rows from signal-driven rows when choosing which retained variants to use for AF/SD computations — both continue to consume every retained row with usable allele-frequency data uniformly. Retaining the QC panel already directly grows that pool for low-power Analyses; preferring QC-panel rows exclusively would need to discard perfectly good signal-driven rows for well-powered Analyses, for no demonstrated ascertainment benefit. This can be revisited if evidence of an ascertainment problem emerges, but is not assumed by default.

title: Release Bundle schema
text: A release bundle is acceptable when analyses.tsv is enough for OpenGWASDB to build the intended store, release.yaml and build.yaml are enough to explain what the store is and how to rebuild it, and sidecars are enough to audit any non-obvious derived metadata without blocking low-effort source ingestion. Run pixi run bundle-check to confirm it.

Issue #152 addresses two blocking Reference Resource decisions before Phase B candidate generation for the full EBI GWAS Catalog European Hybrid Release Candidate (gwas-catalog-ssf-eur-hybrid-2026-09-10, 4,570 ready Analyses):

title: Execution-only amendment: n-workers: 16 for MVP observed Stores 12/13/14/16
text:
Owner-authorized execution amendment, recorded 2026-10-14 (owner instruction 17:43 UTC: “use 16 workers per build please”). It changes only the runtime worker count in the Build Recipe of the four MVP observed Stores (OGS-00012, OGS-00013, OGS-00014, OGS-00016) so the supported dev batch can run three concurrent builds × 16 workers.


stores/OGS-000{12,13,14,16}/build.yaml gain exactly one Build Recipe option:
build:
  options:
    n-workers: 16
Nothing else in those bundles changes. analyses.tsv (membership and Analytical Metadata), release.yaml (identity, status, source_snapshot, accepted_at), validation.yaml, the pinned runtime commit 4e922566, the source inputs and the reference axis are byte-unchanged. OGS-00015 (EAS) and OGS-00017 (FinnGen) are untouched.



ADR 0004 requires a new Store Release when the accepted Release Manifest changes or when a material Build Recipe choice changes the produced analytical asset. This amendment changes neither:

The Release Manifest (analyses.tsv) is identical, so the accepted input membership is not re-accepted and no new Store Release ID is minted.
The worker count is a pure runtime knob: opengwasdb ADR 0024 (0024-parallel-dense-vcf-build-disk-spill) parallelises Pass 2 by disk-spill with no large IPC, and states “n_workers is a pure runtime knob; results are independent of it”, verified by test_two_workers_matches_serial (serial and 2-worker builds bit-identical). The produced analytical asset is therefore independent of the value.

So the accepted input membership, Release IDs, scientific-acceptance posture and format are unchanged and remain immutable; this is a deployment scheduling choice, not an interpretation change.



ADR 0014, ADR 0031 and the workflow spec state that an accepted bundle is immutable. This amendment does edit the Build Recipe of accepted bundles, so it is recorded explicitly rather than applied silently, and it is deliberately limited to the execution-only n-workers option:

the owner authorized this execution change (2026-10-14);
ADR 0004’s material-choice test is not met (the produced asset is independent of n_workers; core ADR 0024), so no new Store Release or lineage is minted;
the Release Manifest and every identity/source field are byte-unchanged, so the accepted input membership is not re-accepted.

If the project decides that any edit to an accepted bundle must mint a new erratum Release rather than a recorded non-material amendment, this change is the trigger to revisit that rule; it is flagged here before any broader recipe patch.




Applies to the four MVP observed Stores above only.
No new general runtime override, scheduler or thread API is introduced; the option is the existing build-dense-vcf --n-workers flag already used by OGS-00017 (n-workers: 32).
The pinned runtime 4e922566d7fa4c13a11be3637069da63e48be28c remains read-only; no environment, source, reference or artifact write is part of this amendment. pixi run index regenerates stores.tsv, STORES.md, the bundle summary.yaml and stores/by-label/ from these tracked files with the artifact root unset, so the artifact root is not written.

text:
Snapshot: evidence captured 2026-10-11; owner decision recorded 2026-10-12. Records the owner decision on the dbGaP phs002453 GIA acquisition against the PMID 39024449 candidate table (epic #232, ticket #220) and the resulting metadata-only reconciliation. No association rows were read, no conversion or download was run, and no ancestry grouping was settled (ticket #221).

The decision is committed in resources/generators/dbgap-mvp/dbgap-phs002453-key-discrepancies.yaml (owner_decisions), and each resolved record carries its owner_decision.

Every row’s disposition is derived from the validated, cited owner_decisions trait policy in the ledger: resolved_dbgap_authoritative when that policy is complete, and the category’s original pending default (formatting_only_pending_policy or owner_scientific_review) when it is missing or incomplete, so a fixture or partial ledger never implies a resolution. trait_category is the raw classification. Unit tests were rerun with the adopted environment /home/gh13047/repo/opengwasdb-stores-wt/218-current-runtime/.pixi/envs/dev/bin/python (core opengwasdb at 4e92256). No core or stores consumer validates the dbGaP -meta.yaml keys: the sidecar is only read generically (yaml.safe_load) by the acquisition tooling/tests, and it already carried the extra source and dbgap_analysis_description fields before this change. The catalog_metadata block is therefore additive provenance; the EBI field set is unchanged and any strict consumer can ignore the extra keys. If a future strict schema forbids extras, the same values remain in the ledger and mapping.tsv.

No full Store build, release acceptance/promotion or identity change.
No edit to the global source-candidate TSV; the Catalog values are preserved as provenance rather than rewritten.
No ancestry grouping or META-store split (ticket #221).




This record proves a metadata-only mapping reconciliation, not acquisition completion. Two converted files are still absent, and the pre-existing converted canonical outputs for the two accessions (if any) are stale and need a bounded retry once conversion is authorised. Do not claim “6,022 converted” or acquisition complete from this document.




Targeted conversion of GCST90476298 and GCST90481129 and manifest refresh with genuine sha256; re-verify the resulting sidecar carries the dbGaP canonical metadata and the preserved Catalog provenance.
Freeze the TSV Source Inventory for candidate generation once the ancestry/META split (#221) is settled.

title: Overview
text:
Where OpenGWASDB stands: what the registry holds, what each epic changed, and what the engine can do.
This page is the site’s home and is filled by #391: milestone progress, each workstream’s active epics with their Next line, and headline numbers with trends. Until then:

Reports lists the published reports: curation, trait mapping, imputation filters and the October 2026 progress update.
Registry holds this repository’s decisions, specifications and guides, and the glossary (CONTEXT.md, staged at render time).
Engine holds opengwasdb’s own documentation, rendered from the revision pixi.lock pins, so it describes the runtime the registry imports.

Links from these pages to files outside docs/ (a module under src/, a specification fragment under resources/, CONTRIBUTING.md) point at GitHub at the commit being rendered.



 Back to top

title: HGDP+1kGP LD panel release evidence
text:
Status: SHIP AFR/EAS/SAS panels for ancestry-matched reference completion.
Generation completed on 2026-08-06 under /data/opengwasdb/reference/hgdp1kgp-hg38/panel using MAC ≥ 50 and a 0.99 cumulative-variance target with a 250-component floor. Corrected populated block counts are AFR 1,580, EAS 1,120, SAS 1,267, and EUR calibration 1,357. The sole unpopulated declared interval, EAS chr14:16038675-16100330, contains no retained variant and is explicitly empty.
The five-region paired masking experiment used 2,514 UKB-B analyses and held out 20% of variants shared by the observed store and both EUR panels. HGDP+1kGP EUR accepted 12,430/12,570 eligible analysis-region fits (98.9%) with median held-out beta correlation 0.963. UKB EUR accepted 12,559/12,570 (99.9%) with median 0.978. Among 12,421 paired successful fits, UKB’s median advantage was 0.014 correlation points and it was higher in 91.2% of pairs.
The exploratory release gate was acceptance ≥98%, median correlation ≥0.95, and median paired loss versus UKB EUR ≤0.02. The calibration passes all three. This supports shipping the ancestry-matched panels but not replacing UKB EUR. Full method, region-level results, plots, limitations, and the allele-orientation defect found and corrected during validation are in docs/eur-panel-imputation-comparison.html. The compact tracked results are in docs/data/eur-panel-imputation-summary.csv; the 5 MB analysis-level table remains external at /data/opengwasdb/wip/eur-panel-imputation-comparison.csv.
Issue #40 remains separately blocked: as checked on 2026-08-06, explodecomputer/opengwasdb#10 is still open, so the required real consumer smoke test cannot yet be claimed.


The 601 historically under-resolved UKB EUR eigendecompositions were regenerated at cumulative variance 0.99 and swapped into /data/opengwasdb/reference/ukb-hg38/EUR. A production scan on 2026-08-06 found zero of the 1,345 then-present eigendecompositions under-resolved at the consumer’s 0.9 threshold. The same audit identified 12 legacy matrix-backed blocks without an eigendecomposition; these were backfilled in the same session (250–715 components, achieved variance 0.990002–0.992257). The directory now contains 1,357/1,357 .ldeig.npz artifacts.
The rebuilt UKB-B completion is recorded externally at /data/opengwasdb/wip/ukb-b-c128-completed.PROVENANCE.md: completion-quality mean Pearson correlation improved from 0.9719 to 0.9770 and missing cells fell from 22,016,187 to 18,648,444 relative to the pre-issue-#34 completed store.

title: AMR Reference-Completion LD panel: a calibration proposal
text:
Status: proposal for owner decision — not an approved production policy. Author: OpenGWASDB Stores agent (ticket #217 research follow-up) Date: 2026-10-12 Scope: which GRCh38 LD Reference Resource, if any, may complete MVP AMR-assigned Analyses (#229). This document proposes a calibration panel only. It authorises no download, genotype construction, panel build, Store build or association read. Production adoption requires the owner decision recorded in Open owner decisions and independent review.


Epic #232 requires a completed descendant for each MVP ancestry except META, and ticket #229 states the operational prerequisite plainly: a verified AMR, assembly-compatible LD Reference Resource is required before Reference Completion; a convenient EUR panel is not an acceptable silent substitute.
The registry currently declares no AMR panel. Two facts make that a blocker rather than an opt-out:

resources/reference-resources/hgdp1kgp-hg38-ld/resource.yaml declares ancestry: [AFR, EAS, SAS]; its description says Analyses assigned AMR/MID/NAF “remain observed-only” until a panel exists.
resources/reference-resources/hgdp1kgp-hg38-ld/populations_to_superpop.tsv maps CLM, MXL, PEL, PUR (1kGP Admixed American) and Pima, Maya, Karitiana, Surui, Colombian (HGDP American) to excluded / no_AMR_panel, and ld_regions_hg38.tsv (host: /data/opengwasdb/reference/hgdp1kgp-hg38/ld_regions_hg38.tsv) defines block boundaries for AFR, EAS, EUR and SAS only.

So the current behaviour is correct-by-design (ADR 0020), but it cannot satisfy #229. docs/epic-232-execution.md (orchestrator-owned, not modified here) already records: “#229 needs an explicitly suitable LD resource; HGDP resource declares AFR/EAS/SAS, not AMR. Missing reference is not observed-only success.”
This proposal answers the owner’s question, “1kg?”, by evaluating the candidate sample sources and recommending a calibration design.





The authority for Phase 3 sample counts is the official IGSR sample panel integrated_call_samples_v3.20130502.ALL.panel (55,156 bytes; SHA-256 b4023dc6ee2d62ee89c8d4d347db4d348e65518d66d346574cdae7a4bbd76858), not a search summary. Verified from that file: 2,504 samples total, of which 347 are AMR. The four AMR populations and their Phase 3 counts:



Population
Phase 3 samples
Region




CLM (Colombians, Medellín)
94
AMR


MXL (Mexican Ancestry, Los Angeles)
64
AMR


PEL (Peruvians, Lima)
85
AMR


PUR (Puerto Ricans)
104
AMR


Total
347




The 347 total is verified from the panel file, not assumed. Phase 3 is the 2,504-sample panel — the “original unrelated” baseline cited in §2.2 — and the 698 related samples / 602 trios belong to the separate 3,202 high-coverage expansion, so they must not be attributed to these 347. The Phase 3 VCFs are GRCh37 and would need liftover, so they are cited for counts only and are not the proposed genotype source (IGSR Phase 3, IGSR FAQ).



The primary description is Byrska-Bishop et al., Cell 185, 3426–3440 (2022): 3,202 samples, 602 complete parent–child trios, 2,504 original unrelated + 698 additional related samples, re-sequenced to ~30× and aligned to GRCh38 (PubMed 36055201, DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2022.08.004; IGSR 30× collection). Filtering the related subset is advised for analyses that assume independence; the extra depth improves variant discovery, not sample independence. A panel built from all 3,202 would include 698 non-independent individuals.



The registry already acquires this joint GRCh38 genome-wide callset (acquire_hgdp1kgp.py, gnomAD v3.1.2). The primary description of the subset’s sample QC and relatedness handling is Koenig et al. 2024, Genome Research 34(5):796–809 (DOI 10.1101/gr.278378.123; PMID 38749656; PMC11216312). Their pipeline reduces the raw source 4,150 → 4,117 after 33 QC failures → 4,094 after 23 ancestry outliers; the published 4,094 set contains 3,400 inferred unrelated individuals. The 3,419 unrelated + 698 related partition belongs to the earlier 4,117-sample PCA stage, not the final 4,094 set. The harmonized callset is genome-wide on GRCh38 (primary paper; download availability). The kinship > 0.05 / maximal-independent-set prune reused for the LD subset here is a proposed reuse of the paper’s PCA-relatedness QC choice, not a claim that upstream calibrated that threshold for LD-panel construction, and the choice is this pilot’s pending owner approval.
Measured directly from the host’s cached /data/opengwasdb/reference/hgdp1kgp-hg38/source/cohort_populations.tsv (sample metadata only — no genotype read):

The cache has 4,151 rows = 3,202 1kGP + 948 HGDP + 1 control; high_quality == true is 4,097 = 3,166 1kGP + 931 HGDP. This named local high_quality set is not the same selection as the published 4,094: the paper’s pipeline is raw 4,150 → 4,117 (33 QC) → 4,094 (23 ancestry outliers). The task is therefore to reconcile exact QC and ancestry-outlier membership against the paper’s selection, not to resolve a 3-row count difference in isolation.
AMR rows: 1,000 Genomes 490, HGDP 62 (all-project); high_quality gives 487 1kGP AMR and 62 HGDP American.
The official Phase 3 AMR baseline is the 347 IDs from §2.1. All 347 are in the metadata; after the gnomAD high_quality flag 345 remain (CLM 92, MXL 64, PEL 85, PUR 104); HG01137 and HG01366 fail. The baseline is therefore ≤ 345 after QC/kinship filtering, and the final n is unknown until the joint callset’s own kinship/pedigree is applied. The other 143 cached AMR samples are the expanded related additions and are not an unrelated baseline.
Native GRCh38, not a Phase 3 lift-over. The joint callset is gnomAD v3.1.2 GRCh38 genome-wide; no liftover is required, unlike the GRCh37 Phase 3 VCFs.
This cached callset is a candidate, not a verified panel input: its sample identity and QC still need reconciliation, and a different callset could carry different QC and genotypes.




The HGDP American continent is represented by five indigenous populations — Pima, Maya, Karitiana, Surui and Colombian — with small, relatedness-heavy samples (the HGDP-CEPH panel has ~25 each before removing duplicate/relative pairs; e.g. Karitiana/Surui are strongly bottlenecked and homozygous) (HGDP resource, Cann et al. 2002, PubMed 11954565). 1kGP AMR (CLM/MXL/PEL/PUR) are modern admixed populations with tripartite Native-American/European/West-African ancestry. They are not interchangeable: the HGDP groups are baseline indigenous references; the 1kGP groups are contemporary admixed cohorts.




Pooling HGDP American Pima/Maya/Karitiana/Surui/Colombian with 1kGP CLM/MXL/PEL/PUR into one “AMR” panel is a scientific-suitability decision, not a categorical invalidity. A four-population 1kGP AMR panel is itself a pool, and the registry’s ADR 0028/0039 ancestry alias matching would accept a declared pool just as it accepts that one. The concerns are instead:

A different LD regime. Bottlenecked, highly homozygous indigenous Amazonian groups and post-Columbian admixed urban cohorts have different long-range LD; a merged eigenbasis may not be the LD of any Analysis.
Auditability is not suitability. ADR alias matching can audit that the panel a release used matches its declaration; it cannot certify that the pooled LD is scientifically appropriate.
It needs its own policy and calibration. If HGDP American samples are ever pooled with 1kGP AMR, that must be an explicit, separately calibrated policy decision — not a default or an implicit side effect.

Recommendation: keep the HGDP American populations on a separate calibration axis and out of the primary AMR panel for now, but treat this as a policy/calibration question rather than a prohibition.



Propose a calibration-only AMR panel built from the official 347 Phase 3 AMR IDs (≤ 345 after gnomAD QC/kinship), sourced from the native-GRCh38 joint callset, and estimated on the existing block layout. Then decide production from measured calibration evidence, not from this proposal.
Rationale:

Start from the cached joint callset as a candidate. It contains the 347 Phase 3 AMR IDs, but it is not yet a verified input: identity and QC need reconciliation (§2.3). A fresh 1kGP 30× callset may differ in QC, calls and source identity and would include 698 related samples; it is a genuine alternative, not automatically deeper or better, and the owner may prefer it.
n is small and the floor is not fixed. The official baseline is 347 (≤ 345 after QC), and the expanded 490/487 are not an unrelated baseline; the final n is unknown until kinship filtering is applied. The production AFR/EAS/SAS panels use 804/817/783 samples, so AMR is a calibration artifact whose quality must be measured (ADR 0020, ADR 0031). MAC ≥ 50 at n = 347 implies MAF ≥ 7.20%, so the variant-inclusion floor must be chosen by the sensitivity pilot (§6), not inherited.
Separate resource declaration. A new hgdp1kgp-hg38-amr-calibration/ resource mirrors hgdp1kgp-hg38-eur-calibration/ (status available, explicitly non-production, role: calibration). The production hgdp1kgp-hg38-ld policy stays unchanged (no AMR), so no silent policy expansion occurs.




ld_regions_hg38.tsv has no AMR rows. Options assessed:








Option
Basis
Assessment




A. Reuse EUR boundaries (1,357 blocks)
Matches the already-built HGDP+1kGP EUR calibration control’s layout
Recommended for calibration. The rationale is a fixed, matched control layout — comparable boundaries and a like-for-like comparison — not any assumption about AMR admixture proportions. Avoids re-deriving boundaries from n ≈ 347.


B. Reuse AFR boundaries (1,580)
Captures the African-ancestry component
Use as a sensitivity check where A and B differ; not the primary layout.


C. Union/intersection of A and B
Hybrid
Adds complexity before the primary calibration is understood. Defer.


D. Derive AMR boundaries de novo
Recombination structure of the AMR sample
Not chosen for the first calibration, not categorically rejected. Boundary detection at n ≈ 347 on an admixed sample is noisier than the pinned production set (ADR 0020) and breaks comparability, but de-novo boundaries remain a legitimate future option.



Critical distinction: reusing EUR block boundaries is not substituting the EUR panel. The LD/eigenvectors are still estimated from AMR samples. The boundary reuse must be declared explicitly in the resource; a reader must never be able to mistake this for the EUR panel. Boundary choice is labelled calibration until the owner approves a production policy.
What the EUR-boundary control cannot see. Reusing EUR boundaries may omit LD that crosses a EUR boundary in the admixed AMR sample, so a future production gate must include an explicit cross-block test (AMR-panel imputation across boundary edges, plus a de-novo-boundary sensitivity), not only within-block quality.










Concern
Proposal




Assembly / identifiers
Native GRCh38 joint callset; canonical ALID chr:pos:A1:A2, matching construct_block.canonical_alid (ADR 0020/0031)


Variant inclusion
Do not blindly copy MAC ≥ 50. At n = 347 diploid (694 chromosomes) MAC ≥ 50 implies MAF ≥ 7.20%; the optional expanded n = 487 only lowers that to 5.13% and is not the baseline. Propose a MAC/MAF sensitivity pilot over candidate floors (e.g. MAC 20/30/50) and adopt no lower cutoff without calibration evidence


Missingness
mean-impute (existing construct_block), invariant/all-missing variants dropped


Orientation
canonical EA = min(allele) with the existing reverse-code rule


Relatedness
apply the joint callset’s own pedigree/QC and the Koenig et al. 2024 kinship > 0.05 / maximal-independent-set prune (proposed reuse of their PCA QC choice); record the retained count; the baseline is the official 347 (≤ 345 by high_quality) and the final n is unknown until this runs


Sample inventory
start from the official Phase 3 AMR IDs (CLM 94/MXL 64/PEL 85/PUR 104; 345 after high_quality); the 143 expanded related AMR IDs are optional pruned sensitivity only; HGDP American excluded from the primary panel by default; a membership.json per panel


Assembly check
reuse verify_vcf (GRCh38 header) and verify_index; no liftover


Provenance
every block’s .provenance.json (n individuals, input/retained variants, MAC, cumvar, components, achieved variance)



MAC/MAF is the sharpest open methodological question. The existing AFR/EAS/SAS panels use MAC ≥ 50 because MAC tracks estimation precision at n ≈ 800 while MAF would not (ADR 0020). At AMR’s ~345 samples the same MAC floor is a ≥ 7.20% MAF filter, and a smaller retained n raises it further, which could exclude exactly the lower-frequency variants completion needs. The pilot must compare floors rather than inherit one, and must state the chosen floor’s MAF-equivalent and retained variant counts per block. No lowered cutoff is adopted by this proposal.
The sample-metadata TSV is CRLF-terminated; any consumer must normalise line endings before comparing high_quality (found while measuring §2.3), and must not infer relatedness from the high_quality flag alone.



The panel must satisfy the existing core public contract, not invent a new one:

Representation: eigendecomposition, not an LD matrix (core ADR 0031). load_ld_eigenvectors reads .ldeig.npz; the matrix is optional/dead weight.
Components: variance-driven, cumulative target 0.99. The existing component_floor of 250 is a minimum request limited by available rank, not a mathematical guarantee that every block has ≥ 250 components at n ≈ 347; record the achieved component count and variance per block, and require the consumer’s 0.9 truncation to be satisfiable from stored data (find_underresolved_blocks.py zero under-resolved blocks at 0.9).
PSD: the thin-SVD construction yields eigenvalues = s² ≥ 0 by construction, so PSD is structural; the pilot still asserts non-negative eigenvalues and finite vectors.
resource.yaml: kind: ld_panel, ancestry: [AMR], genome_build: GRCh38, variant_id_convention: "chr:pos:a1:a2", ld.block_file, ld.representation, ld.components_retained: variance_driven, ld.components_cumvar_target: 0.99, source.n_individuals.AMR, source.variant_inclusion (the calibrated MAC/MAF floor, with its MAF-equivalent recorded), source.population_map (calibration policy), source.generator, and an explicit description that the block boundaries are reused from the EUR production layout and the panel is calibration, not production.
Membership policy: a separate calibration mapping (e.g. populations_to_superpop.amr-calibration.tsv) so the production populations_to_superpop.tsv keeps no_AMR_panel until the owner changes it. make_membership.py’s hard-coded ("AFR","EAS","SAS","EUR") handle list would need an AMR entry in the calibration path only.





Pilot scope. One to five blocks (mirror the EUR control’s 5-block, 2,514-analysis design), sufficient to measure wall time, peak RSS, block success rate and eigenvalue conditioning. No genome-wide build.
Integrity. Per-block provenance present and positive; find_underresolved_blocks.py --thresh 0.9 reports zero; sample counts match membership.json; the cache-vs-release sample discrepancy (§2.3) is reconciled first.
Scientific validation. A paired held-out comparison on AMR-assigned MVP Analyses, mirroring compare_eur_imputation.py/evaluate_calibration.py: compare AMR-panel imputation quality against a pre-registered baseline with an explicit acceptable mean loss. The honest baseline is an AMR-aware comparison (e.g. held-out ALIDs within the AMR cohort), not the EUR panel silently standing in for AMR.
Representation trade-offs to report. 1kGP-only vs 1kGP+HGDP (separate vs pooled); EUR-boundary vs AFR-boundary sensitivity including an explicit cross-block test at boundary edges; per-population versus pooled AMR estimates; MAC/MAF-floor sensitivity (MAC 20/30/50 with the MAF-equivalent and retained-variant counts); and the effect of relatedness pruning on n and on block conditioning.
Budget. Measure in the pilot (wall time, peak RSS, scratch per block, job count) and record it with the evidence. Do not infer the budget from core #254, which is a validation-memory workstream, not an LD-panel measurement.





No European-panel substitution for AMR completion.
No full production AMR panel or Store build before owner approval.
No silent change to the production no_AMR_panel policy.
No download, genotype construction or association read in this proposal.
No change to the AFR/EAS/SAS/EUR block file or the existing panels.





Approve a calibration AMR panel from the existing gnomAD HGDP+1kGP cache using 1kGP CLM/MXL/PEL/PUR (recommended), or require a fresh 1kGP 30× download, or defer AMR completion.
HGDP American sample use: exclude from the primary panel (recommended), or build a separate HGDP-American-only sensitivity panel; never silently pool.
Block boundaries: adopt reused EUR boundaries for calibration (recommended), with AFR-boundary sensitivity; or commission AMR boundary derivation.
Production gate: the minimum pilot evidence (n retained, blocks resolved, mean imputation-quality loss, peak RSS) required before AMR completion is declared production-suitable, and who signs it off.
Acceptability: the measured retained AMR n is the primary baseline of at most 345 (unknown after kinship pruning), not 487. If that is inadequate for a production panel, the Reference-Completed release remains blocked — a missing reference is not an observed-only epic success.
Variant floor: the MAC/MAF floor adopted after the sensitivity pilot (no lowered cutoff without calibration), and whether a floor that implies a high MAF is acceptable for AMR completion.




This proposal answers the owner’s AMR reference question recorded on the epic: https://github.com/opengwas/opengwasdb-stores/issues/232#issuecomment-6133854434. It is submitted for independent review before any owner approval, and no panel build is authorised by writing it.




Primary Phase 3 sample panel (source of the 347 counts): https://ftp.1000genomes.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/ftp/release/20130502/integrated_call_samples_v3.20130502.ALL.panel (55,156 bytes; SHA-256 b4023dc6ee2d62ee89c8d4d347db4d348e65518d66d346574cdae7a4bbd76858).
IGSR Phase 3 collection (2,504 unrelated, 26 populations): https://www.internationalgenome.org/data-portal/data-collection/phase-3
Byrska-Bishop et al. 2022, Cell 185, 3426–3440 (3,202 = 2,504 unrelated + 698 related; 602 trios; GRCh38); DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2022.08.004, PMID 36055201, PMC9439720: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36055201/
IGSR 30× high-coverage GRCh38 collection: https://www.internationalgenome.org/data-portal/data-collection/30x-high-coverage
IGSR population pages (CLM/MXL/PEL/PUR): https://www.internationalgenome.org/data-portal/population/CLM, https://www.internationalgenome.org/data-portal/population/MXL, https://www.internationalgenome.org/data-portal/population/PEL, https://www.internationalgenome.org/data-portal/population/PUR
IGSR FAQ (relatedness/pedigrees): https://www.internationalgenome.org/faq/
gnomAD HGDP+1kGP download availability: https://gnomad.broadinstitute.org/downloads#v3-hgdp-1kg
Koenig et al. 2024, Genome Research 34(5):796–809 (HGDP+1kGP sample QC and relatedness: raw 4,150 → 4,117 → 4,094; 3,419 unrelated + 698 related at the 4,117-sample PCA stage; 3,400 inferred unrelated in the final 4,094); DOI 10.1101/gr.278378.123, PMID 38749656, PMC11216312: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11216312/
HGDP-CEPH resource: https://www.hagsc.org/hgdp/
Cann et al. 2002, “A human genome diversity cell line panel”, Science 296(5566):261–262; DOI 10.1126/science.296.5566.261b, PMID 11954565: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11954565/
Owner AMR-reference request (epic comment): https://github.com/opengwas/opengwasdb-stores/issues/232#issuecomment-6133854434
Core LD-panel contract: docs/adr/0031-ld-panels-store-eigendecompositions.md in opengwas/opengwasdb.
Registry decisions: ADR 0020 (non-EUR panels), ADR 0028 (ancestry-matched completion), ADR 0039 (region identity and ancestry refusal), ADR 0019 (Reference-AF/effect-scale validation).

The registry currently declares no AMR panel. Two facts make that a blocker rather than an opt-out:

resources/reference-resources/hgdp1kgp-hg38-ld/resource.yaml declares ancestry: [AFR, EAS, SAS]; its description says Analyses assigned AMR/MID/NAF “remain observed-only” until a panel exists.
resources/reference-resources/hgdp1kgp-hg38-ld/populations_to_superpop.tsv maps CLM, MXL, PEL, PUR (1kGP Admixed American) and Pima, Maya, Karitiana, Surui, Colombian (HGDP American) to excluded / no_AMR_panel, and ld_regions_hg38.tsv (host: /data/opengwasdb/reference/hgdp1kgp-hg38/ld_regions_hg38.tsv) defines block boundaries for AFR, EAS, EUR and SAS only.

So the current behaviour is correct-by-design (ADR 0020), but it cannot satisfy #229. docs/epic-232-execution.md (orchestrator-owned, not modified here) already records: “#229 needs an explicitly suitable LD resource; HGDP resource declares AFR/EAS/SAS, not AMR. Missing reference is not observed-only success.”
This proposal answers the owner’s question, “1kg?”, by evaluating the candidate sample sources and recommending a calibration design.

title: AMR Reference-Completion LD panel: a calibration proposal
text:
The authority for Phase 3 sample counts is the official IGSR sample panel integrated_call_samples_v3.20130502.ALL.panel (55,156 bytes; SHA-256 b4023dc6ee2d62ee89c8d4d347db4d348e65518d66d346574cdae7a4bbd76858), not a search summary. Verified from that file: 2,504 samples total, of which 347 are AMR. The four AMR populations and their Phase 3 counts:



Population
Phase 3 samples
Region




CLM (Colombians, Medellín)
94
AMR


MXL (Mexican Ancestry, Los Angeles)
64
AMR


PEL (Peruvians, Lima)
85
AMR


PUR (Puerto Ricans)
104
AMR


Total
347




The 347 total is verified from the panel file, not assumed. Phase 3 is the 2,504-sample panel — the “original unrelated” baseline cited in §2.2 — and the 698 related samples / 602 trios belong to the separate 3,202 high-coverage expansion, so they must not be attributed to these 347. The Phase 3 VCFs are GRCh37 and would need liftover, so they are cited for counts only and are not the proposed genotype source (IGSR Phase 3, IGSR FAQ).



The primary description is Byrska-Bishop et al., Cell 185, 3426–3440 (2022): 3,202 samples, 602 complete parent–child trios, 2,504 original unrelated + 698 additional related samples, re-sequenced to ~30× and aligned to GRCh38 (PubMed 36055201, DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2022.08.004; IGSR 30× collection). Filtering the related subset is advised for analyses that assume independence; the extra depth improves variant discovery, not sample independence. A panel built from all 3,202 would include 698 non-independent individuals.



The registry already acquires this joint GRCh38 genome-wide callset (acquire_hgdp1kgp.py, gnomAD v3.1.2). The primary description of the subset’s sample QC and relatedness handling is Koenig et al. 2024, Genome Research 34(5):796–809 (DOI 10.1101/gr.278378.123; PMID 38749656; PMC11216312). Their pipeline reduces the raw source 4,150 → 4,117 after 33 QC failures → 4,094 after 23 ancestry outliers; the published 4,094 set contains 3,400 inferred unrelated individuals. The 3,419 unrelated + 698 related partition belongs to the earlier 4,117-sample PCA stage, not the final 4,094 set. The harmonized callset is genome-wide on GRCh38 (primary paper; download availability). The kinship > 0.05 / maximal-independent-set prune reused for the LD subset here is a proposed reuse of the paper’s PCA-relatedness QC choice, not a claim that upstream calibrated that threshold for LD-panel construction, and the choice is this pilot’s pending owner approval.
Measured directly from the host’s cached /data/opengwasdb/reference/hgdp1kgp-hg38/source/cohort_populations.tsv (sample metadata only — no genotype read):

The cache has 4,151 rows = 3,202 1kGP + 948 HGDP + 1 control; high_quality == true is 4,097 = 3,166 1kGP + 931 HGDP. This named local high_quality set is not the same selection as the published 4,094: the paper’s pipeline is raw 4,150 → 4,117 (33 QC) → 4,094 (23 ancestry outliers). The task is therefore to reconcile exact QC and ancestry-outlier membership against the paper’s selection, not to resolve a 3-row count difference in isolation.
AMR rows: 1,000 Genomes 490, HGDP 62 (all-project); high_quality gives 487 1kGP AMR and 62 HGDP American.
The official Phase 3 AMR baseline is the 347 IDs from §2.1. All 347 are in the metadata; after the gnomAD high_quality flag 345 remain (CLM 92, MXL 64, PEL 85, PUR 104); HG01137 and HG01366 fail. The baseline is therefore ≤ 345 after QC/kinship filtering, and the final n is unknown until the joint callset’s own kinship/pedigree is applied. The other 143 cached AMR samples are the expanded related additions and are not an unrelated baseline.
Native GRCh38, not a Phase 3 lift-over. The joint callset is gnomAD v3.1.2 GRCh38 genome-wide; no liftover is required, unlike the GRCh37 Phase 3 VCFs.
This cached callset is a candidate, not a verified panel input: its sample identity and QC still need reconciliation, and a different callset could carry different QC and genotypes.




The HGDP American continent is represented by five indigenous populations — Pima, Maya, Karitiana, Surui and Colombian — with small, relatedness-heavy samples (the HGDP-CEPH panel has ~25 each before removing duplicate/relative pairs; e.g. Karitiana/Surui are strongly bottlenecked and homozygous) (HGDP resource, Cann et al. 2002, PubMed 11954565). 1kGP AMR (CLM/MXL/PEL/PUR) are modern admixed populations with tripartite Native-American/European/West-African ancestry. They are not interchangeable: the HGDP groups are baseline indigenous references; the 1kGP groups are contemporary admixed cohorts.
crumbs: AMR Reference-Completion LD panel: a calibration proposal

title: AMR Reference-Completion LD panel: a calibration proposal
text:
Pooling HGDP American Pima/Maya/Karitiana/Surui/Colombian with 1kGP CLM/MXL/PEL/PUR into one “AMR” panel is a scientific-suitability decision, not a categorical invalidity. A four-population 1kGP AMR panel is itself a pool, and the registry’s ADR 0028/0039 ancestry alias matching would accept a declared pool just as it accepts that one. The concerns are instead:

A different LD regime. Bottlenecked, highly homozygous indigenous Amazonian groups and post-Columbian admixed urban cohorts have different long-range LD; a merged eigenbasis may not be the LD of any Analysis.
Auditability is not suitability. ADR alias matching can audit that the panel a release used matches its declaration; it cannot certify that the pooled LD is scientifically appropriate.
It needs its own policy and calibration. If HGDP American samples are ever pooled with 1kGP AMR, that must be an explicit, separately calibrated policy decision — not a default or an implicit side effect.

Recommendation: keep the HGDP American populations on a separate calibration axis and out of the primary AMR panel for now, but treat this as a policy/calibration question rather than a prohibition.
crumbs: AMR Reference-Completion LD panel: a calibration proposal

title: AMR Reference-Completion LD panel: a calibration proposal
text:
Propose a calibration-only AMR panel built from the official 347 Phase 3 AMR IDs (≤ 345 after gnomAD QC/kinship), sourced from the native-GRCh38 joint callset, and estimated on the existing block layout. Then decide production from measured calibration evidence, not from this proposal.
Rationale:

Start from the cached joint callset as a candidate. It contains the 347 Phase 3 AMR IDs, but it is not yet a verified input: identity and QC need reconciliation (§2.3). A fresh 1kGP 30× callset may differ in QC, calls and source identity and would include 698 related samples; it is a genuine alternative, not automatically deeper or better, and the owner may prefer it.
n is small and the floor is not fixed. The official baseline is 347 (≤ 345 after QC), and the expanded 490/487 are not an unrelated baseline; the final n is unknown until kinship filtering is applied. The production AFR/EAS/SAS panels use 804/817/783 samples, so AMR is a calibration artifact whose quality must be measured (ADR 0020, ADR 0031). MAC ≥ 50 at n = 347 implies MAF ≥ 7.20%, so the variant-inclusion floor must be chosen by the sensitivity pilot (§6), not inherited.
Separate resource declaration. A new hgdp1kgp-hg38-amr-calibration/ resource mirrors hgdp1kgp-hg38-eur-calibration/ (status available, explicitly non-production, role: calibration). The production hgdp1kgp-hg38-ld policy stays unchanged (no AMR), so no silent policy expansion occurs.

title: AMR Reference-Completion LD panel: a calibration proposal
text:
ld_regions_hg38.tsv has no AMR rows. Options assessed:








Option
Basis
Assessment




A. Reuse EUR boundaries (1,357 blocks)
Matches the already-built HGDP+1kGP EUR calibration control’s layout
Recommended for calibration. The rationale is a fixed, matched control layout — comparable boundaries and a like-for-like comparison — not any assumption about AMR admixture proportions. Avoids re-deriving boundaries from n ≈ 347.


B. Reuse AFR boundaries (1,580)
Captures the African-ancestry component
Use as a sensitivity check where A and B differ; not the primary layout.


C. Union/intersection of A and B
Hybrid
Adds complexity before the primary calibration is understood. Defer.


D. Derive AMR boundaries de novo
Recombination structure of the AMR sample
Not chosen for the first calibration, not categorically rejected. Boundary detection at n ≈ 347 on an admixed sample is noisier than the pinned production set (ADR 0020) and breaks comparability, but de-novo boundaries remain a legitimate future option.



Critical distinction: reusing EUR block boundaries is not substituting the EUR panel. The LD/eigenvectors are still estimated from AMR samples. The boundary reuse must be declared explicitly in the resource; a reader must never be able to mistake this for the EUR panel. Boundary choice is labelled calibration until the owner approves a production policy.
What the EUR-boundary control cannot see. Reusing EUR boundaries may omit LD that crosses a EUR boundary in the admixed AMR sample, so a future production gate must include an explicit cross-block test (AMR-panel imputation across boundary edges, plus a de-novo-boundary sensitivity), not only within-block quality.

title: AMR Reference-Completion LD panel: a calibration proposal
text:
Concern
Proposal




Assembly / identifiers
Native GRCh38 joint callset; canonical ALID chr:pos:A1:A2, matching construct_block.canonical_alid (ADR 0020/0031)


Variant inclusion
Do not blindly copy MAC ≥ 50. At n = 347 diploid (694 chromosomes) MAC ≥ 50 implies MAF ≥ 7.20%; the optional expanded n = 487 only lowers that to 5.13% and is not the baseline. Propose a MAC/MAF sensitivity pilot over candidate floors (e.g. MAC 20/30/50) and adopt no lower cutoff without calibration evidence


Missingness
mean-impute (existing construct_block), invariant/all-missing variants dropped


Orientation
canonical EA = min(allele) with the existing reverse-code rule


Relatedness
apply the joint callset’s own pedigree/QC and the Koenig et al. 2024 kinship > 0.05 / maximal-independent-set prune (proposed reuse of their PCA QC choice); record the retained count; the baseline is the official 347 (≤ 345 by high_quality) and the final n is unknown until this runs


Sample inventory
start from the official Phase 3 AMR IDs (CLM 94/MXL 64/PEL 85/PUR 104; 345 after high_quality); the 143 expanded related AMR IDs are optional pruned sensitivity only; HGDP American excluded from the primary panel by default; a membership.json per panel


Assembly check
reuse verify_vcf (GRCh38 header) and verify_index; no liftover


Provenance
every block’s .provenance.json (n individuals, input/retained variants, MAC, cumvar, components, achieved variance)



MAC/MAF is the sharpest open methodological question. The existing AFR/EAS/SAS panels use MAC ≥ 50 because MAC tracks estimation precision at n ≈ 800 while MAF would not (ADR 0020). At AMR’s ~345 samples the same MAC floor is a ≥ 7.20% MAF filter, and a smaller retained n raises it further, which could exclude exactly the lower-frequency variants completion needs. The pilot must compare floors rather than inherit one, and must state the chosen floor’s MAF-equivalent and retained variant counts per block. No lowered cutoff is adopted by this proposal.
The sample-metadata TSV is CRLF-terminated; any consumer must normalise line endings before comparing high_quality (found while measuring §2.3), and must not infer relatedness from the high_quality flag alone.

title: AMR Reference-Completion LD panel: a calibration proposal
text:
The panel must satisfy the existing core public contract, not invent a new one:

Representation: eigendecomposition, not an LD matrix (core ADR 0031). load_ld_eigenvectors reads .ldeig.npz; the matrix is optional/dead weight.
Components: variance-driven, cumulative target 0.99. The existing component_floor of 250 is a minimum request limited by available rank, not a mathematical guarantee that every block has ≥ 250 components at n ≈ 347; record the achieved component count and variance per block, and require the consumer’s 0.9 truncation to be satisfiable from stored data (find_underresolved_blocks.py zero under-resolved blocks at 0.9).
PSD: the thin-SVD construction yields eigenvalues = s² ≥ 0 by construction, so PSD is structural; the pilot still asserts non-negative eigenvalues and finite vectors.
resource.yaml: kind: ld_panel, ancestry: [AMR], genome_build: GRCh38, variant_id_convention: "chr:pos:a1:a2", ld.block_file, ld.representation, ld.components_retained: variance_driven, ld.components_cumvar_target: 0.99, source.n_individuals.AMR, source.variant_inclusion (the calibrated MAC/MAF floor, with its MAF-equivalent recorded), source.population_map (calibration policy), source.generator, and an explicit description that the block boundaries are reused from the EUR production layout and the panel is calibration, not production.
Membership policy: a separate calibration mapping (e.g. populations_to_superpop.amr-calibration.tsv) so the production populations_to_superpop.tsv keeps no_AMR_panel until the owner changes it. make_membership.py’s hard-coded ("AFR","EAS","SAS","EUR") handle list would need an AMR entry in the calibration path only.
crumbs: AMR Reference-Completion LD panel: a calibration proposal

title: AMR Reference-Completion LD panel: a calibration proposal
text:
Pilot scope. One to five blocks (mirror the EUR control’s 5-block, 2,514-analysis design), sufficient to measure wall time, peak RSS, block success rate and eigenvalue conditioning. No genome-wide build.
Integrity. Per-block provenance present and positive; find_underresolved_blocks.py --thresh 0.9 reports zero; sample counts match membership.json; the cache-vs-release sample discrepancy (§2.3) is reconciled first.
Scientific validation. A paired held-out comparison on AMR-assigned MVP Analyses, mirroring compare_eur_imputation.py/evaluate_calibration.py: compare AMR-panel imputation quality against a pre-registered baseline with an explicit acceptable mean loss. The honest baseline is an AMR-aware comparison (e.g. held-out ALIDs within the AMR cohort), not the EUR panel silently standing in for AMR.
Representation trade-offs to report. 1kGP-only vs 1kGP+HGDP (separate vs pooled); EUR-boundary vs AFR-boundary sensitivity including an explicit cross-block test at boundary edges; per-population versus pooled AMR estimates; MAC/MAF-floor sensitivity (MAC 20/30/50 with the MAF-equivalent and retained-variant counts); and the effect of relatedness pruning on n and on block conditioning.
Budget. Measure in the pilot (wall time, peak RSS, scratch per block, job count) and record it with the evidence. Do not infer the budget from core #254, which is a validation-memory workstream, not an LD-panel measurement.

title: AMR Reference-Completion LD panel: a calibration proposal
text:
No European-panel substitution for AMR completion.
No full production AMR panel or Store build before owner approval.
No silent change to the production no_AMR_panel policy.
No download, genotype construction or association read in this proposal.
No change to the AFR/EAS/SAS/EUR block file or the existing panels.

title: AMR Reference-Completion LD panel: a calibration proposal
text:
Approve a calibration AMR panel from the existing gnomAD HGDP+1kGP cache using 1kGP CLM/MXL/PEL/PUR (recommended), or require a fresh 1kGP 30× download, or defer AMR completion.
HGDP American sample use: exclude from the primary panel (recommended), or build a separate HGDP-American-only sensitivity panel; never silently pool.
Block boundaries: adopt reused EUR boundaries for calibration (recommended), with AFR-boundary sensitivity; or commission AMR boundary derivation.
Production gate: the minimum pilot evidence (n retained, blocks resolved, mean imputation-quality loss, peak RSS) required before AMR completion is declared production-suitable, and who signs it off.
Acceptability: the measured retained AMR n is the primary baseline of at most 345 (unknown after kinship pruning), not 487. If that is inadequate for a production panel, the Reference-Completed release remains blocked — a missing reference is not an observed-only epic success.
Variant floor: the MAC/MAF floor adopted after the sensitivity pilot (no lowered cutoff without calibration), and whether a floor that implies a high MAF is acceptable for AMR completion.

title: Association Coverage is declared in the Release Bundle, in one vocabulary
text:
Association Coverage tells a reader which associations a Store Release holds. It was wrong or missing at every step. The glossary listed six informal values; a release config declared one, in two different spellings; and the value never reached the Release Bundle, so it was lost before the builder and the registry could see it. ADR 0029 had removed association_coverage from release.yaml because no code read it. Two things have changed since, and both reverse that reason: the Analysis Catalog reads it and shows it to users (#313, ADR 0039), and opengwasdb#298 makes it a build input, so the value opengwasdb writes per layout becomes a value the release declares.


It is declared, once, in release.yaml. association_coverage is a required key of the Release Bundle (RELEASE_REQUIRED_KEYS), and bundle.check() refuses a value outside the vocabulary or a value that is not a string. Bundle.association_coverage answers a reader that has already gated on check(): the Analysis Catalog refuses an errored bundle before it reads any fact. It still raises rather than answering a default, as Bundle.trial does, so a reader that has not gated fails loudly instead of reading an absent or unknown value as, say, gwas, which would show a layout’s coverage as the Store’s (CONTRIBUTING: never substitute data).
One vocabulary, and it is opengwasdb’s too. The owner’s decision of 22 Oct 2026 sets four values, in ogstores.bundle.ASSOCIATION_COVERAGES:







Value
What the Store holds




gwas
every association the source reports, genome-wide


cis
a cis window around each Analysis’s target, and nothing else


cis_and_signals
a cis window plus significant signals elsewhere


signals_only
significant signals and their flanks, with no cis window



gwas replaces the registry’s full_gwas and opengwasdb’s full; cis_and_signals replaces cis_plus_signals. cis and signals_only name Stores that were previously mislabelled by their layout.
A region policy declares only two of them. cis_and_signals and signals_only (REGION_POLICY_COVERAGES): a policy selects regions, while gwas and cis describe a Store built from every source row or from cis windows alone, which no filter produces.
A frozen manifest is read, never rewritten. Sun 2018’s Acquisition Manifest records cis_plus_signals in its checksummed region-policy lineage. Rewriting it would break inventory_tsv_sha256 and the freeze and preflight checksums, so the retired spelling is aliased on read, through one function (manifest_generation.region_filter.canonical_association_coverage), and preflight’s “filtered to exactly this policy” comparison still matches. A legacy full in a Store’s manifest.json likewise reads as gwas (opengwasdb#298), so no published Store is rewritten.
Backfilling it is not a new Store Release. It is a descriptive fact about a release, so ADR 0004 (an accepted bundle is not edited) does not make the backfill a new release, and no identity or checksum reads it: the amendment check compares a plan’s argv and the manifest a Store was built from, and release.yaml is neither. The builder receives the declared value. opengwas/opengwasdb#298 makes coverage a build input, and this repository’s pin moved past it (#341): plan() appends --association-coverage <release.yaml value> to every Ragged build step, from the declaration and never from the Build Recipe, whose change would make a new Store Release (ADR 0004). The Dense and Hybrid argv name no flag, because gwas is their default and the only value their layout can carry, which bundle.check() now enforces. register refuses a publication whose producing step reports a coverage other than the declared one, naming both values, and records null when the step reports none.
It qualifies ADR 0037’s exact-argv amendment check, once. A Store published before #341 has a build record whose argv names no coverage, while the plan now names the declared one; read as a change, that would refuse the single-id completion #224 wants for such a Store, for a reason that is not a rebuild. The flag only names what the old builder hard-coded, the Store’s data does not change, and the owner’s pre-release decision on opengwas/opengwasdb#298 applies such metadata changes in place (#359 relabels the manifests). So the amendment check tolerates exactly one difference: a recorded argv that names no --association-coverage matches a planned argv that differs by the declaration-derived pair alone. A record that names a coverage – another value included – is compared whole, as is every other token, and the bundle’s manifest membership is still compared byte for byte. The exception is one-directional: a record that predates the flag cannot witness the value it was built at, so the completion’s own report is what holds the release to its declaration, which register enforces.




Every committed bundle declares its true coverage; pixi run bundle-check requires it and OGS-00006 says signals_only.
The amendment check tolerates that one difference and nothing else (see above), so a published Ragged Store whose build record predates the flag will gain its own completion without a rebuild once single-id Ragged completion lands. That layout is still refused today, by SINGLE_ID_COMPLETION_LAYOUTS in src/ogstores/plan.py; lifting the gate is #336 in epic #232.
Manifest Generation requires association_coverage in every release config, writes it after label: in the candidate release.yaml, and refuses a config without one. For a region-filtered config it must equal region_policy.association_coverage exactly: a release config and a bundle take only the four current values, and canonical_association_coverage is only for reading frozen historical evidence.
The Analysis Catalog reads release.yaml for stores.association_coverage, the coverage count dimension and the summary report; it no longer reads the Validation Record’s observed.association_coverage, which stays the value opengwasdb reports (ADR 0039 is amended accordingly).
docs/spec/release-config.md, docs/spec/analysis-catalog.md, docs/release-metadata-schema.md and CONTEXT.md’s Association Coverage entry state the four values.

Amends ADR 0029. association_coverage is restored to release.yaml; the other nine keys ADR 0029 removed stay removed, and its reasons for removing them are untouched.
