title: The Analysis Catalog is a generated, versioned database over Release Bundles
text:
The API, the website and the R and Python clients (opengwas/opengwasdb#93, #94) need to find every Analysis across every Store Release, and nothing lists them: each built Store carries its own analyses.tsv, frozen at build time, and the registry carries Release Bundles. Which Store Releases to serve, which identifier names an Analysis across Stores, and what the collection holds had no recorded answer. The owner expects multiple millions of Analyses; decided in the design of epic #313 on 21 Oct 2026.
The Analysis Catalog answers them: the service-catalogue layer ADR 0008 reserved and left to a later decision, a generated, versioned SQLite database that one operator command rebuilds from the Release Bundles on dev.


Package. The catalog is a top-level package, src/analysis_catalog/, beside ogstores, manifest_generation and curation, and it reads Release Bundles through the Release Bundle contract in ogstores. Nothing in ogstores imports it, so the catalog can move to the API’s repository when the API takes it over. It reads only Release Bundles and never opens a Store, like the master list (ADR 0023). It never decides which Analyses a Store holds: a Store’s membership is its Release Manifest’s answer, and the catalog’s filter reuses it (ADR 0025).
The serving policy lives here and not in the registry, because ADR 0008 puts default served releases in ADR 0008’s service-catalogue layer. The registry keeps recording facts about releases; the catalog decides what those facts mean for serving.
Inputs. Membership is the Release Manifest’s rows that are not excluded from build — the same filter as ADR 0025’s derived build manifest. An excluded row stays in the bundle as an audit row and never enters the catalog. Store-level facts come from release.yaml, build.yaml and the Validation Record. Analysis metadata comes from the Release Manifest, so the bundle, including any Release Erratum, is authoritative over a Store’s frozen analyses.tsv. A built Store’s copy goes stale: OGS-00001 still carries the ENSEMBL: terms the #141 erratum removed, and OGS-00006’s Store lacks the original_sd its bundle has for all 1,400 rows.
Registry fields it needs are added as release facts, not serving decisions, so no served flag appears. release.yaml gains trial and superseded_by (#321) and association_coverage (#341, ADR 0040); the Validation Record gains reference_assembly (#322); and its n_associations comes from a count OpenGWASDB reports or is null — register’s Dense fallback of n_variants × n_analyses counts matrix cells, not associations, and is removed.
Identifier. An Analysis is named <store_id>:<analysis_id>, for example OGS-00011:GCST000998.

It is unique by construction: OpenGWASDB refuses a duplicate analysis_id within a Store, and analysis_id never contains : (#319), so it always splits into exactly two parts, the Store and the Analysis within it.
An Analysis never moves between Store ids. When its Store is superseded or withdrawn, the catalog keeps its identifier resolvable, so a saved identifier names the same row forever.
A retired Store’s Analyses stay as placeholder rows: resolvable, not listed. A superseded Store’s rows name their successor in superseded_by; a withdrawn Store has no successor, so its rows carry none. A client holding one of their identifiers gets the explanation instead of “not found”.

Serving policy. Every registered Store Release is recorded with a decision and its reason, so “why is this Store not in the catalog?” is answerable from the catalog itself. The rules apply in this order, and the first that matches decides:

bundle.check() returns errors — refused
Trial Store Release — excluded
Access Posture is embargoed — excluded
Release Status is candidate, accepted or built — excluded
Release Status is superseded or withdrawn, and the Validation Record is not passed or passed_with_warnings — excluded
Release Status is validated, and Access Posture is neither public nor controlled — refused
Release Status is validated, superseded or withdrawn, and observed.n_analyses is missing or not an integer — refused
the admitted Release Manifest count differs from observed.n_analyses — refused
a manifest or Validation Record value cannot be stored exactly, or check() tolerates ‘:’ in an analysis_id under #319 — refused
Release Status is superseded or withdrawn — placeholder
Release Status is validated — listed

Rule 5 excludes, and does not refuse, a retired release with no passing Validation Record: it was never served, so there is no fault to report. A retired release that did pass, but records no count, is refused by rule 7 as a validated one is.
The order matters because the first two rules are not about Release Status: a Trial Store Release or an embargoed Store is never resolvable, not even after it is retired, so none of its Analyses can leak out through a placeholder row. A listed controlled Store carries its Access Posture so that the service enforces access itself; the catalog states the posture and does not enforce it (ADR 0008). A refused Store fails loudly: the catalog never lists a membership the Store does not hold, and a missing count is an absence, never a match.
Schema and build. Two main tables and supporting ones, in one SQLite file: stores, one row per listed or placeholder Store Release (an excluded or refused Store has none, so nothing excluded is discoverable there); analyses, one row per Analysis of a listed or placeholder Store, with listed telling them apart; selection, the decision and reason per registered Store Release; catalog_meta, the build’s own facts; and derived tables and indexes for counts, search and paging.

Store-level facts are stored once, never repeated per Analysis, and no Store path is stored: it is a pure function of the id (ADR 0030).
Build internals are left out — source_file, checksums, inclusion_reason, exclude_from_build, analysis_index — because they locate and justify a build input, which is not what a reader queries.
Numeric columns are typed, and analysis_label falls back to source_label, because the MVP bundles have no analysis_label. label_from_source records each fallback, so the summary report can count Analyses with no curated label.
The type of an Analysis is a set of columns of analyses, derived once at build time from fields the row already holds: outcome_type (binary or continuous) from stored_effect_scale and sample_size_kind, binary when either says so (case_control or log_or), continuous when the scale is sd and the kind is any vocabulary value but case_control (the sample size’s granularity does not change what standardised units mean, #362), NULL when neither field gives a reading; trait_class (phenotype or molecular) from context, tissue and trait_chr; and ancestry_category, Assigned Ancestry or META for an unassigned row whose Source Ancestry Label is exactly META. Genome-wide or cis is not derived: it is the Store Release’s declared Association Coverage (release.yaml, one of gwas, cis, cis_and_signals and signals_only), counted as it is and never relabelled, and never a layout’s default. The counts and the report read those columns, so a type is derived once and defined in one place.
A placeholder row is an analyses row with listed = 0. Listing, search and counts see only listed = 1, through the listed_analyses view, and the paging indexes are partial indexes over those rows, so a retired Store costs a listing nothing.

Every rebuild is a full rebuild into a fresh database, one Store’s rows at a time (so memory is set by the largest single Store’s manifest, not by the catalog), done in SQL, so a version is never a mixture of two inputs and a failed build leaves the previous version in place. The prototype’s raw SQL fold, measured on a replication of the real catalog at 5.07M rows, took 39 s for a 2.3 GB file, with lookups, full-text search and first pages under 1 ms, a 4M-row OFFSET at 65 ms and a filtered count at 59 ms. This builder validates and converts every row in Python, and has been measured only at 500k rows in one wide Store: about 25 s and 0.8 GB peak, with a no-op rebuild that reads no manifest row (a few seconds at that size, all of it hashing the files). It is not extrapolated beyond that. So the indexes support server-side paging, including keyset paging; counts per filter value are computed at build time, because a filtered count is the expensive query and only changes when the catalog does; and the full-text index is FTS5, over the label, ontology label, consortium and first author.
Versions and location. A version is a directory under <artifact-root>/catalog/versions/, and current is a symlink to it:
versions/<version>/
  catalog.sqlite
  stores.tsv
  analyses.tsv.gz
  summary.html
  report.md
current -> versions/<version>

The version is a hash of everything a decision depends on: every file of every registered Release Bundle, the list of registered store ids, the source of analysis_catalog (which includes the serving policy) and of ogstores (check() and Bundle), the installed opengwasdb’s version and commit (its reader parses the manifest), and the summary template. Decisions are a pure function of those inputs, so they are not hashed, and the version is known before any manifest row is read. The bundle inputs are wider than the selected bundles’ contents on purpose: bundle.check() reads every file of every bundle, so an edit to an excluded Store’s manifest can change its decision, and a change to a decision, from a bundle or from the code that reads it, must give a new version, or the reasons in selection go stale. A rebuild whose version already exists writes nothing and reads no manifest row: it reports the decisions recorded in that version’s selection.
A version is immutable and the last few are kept, so rollback is moving current back: a rebuild writes a new directory and swaps current atomically, no reader sees a half-written catalog, and nothing is reconstructed from git. The files and directories are fsynced before the rename and the swap, because an immutable version that a crash tore would never be rebuilt.
The catalog is a generated artifact under the Artifact Root with no Store id, because it belongs to no single Store Release. Bulk download is TSV.gz beside the SQLite file, so a client that wants every Analysis reads a flat file, and the API and website read current (#173).

Trigger. An operator runs the command on the host after a merge to dev, from a dedicated clean checkout of origin/dev, not a shared working checkout. The catalog depends only on bundles, so a rebuild then picks up everything merged: a Store Release Build publication alone changes nothing, and a Store enters the catalog when its reviewed validated edit merges. Automating the trigger is out of scope.
Summary report. A Quarto report is rendered into each version before current is swapped, and a failed render fails the rebuild, so a published version always has its report. Every number in it comes from the catalog’s own tables, so it cannot disagree with what the service serves. It covers the served Stores, the excluded and refused ones with their reasons, Analyses by Assigned Ancestry and by type, Trait Ontology Mapping coverage, the change since the previous version, and every total, where a total is shown as “unknown (k of n Stores report it)” whenever a Store reports none, so a partial sum is never presented as the total.



A bare global analysis_id, kept unique by a registry-wide check. Rejected. analysis_id is not a global key. Today’s overlaps are lineage and trial-then-full pairs, but gene-and-tissue identifiers (ENSG…::whole_blood) collide between eQTL sources, and the MVP dbGaP release re-serves GWAS Catalog GCST accessions. A registry-wide check would answer that by refusing the second Store: a legitimate Store’s membership would then depend on another Store’s, which is a decision about what a Store holds — the one thing the registry never makes.
Serving whatever is on disk rather than gating on Release Status. Rejected. Most of what is on disk is not ready: the prototype found OGS-00008–11 and OGS-00017 built but candidate or accepted with no publication.json, so a disk-driven selection listed 9,347 Analyses where a status-driven one listed 1,400. It would also serve Trial Store Releases and embargoed Stores, which nothing but metadata marks, and it fails the wrong way: an unreviewed publication becomes visible to users and nothing can say why. validated makes the reviewed edit that validates a release the decision to serve it. Disk membership is stale besides: OGS-00011’s published Store holds 148 Analyses its current bundle excludes.
Parquet as the served format. Rejected. The served file has to answer full-text search, server-side paging with a cursor, and per-filter counts, and the prototype’s one SQLite file met all three at 5.07M rows within a 39 s build and 2.3 GB. A Parquet dataset has no full-text index and no per-row addressing, so each of those queries would need a second, derived structure beside it, maintained in step with the first. It gains readers nothing either: bulk download is a plain TSV.gz, which any client can read without a columnar engine. Parquet remains a possible export alongside it, not the served store.




Association Coverage is the release’s declaration, not the builder’s report (#341). The catalog reads release.yaml for stores.association_coverage, the coverage count dimension and the summary report; the Validation Record’s observed.association_coverage stays what opengwasdb reported, and is not what the catalog serves. This ADR’s earlier statement that the Validation Record gains the field is superseded by ADR



CONTEXT.md gains Analysis Catalog, and the Store Registry entry’s _Avoid_: catalogue now forbids the word for the registry rather than for the catalog.
ADR 0008’s service-catalogue layer is now built and named. Its boundary is unchanged: routing, authorisation enforcement, billing, quotas and usage audit still belong to the service.
The catalog is empty today. The only validated Store Releases are OGS-00002 and OGS-00005, both Trial Store Releases, so the selection lists nothing until the API-ready Stores reach validated.
Per-Analysis facts that only a built Store holds are not carried, such as hit counts; a later version can take them from a sidecar of OpenGWASDB’s output.
The API, the website, the client packages, the trigger automation and a Parquet export are out of scope here. The code follows in the catalog’s command and versions (#323), its search, counts, paging indexes and placeholder rows (#324) and its summary report (#325). This adds no code.

title: The Analysis Catalog is a generated, versioned database over Release Bundles
text:
A bare global analysis_id, kept unique by a registry-wide check. Rejected. analysis_id is not a global key. Today’s overlaps are lineage and trial-then-full pairs, but gene-and-tissue identifiers (ENSG…::whole_blood) collide between eQTL sources, and the MVP dbGaP release re-serves GWAS Catalog GCST accessions. A registry-wide check would answer that by refusing the second Store: a legitimate Store’s membership would then depend on another Store’s, which is a decision about what a Store holds — the one thing the registry never makes.
Serving whatever is on disk rather than gating on Release Status. Rejected. Most of what is on disk is not ready: the prototype found OGS-00008–11 and OGS-00017 built but candidate or accepted with no publication.json, so a disk-driven selection listed 9,347 Analyses where a status-driven one listed 1,400. It would also serve Trial Store Releases and embargoed Stores, which nothing but metadata marks, and it fails the wrong way: an unreviewed publication becomes visible to users and nothing can say why. validated makes the reviewed edit that validates a release the decision to serve it. Disk membership is stale besides: OGS-00011’s published Store holds 148 Analyses its current bundle excludes.
Parquet as the served format. Rejected. The served file has to answer full-text search, server-side paging with a cursor, and per-filter counts, and the prototype’s one SQLite file met all three at 5.07M rows within a 39 s build and 2.3 GB. A Parquet dataset has no full-text index and no per-row addressing, so each of those queries would need a second, derived structure beside it, maintained in step with the first. It gains readers nothing either: bulk download is a plain TSV.gz, which any client can read without a columnar engine. Parquet remains a possible export alongside it, not the served store.
crumbs: The Analysis Catalog is a generated, versioned database over Release Bundles

title: The Analysis Catalog is a generated, versioned database over Release Bundles
text:
Association Coverage is the release’s declaration, not the builder’s report (#341). The catalog reads release.yaml for stores.association_coverage, the coverage count dimension and the summary report; the Validation Record’s observed.association_coverage stays what opengwasdb reported, and is not what the catalog serves. This ADR’s earlier statement that the Validation Record gains the field is superseded by ADR



CONTEXT.md gains Analysis Catalog, and the Store Registry entry’s _Avoid_: catalogue now forbids the word for the registry rather than for the catalog.
ADR 0008’s service-catalogue layer is now built and named. Its boundary is unchanged: routing, authorisation enforcement, billing, quotas and usage audit still belong to the service.
The catalog is empty today. The only validated Store Releases are OGS-00002 and OGS-00005, both Trial Store Releases, so the selection lists nothing until the API-ready Stores reach validated.
Per-Analysis facts that only a built Store holds are not carried, such as hit counts; a later version can take them from a sidecar of OpenGWASDB’s output.
The API, the website, the client packages, the trigger automation and a Parquet export are out of scope here. The code follows in the catalog’s command and versions (#323), its search, counts, paging indexes and placeholder rows (#324) and its summary report (#325). This adds no code.

title: Allele Orientation & Ancestry Gate Failure Modes
text:
This note summarizes the failure modes identified during ancestry assignment and effect-scale validation in the GWAS Catalog EUR Hybrid candidate release (OGS-00011), the empirical investigation of allele-orientation failures, and the classification of rescuable vs. non-rescuable studies.



Across the 4,783 selected ready Analyses in OGS-00011, the multi-gate admission rule (opengwasdb.ancestry.mixture.apply_gates, ADR 0028) evaluated the source allele frequencies against the 5.8M-variant Ancestry Reference Panel (ref_freqs.hg38.tsv.gz).
Gate Reason              Count    Description
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ok                       3,286    Passed all 5 gates (3,283 EUR, 3 non-EUR: 2 EAS, 1 AFR)
overlap                  1,119    < 5,000 overlapping reference variants (1,066 have 0 overlap / no AF)
residual                   226    NNLS RMS residual > 0.06 (median 0.246; noisy, admixed, or poor fit)
eaf_orientation            145    Strong negative frequency correlation (r <= -0.50, median -0.977)
proportion                   4    Dominant super-population proportion < 0.50 (heavily admixed)
margin                       2    Dominant margin over runner-up < 0.20 (near-tie between ancestries)
resolution_failed            1    GCST006329: duplicate 'beta' column in upstream header
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Total                    4,783




In addition to the 145 studies flagged with gate_reason == 'eaf_orientation', 17 studies flagged with gate_reason == 'residual' also exhibited negative frequency correlation (\(r < 0\)). In total, 162 studies showed inverted or discordant frequency orientation.


An inverted frequency correlation (\(r_{\text{EAF}} \approx -1.0\)) against the reference consensus arises from two fundamentally different upstream mechanisms:

Allele Column Swap (swap_alleles):

The authors or pipeline accidentally inverted the column headers effect_allele and other_allele in the summary statistics table.
Because the reported effect allele is actually the non-effect allele, the reported \(\beta\) has the opposite biological direction.
Remedy: Swapping effect_allele and other_allele values fixes the alleles, the frequency orientation, and restores the true biological direction of \(\beta\).

Frequency Column Mislabelling (flip_frequency):

The authors correctly assigned effect_allele, other_allele, and \(\beta\), but the frequency column represents the non-effect allele frequency (or unoriented minor allele frequency, \(1 - \text{EAF}\)).
Remedy: Transforming \(\text{EAF} \leftarrow 1.0 - \text{EAF}\) without modifying the alleles or \(\beta\).
Danger: Swapping the alleles in this group would corrupt \(\beta\), reversing the biological effect direction for all variants across the genome.







To objectively distinguish between swap_alleles and flip_frequency, each of the 162 target studies was matched against independent comparison studies from either OGS-00010 (UK Biobank 2,024 traits) or the 3,286 ok analyses in OGS-00011:

Top Variants: Extracted the top 100 variants (by p-value) from the target study.
Canonical ALID Alignment:

Both target and comparison betas were harmonised to the canonical variant ALID (chr:pos:a1:a2 where a1 < a2): \[\beta_{\text{ALID}} = \begin{cases} \beta & \text{if effect\_allele} = a_1 \\ -\beta & \text{if effect\_allele} = a_2 \end{cases}\]

Correlation: Calculated Pearson and Spearman correlation between aligned target and comparison effects:

\(r \ge 0.20 \implies\) flip_frequency (canonical betas agree; alleles are correct, only frequency was inverted)
\(r \le -0.20 \implies\) swap_alleles (canonical betas are inverted; alleles were swapped in the source file)
\(|r| < 0.20\) or low overlap \(\implies\) inconclusive

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
swap_alleles                       58                         61
flip_frequency                     33                         37
inconclusive                       15                         18
no_matching_trait                  39                         46
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
Total                             145                        162

title: AMR LD calibration pilot: evidence (#241)
text:
Status: calibration evidence for the owner’s AMR decision in #229. This is not a production panel, and the run claims no PASS. No production panel, population mapping, block definition or Store was changed.
Run: - Output: /data/opengwasdb/work/epic232/229/amr-pilot-20261021T234743Z/. The receipt and summary are copied to data/amr-ld-pilot-receipt.json and data/amr-ld-pilot-summary.json. - Revision 0b11759, branch ticket/241-amr-ld-pilot. - Ran from 2026-10-21T23:47:44Z to 2026-10-22T14:58:12Z. All 79 steps exited 0. - Command:
taskset -c 220-223 env PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 \
  pixi run -e dev python3 tools/ld-panel/run_amr_pilot.py --out <dir>









Decision
Implementation




1kGP AMR samples from the existing gnomAD cache
The native GRCh38 gnomAD v3.1.2 HGDP+1kGP VCFs. No download, no Phase 3 GRCh37 genotypes.


Exclude HGDP
The pilot mapping (resources/reference-resources/hgdp1kgp-hg38-amr-ld/populations_to_superpop.tsv, under hgdp1kgp-hg38-ld/amr-pilot/ when the pilot ran) includes only CLM, MXL, PEL and PUR. It excludes Pima, Maya, Karitiana, Surui and Colombian by name. The production mapping is unchanged.


EUR block boundaries
Five frozen EUR-layout blocks (amr-pilot/blocks.tsv), the same five regions as the EUR calibration control’s comparison. LD is estimated from AMR genotypes only.


Start with 345
The 347 Phase 3 AMR IDs, filtered by gnomAD high_quality, give 345. Nothing is substituted for the two failures.


MAF = 0.01
construct_block --maf 0.01. MAF is the minor-allele count over twice the called individuals. A MAF floor replaces the MAC floor (every block’s provenance records mac_threshold: null), and the CLIs refuse both together.


FILTER (asked in-session)
Match the existing panels: no FILTER filter. Composition is reported below.






All five chromosome VCFs declare GRCh38 and answer an indexed region query. All 1,116 AMR and EUR-control members appear in every header. The receipt records each VCF’s size, mtime, cache marker and tabix-index SHA-256.
The cached per-ancestry PGENs cannot serve the pilot: - they exist only for AFR, EAS, EUR and SAS; - they were converted with MAC >= 50, a 7.2% MAF filter at n = 345.
The raw VCFs are unfiltered, so the MAF 0.01 floor is supported and there is no blocker. Each block region is read by index for the 345 members and converted with no frequency floor. The floor is then applied once, in construct_block.

verify_block re-reads each written block against freshly extracted genotypes. It checks: - one row per eigenvector row, with unique canonical ALIDs; - finite, non-negative, descending eigenvalues; - agreement with provenance, and EAF; - exact row and allele binding (||X v_j||^2 = λ_j, relative error ≤ 2e-15); - loading through core’s list_all_blocks and load_ld_eigenvectors.
find_underresolved_blocks --thresh 0.9 reports zero. Every block is rank-deficient at n − 1 = 344, as ADR 0020 anticipates. The MHC block reaches 0.99 of the variance in under 250 components, so the 250-component floor sets its count.

About half of every block’s retained variants have MAC < 50, which the inherited floor would have dropped.
A variant can show MAC < 7 at MAF ≥ 0.01 only when calls are missing. MAF is measured over called individuals, so sparsely called sites pass: up to 99.4% of calls are missing at a retained site. Outside the MHC block, 8–14% of retained variants are more than 50% missing. No missingness filter was approved, so this is reported rather than applied.




The pilot may read reference genotypes only, so its GWAS is simulated (tools/ld-panel/heldout_calibration.py): 1. Split the 345 into 230 training and 115 held-out individuals, stratified by population. 2. Build the panel from the training individuals. 3. Draw each replicate’s z-scores with the held-out individuals’ own LD: one to three causal variants scaled to a peak |z| of 8, plus N(0, R_test) noise. 4. Mask 20% of variants and impute them with core’s impute_z_block (truncation 0.9, min_cor 0.7).
A panel built from the held-out individuals themselves gives the in-sample upper bound. Each block ran 20 replicates per panel.

Every replicate passed the quality gate. Outside the MHC, held-out masked-z recovery has a median r of 0.80–0.88, against 0.97–0.99 in-sample. The slopes of 0.64–0.77 mean imputed z-scores are shrunk toward zero.
These numbers are not comparable with the EUR control’s 0.963 (docs/hgdp1kgp-ld-release-evidence.md). That figure is a real-GWAS masking comparison at n = 771. Here, the “GWAS” LD is itself a 115-person estimate, which makes the metric pessimistic. It is also optimistic: training and held-out individuals come from the same four populations, which need not match MVP’s Hispanic/Latin American ancestry mix.



Each of the ten block edges was tested for LD crossing it. The test takes a ±250 kb window at the edge and applies the same MAF floor separately in each cohort: the 345 AMR members and the 771 HGDP+1kGP EUR-control members (tools/ld-panel/boundary_ld.py). It then measures r² between every variant left of the edge and every variant right of it.

The owner accepts this quality as the best available until a better AMR reference exists, and is considering the genome-wide build. Variant QC for any build from these tools:







Rule
Implementation




Drop variants that are not PASS
conversion_command(pass_only=True), which is plink2 --var-filter, at conversion. FILTER does not survive into the PGEN.


Require ≥ 80% of individuals called
construct_block --max-missing 0.2, inclusive at exactly 80%. Drops are counted as n_variants_high_missing.


For a shared ALID, keep one record
Of the records that pass every filter, keep the one with the higher MAF, then the higher call rate, then the first. Provenance records alid_collision_rule: keep_highest_maf.



Measured on the pilot blocks’ own genotypes and FILTER values by tools/ld-panel/pilot_qc_effect.py, which reruns plink2 --freq --missing variant-only over the pilot’s pfiles and writes data/amr-ld-pilot-qc-effect.json; that JSON reproduces this table exactly.




Records / variants




Pass MAF ≥ 0.01
47,466


…and PASS and ≥ 80% called
38,891


Collision pairs among those (no ALID names more than two)
938


Retained if both records of a pair are dropped
37,015


Retained when one record is kept
37,953



PASS and the call-rate rule resolve most collisions on their own: the pilot’s drop-all rule removed 6,504 records. In a remaining pair, the two records differ in MAF by a median of about 0.10, so they are distinct variants. The kept record is the one a GWAS reporting that ALID most likely means; the ALID itself cannot say which.
run_amr_pilot.py now applies all three rules by default. The calibration and boundary numbers above predate them.

Both block checks count the SNP column of every block table. The 1,198 cross-boundary ALIDs are the layout, not a duplicate: adjacent EUR-layout blocks share their boundary position and plink2’s --from-bp/--to-bp include both ends, so a variant kept at a boundary is written into both blocks. They fall on 1,186 of the panel’s 1,335 adjacent block pairs, and no ALID repeats inside one block. UKB EUR on chr22, where this layout comes from, has the same shape: 12 ALIDs in two adjacent blocks, across 12 of its 19 edges.

Explicit human acceptance freezes the Release Manifest Candidate. Material membership/recipe choices require a new immutable identity and lineage.
Verify the pinned runtime, required capabilities, format-compatible parent and ancestry-/assembly-matched Reference Resources before writes.
The existing Phase A pixi run release interface owns locking, recovery and execution. No direct Snakemake bypass or registry-side association processing.

Lightweight tests: at most four CPUs per worker, BLAS threads one.
Bulk source scans: one coordinated slot, at most two readers. #219’s completed source verification released that slot; no new bulk scan is authorised here.
#220 may inspect mapping tables and named metadata/header probes; no recursive multi-TB content scans or automatic downloads/conversions.
Full release execution needs its own acceptance gate and resource allocation.
No recursive delegation; each ticket has a DeepSeek Flash worker and separate Gemini 3.8 Flash reviewer in an isolated ticket worktree/Herdr tab. Session handles are ephemeral operator state, not release provenance.




Core #254 merged through core PR #276 as 4e922566d7fa4c13a11be3637069da63e48be28c. The separately owned implementation passed 2,327 tests. Reported full-run peak RSS dropped 33.7→2.35 GiB (OGS-00009) and 36.5→3.01 GiB (OGS-00010), both validating clean; wall times fell 88→71 and 135→109 minutes. Its two validation processes finished. These measurements are not a concurrency budget or qualification of new releases.
Stores #218 initially pinned core 1be2a156649e4d444f31f9b4107c3f47a046f855 and then repinned to 4e922566d7fa4c13a11be3637069da63e48be28c at af6fc75. Independent reviewer GO and orchestrator verification confirmed equality of the runtime constant, pixi.toml, pixi.lock and installed direct_url.json. Python 3.12, zarr 3.4.1 and numcodecs 0.17 remain unchanged. Format 0.2.0, fail-closed executable-bound revision checks and scheduled-step-aware completion gates are preserved. No historical Store was converted or requalified by this upgrade.
Repin checks: runtime-guard 19/19, plan 91/91, workflow 29/29, bundle-check 12/12, env-check and lock-check. Read-only real-host smoke refused OGS-00010 complete-only against its 0.1.0 parent; same-run OGS-00009 build + OGS-00010 complete and enhancement-only reruns passed the guard.



Original exact reviewed checkpoint: 886082bb0f83dd9d9f84cf79972923bb5c377d92, independent GO; original CI passed in 16m34s. Orchestrator checks: 26 readiness tests, 12 index tests, 54 bundle test cases / 128 checks and bundle-check 12/12. Two explicit legacy #134 tolerated gaps remain visible.
The view separates intended Source Inventory, manifest/admitted/excluded IDs, actual built IDs, source acquisition, observed build, completion, required indexes, optional HM3, validation, registration, format/runtime, lineage and warnings. Built IDs use read_analyses(open_store(path).analyses_path); historical committed baseline differences are a separate channel. Configured, unknown, missing or historical evidence cannot become a current clean pass.
OGS-00011’s target is exactly 3,169 admitted Analyses; the 3,317-Analysis published artifact remains historical. OGS-00009/00010 remain the incomplete historical UKB pair. FinnGen history remains preserved, including the receipt’s '1.0' versus published '0.1.0' discrepancy on local evidence branch fix/ogs-00016-build-tmpdir@c871b61; no blanket branch adoption occurred.




Exact intended/available/provider-resolved membership: 2,514, not an approximate 2,524; 490 restored beyond the historical 2,024 built IDs.
Frozen per-file data and index identities; source bytes 425,402,488,477. SHA freeze took 258.9 seconds with two readers. Full decompression and Tabix contig checks passed 2,514/2,514; retain their recorded coverage limitations.
Three historical API-missing records were resolved independently with exact-ID/batch-checked, checksum-bound provider JSON. Comparison coverage is shared 2,514 / evaluated 2,511 / skipped 3, zero evaluated-field disagreements; provider-only resolutions are not API comparison matches.
Candidate OGS-00030 remains candidate, unaccepted and unregistered, staged under /data/opengwasdb/work/epic232/219/candidates/OGS-00030. OGS-00031 is not emitted; its completion reference is unresolved.
Durable evidence lives under /data/opengwasdb/work/epic232/219/ and committed resources/inventories/ukb-b-*. No historical OGS-00009/00010 artifact changed.
Original hermetic checks: 38 UKB tests and bundle-check 12/12; staged candidate check had zero errors/tolerated gaps. The ancestry-evidence correction adds eight hermetic regressions (46/46 total); its exact-head verdict is separate from the original staged emission.

The ten-Analysis trial measured ancestry at ~26.6 minutes and SD at ~1.9 minutes (two workers, BLAS one). All ancestry outputs were residual-gated Unassigned: GRCh37 source coordinates were queried against a GRCh38 reference without liftover. This is not valid calibration evidence or a valid lifted full-run cost estimate. Candidate ancestry remains source_fallback, check not_run; SD trial output did not replace candidate metadata. No full 2,514 run authorised.




UKB acceptance: explicit acceptance of the staged 2,514 membership and material Build Recipe before any full build/registration.
UKB completion reference: historical HGDP+1kGP EUR is calibration-only; production GPM UKB EUR is a different panel. Both panels are absent on this host; neither reuse nor switching is auto-approved.
MVP D1 GCST90476298: Catalog N=235 vs dbGaP Platelet_Mean_INT.AFR N=114,731. Owner must choose provenance correction/binding or unavailable.
MVP D2 GCST90481129: Catalog four-ancestry META N=577,873 vs dbGaP three-ancestry META N=571,620; difference exactly EAS 6,253. Owner must decide intended Analysis versus distinct/unavailable deposit, or documented correction.
57 MVP labels: 30 punctuation-only and 27 lexical differences require recorded policy/individual review; no fuzzy automatic binding. Bijection stays red at 6,020/6,022; no conversion or manifest promotion. Acquisition tests 27/27.
Core #277: ancestry CLI liftover wiring; #207 owns the one-pass resolver’s GWAS-VCF rejection. Separate ancestry/SD commands read VCF; do not claim all VCF resolution is unsupported. No registry pre-lifting or residual-threshold relaxation.
AMR completion: #229 needs an explicitly suitable LD resource; HGDP resource declares AFR/EAS/SAS, not AMR. Missing reference is not observed-only success.




#221 follows #220 and freezes disjoint MVP ancestry/META membership plus identity planning; FinnGen renumbering, if chosen, must preserve core identity and history. OGS-00017/00018 remain free; OGS-00030/00031 are UKB candidate proposals only.
#222 follows #218/#219; #223 follows #218/#221. #224 (Chen EUR Ragged) and #225 (Catalog 3,169-Analysis Hybrid) follow #218 and their own scientific/reference gates. Do not restore the 148 routed-out Catalog Analyses or alter MAF/panel policy. #226–#230 follow #218/#221: META is observed-only; EUR/AFR/AMR/EAS each require an appropriate observed/completed pair. #231 rehearses bounded ingestion only after the required full-release gates actually pass.



Initial stores baseline 3a9cf780b5b77427f275533213b8a2c94b2afc82; initial core baseline 1be2a156649e4d444f31f9b4107c3f47a046f855. Copy completion removed the UKB copy prerequisite, not identity verification or acceptance. Initial runtime and UKB candidate NO-GO verdicts were corrected through review rounds; later exact SHAs supersede them. PR #233 records this chronology, not full epic completion.
Missing required completion, membership acceptance or correctness gates prevent a blanket mass-ingestion-readiness claim.

Fingerprint is inherited, not body-hashed (public read code). Producing this selection TSV (reading the mapping, manifests and sidecars only) is within the existing permitted metadata scope and does not need the body-read authorization of §6. It is written with per-row binding evidence, not summarised labels: analysis_id, mapping_ancestry, study_design, mapping_sample_size, n_cases, n_controls, source_file_path (the metadata-root symlink), source_file_size (target stat), source_genome_build (sidecar), sidecar_gwas_id, sidecar_data_file_name, metadata_content_sha256 (1f14…). No core call, no body open.




Assigned Ancestry: core gates only; unassigned and gate_reason recorded verbatim, never coerced.
Effect scale is source-provenance, not a study-design default. A quantitative Analysis is not automatically sd. The registry records the public StoredEffectScale/original_effect_scale value only when the source provenance supports a core-supported conversion (for example a raw-unit or standardized beta+se that the core maps to sd, or a declared log_or/log_hazard); unknown or ambiguous provenance stays pending and is never silently defaulted to sd.
Phenotype SD — per-trait method eligibility. Quantitative rows are eligible for an actual SD tier (estimated_from_source_maf, estimated_from_reference_maf, estimated_from_beta_distribution, source_provided, declared_standardised); case-control rows are legitimately binary_trait with no SD. RecordStatus=success means the row’s eligible method resolved, not that every row carries an SD. unavailable stays pending (blank, no default).
Source AF/SE and orientation: eaf_orientation/eaf_orientation_r recorded; an orientation failure is a controlled failure/pending, never a loosened threshold. standard_error is exactly what the reader reports (#NA/absent stays absent).
Failures: core RecordStatus success / controlled_failure / skip; only success with the eligible real method tier counts as resolved. A --max-rows-bounded run is a capped diagnostic: its SD evidence is marked source_evidence_scope: capped_pilot_diagnostic, and success alone does not promote a partial estimate to whole-source qualification.




The existing #220 owner authority covers only the two conversion inputs (GCST90476298, GCST90481129) plus metadata, and forbids reads of the other 6,020 association bodies. Metadata-only selection (§4) is allowed now. For the next pilot, parent start requires a new owner/operator GO authorizing:

one bounded read of each of the 15 named association bodies;
loading the ancestry reference ref_freqs.hg38.tsv.gz (494,105,972 bytes), ancestry_groups.tsv (385 bytes) and the tracked qc_panel.tsv (420,582 bytes);
no source-body hashing/checksum recomputation (the resolver inherits the recorded SHA/stat, §3) and no separate SD re-scan;
no genotype/LD/panel build, no Store operation.




The core always infers a dominant super-population mixture per Analysis and has no flag to skip inference. The registry keeps the core record immutable (its inferred evidence stays as provenance in the receipt) and canonicalises the META bundle’s assigned_ancestry to empty by explicit registry policy. This is a policy decision, not a promise that the resolver will not assign an ancestry; nothing rewrites the core record. META remains observed-only with no completion.



The AMR LD calibration pilot is already approved (ticket #241, MAF 1%); this plan does not re-ratify it. The resolver may assign AMR or leave it unassigned. No AMR LD production is assumed: the AMR completed definition stays a pending, blocked plan until a production qualification exists.



The limits below are proposed; the enforcing wrapper is not implemented in this plan. A future wrapper must: impose a whole-pool wall timeout; measure aggregate process-tree RSS (acknowledging shared-page double-accounting); apply real CPU affinity and BLAS/OpenMP=1; and isolate failed/partial outputs so a failed worker cannot leave a partial record in the committed set.

Proposed: ≤ 2 resolver workers, ≤ 4 CPU, BLAS/OpenMP 1, whole-pool wall ≤ 1800 s, aggregate process-tree RSS ≤ 4096 MB.
Write ownership. The core owns its per-record and index.json writes (_atomic_write_json: a sibling .tmp_<name>_<uuid> file, fsync, then os.replace, with mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)) — the adapter does not claim these use the registry helper. The adapter preflights a fresh root (must not exist; no symlinked ancestors) and uses the exclusive resources/generators/lib/safe_write.py temps only for its own selection.tsv and resolution-receipt.json.
Staging root (fresh; the actual run root gets a runtime-allocated UTC timestamp at START, not the historical metadata timestamp): /data/opengwasdb/work/epic232/221/metric-pilot-staging/.
Receipt resolution-receipt.json records: core commit 4e922566, metadata content hash 1f14…, exact reference paths plus the resolver-computed anc_ref_sha256/anc_grp_sha256/panel_sha256, the gate flags, per-row RecordStatus/original_sd_method/stored_effect_scale/ source_evidence_scope, and the measured wall/RSS.





Pilot accepted only if every row resolves its eligible method (quantitative: SD/effect tier; case-control: binary_trait + log_or), or is an explicitly classified controlled_failure/skip; ancestry/SD/orientation outcomes are internally consistent; proposed resources stay inside §9; and the metadata content hash still equals 1f14….
Stop and report on any budget breach, unexpected orientation failure, resolver setup error, or metadata-hash mismatch. A capped result is reported as a diagnostic, never a whole-source qualification.
A full 6,022 run is a separate parent decision with a fresh measured budget.




The 2026-10-13 owner decision (“reorder the IDs”) fixed the allocation: observed OGS-00012 EUR / 00013 AFR / 00014 AMR / 00015 EAS, META observed-only OGS-00016, completed definitions OGS-00018/19/20/21, and FinnGen OGS-00017. FinnGen was migrated OGS-00016 -> OGS-00017 (membership, recipe and association/index artifacts unchanged; directory, store_id and a migration/erratum note only) under ADR 0022’s owner-authorized-renumbering amendment; the old identifier stays discoverable through the migration block, erratum and git history. The published artifact under the artifact root must be relocated to <artifact-root>/OGS-00017/ as a separate operational step.



This document is documentation only; it opens no association root, runs no resolver, and touches no genotype. It must be independently reviewed before any PR. The first operational step after the §6 owner GO is the metadata-only selection TSV (§4), then the bounded pilot with the measured receipt (§9).

title: Registry
text: The registry’s own documentation: what the vocabulary means, what was decided and why, what each contract is, and the guides that record how the repository is laid out and worked in.

title: Registry
text:
Glossary
CONTEXT.md is the authority on project vocabulary, and the site stages it at render time as this page. Use its terms in code, configuration, documentation, issue comments and commit messages.

title: Registry
text:
Decisions (ADRs)
One numbered decision per constraint on future work, from the Store Registry boundary (0001) to the Analysis Catalog (0039) and Association Coverage in the Release Bundle (0040). A later ADR supersedes an earlier one explicitly rather than quietly contradicting it. The whole set is in the sidebar, or in docs/adr/.

title: Registry
text:
Specifications
The contracts the code is held to: the Release Bundle schema, the Store Release workflow and its boundary, the QC Panel Concordance preregistration, release configuration, and source connectors.

title: Registry
text:
Guides
The repository’s layout, its runtime, the software-management proposal and audit, and the evidence records from the MVPs and pilots. They are docs/*.md, and the sidebar lists them.

title: Registry
text:
How the pages are built
Every page here comes from a file under docs/ and keeps its path. A link from a page to a file outside docs/ — a module under src/, a table under resources/, CONTRIBUTING.md — is rewritten at render time to the GitHub blob URL of the commit being rendered, so it works on the site and still points at the same file. See the site page for how to preview and publish.

title: Release seam audit
text:
Historical record. This audit was written on 2026-09-10 and is kept as written. Its relative links into the family-first bundle archive are dead: that directory was retired in #252, and each bundle it held is now registered in stores/<store-id>/ or retired with git history keeping it.

Research for Audit the existing release seam decisions and working-store evidence, against repository commit 8bd722b on 2026-09-10. The seed is The release seam to opengwasdb has no interface: builder.entrypoint is inert, the Builder Manifest adapter is copy-pasted and lossy, and the bundle format has no owner module.


The seed’s central diagnosis stands: this repository has working pieces for several source/layout combinations, but no release-centric interface joins them into one observable, resumable route from an acquired Source Inventory to a validated Release Artifact. Four of its five directions remain live, with two important corrections:

The release seam is still inert, but its boundary is already decided. All 20 committed build.yaml files declare builder.entrypoint, but no runtime code reads that field. Instead, three standalone build wrappers and the BESD generator import OpenGWASDB builders directly; Reference Completion and rho construction recorded in committed releases were run manually through the OpenGWASDB CLI. The seed is wrong that all four paths use “the same import”: Dense, Hybrid, Ragged SSF and BESD have distinct call shapes. The missing work is therefore not another repository-boundary decision or a naive dynamic import. opengwasdb-stores <-> opengwasdb interface and script placement already decided that the Release Bundle is the handoff, this repository owns orchestration, and OpenGWASDB owns readers and builders. Unify repository software management with Pixi also already selected pixi run <task> as the operator interface. The later design must implement those decisions.
The Builder Manifest adapter is still duplicated and the Hybrid path is still lossy. The Dense wrapper translates and passes the interpretation-bearing fields at write_builder_manifest, and its FinnGen end-to-end test verifies their read-back from a real built fixture (test). The Hybrid wrapper has a separate, shorter map that omits sample_size_kind, sample_size_scope, n_cases, n_controls, original_effect_scale, ancestry_assignment_method, and all ancestry_prop_* fields (Hybrid adapter). Its read-back then asks for several of the omitted fields (Hybrid checks), and both Hybrid Trial Store Releases record the resulting omissions (case-control validation, quantitative validation). The old upstream defect is fixed: Dense/Hybrid VCF-manifest builders drop n_cases/n_controls/sample_size_kind/sample_size_scope/original_effect_scale, and fabricate ancestry_assignment_method confirms the current builder accepts all six fixed fields. A current rebuild loses them because the local Hybrid adapter never supplies them. The seed also overstates the test gap: Dense translation is integration-tested, although neither adapter has a focused contract test and Hybrid has no corresponding build test.
The Release Bundle still has no owner module, but analyses.tsv is no longer merely prose. release_yaml.py remains a custom subset parser plus validation merger, while five generator implementations write the bundle independently. The R Ragged and Hybrid generators also retain separate validation-merge implementations (Ragged, Hybrid). However, the seed’s claim that the schema is “enforced by nothing” is superseded by Schema-conformance check against an opengwasdb-owned schema: the current bridge delegates analyses.tsv validation to opengwasdb.model.analyses (implementation) and tests both failures and real bundles (tests). A Release Bundle owner must compose, not duplicate, OpenGWASDB’s shared Analysis schema and must additionally own registry-specific structure, I/O, state transitions, and validation merging.
The naming collision is real; the proposed directory layout is not yet a decision. families/<family>/generators/ contains the family-specific configuration and thin shims that match the domain definition of Manifest Generator, while resources/generators/<source-format>-<layout>/ also contains shared selection, download/filter, annotation, building, and validation code. The latter names conflate Source Format, Store Layout, and several phases. Family-first external artifact layout settles durable artifact paths only, so applying the same rule to source-code layout would be a new design choice. store_key is likewise absent from CONTEXT.md, yet is used as candidate-grouping data, written into some release.yaml files, used as a physical store name, and sometimes substituted for OpenGWASDB’s store_id (Ragged build). Its candidate-pool role must be distinguished from Store Release identity; it should not become a fourth authoritative identifier by accident.
Release identity and lineage should not be reopened. Store release identity, Family-scoped release IDs, and Reference completion as release lineage already establish immutable releases, the (Store Family ID, Family Release ID) identity pair, source-natural family-scoped IDs, and Reference-Completed releases linked to their observed-only parents. Contrary to the seed, the ukb-b resolved and completed bundles do populate lineage.derived_from (resolved, completed). Existing IDs do redundantly encode layout, completion, and even an issue reference, but they are immutable historical identifiers. Preserve them; enforce the existing source-natural convention for future releases rather than inventing a new identity scheme.




Later design tickets should treat the following as constraints, not open questions.



Concern
Existing decision
Consequence for the workflow




Repository boundary
Store registry boundary, Manifest generators own orchestration only
This repository orchestrates and records releases. Reusable source readers, normalisation, statistical logic, storage builders, and query behavior remain in OpenGWASDB.


Source model
Source formats and reader capabilities, Single-source store families, Reference resources are build resources
One Store Family consumes one homogeneous Source Collection; reader capability and Reference Resources are explicit inputs, not branches inferred from paths.


Handoff shape
Custom manifest generators with standard release manifests, Separate release manifests from build recipes, YAML metadata and TSV tables, Release manifest bundles
Preserve the four-file Release Bundle, the separation of accepted membership from Build Recipe, and YAML/TSV conventions. A module may own the format without collapsing it into one file.


Metadata authority
OpenGWASDB owns the shared analysis schema, Trait Ontology Mapping lookup lives in the registry, not OpenGWASDB
Validate shared Analysis fields against OpenGWASDB; keep registry provenance fields and the deliberate ontology-lookup exception here. The adapter must be lossless across this seam.


Existing manifest phases
Metadata pipeline for ragged release manifests, docs/release-metadata-schema.md
discover -> select -> derive -> emit -> accept is existing language. A larger execution workflow should contain or map these stages explicitly, not silently redefine them.


Release and artifact identity
Store release identity, Family-scoped release IDs, Reference completion as release lineage, Family-first external artifact layout
Material manifest/build changes and Reference Completion produce immutable lineage-linked Store Releases; durable paths use Family and Family Release identity.


Storage boundary
Registry not artifact store
Keep source data, stores, checkpoints, and large logs outside Git; retain small manifests, summaries, and report pointers here.


Publication boundary
Registry and service catalogue boundary
Building and validating can end at the Release Artifact. Activation, routing, and default served releases belong elsewhere.


Environment
Unify repository software management with Pixi, pixi.toml
Keep one Pixi-fronted operator interface and an immutable OpenGWASDB pin; do not add a competing user-facing environment/runner interface.



The current Release Status vocabulary is a registry lifecycle (candidate, accepted, built, validated, superseded, withdrawn), not execution state (domain definition). A resumable workflow therefore needs a separate phase/checkpoint record; repurposing release.yaml.status as scheduler state would contradict the domain model.



The exact seven-store development set is enumerated by Rebuild all pilot stores on current main and stress-test the new encodings. It is a useful coverage matrix, but these are evidence fixtures rather than seven implementations to preserve.



Trial Store Release
Distinct coverage
Evidence and seam exposed




eqtlgen-cis-pilot/pilot-10
BESD -> Ragged, cis, shared multi-Analysis source bundle
The generator performs selection, build, read-back, report writing, and bundle emission in one Python program; it does not expose the staged interface used by other families.


eqtlgen-cis-pilot/pilot-10-completed
BESD -> Ragged Reference-Completed
Completion uses a different OpenGWASDB API and was invoked manually. The first rebuild used the wrong Analysis IDs because tissue was an implicit generator argument, then had to be redone; that is direct evidence of operator-only invocation knowledge (rebuild record).


finngen-r13/r13-pilot-20
FinnGen tabular -> Dense, binary and quantitative Analyses
Its documented five-command route separately emits, acquires, annotates, builds, and assesses (family instructions). Acquisition is already resumable and checksummed, and the assessment can issue a NO-GO despite a valid store, as recorded by Derive and build the 20-analysis FinnGen R13 pilot release. This is the strongest precedent for Source Acquisition Helpers and a human review report, but there is no workflow checkpoint model joining the commands.


gwas-catalog-eur-hybrid/eur-hybrid-pilot-10
GWAS-SSF -> Hybrid, case-control
Proves both Dense Component and Ragged Overflow, while exposing the live Hybrid adapter metadata loss described above.


gwas-catalog-eur-hybrid/eur-hybrid-quant-pilot-10
GWAS-SSF -> Hybrid, quantitative, source/reference-AF SD estimation
Proves effect-scale derivation and its sidecar before build; shares the lossy Hybrid adapter. Both Hybrid routes were recorded by Add gwas-ssf-hybrid generator: case-control + quantitative pilots.


metabolome-plasma-2023/2023-chen-full-european
GWAS-SSF -> Ragged, full 1,400-Analysis ancestry slice, no cis target
Exercises ancestry, SD, sparse-region and no-cis behavior at the largest Ragged scale in the development set. The Release Bundle records a real duplicate-cell warning and an upstream limitation that prevented Reference Completion (release evidence); adverse outcomes are part of the required regression coverage.


pqtl-interval-2018/2018-sun-pilot-10
GWAS-SSF -> Ragged, cis plus signals
Its instructions require separate emit, validate, filter, effect-scale and build commands and support partial filtering reports (family instructions). This ten-Analysis slice was explicitly created as an independent end-to-end proof rather than a replacement for the 100-Analysis release (release evidence), making it the appropriate fast workflow fixture. The catalogue separately records artifact-path drift and a legacy schema in the 100-Analysis predecessor (catalogue).



This matrix spans three Store Layouts, four input shapes/capabilities, single-file-per-Analysis and shared bundles, cis and no-cis Ragged policies, observed-only and lineage-linked completion examples, and both successful and deliberately adverse validation outcomes. It also shows inconsistent report contracts: validation.yaml.reports ranges from empty to selection, downloads, derivations, ancestry, SD, filter, build, and narrative assessment reports, with different stage combinations per family. A common envelope should require phase identity, inputs, outputs, tool/environment provenance, status, timings/resource use, checks, warnings/errors, and pointers while allowing layout-specific payloads.
All seven were rebuilt successfully as format 2.0, but outside the curated release paths, while the repository remained pinned to an older OpenGWASDB revision (rebuild record, storage follow-up). The same rebuild exposed GCST002047 is stored with z uncorrelated with its own p-values: its source beta column is odds ratios: both old and rebuilt stores passed structural validation despite an entire Analysis being scientifically nonsensical. The Preflight Review Gate and scientific reports are therefore essential; validate_store alone is not an acceptance decision.
All committed catalogue stores were built using OpenGWASDB format 0.1; Store format 1.0: z is int16 fixed point, and the manifest declares its encoding (opengwasdb#114) records that they remain readable but require rebuilding for the newer format (catalogue warning). Trial coverage should therefore be asserted through reproducible behavior and reports, not byte-for-byte preservation of old artifacts.



The committed ukb-b/dense-observed-vcf-c128-completed-issue34 release is the original scale proof: 2,514 Analyses, 11.19 million variants, 11.27 billion imputed cells, a 71 GB completed store, and about 7.7 hours for Reference Completion (release evidence, catalogue). It was produced with a manual opengwasdb complete-dense command and formally registered later, including an in-place schema migration. This validates OpenGWASDB’s engine, but demonstrates that operator memory and retrospective bookkeeping still bridge the release seam.
Newer tracker evidence is even stronger. Verify ukb-b at genome scale: build and migration under format 3.0 records a fresh 2,511-Analysis by 9,847,701-variant build taking 13 hours 30 minutes; its measurement report records 424.84 GB of input, a 41.66 GB format 3.0 store, and an 11-hour-35-minute format 2.0 baseline. Its Reference-Completed sibling adds roughly 7 hours over 1,357 LD blocks. These are authoritative current-server scale measurements, not projections.
Additional uncommitted operator-worktree evidence was inspected read-only on 2026-09-10:

families/ukb-b/releases/dense-observed-vcf-c128-rebuild117/sidecars/build_report.tsv records a current Dense rebuild of 2,511 buildable Analyses from 424.8 GB of source data to a 42.6 GB store in 48,607.7 seconds (about 13.5 hours), with store validation passing.
/data/opengwasdb/raw/ contains 17,300 files totalling about 2.35 TB, including the mass GWAS Catalog download in progress.
.rebuild133/ contains fresh runs overlapping the development matrix plus the ukb-b Dense trial, but the operator invoked them through family/layout-specific paths and collected them manually.

These local observations are not committed evidence and should not be promoted into registry truth as-is. They do confirm the operational requirements: completion markers must survive multi-hour phases; a rerun must distinguish reusable outputs from partial/corrupt ones; source acquisition must finish and produce a verifiable Source Inventory before the main workflow starts; and reports/checkpoints must be discoverable without reconstructing commands from shell history.




Start from an acquired, verified Source Inventory. Repository-owned Source Acquisition Helpers are valuable, and FinnGen already proves resumable download mechanics, but they should terminate at a common inventory contract. The main workflow starts there. Today the GWAS Catalog Source Collection declares inventory: null, and the OpenGWAS inventory is only a header (source collections); this handoff is not yet implemented.
Use one release-centric operator command. It should select the family/release, validate configuration and inventory, run or resume explicit phases, expose the single Preflight Review Gate, and stop at a validated Release Artifact. Pixi fronts that command; a workflow engine may implement it.
Treat builder.entrypoint as typed dispatch, not arbitrary dynamic import. Current builder APIs have different signatures and require registry-side translation, Reference Resources, validation, and report handling. The design must decide whether the manifest names a supported adapter/capability or an OpenGWASDB callable, but the runner must fail closed on unsupported combinations and always preserve the standard read-back/validation contract.
Make adapter ownership singular and lossless. One tested seam should transform the accepted registry Analysis rows into whatever an OpenGWASDB builder requires. Per-layout differences should be explicit data or implementations behind that seam, not divergent copies. Test the exact shared-core and registry-to-builder column contract for Dense, Hybrid, Ragged, and BESD.
Give the Release Bundle one owner without stealing OpenGWASDB’s schema. Centralise reading, writing, registry-specific structural validation, status transitions, and cumulative validation/report merging. Continue delegating the shared analyses.tsv contract to OpenGWASDB.
Separate lifecycle, execution, and approval state. release.yaml.status, per-phase completion/checkpoints, and the one human Preflight approval are different facts. Record each explicitly, with input/config/code/environment fingerprints so “complete” means safely reusable.
Model expensive build and derived work as phases with declared dependencies. The phase model must place build, read-back validation, top-hit construction, rho construction where applicable, and final artifact validation, with visible reports and useful restart boundaries. Reference Completion remains a separate derived Store Release connected through Release Lineage, not an in-place phase that mutates its observed-only parent.
Standardise the report envelope, not every report body. The Trial Store Releases prove that source/layout-specific evidence is necessary. Require consistent phase status, provenance, metrics, checks and artifact pointers, then allow ancestry, SD, sparse-region, Hybrid partition, top-hit and rho-specific schemas beneath it.
Preserve historical release IDs and migrate incrementally. Existing bundles and family commands should be adoptable behind adapters while the common workflow is introduced. Do not rename published IDs, rewrite old store artifacts, or make the outdated 0.1 binaries the conformance oracle.
Keep the scoped exclusions firm. No multi-store queue, HPC/cloud abstraction, publishing/activation, or storage/query redesign is needed to close this seam.




The route should build on the seed rather than restart it: implement the already-decided Release Bundle handoff and Pixi interface; centralise Release Bundle and adapter ownership; preserve existing domain, identity, and repository boundaries; and add a separate resumable phase/evidence model proven across the seven Trial Store Releases and the full-scale ukb-b case. The only seed proposal that should not become a fresh design debate is Release identity/lineage—the ADRs already answer it. The schema claim also needs narrowing: shared Analysis validation exists; bundle-level ownership does not.

Preserve historical release IDs and migrate incrementally. Existing bundles and family commands should be adoptable behind adapters while the common workflow is introduced. Do not rename published IDs, rewrite old store artifacts, or make the outdated 0.1 binaries the conformance oracle.
Keep the scoped exclusions firm. No multi-store queue, HPC/cloud abstraction, publishing/activation, or storage/query redesign is needed to close this seam.

title: Release seam audit
text: The route should build on the seed rather than restart it: implement the already-decided Release Bundle handoff and Pixi interface; centralise Release Bundle and adapter ownership; preserve existing domain, identity, and repository boundaries; and add a separate resumable phase/evidence model proven across the seven Trial Store Releases and the full-scale ukb-b case. The only seed proposal that should not become a fresh design debate is Release identity/lineage—the ADRs already answer it. The schema claim also needs narrowing: shared Analysis validation exists; bundle-level ownership does not.

title: The release runtime: pinned, current-format, and gated before writes
text:
This document records the one opengwasdb runtime the supported release workflow uses (stores#218, adopting the runtime portion of stores#197), what it provides, and what upgrading it does not do.









Fact
Value




Repository
https://github.com/opengwas/opengwasdb


Revision
0d59f151c7618933747a59f825deeef6a51de9e1, the core dev merge of PR #329; its first parent is PR #328’s merge, its second PR #329’s branch head 555e2e6


Core merge
opengwas/opengwasdb PR #329 (core #302: a BESD Ragged build stores each pair’s published sample size, and the .esi allele frequency per association on request; ADR 0067), on top of dev with #298, #326, #331, #295/#296/#306/#324 and #328; earlier pins: PR #330’s branch head 5fc0766 (stores #326), the dev merge of PR #298 75f0e77 (stores #341), the dev merge of PR #305 d8896e4 (stores #314), the dev merge of PR #291 d405de0 (stores #312), PR #291’s branch head 023774a7 (stores #306, which excluded #288), PR #276 (4e922566, bounded Dense validation, core #254) and PR #275 (1be2a15)


Package version
0.3.0


Writers’ Store format_version
0.2.0


Python floor
3.12


Zarr / numcodecs
