The pin is an immutable git revision, not a branch or a floating tag. The executable form of it is the opengwasdb entry in pixi.toml’s [feature.store-build.pypi-dependencies] and the resolved package in pixi.lock. The Python 3.12 / zarr 3.4 / numcodecs 0.17 floors are not preferences: the pinned runtime requires them, and a zarr 2.x environment cannot open a format-0.2.0 Store.
ogstores.runtime.PINNED_OPENGWASDB_REVISION is the single source of truth the tests assert pixi.toml and pixi.lock against. Change all three together, and re-run pixi lock in the same commit.




Format-0.2.0 builders (opengwas/opengwasdb#247): Zarr v3 with the sharding codec; Dense inner chunk [1000, 64] and shard [100000, 1024]. build-dense-vcf, build-hybrid, build-ragged-ssf and build-ragged-besd all write it, and the converter writes the same layout from a 0.1.0 source.
The required Ragged/Overflow by_variant/ index (opengwas/opengwasdb#252/#268). Every Ragged and Hybrid builder writes it inline; opengwasdb validate fails without it. It is part of the format contract, not an optional enhancement, and the registry plans no separate step for it.
Indexed Variant Subset support (opengwas/opengwasdb#264/#269/#271), including Dense, completed-Dense and Hybrid Dense components: build-indexed-subset, audited by validate and reported by overview.
The shared HM3 benchmark seam (opengwas/opengwasdb#272).
One strand-aware hg19 lift (opengwas/opengwasdb#288, core #284; moved here for stores #312’s OGS-00009 rebuild). The resolver and the Dense, Hybrid and BESD builders share it, so signed statistics and EAF follow the projected allele pair on a reverse-strand variant. A single-pass Hybrid build whose off-reference rows lift onto the reverse strand is refused.
A policy for the Hybrid build’s rsid harvest (opengwas/opengwasdb#306, moved here for stores #225’s OGS-00011 rebuild). build-hybrid --on-rsid-conflict {refuse,drop} decides what a routing key its sources name differently stores, and the build always reports what it compared as rsid_conflicts. See “Coordination with core #306”.
A policy for a Hybrid subset’s Overflow-only ALIDs (opengwas/opengwasdb#324, moved here for the same rebuild). build-indexed-subset --overflow-only {refuse,skip} decides a requested ALID only the Hybrid’s shared axis carries, and a skip build records how many. See “Coordination with core #324”.
One policy for a post-lift variant collision (opengwas/opengwasdb#304; moved here for stores #314’s OGS-00027). A chain set need not be injective: two hg19 loci can map into one hg38 position, and when their projected alleles agree they become one canonical variant. build-ragged-besd now drops every ESI entry in such a colliding group, with its associations, exactly as a liftover failure is, and records the counts in provenance.lift; a Ragged CSR cannot hold one variant_index twice in one Analysis’s segment. validate requires each Analysis’s variant_index slice to be strictly increasing, on every release, and reports a repeat separately from a decrease.
Per-association sample size, and the .esi allele frequency on request (opengwas/opengwasdb#302, ADR 0067; moved here for the OGS-00027 replacement, stores #314 in epic #282). build-ragged-besd --sample-size-table stores each stored pair’s published sample size in an opt-in uint32 n plane and its by-variant copy, and never estimates one the table omits; --store-esi-eaf stores the .esi frequency per association, oriented to the effect allele and checked once against --eaf-reference. A Store holding an n plane keeps se in float16, the loader and validate refuse an n plane beside residual-coded se, every Ragged query result then carries n, and info reports n=uint32.




Before the entry point snapshots anything or a build writes a Store, ogstores.runtime.verify_runtime_for_releases (called from workflow/release.py, and from the Snakefile onstart for a direct snakemake run) refuses a run when:

no opengwasdb executable resolves on PATH;
the revision cannot be proven from the executed install’s own metadata, or is a known revision other than the tracked pin – an unprovable identity is refused, not assumed, so an ad-hoc executable substituted onto PATH cannot silently become the factory runtime;
the runtime does not provide every subcommand the scheduled jobs will run (probed with --help); or
a scheduled complete job would consume an existing parent Store whose declared format_version is not 0.2.0.

The gate is scheduled-step-aware, because an id appearing in the dry run is not proof that the Store is rebuilt. workflow/release.py and the Snakefile onstart pass (artifact_root, store_id, step) for every dry-run job, so:

the parent format is gated only when the child’s own complete job will run; an enhancement-only rerun of an existing completed Store (build its HM3 subset, validate, overview) never consults its unused completion recipe;
a same-run build or complete job for the parent produces a fresh format-0.2.0 Store, so the stale on-disk artifact is not consumed and is not gated;
a parent that is neither on disk nor scheduled to be produced is refused loudly before Snakemake starts.

The parent’s declared format is read through opengwasdb info --format json – the core’s supported reporting interface – not by opening the Store in this repository. The run prints the resolved identity it will use, and every Step’s durable record already carries the exact opengwasdb revision and executable that ran.
The format-0.2.0 and required-by_variant guarantees rest on the verified pin identity, not on the --help probes: the subcommand probe only proves the CLI surface a scheduled step calls exists. That is why an unprovable revision is refused even when the commands answer.
The ordinary invocation therefore uses the pinned runtime with no PATH overlay:
pixi run release OGS-00016
The HM3 pipeline proof’s temporary explicit --opengwasdb-checkout remains a proof tool, not the supported release entry point.



A 0.1.0 parent is readable but not completable by a format-0.2.0 builder (opengwas/opengwasdb ADR 0038 §4); completion writes into the source’s arrays and never re-encodes them. When a build ticket needs a completed descendant of an existing 0.1.0 Store, it has two supported orders, both core-owned procedures rather than registry API:

Convert, then complete. In the pinned opengwasdb checkout, convert the parent to format 0.2.0 with the core’s conversion tool (scripts/convert_store_to_0_2_0.py; see the core’s own documentation and CHANGELOG), register the converted parent as its own release, then run the completion against the converted Store. The core tool is the authority on which layouts it supports and on its verification gate.
Rebuild the parent, then complete. A fresh pixi run release <parent> at the pinned runtime writes a new format-0.2.0 observed Store; the completion can then consume it. This is the only order that applies the current builder fixes to the parent’s bytes.

The runtime gate refuses the wrong order before any write and directs the operator here; it does not itself invoke a converter. Remember that converting or rebuilding a registered release is a catalogue action with its own gates, not a side effect of a completion run.



Bumping the pin changes what a new build is. It does not rebuild, convert, revalidate or requalify any published Store. Every registered Store built before the pin is still format 0.1.0, remains readable, and stays exactly as it was.
Consequences a build ticket must handle explicitly:

A Reference Completion of a 0.1.0 parent is refused at the gate above and by the core builder itself. Convert the parent to format 0.2.0 with the core’s conversion procedure, or rebuild the parent at the pinned runtime, then complete the converted/rebuild release. A completion never re-encodes its source. See “Converting or rebuilding a format-0.1.0 parent” above.
Each build ticket must therefore supply a compatible observed parent before it can register a completed descendant. The existence of a published 0.1.0 parent is not that parent.
The required by_variant/ index is part of a 0.2.0 build; a converted or older working copy that predates its required status still needs current validation.




Core opengwas/opengwasdb#254 (bounded Dense-validation memory) was not on dev when this pin was first taken (1be2a15). It has since merged (PR #276) and this pin was re-coordinated to 4e922566, which carries the same format and capability set plus the reduced validation memory bound (full-run peak RSS on OGS-00009 33.7 → 2.35 GiB, OGS-00010 36.5 → 3.01 GiB, validate clean). The earlier prohibition stands: do not install an uncommitted core checkout as the chosen runtime, and treat any future repin as a deliberate coordinated change.



Core opengwas/opengwasdb#289 adds opengwasdb check-observed-view, the Observed-View Check that gates a single-id completion’s swap (stores #306, ADR 0037). The pin was raised to 023774a7, the head of its PR #291, so the tracked runtime has the command. That PR merged into core dev as d405de0 (second parent 023774a7), and stores #312 then moved the pin to d405de0 itself, because the OGS-00009 rebuild needs core #288’s strand-aware hg19 lift, its first parent’s merge. A release that completes its own Store (ADR 0037) on a runtime without the command is refused before anything is written, by resources.verify_observed_view_check_for_releases, which the entry point calls in its dry run and its run, and the Snakefile in onstart, beside the Indexed Variant Subset guard.



Core opengwas/opengwasdb#295 extends check-observed-view from Dense pairs to Hybrid pairs: the Dense Components, every crossover (a source Overflow association whose ALID becomes a Dense row on completion), and a seeded sample of whole Overflow Analyses with exhaustive per-Analysis counts. Stores #333 moved the pin to eb4c749b, #295’s merge into the core integration branch orch/232-observed-view (core PR #303), so that a Hybrid release can complete its own Store (ADR 0037). That revision is not yet on core dev. The pin has since moved to the merge of core dev into that branch, which carries dev’s #304 and #298 as well (the pin table above); the branch itself has not merged into dev yet.
--help shows the same check-observed-view command on revisions that compare only Dense pairs, so the capability probe above cannot tell them apart. The exact-pin check is what refuses an older runtime for a Hybrid or Ragged single-id release: any revision other than the pin is refused before anything is written.



Core opengwas/opengwasdb#296 extends check-observed-view to Ragged pairs. A Ragged Store has no chunk-rows, so the check samples whole Analyses (--n-random of them, from the same seed) and, for each, rebuilds the regions completion retained from the LD panel: every observed association must come back identical and not imputed, and every imputed association must lie inside a retained region. That rebuild needs the panel completion used, so the check refuses a Ragged pair without --ld-panel (exit 2); --ancestry defaults to the one the completed Store records and, when given, must match it. The planner passes both from the bundle’s complete options. Stores #336 moved the pin to 32f47b3b, #296’s merge into the same integration branch, so that a Ragged release can complete its own Store (ADR 0037). Like eb4c749b, it is not yet on core dev.
The capability probe cannot tell 32f47b3b from eb4c749b either: it asks only whether check-observed-view --help succeeds, and on both it does. Here too the exact-pin check, not the probe, is what refuses an older runtime for a Ragged single-id release.
The check compares observed SE exactly. complete-ragged refits and re-quantises SE stored as int8_residual, which on real data moves every observed SE slightly (opengwas/opengwasdb#301), so a Ragged Store whose builder chose that encoding, as OGS-00006’s did, fails the check until #301 is resolved.



Core opengwas/opengwasdb#304 is the fix for the collision class the full eQTLGen cis Store (OGS-00027, stores #314) hit: 13 of its hg19 SNPs land on one hg38 variant after the lift, so d405de0’s validate passed a Store whose CSR held a variant_index twice in one Analysis’s segment. The pin moved to d8896e4, the dev merge of PR #305, whose range from d405de0 is #304’s three commits and its merge plus a docs-only merge (#293). The tightened ordering rule is a validation rule, so it applies to every release, not only to new builds: it reads each registered Ragged and Hybrid Store’s full variant_index and finds no repeat, so no published Store becomes invalid at this pin. A Store built before it that does carry a repeat must be rebuilt, not revalidated. ## Coordination with core #306
A single-pass Hybrid build whose variant reference names no rsids harvests a name for each source site, and two sites that case-fold to one routing key can disagree: the EBI GWAS-SSF Sources spell some alleles in lower case and carry a compound variant_id as their name. Refusing that was what stopped the OGS-00011 rebuild of 2026-10-22, at 1:905:C:T, and no option resolved it.
Core opengwas/opengwasdb#306 adds build-hybrid --on-rsid-conflict {refuse,drop}, default refuse, which is the behaviour it had. Under drop the disputed routing key gives no rsid to the variants it reaches: the table cell is . and the key is absent from the rsid index, which is how a Store already records a variant it can name no other way. The build always reports what its harvest compared as rsid_conflicts: {policy, n_keys, n_variants, sample} in its stdout JSON, with both counts 0 when nothing was disputed and null when no names were compared across sources (--reference-panel, or a reference that names its own rsids); a --reference-panel build refuses drop rather than ignore it. The same change normalises a compound rsN:pos:a:b id and the first item of a ; list in the readers, so a name that is really one rsid is compared as that rsid.
The policy is per Build Recipe, so it is the recipe that declares it; stores #225 adds on-rsid-conflict: drop to OGS-00011’s, as a Release Erratum, and register copies the counts into the Validation Record’s observed.rsid_conflicts. A release that completes its own Store carries them from its build phase, because complete-hybrid reports none: the counts describe the completed Store too. A checkpoint records the policy, so a build checkpointed before the option existed reads as refuse: resuming it under drop is refused, as resuming under any other changed parameter is.



A subset build on a Hybrid root indexes the release’s nested Dense Component, not the whole release: an ALID the release carries only on the shared/Overflow axis has a Variant Index there that this index cannot address. Resolving it against the Dense Component alone would count it absent and leave it out silently, so the builder refused the whole request and named the ALIDs. That is what stopped the OGS-00011 rebuild of 2026-10-23: 17,151 of the 1,206,903 HM3 ALIDs it requested were Overflow-only, and 149 were absent from the release altogether.
Core opengwas/opengwasdb#324 adds build-indexed-subset --overflow-only {refuse,skip}, default refuse, which is the behaviour it had and names the skip remedy when it refuses. Under skip the Overflow-only ALIDs stay out of the index, and the group records overflow_only_count – always written, 0 when there were none – beside the first 20 skipped ALIDs as overflow_only_sample, in variant-list order. The count is never folded into absent_count, which keeps its meaning: the release does not carry the ALID at all. The recorded counts must sum requested_count = resolved_count + absent_count + overflow_only_count, and both the read seam and validate enforce it. A group written before the option records neither attribute and is read as 0, because the builder that wrote it could only refuse such a request; a Dense root has no Overflow axis, so it accepts the flag with no effect.
The policy is per declared subset, so it is the declaration that carries it: stores #225 gives OGS-00011’s hm3 declaration options: {overflow-only: skip}, and the planner passes the whole options mapping through to both phases’ build-indexed-subset argv. The build prints the human counts and a JSON summary whose overflow_only block holds policy, n_overflow_only and the sample. register harvests no subset output – it reads the Store’s build or completion step – so the counts of a subset built here live in that step’s record, records/<phase>indexed-subset-<name>.json, and nowhere in the Validation Record.

title: The release runtime: pinned, current-format, and gated before writes
text:
Core opengwas/opengwasdb#295 extends check-observed-view from Dense pairs to Hybrid pairs: the Dense Components, every crossover (a source Overflow association whose ALID becomes a Dense row on completion), and a seeded sample of whole Overflow Analyses with exhaustive per-Analysis counts. Stores #333 moved the pin to eb4c749b, #295’s merge into the core integration branch orch/232-observed-view (core PR #303), so that a Hybrid release can complete its own Store (ADR 0037). That revision is not yet on core dev. The pin has since moved to the merge of core dev into that branch, which carries dev’s #304 and #298 as well (the pin table above); the branch itself has not merged into dev yet.
--help shows the same check-observed-view command on revisions that compare only Dense pairs, so the capability probe above cannot tell them apart. The exact-pin check is what refuses an older runtime for a Hybrid or Ragged single-id release: any revision other than the pin is refused before anything is written.

title: The release runtime: pinned, current-format, and gated before writes
text:
Core opengwas/opengwasdb#296 extends check-observed-view to Ragged pairs. A Ragged Store has no chunk-rows, so the check samples whole Analyses (--n-random of them, from the same seed) and, for each, rebuilds the regions completion retained from the LD panel: every observed association must come back identical and not imputed, and every imputed association must lie inside a retained region. That rebuild needs the panel completion used, so the check refuses a Ragged pair without --ld-panel (exit 2); --ancestry defaults to the one the completed Store records and, when given, must match it. The planner passes both from the bundle’s complete options. Stores #336 moved the pin to 32f47b3b, #296’s merge into the same integration branch, so that a Ragged release can complete its own Store (ADR 0037). Like eb4c749b, it is not yet on core dev.
The capability probe cannot tell 32f47b3b from eb4c749b either: it asks only whether check-observed-view --help succeeds, and on both it does. Here too the exact-pin check, not the probe, is what refuses an older runtime for a Ragged single-id release.
The check compares observed SE exactly. complete-ragged refits and re-quantises SE stored as int8_residual, which on real data moves every observed SE slightly (opengwas/opengwasdb#301), so a Ragged Store whose builder chose that encoding, as OGS-00006’s did, fails the check until #301 is resolved.

title: The release runtime: pinned, current-format, and gated before writes
text:
Core opengwas/opengwasdb#304 is the fix for the collision class the full eQTLGen cis Store (OGS-00027, stores #314) hit: 13 of its hg19 SNPs land on one hg38 variant after the lift, so d405de0’s validate passed a Store whose CSR held a variant_index twice in one Analysis’s segment. The pin moved to d8896e4, the dev merge of PR #305, whose range from d405de0 is #304’s three commits and its merge plus a docs-only merge (#293). The tightened ordering rule is a validation rule, so it applies to every release, not only to new builds: it reads each registered Ragged and Hybrid Store’s full variant_index and finds no repeat, so no published Store becomes invalid at this pin. A Store built before it that does carry a repeat must be rebuilt, not revalidated. ## Coordination with core #306
A single-pass Hybrid build whose variant reference names no rsids harvests a name for each source site, and two sites that case-fold to one routing key can disagree: the EBI GWAS-SSF Sources spell some alleles in lower case and carry a compound variant_id as their name. Refusing that was what stopped the OGS-00011 rebuild of 2026-10-22, at 1:905:C:T, and no option resolved it.
Core opengwas/opengwasdb#306 adds build-hybrid --on-rsid-conflict {refuse,drop}, default refuse, which is the behaviour it had. Under drop the disputed routing key gives no rsid to the variants it reaches: the table cell is . and the key is absent from the rsid index, which is how a Store already records a variant it can name no other way. The build always reports what its harvest compared as rsid_conflicts: {policy, n_keys, n_variants, sample} in its stdout JSON, with both counts 0 when nothing was disputed and null when no names were compared across sources (--reference-panel, or a reference that names its own rsids); a --reference-panel build refuses drop rather than ignore it. The same change normalises a compound rsN:pos:a:b id and the first item of a ; list in the readers, so a name that is really one rsid is compared as that rsid.
The policy is per Build Recipe, so it is the recipe that declares it; stores #225 adds on-rsid-conflict: drop to OGS-00011’s, as a Release Erratum, and register copies the counts into the Validation Record’s observed.rsid_conflicts. A release that completes its own Store carries them from its build phase, because complete-hybrid reports none: the counts describe the completed Store too. A checkpoint records the policy, so a build checkpointed before the option existed reads as refuse: resuming it under drop is refused, as resuming under any other changed parameter is.

title: The release runtime: pinned, current-format, and gated before writes
text:
A subset build on a Hybrid root indexes the release’s nested Dense Component, not the whole release: an ALID the release carries only on the shared/Overflow axis has a Variant Index there that this index cannot address. Resolving it against the Dense Component alone would count it absent and leave it out silently, so the builder refused the whole request and named the ALIDs. That is what stopped the OGS-00011 rebuild of 2026-10-23: 17,151 of the 1,206,903 HM3 ALIDs it requested were Overflow-only, and 149 were absent from the release altogether.
Core opengwas/opengwasdb#324 adds build-indexed-subset --overflow-only {refuse,skip}, default refuse, which is the behaviour it had and names the skip remedy when it refuses. Under skip the Overflow-only ALIDs stay out of the index, and the group records overflow_only_count – always written, 0 when there were none – beside the first 20 skipped ALIDs as overflow_only_sample, in variant-list order. The count is never folded into absent_count, which keeps its meaning: the release does not carry the ALID at all. The recorded counts must sum requested_count = resolved_count + absent_count + overflow_only_count, and both the read seam and validate enforce it. A group written before the option records neither attribute and is read as 0, because the builder that wrote it could only refuse such a request; a Dense root has no Overflow axis, so it accepts the flag with no effect.
The policy is per declared subset, so it is the declaration that carries it: stores #225 gives OGS-00011’s hm3 declaration options: {overflow-only: skip}, and the planner passes the whole options mapping through to both phases’ build-indexed-subset argv. The build prints the human counts and a JSON summary whose overflow_only block holds policy, n_overflow_only and the sample. register harvests no subset output – it reads the Store’s build or completion step – so the counts of a subset built here live in that step’s record, records/<phase>indexed-subset-<name>.json, and nowhere in the Validation Record.

title: Software management audit
text:
Historical record. This audit was written on 2026-08-05 and is kept as written. Its relative links into the family-first bundle archive are dead: that directory was retired in #252, and each bundle it held is now registered in stores/<store-id>/ or retired with git history keeping it.

Date: 2026-08-05


The repository has no unified, machine-readable software environment. There is no Python project/requirements file, R lockfile, Conda environment, container, tool-version file, Makefile, or CI workflow in the tree. Software requirements are instead implicit in imports, subprocess calls, shebangs, prose, and an external sibling checkout. Consequently a fresh checkout cannot be reproduced from repository metadata, and release-level script hashes preserve generator identity but not the software environment that executed the generator.
The workloads naturally divide into one shared environment plus two explicit external integrations:

Python/R report, generator, validation, and test code.
Bioinformatics command-line tools (plink2, bcftools) used by LD-panel acquisition and construction.
The separately developed opengwasdb Python package, currently consumed from a user-supplied checkout rather than declared as a package dependency.

The recommended target is a repository-owned Pixi workspace for Python, R, Quarto, and native tools, with one manifest, one lock, and named tasks; renv should not be added as a second competing resolver. CI should install the locked environments and run all lightweight tasks. opengwasdb should be declared at an immutable Git revision (or released package version) instead of being found through PYTHONPATH. Tools must live in the environment, never below a reference-data directory. The detailed decision is in software-management-proposal.md.



This is a static audit of tracked source files. Generated HTML was excluded as software evidence, as were local .git and .claude state and the contents of /data. The repository explicitly says that it stores metadata and small reports while large source/build artifacts live externally (README.md); that separation should also apply to software environments.








Runtime
Evidence and use
Version status




Python
Python 3 shebangs are used by the LD acquisition and generation scripts (acquire_hgdp1kgp.py) and tests (run_tests.py). Store builders use the ambiguous #!/usr/bin/env python shebang (build-store.py).
No version declared. Syntax such as X | None requires Python 3.10+, while datetime.UTC in resources/generators/lib/release_yaml.py requires 3.11+, making 3.11 the effective minimum.


R
Generators and tests run as Rscript; the shared generator workflow documents direct invocations (generator README).
No R version declared or locked.


Bash
The site build is a Bash script with strict mode (build-site.sh).
No Bash/platform version declared. It also assumes GNU-like utilities.


Quarto
Quarto renders the reports in the site build (build-site.sh).
No version declared. Only prose says to use an activated Conda environment (build-site.sh).


YAML/TSV/Markdown/QMD
Configuration, release metadata, manifests, documentation, and executable reports. Release build metadata names an import-style builder entry point (build.yaml).
Schema versions exist for domain metadata, but do not constrain software.






The only direct third-party scientific imports in this repository are:

numpy: LD construction, eigendecomposition, fixtures/tests, and the consumer smoke test (for example construct_block.py).
scipy (scipy.linalg): LD eigendecomposition (backfill_eigendecomposition.py).
opengwasdb: store construction/read-back, ancestry assignment, variant normalization, and LD consumption. Store construction imports its APIs directly (build-store.py).

Everything else imported is from the Python standard library or local resources.lib code. None of these packages has a declared version constraint. The documented workflow points PYTHONPATH at a separate checkout and invokes that checkout’s virtual-environment Python (generator README, ancestry workflow). The LD consumer similarly accepts an --opengwasdb-repo path and mutates sys.path (smoke_test_consumer.py).



Direct package usage comprises:

Core pipeline/tests: data.table, yaml (for example generate.R and run_tests.R).
Network-assisted SomaScan metadata generation: curl alongside data.table (generate-somascan-targets.R).
Curation/dashboard: tidyverse, data.table, and jsonlite (the broad tidyverse dependency is loaded in ebi-studies.r).
Reports: dplyr, ggplot2, knitr, scales, tibble, tidyr, DT, and data.table; the beta-scale report lists most explicitly (beta-scale-estimation.qmd) and the curation report also calls DT::datatable and knitr::kable.

No package versions or repository snapshot are recorded. Some dependencies are declared only through namespace calls rather than library(), which makes an informal package list easy to miss.






Executable/facility
Consumers
Declaration/pinning




plink2
Block extraction/export (construct_block.py) and VCF-to-PGEN conversion (materialize_reference.py).
Not versioned. Usually PATH-resolved, but materialization uniquely hard-codes <reference-root>/tools/bin/plink2.


bcftools
Header verification and index checks (acquire_hgdp1kgp.py, same file).
Not versioned; PATH-resolved.


curl CLI
Resumable gnomAD downloads (acquire_hgdp1kgp.py).
Not versioned; distinct from the R curl package.


GitHub CLI gh
Checks whether an external consumer issue is closed before smoke testing (smoke_test_consumer.py).
Not declared/versioned; also introduces network/auth/API availability into a smoke test.


git
resources/generators/lib/release_yaml.py discovers the repository root using git rev-parse.
Not declared/versioned.


GNU du
Store-size measurement invokes du -sb from Python (build-store.py); -b is not portable to BSD/macOS du.
Undeclared platform assumption.


Rscript, quarto, bash, cp
Generators/tests and documentation build (build-site.sh).
Only prose requirements, no versions.



Standard-library gzip readers handle compressed files in both languages; no direct bgzip/tabix subprocess dependency was found. bcftools supplies the VCF/index validation behavior.



There is no single project CLI or task definition. Users invoke scripts directly:

R generator modes (emit, filter, effect-scale, and refresh operations) are documented in the shared generator README (README).
Python store construction and ancestry assignment are separate direct script invocations using an external Python interpreter (README, README).
LD panel acquisition, membership, construction, orchestration, calibration, backfill, and consumer checks are individual scripts in resources/scripts/ld-panel/; run_panels.py composes construct_block.py using the current interpreter.
Tests are standalone Python/R scripts rather than a common test framework; the generation suite is run with python3 (test README).
The site has its own Bash orchestration script.

Release metadata records a generator script SHA-256 and command (release.yaml). This is valuable provenance, but it omits interpreter, libraries, native tools, platform, and the opengwasdb revision.



No tracked declaration was found for pip/uv/Poetry, Conda/Mamba, renv/pak, Nix, Docker/Apptainer, runtime version managers, or system packages. There are also no tracked GitHub Actions workflows or other CI definitions. The sole environment-management statement is the site’s comment that it expects an activated Conda environment, but that environment is not defined (build-site.sh).
The .gitignore deliberately separates generated/downloaded data from source (.gitignore), but has no standard local-environment entries such as .venv/, .Rproj.user/, or Conda prefix directories. This is another signal that a repository-local environment contract has not yet been established.





No reproducible bootstrap. A contributor cannot determine compatible Python, R, package, Quarto, PLINK, or bcftools versions from the checkout. Test success can depend on whatever happens to be installed on the host.
Software is mixed with reference data. materialize_reference.py hard-codes args.root / "tools/bin/plink2" (lines 13-16), while construct_block.py defaults to PATH-resolved plink2 (lines 158-166). These two resolution policies can silently run different versions and explain why an entire Conda prefix appeared beneath /data/opengwasdb/reference.
Two undeclared Python environments. General tests use python3; store workflows use a sibling checkout’s .venv/bin/python; two scripts use #!/usr/bin/env python; LD composition uses sys.executable. Results depend on invocation path.
External package revision is unrecorded. opengwasdb APIs are central to builds but are not pinned. The issue-state gate checks compatibility process, not the exact code executed.
R dependency surface is implicit and broad. tidyverse pulls a larger transitive set than the directly used packages, while report-only packages appear only inside QMD namespace calls. There is no lockfile or restore test.
No continuous verification. Standalone test scripts cover useful behavior, but nothing in the repository ensures they run together on a clean environment.
Platform assumptions are undocumented. GNU du -sb, Bash, and native bioinformatics binaries make the practical target Linux, yet no supported platform is stated.
Provenance stops at source code. Generator hashes and pinned data releases do not capture software versions, lockfile digest, commands of every pipeline stage, or platform. Rebuilding an immutable release therefore remains under-specified.






Add a human-maintained pixi.toml and generated pixi.lock. Use strict channels and include:

Python 3.11 (the effective current minimum), NumPy, SciPy, and the chosen packaging/bootstrap tools.
R plus the enumerated R packages (data.table, yaml, curl, jsonlite, dplyr, ggplot2, knitr, scales, tibble, tidyr, DT; avoid the tidyverse metapackage unless its full surface is intentionally required).
Quarto, PLINK2, bcftools, curl, Git, and GitHub CLI.

This repository spans Python, R, Quarto, and compiled bioinformatics tools; Pixi uses the Conda ecosystem already assumed in project prose and can describe the whole stack while also providing named environments and tasks. Adding renv as well would create two authorities for R packages. If exact cross-platform R locking proves unreliable, declare Linux x86-64 as the supported production platform rather than pretending to offer an untested portable environment.
Keep the installed prefix in a user/cache location such as /data/opengwasdb/software/envs/opengwasdb-stores/<lock-digest> or the standard Conda package/env cache. Never place it under /data/opengwasdb/reference/<resource-id>; reference directories should contain only source data, derived artifacts, manifests, and logs.



Prefer a released package version. Until one exists, pin an immutable Git commit in the environment’s pip subsection (or a small pyproject.toml dependency group) and install it into the same environment. Remove PYTHONPATH mutation and sibling .venv assumptions. If simultaneous development of both repositories is required, document an explicit editable-install override as a developer-only workflow; release production must record and use a commit.



Resolve plink2, bcftools, curl, and gh from PATH after environment activation, with optional CLI overrides for exceptional deployments. Add a preflight command that prints and validates every required executable and package version. Remove <reference-root>/tools/bin/plink2; a reference root is data configuration, not software configuration.



Define Pixi tasks that orchestrate existing scripts, for example env-check, test, test-python, test-r, docs, ld-acquire, and ld-materialize. Commands should use python and Rscript from the selected locked environment. Standardize all Python shebangs on #!/usr/bin/env python3 (or avoid relying on shebangs in recipes).
The task interface should not hide data-intensive behavior: LD acquisition and panel generation must remain explicit targets requiring a reference root, never part of the default test target.



Add Linux CI that installs the Pixi environments (cached by lock digest) and runs every lightweight test script plus a site-render smoke test. Large downloads and full panel builds should be excluded; fixtures already allow the LD numerical behavior to be tested cheaply. A scheduled or manually dispatched job may exercise network-dependent metadata acquisition separately.



Alongside the existing generator hash, record:

Git commits for this repository and opengwasdb.
pixi.lock SHA-256 and environment/platform identifier.
python --version, R --version, plink2 --version, bcftools --version, and quarto --version.
The exact stage command and relevant non-secret environment configuration.

Store this as a small tracked or externally referenced build-environment manifest. It complements, rather than replaces, release metadata’s generator hash.





Create and lock pixi.toml from the inventory above; add an environment preflight script and verify all current lightweight tests.
Pin/install opengwasdb in that environment and eliminate sibling checkout and PYTHONPATH requirements.
Change LD scripts to PATH-based tools with optional overrides, then move or rebuild the current environment outside the reference resource directory. Do not move/delete an environment while active panel processes use it.
Introduce the task runner and CI using the same lock files.
Add the build-environment provenance manifest to the next generated release and reference-resource build.

This sequence leaves existing data and running jobs untouched while establishing one authority for all future software installation and execution.

The task interface should not hide data-intensive behavior: LD acquisition and panel generation must remain explicit targets requiring a reference root, never part of the default test target.



Add Linux CI that installs the Pixi environments (cached by lock digest) and runs every lightweight test script plus a site-render smoke test. Large downloads and full panel builds should be excluded; fixtures already allow the LD numerical behavior to be tested cheaply. A scheduled or manually dispatched job may exercise network-dependent metadata acquisition separately.



Alongside the existing generator hash, record:

Git commits for this repository and opengwasdb.
pixi.lock SHA-256 and environment/platform identifier.
python --version, R --version, plink2 --version, bcftools --version, and quarto --version.
The exact stage command and relevant non-secret environment configuration.

Store this as a small tracked or externally referenced build-environment manifest. It complements, rather than replaces, release metadata’s generator hash.

title: Software management audit
text:
Create and lock pixi.toml from the inventory above; add an environment preflight script and verify all current lightweight tests.
Pin/install opengwasdb in that environment and eliminate sibling checkout and PYTHONPATH requirements.
Change LD scripts to PATH-based tools with optional overrides, then move or rebuild the current environment outside the reference resource directory. Do not move/delete an environment while active panel processes use it.
Introduce the task runner and CI using the same lock files.
Add the build-environment provenance manifest to the next generated release and reference-resource build.

This sequence leaves existing data and running jobs untouched while establishing one authority for all future software installation and execution.

title: Analysis Catalog
text:
The specification of pixi run catalog (#323, epic #313). The decisions behind it are ADR 0039; the words are CONTEXT.md’s. This file is the contract: the command, the serving decisions, the tables, and the files a rebuild writes.
The catalog is the package src/analysis_catalog/. It imports only ogstores.bundle and ogstores.paths from ogstores, and nothing in ogstores or manifest_generation imports it (tests/packaging/test_boundary.py). It reads Release Bundles and never opens a Store (ADR 0023).


pixi run catalog [--registry stores] [--artifact-root PATH]

--registry is the directory of Release Bundles; it defaults to stores/ of the checkout.
The Artifact Root resolves as ogstores.paths.artifact_root does: --artifact-root, then OPENGWASDB_ARTIFACT_ROOT, then ogstores.yaml.
It refuses to build, and writes nothing, when the registry is a git repository with uncommitted or untracked changes, because the commit it records would then be false. A registry that is not a git repository (a test fixture) records a NULL commit.
Run it on the host after a merge to dev, from a dedicated clean checkout of origin/dev, not a shared working checkout (ADR 0039). It prints each registered Store Release’s decision, the version, and whether it published, moved current, or was a no-op.




Every registered Store Release (each OGS-xxxxx directory of the registry) gets one decision and a reason, in selection. The first rule that applies decides:









#
Fact
Decision
Reason




1
bundle.check() returns errors
refused
bundle.check() failed: and the errors


2
Trial Store Release
excluded
Trial Store Release


3
Access Posture is embargoed
excluded
Access Posture is embargoed


4
Release Status is candidate, accepted or built
excluded
Release Status is <status>, not validated


5
Release Status is superseded or withdrawn, and the Validation Record is not passed or passed_with_warnings
excluded
retired before validation


6
Release Status is validated, and Access Posture is neither public nor controlled
refused
Access Posture is <value>; a listed Store is public or controlled


7
Release Status is validated, superseded or withdrawn, and observed.n_analyses is missing or not an integer
refused
Validation Record has no integer observed.n_analyses


8
the admitted Release Manifest count differs from observed.n_analyses
refused
Release Manifest admits <n> Analyses but the Validation Record's observed.n_analyses is <m>


9
a manifest or Validation Record value cannot be stored exactly, or check() tolerates ‘:’ in an analysis_id under #319
refused
analyses.tsv row '<analysis_id>': <column> '<value>' is not an integer (or a finite number, and so on), or the Release Manifest carries analysis_id values containing ':' (<n>), tolerated by bundle.check() under #319


10
Release Status is superseded or withdrawn
placeholder
Release Status is <status>: kept as placeholder rows, not listed


11
Release Status is validated
listed
Release Status is validated, Access Posture is <public or controlled>



The Fact and Decision columns are analysis_catalog.policy.RULES verbatim and in order, which decide implements, catalog_meta.serving_policy records, report.md quotes when nothing is listed, and tests/catalog/test_catalog.py checks this table and ADR 0039’s list against.

A refused Store does not stop the build; the other Stores are decided on their own.
check() runs first because Bundle.trial raises on a malformed trial.
A placeholder Store passes the same count and type checks as a listed one (rules 7 to 9), and a failure refuses it, so a refused retired Store is not resolvable. A retired Trial Store Release or embargoed Store is excluded by rules 2 and 3 first, and never becomes a placeholder.
A retired release that never passed validation was never served, so it is excluded (rule 5), not refused, and has no rows. That is every retired release whose Validation Record is missing or not passed or passed_with_warnings: check() does not require a record of a retired release, and a candidate or accepted one that was retired has null counts. A retired release that did pass but has no observed.n_analyses is refused by rule 7, as a validated one is.
check() reads superseded_by only on a superseded release (it refuses it on any other status), so the catalog reads it through Bundle.superseded_by and has no rule of its own for a withdrawn one.
A n_associations below 0 refuses the Store, as register refuses it.
The one exception is the schema’s own absence marker: a literal NaN in info_score_threshold (“unavailable”) or maf_threshold (“no MAF filter”) is NULL (docs/release-metadata-schema.md), distinct from 0, which stays 0.0. Reading the marker is not a coercion; in any other numeric column NaN refuses the Store.
A value is never coerced or rounded: an integer outside SQLite’s signed 64 bits, a NaN or infinity, and a finite nonzero real that would become 0.0 or inf each refuse the Store, naming the Analysis, column and value. A bad cell never stops the build.
A value is never coerced: a non-numeric cell in a numeric column refuses its Store, naming the Analysis and the column.




One SQLite file, catalog.sqlite, built in one transaction into a fresh file, one Store at a time: a Store’s rows are inserted as its decision is made, and a Store refused on a value in its rows is rolled back whole. Memory is set by the largest single Store’s manifest. The columns and their types are src/analysis_catalog/columns.py.

stores: one row per listed or placeholder Store Release, with the columns of epic #313. superseded_by is the successor’s Store id for a superseded Store and NULL for a withdrawn one (check() refuses a superseded_by on any other status). A Store that is excluded or refused has no row, so nothing excluded is discoverable here; selection is where it is accounted for. Facts come from release.yaml (label, description, status, superseded_by, access_posture, source_snapshot_id, accepted_at, notes, and association_coverage), build.yaml (layout, completion_state) and validation.yaml (validated_at, build_environment.opengwasdb_version, and from observed: n_analyses, n_variants, n_associations, store_bytes, format_version, reference_assembly). reference_assembly is opengwasdb’s value stored as reported, and NULL while a record lacks it (opengwasdb#294). association_coverage is the release’s own declaration, in the one vocabulary of ADR 0040 (gwas, cis, cis_and_signals, signals_only), never the Validation Record’s observed value: opengwasdb#298 makes coverage a build input, so the bundle states it. It is never NULL for a registered bundle, because bundle.check() requires it. A count that is not an integer refuses the Store.
analyses: one row per admitted Release Manifest row of a listed or placeholder Store (ADR 0025: rows not excluded from build), keyed by id <store_id>:<analysis_id>. status is the Store Release’s Release Status, and listed is 1 for an Analysis of a listed Store and 0 for a placeholder row. A client resolves any identifier by id; the successor is stores.superseded_by. A column a bundle lacks, and an empty cell, are NULL, never 0 or ''. sample_size, n_cases, n_controls and trait_bp are INTEGER; original_sd, maf_threshold and info_score_threshold are REAL. analysis_label falls back to source_label, and label_from_source is 1 on a row where it did (the manifest had no analysis_label), 0 otherwise. Build internals (source_file, checksums, inclusion_reason, exclude_from_build, analysis_index) are not carried.
selection: store_id, decision, reason, for every registered Store Release.
catalog_meta: key, value: version, built_at, registry_commit (NULL outside git), builder_version, and serving_policy (the rules above, as a JSON list).



Each new version carries summary.html, rendered from docs/reports/analysis-catalog-summary.qmd after the version’s other files are written and before current moves. A render failure fails the rebuild: the .partial version is removed and current stays. A no-op rebuild renders nothing. The report opens catalog.sqlite read-only and reads the version’s changes.tsv; it recomputes nothing from the bundles. A total over Stores is unknown (k of n Stores report it) whenever any listed Store has a NULL, and is never a partial sum. An empty catalog renders and says so.
Rendering needs Quarto and R beside the builder, so the operator runs pixi run catalog, which runs in the dev environment (the task’s default-environment) and uses that environment’s own Quarto, refusing before it builds anything when none is active. pixi run -e dev catalog-summary-smoke renders the report against a fixture catalog (tests/catalog/smoke_summary.py).



One way to list. listed_analyses is the view SELECT * FROM analyses WHERE listed = 1. A listing, a keyset page, a region lookup all read it, and every index below is a partial index WHERE listed = 1, which SQLite uses through the view. A search joins analyses by rowid, because the full-text index holds listed rows only. A placeholder row is reached only by id (or store_id) on analyses.
Analysis type and ancestry category are three columns of analyses, derived once at build (analysis_catalog.policy.outcome_type, trait_class and ancestry_category):

outcome_type: binary when sample_size_kind is case_control or stored_effect_scale is log_or (#324), so (sd, case_control) and (log_hazard, case_control) are binary; continuous for (sd, total) and every other (sd, sample size kind) the contract defines but case_control, such as (sd, variant_level) (#362), because an SD effect is standardised whatever the sample size’s granularity; NULL otherwise, including a blank. Never a guess.
trait_class: molecular when any of context, tissue or trait_chr is set, phenotype otherwise. A Store whose bundle lacks the three columns is phenotype.
ancestry_category: assigned_ancestry when set; META when it is empty and source_ancestry_label is exactly META; NULL (unassigned) otherwise. The Assigned Ancestry vocabulary is unchanged: META is the catalog’s category, never a stored Assigned Ancestry.

Counts are the table counts (dimension, value, n_analyses), computed at build over listed Analyses only. The dimensions are store, ancestry (ancestry_category), tissue, effect_scale (stored_effect_scale), outcome_type, trait_class and coverage (the Store Release’s declared association_coverage, never relabelled). A NULL value is a category of its own, and so is META; any other value is counted as it stands. Each dimension sums to the number of listed Analyses.
Search is the FTS5 table analysis_search over analysis_label, trait_ontology_label, consortium and first_author, external-content on the view listed_search_content (listed rows, exposing the analyses rowid), so rebuild and integrity-check agree with what is indexed and a placeholder row is never in it. It joins by rowid:
SELECT a.* FROM analysis_search s JOIN analyses a ON a.rowid = s.rowid
WHERE analysis_search MATCH ? ORDER BY rank LIMIT ?
Indexes (all partial, WHERE listed = 1): (id); (col, id) for each sortable column store_id, analysis_label, trait_ontology_label, assigned_ancestry, tissue, stored_effect_scale, sample_size and the derived ancestry_category, outcome_type and trait_class (the columns of the website table and its filters, user stories 2 and 3 of epic #313); and (trait_chr, trait_bp, id) for region lookups. ORDER BY col, id LIMIT n and WHERE (col, id) > (?, ?) ORDER BY col, id LIMIT n use them. A row-value comparison is never true for a NULL col, so a cursor over a nullable column pages its NULL rows first with col IS NULL AND id > ?, then the rest with the row-value form.




<artifact-root>/catalog/
  versions/<version>/
    catalog.sqlite
    stores.tsv          the stores table, tab-separated, NULL as an empty cell
    analyses.tsv.gz     the analyses table, the same
    changes.tsv         every added, removed or changed Analysis id (not on a first build)
    report.md           every decision and reason, and the change since the previous version
  current -> versions/<version>

The version is the first 16 hex digits of a SHA-256 over exactly these inputs, which are everything a decision depends on:

the builder’s version and the serving policy;
the sorted list of registered store ids, so an empty directory changes it;
every *.py source file of analysis_catalog and of ogstores (check(), Bundle, partition_membership, LEGACY_ANALYSIS_ID_RELEASES);
the installed opengwasdb, whose reader parses the manifest: its distribution version and, when the install records one (direct_url.json), its commit;
the summary template (docs/reports/analysis-catalog-summary.qmd);
every file of every registered Release Bundle directory, read in fixed-size chunks.

Decisions are not hashed: they are a function of those inputs, so the version is known before any Release Manifest row is read. It does not include the build time or the registry commit.
A rebuild whose version exists writes nothing, reads no Release Manifest row, and moves current only if it names another version. Its decisions are those in that version’s selection.
Publication: the build is written to versions/<version>.partial/, renamed to versions/<version>/, and current is then swapped atomically (a temporary symlink, then os.replace). A failed build removes its partial directory and leaves current alone. A .partial directory left by a crash is replaced by the next build. The database is written with synchronous = OFF, so before the rename every file of the .partial directory and the directory itself are fsynced; after it versions/ is, and after the current swap catalog/ is. A host crash cannot leave a torn version, which is immutable and so would never be rebuilt.
Retention: the 5 most recent versions (by built_at) are kept; the version current names is never deleted.
report.md: the registered, listed, placeholder, excluded and refused counts; a sentence beginning No Store Release is listed: when none is; a table of every Store Release’s decision and reason; and, against the previous current, Analyses added, Analyses removed and Analyses with changed metadata as counts, a sample of 20 ids of each (with the columns that changed), and each Store Release whose decision changed. changes.tsv holds every id with its change (added, removed or changed).

title: Analysis Catalog
Release config
text:
The one connector file written per Store Release (#287).
Governed by ADR 0036: a source plugs into Manifest Generation through four files. Three belong to the Source Collection – the Acquisition Manifest, the Source Metadata Table and the Column Map (source connectors) – and the fourth, the release config, belongs to one Store Release. It names everything the shared pipeline needs that is not the Source Collection’s: the release’s identity, the Selection, the Build Recipe shape, the release policy and its Quality Check overrides, the Reference Resources, and the collection-wide defaults.



Contract
Owner




Schema and loader
src/manifest_generation/release_config.py (load_release_config)


Selection grammar
src/manifest_generation/selection.py (spec)


Quality Check names and thresholds
src/manifest_generation/quality_checks.py


Indexed Variant Subset default
src/manifest_generation/indexed_subsets.py



Loading is a gate. An unknown key at any level, a missing required field, a value outside its vocabulary, a Reference Resource reference that names no declared resource (or one of the wrong kind), and the legacy Selection grammar are refused, each by name. Nothing is ignored and no required fact is defaulted. A relative path is relative to the repository root.
A config states release_config_version: 1. A file without it predates this schema: the generator configs that produced the committed bundles (config-full.yaml, config-pilot-10.yaml, …) are kept unchanged as the history their bundles’ generator.commands cite, and are refused here by that key.





Key
Required
Description




release_config_version
Yes
1.


label
Yes
Source-natural release name, written to release.yaml. Never an identifier.


association_coverage
Yes
What associations the Store holds, written to release.yaml right after label:, in one vocabulary with opengwasdb (issue #341, ADR 0040): gwas, cis, cis_and_signals or signals_only. It is declared, never inferred from the Store Layout. A region-filtered config must declare the coverage its region_policy.association_coverage names, so the two cannot disagree.


access_posture
No
public, controlled or embargoed; public only when the key is absent, so an explicit false or blank is refused.


trial
No
true for a Trial Store Release: a deliberately small release that exercises a Source Collection, Source Format or Store Layout (#321). It must be a YAML boolean, so a quoted "yes", a number or null is refused. true writes trial: true to release.yaml (the schema). Absent or false writes no key, which means false, so such a release renders exactly as before the key existed. Every shipped pilot and probe config sets it.


description
Yes
Prose for release.yaml.


notes
No
Prose; the candidate’s own evidence notes follow it in release.yaml.


source_collection
Yes
The Source Collection and its files (below).


selection
Yes
The Selection, in #283’s grammar: exactly one of all: true, analyses: [...] or where: {...}, with an optional expect_rows membership bound.


build
Yes
The Build Recipe shape build.yaml carries (below).


completion
No
For a reference-completed release, the recipe and the LD panel it completes against (below, #340, ADR 0037).


indexed_subsets, indexed_subsets_opt_out
No
Dense and Hybrid releases declare the maintained hm3 Indexed Variant Subset by default; [] with a reason opts out; a Ragged release declares none (stores #210).


defaults
Yes
Collection-wide Analytical Metadata defaults and the method tiers (below).


release_policy
Yes
Membership policy inputs (below).


quality_checks
No
Quality Check threshold overrides: a registered check’s name to its threshold for this release (#285).


reference_resources
Yes
The Reference Resources the run uses (below).


ancestry_assignment
Yes
What Analysis Resolution measures ancestry against (below).


effect_scale_validation
No
Phenotype-SD evidence settings (below).


trait_ontology_mapping
Yes
The Canonical Trait Mapping Table (below).


column_map
No; required exactly when build.options.source-reader-capability is opengwasdb.column-map
The Column Map the release reads its sources through: builtin: <name> or path: <file>, one of the two (below, #292).


region_policy
No
For a region-filtered release, the regions acquisition filters its files to (below, #300).


runtime
No
cores (default 1, capped at 64 by preflight) and min_free_gb (default 0).


output
Yes

Description

Yes

No; both or neither

layout, completion_state, command and post are required, options is not. completion_state is observed_only or reference_completed; a reference_completed config declares the completion block that says what it completes against, and an observed_only one declares none (below). command names an opengwasdb subcommand and options are its flags, passed through verbatim (ADR 0023): options is opaque by design, and its keys are not checked here. post is the registry’s own vocabulary – top_hits, overview, rho and validate, each true or false, the steps ogstores.plan plans – so an unknown key or a non-boolean is refused. A release that is completed against an LD reference panel declares the recipe and the reference (#340, ADR 0037). Required
Description




reference.resource_id
Yes
A declared ld_panel Reference Resource (below).


reference.qualification
Yes
The owner’s: qualified, pending, hold or not_applicable.


reference.activation
Yes

command
Yes

The reference’s declared status is not a key here. It is the Reference Resource declaration’s own status (available), read from its resource.yaml and recorded, and it is kept apart from qualification and activation: a declared status is neither, and a config that restates one is refused as an unknown key.
The bundle completes its Store only when the reference is qualified and active. Then build.yaml declares completion_state: reference_completed, build and complete, and release.yaml carries no derived_from; the build block is exactly the Observed-Only one, so completing a published Store schedules no rebuild (ADR 0037 clarified by #305). Anything short of that – pending, hold, blocked – emits the Observed-Only bundle a config with no completion block emits, and records why: the release notes say the recipe is blocked, and validation.yaml’s acceptance.completion_reference carries the declared reference with blocked: true. A blocked recipe is not an error: the release is still emitted, as the Observed-Only Store it is ready to be.
What the recipe cannot contradict, each refused by name:

a layout other than dense (see above);
a complete-dense option naming the panel;
the reference’s ancestry, from its declaration, differing from release_policy.selection_superpopulation: completion imputes against a panel for the Store’s Assigned Ancestry;
a declaration whose ancestry_dir is not its ancestry, because complete-dense names both the panel directory and the Analyses it completes with one --ancestry (#219);
a qualified, active reference whose declaration records no status: the status is recorded as it is, and never defaulted;
build.completion_state: reference_completed with no completion block, and observed_only with one;
the retired completed_store_id / planned_completed_store_id (ADR 0007’s second id, which ADR 0037 removes).

The panel is resolved only when the reference is qualified and active. Then its location is the reference_resources entry’s, which preflight requires present, and its status, ancestry and ancestry_dir are the declaration’s, so the recipe cannot name a panel other than the one the resource declares. A blocked reference is never opened: its declaration need not exist, its panel need not be present, and no panel need be declared at all – so a blocked recipe still emits the Observed-Only bundle on a host that has no panel.
build:
  layout: dense
  completion_state: reference_completed
  command: build-dense-vcf
  options:
    source-reader-capability: opengwasdb.gwas-vcf
    source-assembly: hg19
    n-workers: 32
  post:
    top_hits: true
    overview: true

reference_resources:
  - resource_id: ukb-hg38-eur-ld
    kind: ld_panel
    location: /data/opengwasdb/reference/ld
    location_kind: external_directory
  # ... the ancestry mixture and the Canonical Trait Mapping Table

completion:
  reference:
    resource_id: ukb-hg38-eur-ld
    qualification: qualified
    activation: active
  command: complete-dense
  options:
    n-workers: 32

Description

Yes

A tier’s sample_size_kind decides whether the Analysis carries case/control counts: case_control keeps its n_cases/n_controls and requires both, and any other kind leaves them blank (analyses.tsv’s absence rule, #133). Required
Description

Yes
The super-population code (AFR AMR EAS EUR MID NAF SAS) the Selection expects, or multi-ancestry for a Selection that names none (#290). The assigned_ancestry Quality Check tests each Assigned Ancestry against it; it never moves an Analysis (ADR 0036). multi-ancestry makes that check not_applicable: the measured fit is recorded and never assigned, so the emitted Assigned Ancestry stays empty with method unassigned and no Analysis is excluded for ancestry.


store_composition.require_maf_filtered
No
The Store Composition Rule (ADR 0033). Needs a positive defaults.maf_threshold.


trust_source_ancestry_without_af

The record shows it only under a MAF request, so the opt-in needs defaults.maf_threshold (0 filters nothing): the resolver then counts every row without a usable frequency (maf_rows_missing), and absence is every row it read (canonical_rows_observed) with no ancestry site. Default false: such an Analysis is ancestry_unassigned. A measured ancestry never takes the source label, and frequencies the fit could not read (palindromic sites, unusable standard errors) are not absent.


keep_unassigned_ancestry_as_warning
No
true opts in to #290’s decision: an Analysis the ancestry gates left unassigned (Assigned Ancestry empty in its Resolution Record, with frequencies it could read) stays in, unassigned – Ancestry Assignment Method unassigned, a warning-level assigned_ancestry result counted in validation.yaml and recorded per Analysis in the Quality Check sidecar. A measured different super-population still excludes as ancestry_not_eur, and the opt-in is refused in a multi-ancestry Selection, which never assigns ancestry.


imputation_score_declarations
No
The reviewed per-Analysis INFO score declarations (#175). The table is the Source Collection’s, so Selections may share it: a declaration may name an Analysis outside the Selection when the collection intends it (the original Source Metadata Table the snapshot’s provenance checksums), and only the Selection’s apply. A declaration the collection does not intend is refused, and so is one outside the Selection when that table is not on the host.

Technologies exempt from the MAF floor (#176). Policy over a fact: an Analysis is exempt when its Source Metadata Table genotyping_technology is non-empty and every technology it lists is named here. maf_filter_exempt_analyses
No
The reviewed per-Analysis MAF-floor exemptions (#176).


effect_placeholder_exclusions
No
The reviewed effect-placeholder listing the effect_placeholder_rows Quality Check reads (#285).






A region-filtered release – Chen 2023, Sun 2018 – keeps only the regions its policy names, and acquisition applies it: download, filter, delete the original, recording the policy in each filtered file’s lineage (ADR 0036 clarified by #300, region-filtered acquisition). The policy is per release config.








Key
Required
Description




region_policy_id
Yes
The policy’s name, recorded in lineage (sig-trans-1mb_suggestive-leads).


association_coverage
Yes
signals_only, or cis_and_signals to keep a cis flank around each Analysis’s target.


cis_flank_bp
For cis_and_signals only
Bases kept either side of the Source Metadata Table’s target span (target_chromosome, target_start, target_end); refused for signals_only.


trans_flank_bp
Yes
Bases kept either side of every significant row outside the cis window.


significant_p, suggestive_p
Yes
p-values in (0, 1]; significant_p may not exceed suggestive_p.


suggestive_lead_min_distance_bp
Yes
How far apart, strictly more than, the suggestive leads kept on one chromosome are.


qc_panel_resource_id
Yes
A declared qc_panel Reference Resource, whose positions every filtered file keeps so Analysis Resolution can measure ancestry and SD. Preflight requires it present.



association_coverage is one of the policy’s, not a free choice: the release’s top-level association_coverage must name the same value, because a policy is what filters the acquisition and the bundle declares what the Store holds.
The frozen acquisition must have been filtered to exactly this policy: preflight and rendering refuse a file whose lineage records another policy, another QC panel sha256 or another target span, a policy declared over unfiltered files, and region-filtered files under a config that declares no region_policy (source connectors).



A release that reads its sources through the opengwasdb.column-map Source Reader Capability names its Column Map, and no other release may: build.options.source-reader-capability: opengwasdb.column-map and a column_map block go together, and either without the other is refused.

builtin is the name of a map OpenGWASDB ships (gwas-ssf, finngen-r13).
path is a map file this release carries, absolute or repository-relative. Its file name must be a valid column_maps/ file name (a .toml name of the Indexed Variant Subset grammar).

The resolver is passed it as --column-map, a built-in’s name or the file’s path. build.yaml binds it as column_map: {name, sha256, file}, with no file for a built-in, and a carried map is copied into the bundle’s column_maps/. name and sha256 are what OpenGWASDB records as each Resolution Record’s resolution_config.column_map, so a built-in’s checksum is the file the pinned package ships. The checksum is part of the resolution contract: a changed map makes every Resolution Record stale and the resolver re-resolves them. The Column Map’s contract and how Store Release Build uses it are in Source connectors and the release metadata schema.



reference_resources lists each resource the run uses: resource_id, kind and location are required; location_kind, version, status, fine_group_map, ancestry, super_populations, genome_build and variant_id_convention are optional. A resource_id declared twice is refused. Four blocks use them, by id:

ancestry_assignment.reference_resource_id (required) names the ancestry mixture the resolver measures against: an ancestry_mixture resource, with a fine_group_map. The resolver’s --reference-build is the genome_build of that resource’s declaration, resources/reference-resources/<id>/resource.yaml, not of this entry; a missing declaration or genome_build is refused, because the resolver never guesses a build (opengwasdb#277). liftover_chain_resource_id (optional) names the chain the resolver lifts a source build that differs from that reference build with: a liftover_chain resource, whose declaration states its from_genome_build, to_genome_build and sha256. The resolver is passed --chain-file for its location; a chain whose to_genome_build is not the reference build is refused when the settings are composed, because that is a declaration. The file’s own bytes are checked before the resolve stage starts the resolver: a chain that is absent, or whose sha256 is not the declared one, refuses the run by name. Without a chain the resolver refuses a source on another build. The declared checksum is part of the resolution contract, and it is the declared one that the settings digest covers – composing a run’s settings reads no liftover chain file, so a config whose chain lives under /data still composes on a CI runner that has no /data. maf_floor (default 0.01), extraction_panel (default none) and gates (tau 0.50, delta 0.20, n_min 5000, residual_max 0.06) are passed to the resolver as written.
effect_scale_validation.reference_resources lists {ancestry, resource_id} reference-AF resources for phenotype-SD estimation. maf_min, maf_max and dispersion_max are recorded in sidecars/sd_estimation.tsv; dispersion_max (default 0.5) marks a high-dispersion estimate.
trait_ontology_mapping.reference_resource_id (required) names the Canonical Trait Mapping Table, a trait_ontology_mapping resource whose location is its resource directory (#286).
completion.reference.resource_id names the LD panel a reference-completed release completes against: an ld_panel resource whose location is the panel root and whose declaration names its status, ancestry and ancestry_dir (#340).

Preflight requires every named resource to be present.
