title: Convert every layout to 0.2.0, and bound the Ragged shards
text:
Issue #248, epic #240. This is a short successor to ADR 0057, which records what format 0.2.0 is and why conversion — not a rebuild — is the migration route. It records the two decisions #248 adds: that the converter handles every layout rather than one, and how the Ragged 1-D arrays are sharded, which #246 does not decide.


ADR 0057 landed a converter for one layout, Dense Observed-Only, as the tracer. The rest of the epic needs the other layouts converted the same way, because a store whose values are right and whose layout is old should not be rebuilt:

Ragged (Observed-Only and Reference-Completed): a CSR group whose parallel sequences are read by Analysis. OGS-00001 and OGS-00002 are the pilots.
Hybrid: a top-level release whose nested Dense Component is a Store Release with its own manifest, index.sqlite and data.zarr (spec §16). OGS-00004 and OGS-00005 are the pilots, and OGS-00011 (#250) is the large one.
Dense Reference-Completed: the Dense tracer plus the imputed mask, on_panel, eaf_reference and the SE/EAF side tables. OGS-00010 is the pilot, 13,549,988 variants × 2,024 Analyses.

#245’s review left a recorded-layout gap it could not close: a Hybrid Dense Component’s manifest has no provenance.dense.chunk_shape; the layout lived only in the outer provenance.hybrid, which the component validator never sees.
The Ragged arrays force a shard decision #246 does not own. #246 benchmarks the Dense Analysis-axis inner chunk and shard. The Ragged sequences are 1-D and read by Analysis, and OGS-00011’s overflow sequences are 3,085,080,783 entries at a 200,000-element inner chunk. #245’s proposed default — about one million elements per shard — would make 3,086 files per sequence, and the whole-array policy it used for exception tables would make OGS-00011’s 180,396,687-entry Ragged eaf_exception_index a single 1.4 GB file.





opengwasdb.store.convert / scripts/convert_store_to_0_2_0.py no longer refuses Dense Reference-Completed, Ragged or Hybrid. role
shard




Ragged association sequences (ragged/z, se, variant_index, eaf, imputed)
50,000,000 elements

10,000,000 elements

10,000,000 elements



Each is rounded to a whole number of inner chunks and clipped to the array, so the shard is always a whole multiple of the inner chunk.

Refuse everything but Dense Observed-Only and convert each layout in its own ticket. It would fork the plan/verify/publish machinery per layout and leave the recorded-layout gap open; rejected.
Keep one million elements per Ragged shard (#245’s proposed default). 3,086 files per OGS-00011 sequence is file-count overhead for no read benefit, since the inner chunk is what a query reads; rejected.

title: Indexed Variant Subsets are optional full-statistic Dense query indexes
text:
Issue #262 asks for extraction of the approximately 1.2 million HapMap3 variants from one Analysis in under one second; issue #263 specifies the implementation. On OGS-00009 the #262 prototype found a membership index alone does not do that: those variants touch 9,822 of the Dense Z plane’s 9,848 row chunks, so selecting their Store-local Variant Indices still took a warm median of 15.37 seconds. This decision adds an optional Analysis-major derived index, accepts its bounded storage cost, and keeps the primary statistic planes authoritative.


An Indexed Variant Subset is a named, optional, rebuildable Dense-store query index over a caller-supplied set of canonical ALIDs. It contains the subset for every Analysis; there is no partial-Analysis mode. It is stored alongside the other optional derived Zarr artifacts:
data.zarr/
  rho/
  top_hits/
  indexed_subsets/
    <name>/
Each subset stores Store Variant Indices and enough Analysis-major statistic planes and encoding side tables to reproduce the release’s ordinary association result over those variants. That means Z and SE always, EAF when the release has it, and Association Status for a Reference-Completed release. Beta and p-value remain derived from Z and SE, and Analysis-level sample size remains in analyses.tsv; none is duplicated into the index.
There is no Z-only profile. The #262 prototype measured the complete HapMap3 index at 5.211 GB (15.0% of the 34.681 GB release), versus 3.676 GB (10.6%) for Z alone: full statistics cost 1.42x, not 2x. The final #267 production run on OGS-00009 measured 6,235,037,696 physical bytes (17.852% over the release’s 34,926,288,896 physical bytes), a build of 4,198 s, and an exact-equivalence warm median of 407.267 ms (max 407.823 ms) for ukb-b-17805’s 1,178,549 present associations (docs/benchmark-output/opengwasdb_267_indexed_subset_benchmark.{json,qmd}, issue #267). Those production figures, not the prototype’s, are the cost of the decision. The extra state and query contract of two profiles are not justified by saving the prototype’s 4.4% of the source release, especially when SE and EAF make the same index useful for instrument extraction and beta reconstruction. Residual-coded SE is also unreadable without the EAF it was coded against, so SE and its EAF dependencies are one indivisible bundle.
The public build and query interface follows the existing flat CLI:
opengwasdb build-indexed-subset STORE SUBSET_NAME \
  --variant-list hm3.alid.txt --reference-assembly GRCh38

opengwasdb query-analysis STORE ANALYSIS_ID --indexed-subset SUBSET_NAME
The variant-list assembly is mandatory because cross-Store Variant Identity is Reference Assembly plus ALID. Generation rejects a mismatched assembly, non-canonical or duplicate ALIDs, an invalid subset name, and a list with no Store matches. ALIDs absent from the Store Variant Table are permitted but counted and recorded; they are never silently treated as present. The index stores its input checksum, assembly, requested/resolved counts, encoding and build provenance.
A query through an Indexed Variant Subset has the same result fields, orientation, missing-cell filtering and genomic ordering as filtering the ordinary analysis() result to the same Store Variant Indices. Requesting an unknown, incomplete, stale or invalid subset fails loudly; it never silently falls back to the primary 15-second path. The named subset is resolved and structurally validated before the Analysis ID is looked up, so a bad selector fails even when the Analysis ID is also unknown, while a valid subset with an unknown Analysis ID keeps the ordinary empty result. A caller that does not request a subset sees unchanged query behaviour.
Indexed Variant Subsets are non-authoritative derived artifacts, like the Top-Hit Index and Rho Matrix. They may be added, atomically replaced or removed in place without minting a Store Release because they change no association or Analytical Metadata and an unaware reader still reads the primary planes correctly. Generation stages the complete named group and publishes it under a release-local lock. Validation checks its identity, shapes, Variant Indices, encoding dependencies and decoded values against the primary planes. Deleting the group leaves a valid release whose ordinary queries are unchanged.
They do not move format_version. This narrows ADRs 0038 and 0041: their “optional array, index, or sidecar” compatibility example applies to optional Store-format content a reader may need to interpret authoritative data, not to a self-describing acceleration artifact that can be deleted without changing any existing query answer. The package and specification learn the optional namespace, while the Store Release’s authoritative representation remains the same format.
The index content remains Dense-only. Ragged already stores each Analysis as a direct CSR slice, so it gets none. A Hybrid release is served by the index over its self-contained Dense Component: issue #271 resolves a Hybrid root to <root>/dense, indexes only that component’s on-panel variants, and never unifies it with the Ragged Overflow (see the amendment below).



Issue #271 extends the public interface without widening the artifact: an Indexed Variant Subset is still Dense-only content, and a Hybrid release’s overlay makes it reachable from the release root.

build-indexed-subset <hybrid-root> ... resolves to <root>/dense and stores dense/data.zarr/indexed_subsets/<name>. It indexes the Dense Component’s on-panel variants only and never reads or merges the Ragged Overflow association planes. The recorded source identity is the nested Dense Component’s own (<store_id>-dense), because that is the release the read seam validates against.
A requested canonical ALID that exists only on the shared/overflow axis is refused by name. Resolving against the Dense Component alone would otherwise count it as “absent from this Store Release” and drop it – exactly the plausible-wrong-answer class the project refuses. An ALID absent from both the Dense Component and the shared union table keeps the existing counted-as-absent handling; the shared table makes the two distinguishable, and that is the only reason the existing handling is preserved. ADR 0065 adds an opt-in skip policy that leaves such an ALID out and records it; refuse remains the default and this rule is unchanged for it.
query-analysis <hybrid-root> ANALYSIS_ID --indexed-subset <name> delegates to the nested Dense Component’s index, remaps the panel-local variant_index through dense_to_shared.npy, and returns the ordinary six arrays over the on-panel subset. It never reads or appends the Overflow and never falls back to either ordinary path. A query without a selector is unchanged.
Discovery (list_indexed_subsets), removal (remove_indexed_subset), validation, overview and the CLI resolve the Hybrid root, so an operator does not name <root>/dense; a direct nested-Dense target remains compatible.
Ragged releases remain refused. The Dense Component is already a valid Dense release, so reusing the unchanged Dense builder, validator and read seam is what makes this a re-rooting rather than a second implementation.

The overflow-only rule is deliberately asymmetric with a direct nested-Dense build: a caller who names <root>/dense has explicitly targeted the Dense Component, so an off-panel ALID there is absent-and-counted as before. Naming the Hybrid root asks for the release’s variants, where an off-panel ALID is a request the index cannot satisfy.




Membership index only. Rejected: its approximately 11 MB footprint is attractive, but HapMap3 intersects 99.736% of OGS-00009’s row chunks and the measured query remains 15.37 seconds, missing the target by over an order of magnitude.
Z-only and full profiles. Rejected initially: the full profile adds 1.535 GB to the measured HapMap3 artifact and removes an entire format, validation and query-state branch. A later measured need may add a new explicit profile; arbitrary per-plane switches are not admitted.
Per-Analysis indexes. Rejected: they add partial coverage, cold-query and discovery states for little benefit. An Indexed Variant Subset covers every Analysis or does not exist.
External projection artifact. Rejected: callers would have to locate and match a second path to a release. The established Rho and Top-Hit pattern puts optional derived artifacts under data.zarr and validates them with the release they accelerate.
A new Store Release. Rejected: the index changes no authoritative association data or metadata and is entirely rebuildable from the release and variant list.
“Projection” as the public term. Rejected: it describes the array/database implementation but not the user concept. “Indexed Variant Subset” states both the selected domain object and its acceleration purpose.





OGS-00009 users may choose no extra storage or one HapMap3 index; no Store Release pays the cost by default. The #262 prototype put that index at 5.211 GB, and the final #267 production index measured 6,235,037,696 physical bytes (17.852% of the release’s physical bytes).
The #262 prototype Z path returns 1,178,549 present associations for ukb-b-17805 in 11.9 ms median and is byte-equivalent after decoding, including exact overflow values; that is a prototype, Z-only figure, not the production cost. The #267 production run measured the full-statistic index at a 407.267 ms warm median over the same 1,178,549 associations, byte-exact against the primary result, and a 4,198 s build.
The #267 production build’s peak RSS was 1,234.8 MB against its declared band-plus-fixed-overhead bound of 1,146.1 MB, so the run recorded peak_rss_within_bound = false. The miss is reported honestly rather than the bound being widened after the fact; the peak is independent of the full matrix. The #270 per-phase measurement below shows it is set by ALID resolution, not by the writer band.
#270 removed the build’s output-chunk write amplification and made the build’s publication gate a documented deterministic sample. The old writer banded by cell budget alone – about 1,976 subset variants on OGS-00009 – and so partially read, recomputed and recompressed each 65,536-variant output chunk about 33 times per plane. The writer now walks whole physical output files (a v2 chunk, or a v3 shard so a shard is never a read-modify-write), plane at a time, and tiles the Analysis axis within the band. The tile is capped by the band budget with a floor of one Analysis, so the largest materialised source block is max(band_cells, write unit) – one physical output unit when the budget is smaller – independent of the subset’s length; a tile that fits the budget is a whole multiple of the primary’s read unit, and a budget below that unit decodes the primary once per tile rather than materialising write unit x read unit cells. DEFAULT_BAND_CELLS is exactly one output write unit times a representative primary read unit (65,536 x 1,000 = 65,536,000 cells), so a v2 build decodes each primary file once: the historical 4,000,000-cell budget gave a 61-Analysis tile and split one 1,000-Analysis primary read unit into 17 tiles, while the default gives a 1,000-Analysis tile. On the fresh #270 OGS-00009 HapMap3 build every one of the 38,456 z, se and eaf physical files was encoded exactly once (measured at the store layer). The build took 187.53 s – write 176.076 s and the publication gate 1.939 s – against the #267 build’s 4,198 s, with byte-exact six-field equivalence, 6,235,009,024 physical index bytes (17.852%) and a 1,234.8 MB peak RSS. The writer-memory invariant is independent of RSS: max_materialized_cells <= max(band_cells, write unit) (65,536,000 cells here), with the derived raw buffer bytes recorded per plane/dtype. The benchmark’s RSS target is deliberately unchanged from the #267 acceptance threshold of 1,146.1 MB (the original 4,000,000-cell declaration), so the run still records peak_rss_within_bound = false; the peak is ALID-resolution-bound, not writer-band-bound, and the threshold is not widened to turn it green.
The build’s gate validates the structural invariants exhaustively (identity and attributes, exact array set, shapes/dtypes/chunking, the full Variant Index, counts and provenance), together with the small side-table remapping and the per-variant EAF baseline/reference, and replaces the full-matrix decoded comparison with a bounded deterministic stratified sample: the four corners, the slot before/at/last-of a spread of physical write-unit boundaries and, separately, a small inner-chunk spread, 16 evenly spaced Analyses, and input-checksum-seeded cells – 528 cells on the #270 run (seed 166638625948460791), independent of the matrix. Standalone validate_store/validate_indexed_subsets remain exhaustive and decode every indexed cell, side table, imputed mask and reference EAF, so an isolated corruption the build sample can miss is refused by an explicit audit. That pass uses its own EXHAUSTIVE_VALIDATION_BAND_CELLS (4,000,000 cells, unchanged from #267) so its float32 decode does not grow to the writer’s 65,536,000-cell source block; the build records the mode, sample strategy, seed, cell count and sampled duration. The risk is documented rather than hidden, and the low build cost is part of this ADR’s outcome.
The #270 query latency was measured at 456.64 ms warm median in that benchmark run. The index chunk/shard geometry and per-plane physical bytes are identical to #267’s and the query path is unchanged, so the difference from the #267 figure is not attributable to this change.
The store format gains a compatible optional index namespace and validation rules. The specification, overview rendering, CLI documentation and sibling repository walkthrough must describe it in the implementation change.
The existing broad immutability wording must distinguish authoritative Store contents from rebuildable derived indexes, making the already-shipped Top-Hit/Rho in-place precedent explicit rather than leaving it exceptional by accident.

text:
Issue #271 extends the public interface without widening the artifact: an Indexed Variant Subset is still Dense-only content, and a Hybrid release’s overlay makes it reachable from the release root.

build-indexed-subset <hybrid-root> ... resolves to <root>/dense and stores dense/data.zarr/indexed_subsets/<name>. It indexes the Dense Component’s on-panel variants only and never reads or merges the Ragged Overflow association planes. The recorded source identity is the nested Dense Component’s own (<store_id>-dense), because that is the release the read seam validates against.
A requested canonical ALID that exists only on the shared/overflow axis is refused by name. Resolving against the Dense Component alone would otherwise count it as “absent from this Store Release” and drop it – exactly the plausible-wrong-answer class the project refuses. An ALID absent from both the Dense Component and the shared union table keeps the existing counted-as-absent handling; the shared table makes the two distinguishable, and that is the only reason the existing handling is preserved. ADR 0065 adds an opt-in skip policy that leaves such an ALID out and records it; refuse remains the default and this rule is unchanged for it.
query-analysis <hybrid-root> ANALYSIS_ID --indexed-subset <name> delegates to the nested Dense Component’s index, remaps the panel-local variant_index through dense_to_shared.npy, and returns the ordinary six arrays over the on-panel subset. It never reads or appends the Overflow and never falls back to either ordinary path. A query without a selector is unchanged.
Discovery (list_indexed_subsets), removal (remove_indexed_subset), validation, overview and the CLI resolve the Hybrid root, so an operator does not name <root>/dense; a direct nested-Dense target remains compatible.
Ragged releases remain refused. The Dense Component is already a valid Dense release, so reusing the unchanged Dense builder, validator and read seam is what makes this a re-rooting rather than a second implementation.

The overflow-only rule is deliberately asymmetric with a direct nested-Dense build: a caller who names <root>/dense has explicitly targeted the Dense Component, so an off-panel ALID there is absent-and-counted as before. Naming the Hybrid root asks for the release’s variants, where an off-panel ALID is a request the index cannot satisfy.
crumbs: Indexed Variant Subsets are optional full-statistic Dense query indexes

title: Indexed Variant Subsets are optional full-statistic Dense query indexes
text:
Membership index only. Rejected: its approximately 11 MB footprint is attractive, but HapMap3 intersects 99.736% of OGS-00009’s row chunks and the measured query remains 15.37 seconds, missing the target by over an order of magnitude.
Z-only and full profiles. Rejected initially: the full profile adds 1.535 GB to the measured HapMap3 artifact and removes an entire format, validation and query-state branch. A later measured need may add a new explicit profile; arbitrary per-plane switches are not admitted.
Per-Analysis indexes. Rejected: they add partial coverage, cold-query and discovery states for little benefit. An Indexed Variant Subset covers every Analysis or does not exist.
External projection artifact. Rejected: callers would have to locate and match a second path to a release. The established Rho and Top-Hit pattern puts optional derived artifacts under data.zarr and validates them with the release they accelerate.
A new Store Release. Rejected: the index changes no authoritative association data or metadata and is entirely rebuildable from the release and variant list.
“Projection” as the public term. Rejected: it describes the array/database implementation but not the user concept. “Indexed Variant Subset” states both the selected domain object and its acceleration purpose.

title: Indexed Variant Subsets are optional full-statistic Dense query indexes
text:
OGS-00009 users may choose no extra storage or one HapMap3 index; no Store Release pays the cost by default. The #262 prototype put that index at 5.211 GB, and the final #267 production index measured 6,235,037,696 physical bytes (17.852% of the release’s physical bytes).
The #262 prototype Z path returns 1,178,549 present associations for ukb-b-17805 in 11.9 ms median and is byte-equivalent after decoding, including exact overflow values; that is a prototype, Z-only figure, not the production cost. The #267 production run measured the full-statistic index at a 407.267 ms warm median over the same 1,178,549 associations, byte-exact against the primary result, and a 4,198 s build.
The #267 production build’s peak RSS was 1,234.8 MB against its declared band-plus-fixed-overhead bound of 1,146.1 MB, so the run recorded peak_rss_within_bound = false. The miss is reported honestly rather than the bound being widened after the fact; the peak is independent of the full matrix. The #270 per-phase measurement below shows it is set by ALID resolution, not by the writer band.
#270 removed the build’s output-chunk write amplification and made the build’s publication gate a documented deterministic sample. The old writer banded by cell budget alone – about 1,976 subset variants on OGS-00009 – and so partially read, recomputed and recompressed each 65,536-variant output chunk about 33 times per plane. The writer now walks whole physical output files (a v2 chunk, or a v3 shard so a shard is never a read-modify-write), plane at a time, and tiles the Analysis axis within the band. The tile is capped by the band budget with a floor of one Analysis, so the largest materialised source block is max(band_cells, write unit) – one physical output unit when the budget is smaller – independent of the subset’s length; a tile that fits the budget is a whole multiple of the primary’s read unit, and a budget below that unit decodes the primary once per tile rather than materialising write unit x read unit cells. DEFAULT_BAND_CELLS is exactly one output write unit times a representative primary read unit (65,536 x 1,000 = 65,536,000 cells), so a v2 build decodes each primary file once: the historical 4,000,000-cell budget gave a 61-Analysis tile and split one 1,000-Analysis primary read unit into 17 tiles, while the default gives a 1,000-Analysis tile. On the fresh #270 OGS-00009 HapMap3 build every one of the 38,456 z, se and eaf physical files was encoded exactly once (measured at the store layer). The build took 187.53 s – write 176.076 s and the publication gate 1.939 s – against the #267 build’s 4,198 s, with byte-exact six-field equivalence, 6,235,009,024 physical index bytes (17.852%) and a 1,234.8 MB peak RSS. The writer-memory invariant is independent of RSS: max_materialized_cells <= max(band_cells, write unit) (65,536,000 cells here), with the derived raw buffer bytes recorded per plane/dtype. The benchmark’s RSS target is deliberately unchanged from the #267 acceptance threshold of 1,146.1 MB (the original 4,000,000-cell declaration), so the run still records peak_rss_within_bound = false; the peak is ALID-resolution-bound, not writer-band-bound, and the threshold is not widened to turn it green.
The build’s gate validates the structural invariants exhaustively (identity and attributes, exact array set, shapes/dtypes/chunking, the full Variant Index, counts and provenance), together with the small side-table remapping and the per-variant EAF baseline/reference, and replaces the full-matrix decoded comparison with a bounded deterministic stratified sample: the four corners, the slot before/at/last-of a spread of physical write-unit boundaries and, separately, a small inner-chunk spread, 16 evenly spaced Analyses, and input-checksum-seeded cells – 528 cells on the #270 run (seed 166638625948460791), independent of the matrix. Standalone validate_store/validate_indexed_subsets remain exhaustive and decode every indexed cell, side table, imputed mask and reference EAF, so an isolated corruption the build sample can miss is refused by an explicit audit. That pass uses its own EXHAUSTIVE_VALIDATION_BAND_CELLS (4,000,000 cells, unchanged from #267) so its float32 decode does not grow to the writer’s 65,536,000-cell source block; the build records the mode, sample strategy, seed, cell count and sampled duration. The risk is documented rather than hidden, and the low build cost is part of this ADR’s outcome.
The #270 query latency was measured at 456.64 ms warm median in that benchmark run. The index chunk/shard geometry and per-plane physical bytes are identical to #267’s and the query path is unchanged, so the difference from the #267 figure is not attributable to this change.
The store format gains a compatible optional index namespace and validation rules. The specification, overview rendering, CLI documentation and sibling repository walkthrough must describe it in the implementation change.
The existing broad immutability wording must distinguish authoritative Store contents from rebuildable derived indexes, making the already-shipped Top-Hit/Rho in-place precedent explicit rather than leaving it exceptional by accident.

title: Read tabular collections through a Column Map
text:
opengwasdb-stores ADR 0036 makes Manifest Generation one pipeline that every Source Collection plugs into through files. One of those files is the Column Map: how OpenGWASDB’s tabular reader reads the collection’s summary statistics. This ADR records the map’s file format, how a caller names one, how it is read, and why every convention in it is declared rather than defaulted (issue #281).


Each tabular Source Format has had its own reader (opengwasdb.gwas-ssf, opengwasdb.finngen-r13), and a collection in any other layout has been rewritten into GWAS-SSF before OpenGWASDB could read it. dbGaP MVP (phs002453) is the current example: acquire-dbgap-phs002453.py passes each of 6,022 deposit files through an awk program that renames its columns, derives other_allele from ref/alt/ea, splits a lower,upper interval into two columns, rewrites 2.4e+07 positions as integers and writes NA as #NA. The next dbGaP datasets will each look different, so this costs a converter per collection, a second copy of every file, and a reader nobody tests against the original bytes.
The GWAS-SSF and FinnGen readers already differ only in column names and a few conventions; the tabular core (readers/tabular.py) reads both by declaration. Every convention those declarations leave implicit is a way to read a file wrongly and plausibly:

a frequency of the other allele read as the effect allele’s (the stored-EAF defect ADR 0036 fixed);
the effect read on the wrong allele, which flips every sign;
PLINK’s 25 (XY) read as MT, which ADR 0052’s alias table does;
a GRCh38 source assumed hg19 and lifted a second time (issue #85);
an unexpected token in a statistic column read as missing, so a broken file looks like a sparse one.




A tabular collection is read through a Column Map: a TOML file declaring the provider column for each field and every convention the values follow. The reader translates the file into GWAS-SSF’s columns as it streams and reads it with the GWAS-SSF reader’s rules.


column_map_version = 1
name = "dbgap-phs002453-mvp-gia"
description = "MVP GIA summary statistics as deposited on dbGaP"   # optional
ignored_columns = ["case_af", "num_cases", "control_af", "num_controls", "r2"]

[columns]                 # each must be in every file the map reads
rsid = "SNP_ID"
chromosome = "chrom"
position = "pos"
ref = "ref"
alt = "alt"
effect_allele = "ea"
frequency = "af"
sample_size = "num_samples"
p_value = "pval"

[optional_columns]        # read when a file carries them
beta = "beta"
standard_error = "sebeta"
odds_ratio = "or"
confidence_interval = "ci"

[conventions]
missing_values = ["", "NA"]
unmapped_columns = "refuse"
alleles = "ref_alt_and_effect_allele"
frequency_allele = "effect_allele"
p_value_form = "p"
position_notation = "integer_or_exact_scientific"
chromosome_spelling = "adr-0052"
genome_build = "GRCh38"
confidence_interval_separator = ","
rsid_separator = "none"
A field’s value is one column name or a list of spellings, of which a file may carry exactly one. The fields are chromosome, position, effect_allele, other_allele, ref, alt, beta, odds_ratio, z_score, standard_error, frequency, p_value, ci_lower, ci_upper, confidence_interval, sample_size, rsid and variant_id.








convention
values
declared




missing_values
a list of tokens, after which any other non-numeric statistic is refused; or "any_non_numeric", the rule GWAS-SSF and FinnGen have always been read under
always


unmapped_columns
ignore; refuse, which fails on a column neither mapped nor in ignored_columns
always


alleles
effect_and_other; ref_alt_effect_is_alt; ref_alt_and_effect_allele, where the other allele is whichever of ref/alt the effect allele is not
always


position_notation
integer; integer_or_exact_scientific
always


chromosome_spelling
adr-0052 (optional chr; 23 = X, 24 = Y, 25/26/M = MT); plink is refused
always


genome_build
GRCh37/hg19, GRCh38/hg38, or per_analysis
always


frequency_allele
effect_allele; other_allele is refused
with frequency


p_value_form
p; neg_log10_p is refused
with p_value


confidence_interval_separator
one character; never none, since an interval cell always holds two bounds, and the reader has no fallback
with confidence_interval


rsid_separator
none, or one character: the first of a list is the rsid
with rsid or variant_id



Loading refuses an unknown key, field, convention or value; a required field (chromosome, position, and the allele convention’s fields) that is undeclared or declared optional; a convention left undeclared, or one about a column the map does not declare; a map with no effect column; and one provider column mapped to two fields. A value the reader understands but cannot honour is refused with the reason, not read as the nearest value it can.
The effect type is declared by the field a column maps to, not by one collection-wide convention: beta is an effect on the Analysis’s stored scale (a beta, or a log-odds or log-hazard ratio), odds_ratio is exponentiated and read as its log, and z_score is a signed z (ADR 0049–0051). MVP’s deposit has a beta in its quantitative files and an or in its binary ones, so a single value could not describe it.
A map that declares several effect columns, as both MVP and gwas-ssf do, does not pick one for the collection. Each file’s effect is chosen from the columns that file carries, by ADR 0049–0051’s precedence: beta, then odds_ratio, then z_score. An odds_ratio beside a beta is the per-row fallback of ADR 0055.
A log-OR is a beta column plus the Analysis’s stored_effect_scale = log_or. The manifest owns that scale (ADR 0004); the map never declares it.



A caller names a map by file path, or by the name of a built-in: gwas-ssf or finngen-r13. A string is a built-in exactly when it is one of those names; a built-in name that is also a file in the working directory is refused as ambiguous. The map’s sha256 is the checksum of its file’s bytes.
A manifest row reads through a map by declaring source_reader_capability = opengwasdb.column-map. resolve-analyses, build-dense-vcf, build-hybrid, build-hybrid-from-catalogue and extract-variant-reference take --column-map, which every such row is read through. These are refused before any source is read:

a mapped row with no --column-map;
a --column-map that no row reads through;
a row whose declared build is not the map’s genome_build.

The registry refuses the capability without a map and a map with any other capability.
One rule gives a mapped row its build, in resolution and in every build (mapped_row_build): the row’s own build, else the caller’s explicit fallback (--source-build / --source-assembly), else the map’s genome_build. Under per_analysis, a row with none of the three is refused. It is never read as hg19 because that is a builder’s default for an unmapped row.
Provenance.

Resolution Records. resolve-analyses records {"name", "sha256"} in a mapped record’s fingerprint as resolution_config.column_map. Every other record omits the key, so its digest is what it was before Column Maps and --resume keeps reusing it. A mapped record is never resumed under another map.
Stores. build-dense-vcf and build-hybrid write the same {"name", "sha256"} to manifest.json as provenance.column_map, again only when a row was mapped. It is a provenance key like variant_reference, not a format change.
Checkpoints. A checkpointed Hybrid build records the map’s spec and checksum, and refuses to resume once the map has changed. The spec is a built-in’s bare name or a file’s absolute path, so ./gwas-ssf stays that file and a resume from another directory finds it.
Variant references. The *.variant-ref.tsv.gz artifact has no provenance slot: its first line is the column header its readers detect it by. It records no map. A build that consumes it records its own.




ColumnMapReader hands the GWAS-SSF reader a MappedSource: the provider file with its header renamed to GWAS-SSF’s columns. Each declared column takes its GWAS-SSF name, and every other column is renamed out of reach, so an undeclared column that happens to be called beta, n or p_value is never read. A declared column a file lacks fails loudly, and so does a field the file names twice, compared without surrounding whitespace (the GCST006329 shape, ADR 0049). The column an imputation-score declaration names (stores #175) keeps its own name.
Data rows pass through untouched unless a convention needs them. Four do: deriving the other allele, splitting an interval, reading an exactly integral scientific position, and refusing a statistic that is neither a number nor a declared token. A row the MVP converter would abort on fails the same way: an effect allele naming neither ref nor alt, an interval with other than one separator, or a row longer than the header. A shorter row is padded only at its trailing edge with missing cells, matching delimited-text semantics and MVP’s raw files, which omit trailing empty pval and r2 cells. rsid_separator is applied by the variant projection itself, so FinnGen’s rsids costs nothing per row.
Every rule the GWAS-SSF reader carries then holds for every mapped collection: effect resolution, recovery of a standard error from an interval or a p-value (ADR 0055), z-score derivation and its refusals, and the parity of the row-wise and blocked projections.



gwas-ssf and finngen-r13 are the two dedicated readers’ columns and rules written as maps, and they ship in the package (readers/column_maps/). They exist so that every tabular collection can be read through a map, with the GWAS Catalog naming gwas-ssf, and so that the format is proven able to express them. Read through their built-ins, the fixtures the dedicated readers’ own tests cover give the same associations, variants, metrics, blocked metrics and site extraction, byte for byte. MVP’s raw deposit files give exactly the rows that the real converter’s output gives through the GWAS-SSF reader, in all three shapes. The same holds for Dense and Hybrid stores built from them.
The opengwasdb.gwas-ssf and opengwasdb.finngen-r13 capabilities still resolve to the dedicated classes. They move onto their built-ins after a parity run on real data: an OGS-00011 GWAS-SSF sample and a FinnGen R13 release. Fixtures prove logic, and these two readers carry every current tabular store. A dedicated reader remains only where a map cannot describe the format: GWAS-VCF, and BESD (opengwasdb #282).





A reader per format, or a rewrite into GWAS-SSF per collection. This is how things stand. It scales with the number of formats, doubles the storage of every rewritten collection, and the rewrite is a second implementation of the GWAS-SSF reader’s input contract that nobody tests against the original files.
Conventions with defaults (missing_values to GWAS-SSF’s tokens, frequency_allele to the effect allele, genome_build to hg19). This is shorter to write, and each default is one of the silent wrong answers listed above, chosen for the author without being stated.
Applying the conventions inside the tabular core, once in the row-wise projection and once, vectorised, in the blocked one. This would be faster for maps with row conventions. But it doubles every convention across two paths that are held to parity, and it touches the hot path the built-ins and today’s stores depend on. Translation keeps the core as it is: a map without row conventions adds nothing per row.
YAML or JSON. The package has no YAML dependency, and JSON has no comments. A map is reviewed by a person, and its comments carry the reasoning. tomllib is in the standard library, and a TOML value has an unambiguous type.
A map that applies to every tabular row of a manifest. This would be one flag fewer. But a manifest mixing GWAS-VCF and tabular rows would then read one of them in a way its row never asked for. The capability makes the choice per row, and the refusals make a forgotten or unused map loud.





dbGaP MVP’s acquisition can stop rewriting files: its Release Bundle carries a map. stores ADR 0036 requires the bundle to carry the map, checksummed, and the checksum is what the Resolution Record and the build record.
A map with row conventions costs Python translation time per row. The rewrite it replaces reads and writes every file once more. No performance figure is claimed until a committed measurement harness can reproduce it.
Known gaps.

assign-ancestry and estimate-phenotype-sd take no map yet. They refuse a mapped row, because the registry will not build its reader without one.
The variant-reference artifact records no map (see Provenance).

Read through a map, malformed files fail where the dedicated readers were quiet. A FinnGen file lacking beta, a header with both #chrom and chrom, and a duplicated identity column are all refused. Today’s readers read the first as empty, prefer #chrom in the second, and read the third by its last occurrence.
A new convention is an addition to the closed vocabulary, with a reason in _UNHONOURED until the reader can honour it. neg_log10_p (FinnGen’s mlogp) and an other-allele frequency are the first two candidates.

They move onto their built-ins after a parity run on real data: an OGS-00011 GWAS-SSF sample and a FinnGen R13 release. Fixtures prove logic, and these two readers carry every current tabular store. A dedicated reader remains only where a map cannot describe the format: GWAS-VCF, and BESD (opengwasdb #282).
crumbs: Read tabular collections through a Column Map

title: Read tabular collections through a Column Map
text:
A reader per format, or a rewrite into GWAS-SSF per collection. This is how things stand. It scales with the number of formats, doubles the storage of every rewritten collection, and the rewrite is a second implementation of the GWAS-SSF reader’s input contract that nobody tests against the original files.
Conventions with defaults (missing_values to GWAS-SSF’s tokens, frequency_allele to the effect allele, genome_build to hg19). This is shorter to write, and each default is one of the silent wrong answers listed above, chosen for the author without being stated.
Applying the conventions inside the tabular core, once in the row-wise projection and once, vectorised, in the blocked one. This would be faster for maps with row conventions. But it doubles every convention across two paths that are held to parity, and it touches the hot path the built-ins and today’s stores depend on. Translation keeps the core as it is: a map without row conventions adds nothing per row.
YAML or JSON. The package has no YAML dependency, and JSON has no comments. A map is reviewed by a person, and its comments carry the reasoning. tomllib is in the standard library, and a TOML value has an unambiguous type.
A map that applies to every tabular row of a manifest. This would be one flag fewer. But a manifest mixing GWAS-VCF and tabular rows would then read one of them in a way its row never asked for. The capability makes the choice per row, and the refusals make a forgotten or unused map loud.
crumbs: Read tabular collections through a Column Map

title: Read tabular collections through a Column Map
text:
dbGaP MVP’s acquisition can stop rewriting files: its Release Bundle carries a map. stores ADR 0036 requires the bundle to carry the map, checksummed, and the checksum is what the Resolution Record and the build record.
A map with row conventions costs Python translation time per row. The rewrite it replaces reads and writes every file once more. No performance figure is claimed until a committed measurement harness can reproduce it.
Known gaps.

assign-ancestry and estimate-phenotype-sd take no map yet. They refuse a mapped row, because the registry will not build its reader without one.
The variant-reference artifact records no map (see Provenance).

Read through a map, malformed files fail where the dedicated readers were quiet. A FinnGen file lacking beta, a header with both #chrom and chrom, and a duplicated identity column are all refused. Today’s readers read the first as empty, prefer #chrom in the second, and read the third by its last occurrence.
A new convention is an addition to the closed vocabulary, with a reason in _UNHONOURED until the reader can honour it. neg_log10_p (FinnGen’s mlogp) and an other-allele frequency are the first two candidates.
crumbs: Read tabular collections through a Column Map

title: Leave an Overflow-only ALID out of a Hybrid’s Indexed Variant Subset on request, and count it
text:
A Hybrid release’s Indexed Variant Subset indexes its Dense Component only, so a requested ALID that exists only on the shared/Overflow axis cannot be answered from it (ADR 0061, issue #271). The build refuses such a list, which is right for a small subset and fatal for a release-wide one: OGS-00011’s HM3 list names 17,151 ALIDs the Overflow carries and the Dense axis does not, and the refusal came after a 19-hour build (opengwas/opengwasdb-stores#225). This ADR records what a build may do instead, and what it must record (issue #324).


An ALID that resolves against neither the Dense Component nor the shared union table is absent from the release, and the existing contract permits it: it is counted, recorded and never treated as a match. An ALID in the shared union table but not the Dense Component is a different thing — the release carries it, at a Variant Index the index cannot address. Counting it “absent” would be a silent, plausible, wrong answer, so #271 refused it and named it.
Refusing is correct as a default, but it makes a Hybrid subset impossible for any list that mixes the two axes, which is every published panel list: HM3, HapMap3 and most instrument lists contain variants the Dense axis was not built on. The owner’s decision (2026-10-23) is that a subset covers the Dense Component, as documented, and the ALIDs it leaves out are counted.



build-indexed-subset --overflow-only {refuse,skip} decides it; refuse stays the default. Under skip, an ALID present only in the shared union table is left out of the subset, and its count is recorded beside the absent count, never folded into it:

overflow_only_count — always written, 0 when the build skipped none;
overflow_only_sample — the deterministic first 20 skipped ALIDs, in variant-list order;
the same two facts in the command’s JSON summary, under overflow_only, with the policy that produced them.

The requested/resolved/absent sum becomes requested = resolved + absent + overflow-only. Validation and the read seam check that sum, so a group whose recorded count was removed or forged fails rather than hiding a skip.
A group that records neither attribute was built before the option existed, when an Overflow-only request could only fail the build; its count is zero by construction, not an unknown read as zero. The published Dense subsets in service are of that shape and stay valid.
On a Dense root the option is accepted and has no effect, because a Dense release has no Overflow axis; there is nothing to classify, and the recorded count is 0. A direct <hybrid-root>/dense target is the same case: naming the Dense Component explicitly is not a request for the release’s variants.




Refuse on a Dense root. Rejected: a Build Recipe that sets the policy for every store of a series would break on the Dense ones for no reason, and the option’s absence of effect is a fact about the release, not an error.
Count Overflow-only ALIDs as absent. Rejected: it is the plausible-wrong answer #271 exists to prevent. The absent count answers “the release does not carry this ALID”; a skipped one answers “the release carries it, this index does not address it”.
Fetch the Overflow values into the index. Rejected: the subset is the Dense Component’s index (ADR 0061), one Analysis-major matrix over one variant axis. A second axis would be a different artifact and would make the query path’s remap through dense_to_shared.npy conditional.
Record only when non-zero. Rejected: a count that is present only when something happened cannot be distinguished from one that was never taken, which is the reading #306 also refused.





OGS-00011’s HM3 subset can be built with overflow-only: skip in its Build Recipe; the stores side records the counts from the step’s stdout, and its 17,151 Overflow-only ALIDs are answered by the ordinary Hybrid path.
The subset is smaller than its list: a caller who queries an Analysis through it sees the Dense Component’s associations only. That is what an Indexed Variant Subset of a Hybrid release has always meant; the difference is that the omission is now permitted and counted rather than refused.
The recorded sample names which requests the index could not answer, without carrying the whole list in the group’s metadata.
The absent count keeps its meaning on both root types, so an existing operator reading it does not have to know which build produced the group.
The CLI prints one more line (a JSON summary) than it did; a consumer that reads the human lines still finds requested, resolved, absent and overflow-only there.
crumbs: Leave an Overflow-only ALID out of a Hybrid's Indexed Variant Subset on request, and count it

title: Store per-association sample size, and the BESD allele frequency, in Ragged Stores
text:
Issue #302, stage 3 of opengwasdb-stores #282; its consumer is the full eQTLGen cis Store (OGS-00027). Additive to ADR 0036 and ADR 0037; completes what ADR 0062 left undone (“storing the .esi frequency per association is separate work”). It is the exception to ADR 0037 §3’s se selection recorded in §4 below.


eQTLGen’s cis-eQTL summary statistics carry a sample size per gene–SNP pair: NrSamples in the published file, from 99 to 31,684, because genes were assayed in different subsets of the 37 cohorts and SNPs genotyped in different subsets again. Within the ten pilot probes alone there are 14,936 distinct values over 86,373 pairs. Inverse-variance and N-weighted methods need that N per association; a Store held one sample_size per Analysis, and the stores side recorded each probe’s maximum there.
The SMR BESD files eQTLGen is distributed in carry beta and SE per pair and no N. N is recoverable from them, N = 1 / (2p(1−p)·se²) − z², but only where |z| is not small: checked against NrSamples in stores #314, the median relative error is about 31% at |z| < 0.001. Spec §8 already forbids the result: “OpenGWASDB MUST NOT present sample size inferred from effect statistics as an observed participant count.”
The same file set carries one allele frequency per variant – the .esi’s seventh column, the frequency of a1 – which ADR 0062 measured ancestry and orientation from and stored nowhere. A Store Release therefore carried less than the files it was built from, the defect ADR 0036 was written about.
The owner’s scope decisions (issue #302, 2026-10-24) are binding here: Ragged only; the N source is eQTLGen’s published per-pair NrSamples, not the formula; pairs absent from the input are missing, never estimated; the .esi frequency is stored per association with the orientation evidence validate requires. After the first implementation was measured, the owner ruled further (same day): the .esi frequency is opt-in, behind its own flag, as per-Analysis EAF is in ADR 0036; se stays float16 in a Store that carries an n plane; and eQTLGen’s frequencies are checked against the UK Biobank ancestry-mixture reference, not the hgdp1kgp-hg38 panel.





data.zarr/ragged/n is a fifth flat plane, parallel to variant_index, z, se and eaf. It is written only when a build is given a per-association sample size, and the plan says so:
"encoding": {"version": 3, "z": {...}, "se": {...}, "eaf": {...}, "n": {"kind": "uint32"}}

encoding.n is optional and omitted when there is no plane. A release without the plane declares no n, so a build given no sample-size input writes the release it wrote before this decision existed – measured byte for byte below. ENCODING_VERSION stays 3 and format_version stays 0.2.0: the block gained an optional member and every existing release still reads as it did. A reader meeting an n kind it does not implement rejects the release (spec §21), as for every other plan.
uint32, with the top code reserved for missing. N_MISSING = 4,294,967,295 decodes to NaN; 1 … 4,294,967,294 is that many participants; 0 is invalid, not missing, because absence and zero are different. Chosen by measurement on pilot-10’s 86,373 published N under the store’s own codec (Blosc zstd 3 + bitshuffle, 0.2.0 sharding):



candidate
bytes on disk
B/cell




uint32, missing 2³²−1
149,413
1.730


int32, missing −1
149,412
1.730


uint16, missing 2¹⁶−1
149,546
1.731


float32, missing NaN
163,136
1.889



Bitshuffle already discards the two zero high bytes, so uint16 buys nothing and would cap N at 65,534. float32 is 9.2% larger and exact only below 2²⁴. An unsigned type keeps “one code is missing, zero is invalid” a property of the type rather than of a sign convention.
The by-variant index carries n (ragged/by_variant/n, the same codes, re-keyed like z), because every variant-side query reads that copy (ADR 0060). It needs no exception table: its codes are its values.
Top-hit tiers do not carry n. An indexed top-hit query resolves each hit back to its CSR cell, the way an index without eaf is read (n_pairs).
Decoded n is float64, which holds every uint32 count exactly, with NaN for missing – the result contract’s one missing marker.
Dense and Hybrid carry no n: a Dense plane would span about 25 files, and is out of scope.




build-ragged-besd --sample-size-table <path> takes a tab-separated file, gzipped or not, whose header names probe_id, snp_id and n (other columns are ignored). A pair is keyed the way the file set names it: the .epi probe ID and the .esi SNP ID – which is also how the published file names it (Gene, SNP).
Rows are grouped by probe, in .epi order; within a probe, any order. The build streams the table in lock-step with its own probe loop, holding one probe’s rows at a time (a dict of a few thousand entries) in one sequential pass, with no index and no sort. A probe the .epi does not hold may appear anywhere and its rows count as unmatched. Measured at full scale below.
Every violation fails the build, naming the line: a block for a probe the build has already passed or served (the table is not grouped), a pair repeated within a probe, an n that is not a whole number from 1 to N_MAX (NA, 0 and 31684.5 included – an unknown N is omitted, never written as a placeholder), and a table that gives none of the build’s associations an N. An .esi that lists one SNP ID on two rows reaching the variant axis is refused too, because that key cannot say which association it describes.
A pair absent from the table is missing. Nothing is estimated, defaulted or borrowed from the probe’s maximum. The table’s identity and what it matched are recorded as provenance.sample_size_table:
{"path": "...", "sha256": "...", "columns": ["probe_id", "snp_id", "n"],
 "n_rows": 86496, "n_rows_matched": 86373, "n_rows_unmatched": 123,
 "n_associations": 86373, "n_associations_missing": 0}
sample_size_scope follows what was stored, like eaf_scope (ADR 0036 §4): an Analysis holding a per-association N is stamped variant_level. A manifest overlay declaring analysis_level for such an Analysis is refused rather than overwritten, because it claims one N describes every association.



build-ragged-besd --store-esi-eaf stores the .esi’s usable frequency (parse_af: present, in range, not exactly 0 or 1) on every association at its variant, oriented to the stored effect allele: 1 − f where the canonical orientation flipped the allele, the rule z’s sign follows (ADR 0036 §2). A probe holding such an association is eaf_scope=association, otherwise absent.
It is opt-in. Without the flag a BESD build stores no frequency whatever its .esi reports, and is byte-identical to the build before this decision – measured below on pilot-10 with its frequency column. This is ADR 0036’s precedent, where EAF is stored for the Analyses that ask for it: storing a frequency changes a release’s planes, its se encoding and its validation evidence, which no existing build should acquire by upgrading the package. With the flag, an .esi with no usable frequency on any row that reaches the axis fails the build rather than writing an empty plane, and --eaf-reference, --eaf-reference-ancestry and --allow-unverified-eaf without the flag are refused rather than ignored, because a build that named a reference would otherwise look checked while storing nothing.
Orientation is checked once, over the .esi, and the one outcome is recorded against every probe. The check is build/eaf_orientation.py’s, run on a select_sites sample of the axis’s variants against --eaf-reference. It is not the per-Analysis check the other builders run, for a reason specific to this format: with three or more probes and no reference, that check falls back to the consensus of the other Analyses, and every probe holds the same .esi frequency at a shared variant – they would agree by construction and certify one another whatever the .esi reports. Without a reference the outcome is therefore unverified (a validation warning), never a consensus passed. provenance.eaf_orientation records scope: source_file, and each probe’s evidence carries the one measurement’s n_overlap and r. For eQTLGen the reference is the UK Biobank ancestry-mixture reference’s United Kingdom column (stores resource ukb-ancestry-mixture-hg38).
A frequency-complete .esi makes every association’s se eligible for the EAF-complete residual coding (ADR 0037 §3), which the tree takes where it passes its gates and saves bytes – unless the Store carries an n plane (§4).



StoreEncoding.decide never chooses int8_residual for a release that carries per-association sample sizes, and the builder does not run the SE fit or its byte measurement for one. The pairing is also refused where a release is read: StoreEncoding.from_manifest rejects an encoding block that declares n beside int8_residual se, and validate names it, so a release written by anything else cannot be certified with it. The residual coding predicts log(se) = a + b·log(2f(1−f)) with one intercept per Analysis, which assumes one N per Analysis. Where N varies by pair the residual absorbs −½ log N; on eQTLGen, whose N spans 2.5 decades, that forced the widest range, ±2.0. Measured with the first implementation, which allowed it:









SE error against the BESD source
SE bytes




float16 (pilot-10)
median 0.018%, max 0.049%
132,598


int8_residual ±2.0 (pilot-10)
median 0.394%, max 0.7905%
80,787 (−39%)


int8_residual ±2.0 vs OGS-00027’s float16 (full, 127,112,772 cells)
shift median 0.393%, max 0.839%
113,516,047 vs 192,098,865 (−40.9%)



The ±2.0 range’s half-step bound is exp(step/2) − 1 = 0.7905% with step = 2/127, so the measured maximum is the bound. ADR 0037’s gates bound ordinary-cell error at 1% and would pass it; the rule is stated in the tree rather than left to the measurements because a 16-fold loss of SE precision is not a trade a Store carrying per-pair N should make for 40% of one plane’s bytes. A Store whose .esi frequency is stored and which has no n plane keeps the measured choice.



validate requires the n plane exactly when the plan declares one, in its declared dtype; its length equal to the CSR’s; every code a count or N_MISSING; at least one N in the plane (an all-missing plane reads exactly like a release without one); every Analysis holding an N to declare sample_size_scope=variant_level; and the by-variant copy present on both sides or neither, with its sampled cells equal to the CSR’s.
Every Ragged query result carries n exactly when the release has the plane – empty results included, so “no sample sizes here” and “no rows” are distinguishable – and never otherwise. The CLI prints an n column (before association_status, . where missing) and adds n to --format json rows only for such a release; every other release’s output is unchanged.
Ragged Reference Completion refuses a source with an n plane, by name, before any destination or checkpoint exists. Completion rewrites the CSR from decoded planes and would drop n, and an imputed cell has no N of its own.




On eQTLGen pilot-10 (/data/opengwasdb/raw/eqtlgen/pilot-10, hg19 lifted with the UCSC chain, 10 probes, 86,373 stored associations), with a table extracted from the published cis file (3,880,187,026 bytes, sha256 1133a89fe33b795dde7e480e39841fbd0787bfdb5d18ef19058fa749a936f814), built with --sample-size-table, --store-esi-eaf and the UK reference:

Every one of the 86,373 stored N equals the published NrSamples. Each stored |z| is within 0.00069 of the published |Zscore|, so the key reached the right association. The 123 unmatched table rows are 120 SNPs that do not lift to hg38 and 3 pairs whose BESD SE is inf, which the build already drops. No stored association lacks an N.
validate passes with no warnings. Orientation passes against the UK reference at r = 0.996 over 10,320 sites.
se is float16 (§4) and identical to the base build’s on every cell: the shift is 0 at the median, p99 and maximum, and the error against the BESD source is median 0.018%, max 0.0487%, inside float16’s half-ulp bound of 2⁻¹¹ = 0.0488%.
Planes on disk: n 149,413 B (1.730 B/cell) and its by-variant copy 149,600; eaf 283,090 B (3.278 B/cell, float32: at one cell per variant the residual coding’s per-variant baseline costs more than it saves, ADR 0037 §2) and its copy 283,055; se 132,598, as before. The release grows from 8,717,721 to 9,721,187 bytes (+11.5%). The build takes 28.9 s at a 1.97 GB peak, most of it reading the 5.8-million-row reference.
Without the flags – pilot-10 with its frequency column, no table, one Blosc thread – the build is byte-identical to origin/dev’s, from a git archive: all 83 files, manifest.json equal but for created_at.

On the full file set (full-19250: 19,250 probes, 8,927,061 variants, 127,112,772 associations), with a table of all 127,341,798 published rows (1.0 GB gzipped, put in .epi order by one sort in 4m23s). These figures were taken with the first implementation, which stored the frequency unasked and coded se as a residual; the n and reader figures do not depend on either, and the build’s time and size are not re-measured here:

127,112,772 table rows matched and no stored association lacks an N. An independent check of 500 random probes, joined to rows taken straight from the published file, found all 3,634,368 of their N exact. The 229,026 unmatched rows are 226,582 BESD pairs the build already drops (SNPs that do not lift, the 341 associations of the 13 collision groups, 7,444 pairs with an unusable beta or SE) and 2,444 published pairs the BESD does not hold – 1 to 29 in each of 2,115 probes; no probe’s BESD holds a pair the file lacks.
The table reader alone streams the 127 million rows in 90.7 s (1.40 M rows a second) at a 193 MB peak; the largest probe block is 33,744 rows.
n costs 200,856,344 B (1.580 B/cell) and its copy 166,542,912; eaf is int8_residual ±0.5 there – 14 cells a variant, every residual zero – at 29,172,682 B (0.230 B/cell) with a 63,387 B copy. Orientation passes at r = 0.997 over 9,996 sites.





The recovery formula. Declined by the owner: wrong by a median 31% at |z| < 0.001, and spec §8 forbids presenting it as an observed count.
float32 with NaN, or uint16. Measured above: 9.2% larger and inexact above 2²⁴; no smaller, and capped at 65,534.
N in the top-hit tiers. A second copy of a plane the hit can be resolved to; eaf set the precedent of gathering instead.
A table keyed by .esi row and .epi index. Smaller and faster to join, but it binds the table to one file set’s internal order, which no published file names, and a table aligned to a rebuilt file set would join silently wrong.
A table in any order, loaded whole. 127 million (probe, SNP) string pairs held at once is tens of gigabytes of Python objects for an ordering the producer can supply with one sort; requiring the order lets a violation fail loudly instead.
A binary table (Parquet, .npz). Faster to parse, but opaque to the producer’s tools and to a reader auditing lineage; a gzipped TSV is what the published file already is.
Writing NA rows for unknown N. Omission is the one way to say “unknown”, so a placeholder is refused rather than interpreted.
Storing the .esi frequency whenever the .esi has one. The first implementation did; the owner ruled it opt-in (§3).
Residual se beside per-pair N. The first implementation allowed it, and the measurements in §4 are why the owner ruled it out.
A consensus orientation check across probes. Every probe shares the .esi frequency, so the consensus is the .esi agreeing with itself.
Overwriting a manifest’s analysis_level. It would replace a claim the manifest made with one the build made, silently.
Carrying N through completion. Not asked for; refused rather than dropped.





Older packages read but do not validate a release with an n plane. A reader before this change ignores encoding.n and the plane; its validator refuses ragged/by_variant/n (“no ArrayRole is registered for this path”). The stores side must pin a package with this change before it builds one.
A BESD build changes only when asked. Without --sample-size-table and --store-esi-eaf it is byte-identical to the build before this decision. With --store-esi-eaf alone it gains an eaf plane, orientation evidence and, where it saves bytes, a residual se; with --sample-size-table its se stays float16. A --store-esi-eaf build without --eaf-reference records unverified, which validate warns about.
A reference’s orientation must be verified before it is used. The hgdp1kgp-hg38 LD panel’s block tables are not a usable EAF reference: their EAF column is the frequency of OA, not EA. Measured while verifying this ADR, it correlates at r = −0.990 with eQTLGen’s .esi and −0.992 with the Ancestry Reference Panel, and the owner measured r = −0.981 against UK Biobank on 46,003 variants. Read as an EAF reference it refuses a correct .esi as flipped – and would certify a flipped one. The orientation check exists to catch a source reported against the other allele; it cannot catch a reference that is, so a reference is checked against an independent one before a build names it. The panel is being rebuilt in opengwasdb-stores #348 and is not changed here.
A sample-size table is a build input with lineage. The stores side produces it from the published file, grouped in .epi order, and its sha256 travels in the Store’s provenance.
Future work, not decided here: an SE residual model that uses N. With per-pair N stored, log(se) ~ log(2f(1−f)) − ½ log N would leave much narrower residuals than the ±2.0 eQTLGen needed, and might earn the residual coding back beside an n plane. It is a format change of its own.
crumbs: Store per-association sample size, and the BESD allele frequency, in Ragged Stores

title: Store per-association sample size, and the BESD allele frequency, in Ragged Stores
text:
eQTLGen’s cis-eQTL summary statistics carry a sample size per gene–SNP pair: NrSamples in the published file, from 99 to 31,684, because genes were assayed in different subsets of the 37 cohorts and SNPs genotyped in different subsets again. Within the ten pilot probes alone there are 14,936 distinct values over 86,373 pairs. Inverse-variance and N-weighted methods need that N per association; a Store held one sample_size per Analysis, and the stores side recorded each probe’s maximum there.
The SMR BESD files eQTLGen is distributed in carry beta and SE per pair and no N. N is recoverable from them, N = 1 / (2p(1−p)·se²) − z², but only where |z| is not small: checked against NrSamples in stores #314, the median relative error is about 31% at |z| < 0.001. Spec §8 already forbids the result: “OpenGWASDB MUST NOT present sample size inferred from effect statistics as an observed participant count.”
The same file set carries one allele frequency per variant – the .esi’s seventh column, the frequency of a1 – which ADR 0062 measured ancestry and orientation from and stored nowhere. A Store Release therefore carried less than the files it was built from, the defect ADR 0036 was written about.
The owner’s scope decisions (issue #302, 2026-10-24) are binding here: Ragged only; the N source is eQTLGen’s published per-pair NrSamples, not the formula; pairs absent from the input are missing, never estimated; the .esi frequency is stored per association with the orientation evidence validate requires. After the first implementation was measured, the owner ruled further (same day): the .esi frequency is opt-in, behind its own flag, as per-Analysis EAF is in ADR 0036; se stays float16 in a Store that carries an n plane; and eQTLGen’s frequencies are checked against the UK Biobank ancestry-mixture reference, not the hgdp1kgp-hg38 panel.

title: Store per-association sample size, and the BESD allele frequency, in Ragged Stores
text:
data.zarr/ragged/n is a fifth flat plane, parallel to variant_index, z, se and eaf. It is written only when a build is given a per-association sample size, and the plan says so:
"encoding": {"version": 3, "z": {...}, "se": {...}, "eaf": {...}, "n": {"kind": "uint32"}}

encoding.n is optional and omitted when there is no plane. A release without the plane declares no n, so a build given no sample-size input writes the release it wrote before this decision existed – measured byte for byte below. ENCODING_VERSION stays 3 and format_version stays 0.2.0: the block gained an optional member and every existing release still reads as it did. A reader meeting an n kind it does not implement rejects the release (spec §21), as for every other plan.
uint32, with the top code reserved for missing. N_MISSING = 4,294,967,295 decodes to NaN; 1 … 4,294,967,294 is that many participants; 0 is invalid, not missing, because absence and zero are different. Chosen by measurement on pilot-10’s 86,373 published N under the store’s own codec (Blosc zstd 3 + bitshuffle, 0.2.0 sharding):



candidate
bytes on disk
B/cell




uint32, missing 2³²−1
149,413
1.730


int32, missing −1
149,412
1.730


uint16, missing 2¹⁶−1
149,546
1.731


float32, missing NaN
163,136
1.889



Bitshuffle already discards the two zero high bytes, so uint16 buys nothing and would cap N at 65,534. float32 is 9.2% larger and exact only below 2²⁴. An unsigned type keeps “one code is missing, zero is invalid” a property of the type rather than of a sign convention.
The by-variant index carries n (ragged/by_variant/n, the same codes, re-keyed like z), because every variant-side query reads that copy (ADR 0060). It needs no exception table: its codes are its values.
Top-hit tiers do not carry n. An indexed top-hit query resolves each hit back to its CSR cell, the way an index without eaf is read (n_pairs).
Decoded n is float64, which holds every uint32 count exactly, with NaN for missing – the result contract’s one missing marker.
Dense and Hybrid carry no n: a Dense plane would span about 25 files, and is out of scope.




build-ragged-besd --sample-size-table <path> takes a tab-separated file, gzipped or not, whose header names probe_id, snp_id and n (other columns are ignored). A pair is keyed the way the file set names it: the .epi probe ID and the .esi SNP ID – which is also how the published file names it (Gene, SNP).
Rows are grouped by probe, in .epi order; within a probe, any order. The build streams the table in lock-step with its own probe loop, holding one probe’s rows at a time (a dict of a few thousand entries) in one sequential pass, with no index and no sort. A probe the .epi does not hold may appear anywhere and its rows count as unmatched. Measured at full scale below.
Every violation fails the build, naming the line: a block for a probe the build has already passed or served (the table is not grouped), a pair repeated within a probe, an n that is not a whole number from 1 to N_MAX (NA, 0 and 31684.5 included – an unknown N is omitted, never written as a placeholder), and a table that gives none of the build’s associations an N. An .esi that lists one SNP ID on two rows reaching the variant axis is refused too, because that key cannot say which association it describes.
A pair absent from the table is missing. Nothing is estimated, defaulted or borrowed from the probe’s maximum. The table’s identity and what it matched are recorded as provenance.sample_size_table:
{"path": "...", "sha256": "...", "columns": ["probe_id", "snp_id", "n"],
 "n_rows": 86496, "n_rows_matched": 86373, "n_rows_unmatched": 123,
 "n_associations": 86373, "n_associations_missing": 0}
sample_size_scope follows what was stored, like eaf_scope (ADR 0036 §4): an Analysis holding a per-association N is stamped variant_level. A manifest overlay declaring analysis_level for such an Analysis is refused rather than overwritten, because it claims one N describes every association.



build-ragged-besd --store-esi-eaf stores the .esi’s usable frequency (parse_af: present, in range, not exactly 0 or 1) on every association at its variant, oriented to the stored effect allele: 1 − f where the canonical orientation flipped the allele, the rule z’s sign follows (ADR 0036 §2). A probe holding such an association is eaf_scope=association, otherwise absent.
It is opt-in. Without the flag a BESD build stores no frequency whatever its .esi reports, and is byte-identical to the build before this decision – measured below on pilot-10 with its frequency column. This is ADR 0036’s precedent, where EAF is stored for the Analyses that ask for it: storing a frequency changes a release’s planes, its se encoding and its validation evidence, which no existing build should acquire by upgrading the package. With the flag, an .esi with no usable frequency on any row that reaches the axis fails the build rather than writing an empty plane, and --eaf-reference, --eaf-reference-ancestry and --allow-unverified-eaf without the flag are refused rather than ignored, because a build that named a reference would otherwise look checked while storing nothing.
Orientation is checked once, over the .esi, and the one outcome is recorded against every probe. The check is build/eaf_orientation.py’s, run on a select_sites sample of the axis’s variants against --eaf-reference. It is not the per-Analysis check the other builders run, for a reason specific to this format: with three or more probes and no reference, that check falls back to the consensus of the other Analyses, and every probe holds the same .esi frequency at a shared variant – they would agree by construction and certify one another whatever the .esi reports. Without a reference the outcome is therefore unverified (a validation warning), never a consensus passed. provenance.eaf_orientation records scope: source_file, and each probe’s evidence carries the one measurement’s n_overlap and r. For eQTLGen the reference is the UK Biobank ancestry-mixture reference’s United Kingdom column (stores resource ukb-ancestry-mixture-hg38).
A frequency-complete .esi makes every association’s se eligible for the EAF-complete residual coding (ADR 0037 §3), which the tree takes where it passes its gates and saves bytes – unless the Store carries an n plane (§4).



StoreEncoding.decide never chooses int8_residual for a release that carries per-association sample sizes, and the builder does not run the SE fit or its byte measurement for one. The pairing is also refused where a release is read: StoreEncoding.from_manifest rejects an encoding block that declares n beside int8_residual se, and validate names it, so a release written by anything else cannot be certified with it. The residual coding predicts log(se) = a + b·log(2f(1−f)) with one intercept per Analysis, which assumes one N per Analysis. Where N varies by pair the residual absorbs −½ log N; on eQTLGen, whose N spans 2.5 decades, that forced the widest range, ±2.0. Measured with the first implementation, which allowed it:









SE error against the BESD source
SE bytes




float16 (pilot-10)
median 0.018%, max 0.049%
132,598


int8_residual ±2.0 (pilot-10)
median 0.394%, max 0.7905%
80,787 (−39%)


int8_residual ±2.0 vs OGS-00027’s float16 (full, 127,112,772 cells)
shift median 0.393%, max 0.839%
113,516,047 vs 192,098,865 (−40.9%)



The ±2.0 range’s half-step bound is exp(step/2) − 1 = 0.7905% with step = 2/127, so the measured maximum is the bound. ADR 0037’s gates bound ordinary-cell error at 1% and would pass it; the rule is stated in the tree rather than left to the measurements because a 16-fold loss of SE precision is not a trade a Store carrying per-pair N should make for 40% of one plane’s bytes. A Store whose .esi frequency is stored and which has no n plane keeps the measured choice.



validate requires the n plane exactly when the plan declares one, in its declared dtype; its length equal to the CSR’s; every code a count or N_MISSING; at least one N in the plane (an all-missing plane reads exactly like a release without one); every Analysis holding an N to declare sample_size_scope=variant_level; and the by-variant copy present on both sides or neither, with its sampled cells equal to the CSR’s.
Every Ragged query result carries n exactly when the release has the plane – empty results included, so “no sample sizes here” and “no rows” are distinguishable – and never otherwise. The CLI prints an n column (before association_status, . where missing) and adds n to --format json rows only for such a release; every other release’s output is unchanged.
Ragged Reference Completion refuses a source with an n plane, by name, before any destination or checkpoint exists. Completion rewrites the CSR from decoded planes and would drop n, and an imputed cell has no N of its own.

title: Store per-association sample size, and the BESD allele frequency, in Ragged Stores
text:
On eQTLGen pilot-10 (/data/opengwasdb/raw/eqtlgen/pilot-10, hg19 lifted with the UCSC chain, 10 probes, 86,373 stored associations), with a table extracted from the published cis file (3,880,187,026 bytes, sha256 1133a89fe33b795dde7e480e39841fbd0787bfdb5d18ef19058fa749a936f814), built with --sample-size-table, --store-esi-eaf and the UK reference:

Every one of the 86,373 stored N equals the published NrSamples. Each stored |z| is within 0.00069 of the published |Zscore|, so the key reached the right association. The 123 unmatched table rows are 120 SNPs that do not lift to hg38 and 3 pairs whose BESD SE is inf, which the build already drops. No stored association lacks an N.
validate passes with no warnings. Orientation passes against the UK reference at r = 0.996 over 10,320 sites.
se is float16 (§4) and identical to the base build’s on every cell: the shift is 0 at the median, p99 and maximum, and the error against the BESD source is median 0.018%, max 0.0487%, inside float16’s half-ulp bound of 2⁻¹¹ = 0.0488%.
Planes on disk: n 149,413 B (1.730 B/cell) and its by-variant copy 149,600; eaf 283,090 B (3.278 B/cell, float32: at one cell per variant the residual coding’s per-variant baseline costs more than it saves, ADR 0037 §2) and its copy 283,055; se 132,598, as before. The release grows from 8,717,721 to 9,721,187 bytes (+11.5%). The build takes 28.9 s at a 1.97 GB peak, most of it reading the 5.8-million-row reference.
Without the flags – pilot-10 with its frequency column, no table, one Blosc thread – the build is byte-identical to origin/dev’s, from a git archive: all 83 files, manifest.json equal but for created_at.

On the full file set (full-19250: 19,250 probes, 8,927,061 variants, 127,112,772 associations), with a table of all 127,341,798 published rows (1.0 GB gzipped, put in .epi order by one sort in 4m23s). These figures were taken with the first implementation, which stored the frequency unasked and coded se as a residual; the n and reader figures do not depend on either, and the build’s time and size are not re-measured here:

127,112,772 table rows matched and no stored association lacks an N. An independent check of 500 random probes, joined to rows taken straight from the published file, found all 3,634,368 of their N exact. The 229,026 unmatched rows are 226,582 BESD pairs the build already drops (SNPs that do not lift, the 341 associations of the 13 collision groups, 7,444 pairs with an unusable beta or SE) and 2,444 published pairs the BESD does not hold – 1 to 29 in each of 2,115 probes; no probe’s BESD holds a pair the file lacks.
The table reader alone streams the 127 million rows in 90.7 s (1.40 M rows a second) at a 193 MB peak; the largest probe block is 33,744 rows.
n costs 200,856,344 B (1.580 B/cell) and its copy 166,542,912; eaf is int8_residual ±0.5 there – 14 cells a variant, every residual zero – at 29,172,682 B (0.230 B/cell) with a 63,387 B copy. Orientation passes at r = 0.997 over 9,996 sites.
